How could the Way of establishing the proper positions of things, nurturing life, and participating in the transforming and nourishing powers of Heaven and Earth, or the merit of harmonizing yin and yang and assisting in governance, depend upon the mere trivialities of instruments, numbers, and technical arts? Ignorant as I am, I know only of the Three Luminaries remaining whole and the cold and heat arriving in their proper seasons…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其形而預爲之待虞其巧而曲爲之防事
日益新則智日益出而物之變日益滋智
不足以勝物則天下之情將脊脊棼棼而
無所底止而勢於是乎始窮古之君子觀
風會之淳漓而乘其運洞物情之向背而
握其機抑淫詭暢澹漠其創始而化之因
弊而易之也以其意運量乎天下而不示
其所以化之易之之道天下之人化上之
意而不知其所以整齊改革之由王道之
===
行也其庶矣乎愚生伏處奧渫非通達國
體者也雖然竊甞窺陳編而檃桼其槩矣
粤自堯舜禹之相授守一道也其化蕩蕩
其俗于于無捄弊之政也大禹之言政自
養民之外無費詞也夏后氏以還風氣開
而世變日繁聖君賢相始相與反其所敝
而捄其所不足故康王之命畢公曰道有
升降政由俗革則因時之政當時講之詳
矣俗革者法也養民者意也得其意斯得
punctuated:
其形而預爲之待，虞其巧而曲爲之防。事日益新，則智日益出，而物之變日益滋。智不足以勝物，則天下之情將脊脊棼棼而無所底止，而勢於是乎始窮。古之君子，觀風會之淳漓而乘其運，洞物情之向背而握其機，抑淫詭，暢澹漠。其創始而化之、因弊而易之也，以其意運量乎天下，而不示其所以化之易之之道。天下之人化上之意，而不知其所以整齊改革之由。王道之行也，其庶矣乎！

愚生伏處奧渫，非通達國體者也。雖然，竊甞窺陳編而檃桼其槩矣。粤自堯、舜、禹之相授，守一道也。其化蕩蕩，其俗于于，無捄弊之政也。大禹之言政，自養民之外無費詞也。夏后氏以還，風氣開而世變日繁，聖君賢相始相與反其所敝，而捄其所不足。故康王之命畢公曰：「道有升降，政由俗革。」則因時之政，當時講之詳矣。俗革者，法也；養民者，意也。得其意，斯得…
translation_en:
…its form and prepare for it in advance, or worry about its cunning and take elaborate precautions against it. As affairs grow daily more novel, cleverness emerges ever more, and the transformations of things multiply day by day. When cleverness is insufficient to overcome external things, the dispositions of the world will become confused and tangled without end, and at that point the course of circumstances is finally exhausted. The noble men of antiquity observed the purity or decline of prevailing customs and rode their momentum; they penetrated the sympathies and aversions of human sentiment and grasped their pivotal mechanisms, suppressing the extravagant and deceitful while promoting calm simplicity. In initiating transformations and altering things in response to abuses, they encompassed and regulated the empire through their underlying intent, without displaying the specific methods by which they transformed and altered them. The people of the world were transformed by the ruler's intent without knowing the reasons behind the ordering and reforms. In this way, the realization of the Kingly Way came close indeed!

I, a foolish student, live in humble obscurity and am not one who thoroughly comprehends the fundamental principles of the state. Even so, I have ventured to peer into old texts and roughly measure their general outline. Ever since Yao, Shun, and Yu transmitted the succession to one another, they held fast to a single Way. Their transformative influence was vast and boundless, their customs were self-contented and at ease, and there were no policies aimed merely at remedying abuses. When the Great Yu spoke of governance, beyond nourishing the people he wasted no words. From the Xia dynasty onward, cultural trends opened up and worldly changes grew daily more complex; only then did sage rulers and worthy chief councillors begin to work together to reverse what had fallen into decay and remedy what was deficient. Thus, when King Kang charged the Duke of Bi, he said: "The Way has its rises and falls; governance changes in accordance with customs." Governance that adapts to the times was therefore discussed in detail in that era. Changing in accordance with customs is a matter of laws and methods; nourishing the people is a matter of fundamental intent. Once one grasps the intent, one thereby grasps…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其法矣今之論治者曰質文狃於尚也遲
速拘於趣也寬猛岐於術也動靜局於形
也若是乎其樊然殽亂也即聖人欲爲一
切之聰明以要束之亦難矣愚則曰聖人
不能違時也能不失時而已是故有改制
之名無變道之實質文異尚其宜一也遲
速異趣其情均也寬猛異術其用兼也動
靜異形其器豫也昔者夏之政忠忠之弊
小人以野商人承之以質質之弊小人以
===
鬼周人承之以文三王之道若循環然逮
於周而天下之變極矣先進禮樂庶幾乎
彬彬君子哉及其弊也暴孽情飾淫志文
武周公之德其衰矣夫子傷周道而追思
虞夏旣雕旣琢其將復歸於朴乎然則從
周者從其文質之得中者也爲下不倍之
義也感周道之弊者憂文勝之趨如水之
日流於下而不可返也斟酌四代之意也
故曰質文殊而其宜一也齊魯之興也伯
punctuated: 其法矣。今之論治者曰：「質文狃於尚也，遲速拘於趣也，寬猛岐於術也，動靜局於形也。」若是乎其樊然殽亂也，即聖人欲爲一切之聰明以要束之，亦難矣。愚則曰：聖人不能違時也，能不失時而已。是故有改制之名，無變道之實。質文異尚，其宜一也；遲速異趣，其情均也；寬猛異術，其用兼也；動靜異形，其器豫也。昔者夏之政忠，忠之弊，小人以野；商人承之以質，質之弊，小人以鬼；周人承之以文。三王之道，若循環然。逮於周而天下之變極矣，先進禮樂，庶幾乎彬彬君子哉！及其弊也，暴孽情，飾淫志，文、武、周公之德其衰矣。夫子傷周道而追思虞、夏，旣雕旣琢，其將復歸於朴乎？然則從周者，從其文質之得中者也，爲下不倍之義也；感周道之弊者，憂文勝之趨，如水之日流於下而不可返也，斟酌四代之意也。故曰：質文殊而其宜一也。齊、魯之興也，伯
translation_en: … obtains its method. Those who discuss governance today say: "Substance and refinement are bound by what is esteemed; slowness and rapidity are constrained by tendencies; leniency and severity diverge in technique; activity and tranquility are confined by outward form." If things are so tangled and confused as this, even if a sage wished to exercise all-encompassing wisdom to bind and regulate them, it would be difficult indeed. Yet I would say: the sage cannot go against the times; he is merely able not to miss the times. Therefore, there is the name of altering institutions, without the reality of changing the Way. Substance and refinement differ in what they esteem, yet their appropriateness is one; slowness and rapidity differ in tendency, yet their underlying disposition is equal; leniency and severity differ in technique, yet their application is combined; activity and tranquility differ in form, yet their instruments are prepared in advance. In antiquity, the governance of the Xia was marked by loyalty, and when loyalty deteriorated, petty men became rustic; the people of Shang succeeded it with substance [reverence], and when substance deteriorated, petty men became superstitious; the people of Zhou succeeded it with refinement. The Way of the Three Kings was like a revolving cycle. By the time of the Zhou, the transformations of the world had reached their extreme. Those of earlier generations in rites and music were nigh unto the accomplished gentleman in whom substance and refinement were well-blended! Yet when deterioration set in, people exposed perverse passions [?] and adorned licentious ambitions, and the virtue of King Wen, King Wu, and the Duke of Zhou fell into decline. The Master [Confucius] lamented the Way of Zhou and fondly recalled Yu [Shun] and Xia: once carved and polished, should things not return again to uncarved simplicity? Thus, "following Zhou" meant following that in which its refinement and substance achieved the mean, which is the principle that a subject below does not rebel; whereas being moved by the deterioration of the Way of Zhou meant worrying that the trend of refinement prevailing over substance was like water flowing downward day by day without return, which was the intent behind weighing and selecting from the four dynasties. Hence it is said: substance and refinement differ, yet their appropriateness is one. At the rise of Qi and Lu, Bo…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
禽變其俗革其禮三年而報政可謂遲矣
太公簡其君臣禮從其俗五月而報政可
謂疾矣方二公以宿德巍勳肇基啓宇豈
非聖人之遺化好禮樂之國哉然疾者近
於强而不可與持久遲者近於弱而其教
可長存蓋其積漸然也周公之嘆睹微而
推其著也孔子之論由今而反諸古也要
之勢窮則變變則通使魯公能循方冊以
復文武之舊必不至積弱而折入於齊桓
===
公敬仲能惇信明義以脩太公之遺烈則
田氏安得竊齊國而代之惟其衰而莫爲
之捄或捄之而不得其道是以其勢日趨
於極重而不可反耳非其始爲政者之過
也故曰遲速殊而其情均也黃霸施寬和
於綜覈之日乘强之勢者利用惠而法固
未甞弛也若鄭俗之淫未殄餘風子太叔
一朝反其舊而呴濡之衡扼旣解則羣馬
竊轡矣此非寬之失也不善用寬者之咎
punctuated: 禽變其俗，革其禮，三年而報政，可謂遲矣；太公簡其君臣禮，從其俗，五月而報政，可謂疾矣。方二公以宿德巍勳，肇基啓宇，豈非聖人之遺化、好禮樂之國哉？然疾者近於强，而不可與持久；遲者近於弱，而其教可長存，蓋其積漸然也。周公之嘆，睹微而推其著也；孔子之論，由今而反諸古也。要之，勢窮則變，變則通。使魯公能循方冊以復文、武之舊，必不至積弱而折入於齊；桓公、敬仲能惇信明義以脩太公之遺烈，則田氏安得竊齊國而代之？惟其衰而莫爲之捄，或捄之而不得其道，是以其勢日趨於極重而不可反耳，非其始爲政者之過也。故曰：遲速殊而其情均也。黃霸施寬和於綜覈之日，乘强之勢者利用惠，而法固未甞弛也；若鄭俗之淫未殄餘風，子太叔一朝反其舊而呴濡之，衡扼旣解，則羣馬竊轡矣。此非寬之失也，不善用寬者之咎
translation_en:
… [Bo]qin changed their customs and reformed their rites, reporting on his governance only after three years—this may be called slow. The Grand Duke (Taigong) simplified the rites between ruler and minister and followed their customs, reporting on his governance after five months—this may be called swift. When the two dukes, with their venerable virtue and towering merit, first laid the foundations and opened up their territories, were these not states steeped in the lingering transformative influence of the sages and fond of rites and music? Yet what is swift borders on strength, though it cannot be sustained for long; what is slow borders on weakness, though its teachings can endure. This is because of how they gradually accumulated over time. The sigh of the Duke of Zhou was a case of perceiving the subtle and inferring what would become manifest; the judgment of Confucius was a case of proceeding from the present to trace back to antiquity. In sum, when a tendency reaches its limit, it changes; having changed, it finds a way through. Had the dukes of Lu been able to follow the wooden tablets and bamboo slips of the records to restore the old ways of King Wen and King Wu, they surely would not have sunk into cumulative weakness and been broken and absorbed into Qi. Had Duke Huan and Jingzhong [Guan Zhong] been able to foster trustworthiness and clarify righteousness so as to cultivate the glorious legacy of the Grand Duke, how could the Tian clan have usurped the state of Qi and replaced them? It was only because when they declined no one remedied the situation—or someone tried to remedy it without finding the proper way—that the momentum daily hastened toward an extreme gravity that could not be reversed; it was not the fault of those who first instituted their governance. Therefore it is said: slowness and swiftness differ, yet their underlying reality is the same.

Huang Ba practiced leniency and harmony in an age of stringent verification; one who rides a momentum of strength profits from using kindness, while the laws were never actually relaxed. By contrast, when the licentious customs of Zheng had not yet been eradicated of their lingering habits, Zitaishu suddenly reversed the old policy of severity and coddled them; once the yoke and collar were unfastened, the herd of horses stole away with the reins. This was not a failure of leniency itself, but the fault of one who did not know how to use leniency well…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也諸葛孔明承劉璋闇懦之後乗弱之勢
者利用威而惠固未嘗壅也若嚴延年之
鷙烈則馬力竭而猶求焉靡不敗矣此非
嚴之失也不善用嚴者之咎也至矣哉大
舜與孔子乎御衆以寬矣而不捐四裔之
罰寬則得衆矣而不徐徐於兩觀之誅苟
有大舜孔子之心則刑罰者皆至仁之作
用也曾何病於寬乎故曰寬猛殊而其用
兼也宓子賤之宰單父也穆穆乎彈琴而
===
理其逸若此矣巫馬期為之非見星出入
則不能治其勞若彼焉非獨其才不同其
器之深淺異也凡器之所受者大則以我
待物而有餘所畜者隘則以物博我而不
足以單父之褊乃有賢於不齊者五人子
賤事之而稟度順之而行所無事焉居靜
以制動者也巫馬期智巧果敢之列也櫻
其神以役於物知有動焉耳祗勞形怵心
索然而無餘味矣宓子之所為巫馬氏非
punctuated: 也。諸葛孔明承劉璋闇懦之後，乗弱之勢者利用威，而惠固未嘗壅也。若嚴延年之鷙烈，則馬力竭而猶求焉，靡不敗矣。此非嚴之失也，不善用嚴者之咎也。至矣哉，大舜與孔子乎！御衆以寬矣，而不捐四裔之罰；寬則得衆矣，而不徐徐於兩觀之誅。苟有大舜、孔子之心，則刑罰者皆至仁之作用也，曾何病於寬乎？故曰：寬猛殊而其用兼也。宓子賤之宰單父也，穆穆乎彈琴而理，其逸若此矣；巫馬期為之，非見星出入則不能治，其勞若彼焉。非獨其才不同，其器之深淺異也。凡器之所受者大，則以我待物而有餘；所畜者隘，則以物博我而不足。以單父之褊，乃有賢於不齊者五人，子賤事之而稟度，順之而行所無事焉，居靜以制動者也。巫馬期，智巧果敢之列也，櫻其神以役於物，知有動焉耳，祗勞形怵心，索然而無餘味矣。宓子之所為，巫馬氏非
translation_en:
… [of those who do not know how to employ leniency]. Zhuge Kong明 (Zhuge Liang) succeeded the benighted and weak rule of Liu Zhang; one who rides a trend of weakness profits from using severity, yet his kindness was certainly never blocked from flowing. As for the fierce intensity of Yan Yannian, it was like demanding more from horses when their strength is already exhausted—none will fail to collapse! This is not the fault of severity itself, but the blame of one who does not know how to employ severity well. How supreme were Great Shun and Confucius! Shun governed the multitude with leniency, yet he did not abandon the punishments of banishment to the四裔 (four distant frontiers); Confucius said that leniency wins the multitude, yet he did not hesitate in the execution beneath the twin watchtowers (Liangguan). If one truly possesses the mind of Great Shun and Confucius, then punishments and penalties are all the functioning of supreme benevolence—how could they ever be a detriment to leniency? Therefore it is said: leniency and severity differ, yet their applications are combined.

When Fu Zijian (Fu Buqi) governed Shanfu as magistrate, with serene composure he played his zither and order was achieved—such was his ease! When Wuma Qi governed it, unless he went out and returned by starlight he could not keep it in order—such was his toil! It was not merely that their talents were different; the depth and shallowness of their capacities were distinct. Whenever what a vessel can hold is great, one responds to external things from within oneself and has more than enough; when what it stores is narrow, external things overwhelm oneself and one falls short. Even within the narrow confines of Shanfu, there were five men worthier than Buqi himself. Zijian served them and took his measures from them, following their lead and acting without ado; he abided in stillness to control movement. Wuma Qi belonged to the ranks of the clever and resolute. He entangled his spirit in servitude to external things, knowing only how to be in motion; he merely exhausted his body and agitated his mind, left depleted and without any lingering savor. What Master Fu did, Wuma…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
不欲爲之也顧才可竭而器不可强耳故
曰動靜殊而其器豫也嗟夫天下之變其
具可熟數於前矣夫膠柱不可以鼓瑟者
滯於音也夏蟲不可以語氷者篤於時也
曲士不可以語治者溺於聞也故夫質文
也寬猛也遲速也動靜也可用於天下而
不足以用天下天下之勢譬諸人之一身
然善理身者謹食息節嗜欲使寒暑七情
之毒不能奸其中其適乘間而入也爲醫
===
師者必診其虛實急緩標本之候而投之
劑此法之常也有和扁者視之察色觀毫
而見臟腑之癥結辨志氣之强弱則剖胸
易心隨其所投靡不立效要於勿壅勿閼
固其元氣而調其榮衛此神明其意而不
牽於法者也聖人不能使勢之不變猶人
身之不能無疾也燭盈虛之紀達消長之
化猶之視臟腑辨志氣之明也析幾於萌
芽起教於微眇操縱闔闢手撓指顧而四
punctuated:
不欲爲之也，顧才可竭而器不可强耳。故曰：動靜殊而其器豫也。
嗟夫！天下之變，其具可熟數於前矣。夫膠柱不可以鼓瑟者，滯於音也；夏蟲不可以語氷者，篤於時也；曲士不可以語治者，溺於聞也。故夫質文也、寬猛也、遲速也、動靜也，可用於天下，而不足以用天下。天下之勢，譬諸人之一身然。善理身者，謹食息，節嗜欲，使寒暑七情之毒不能奸其中。其適乘間而入也，爲醫師者必診其虛實、急緩、標本之候而投之劑，此法之常也。有和、扁者視之，察色觀毫而見臟腑之癥結，辨志氣之强弱，則剖胸易心，隨其所投，靡不立效，要於勿壅勿閼，固其元氣而調其榮衛，此神明其意而不牽於法者也。聖人不能使勢之不變，猶人身之不能無疾也；燭盈虛之紀，達消長之化，猶之視臟腑、辨志氣之明也。析幾於萌芽，起教於微眇，操縱闔闢，手撓指顧，而四
translation_en:
… did not wish to do it, yet talent may be exhausted whereas capacity cannot be forced. Therefore it is said: activity and stillness differ, and one's capacity is determined beforehand.

Alas! As for the changes in the world, their means can be thoroughly enumerated from the past. One cannot play the zither with glued pegs because one is stuck on a single note; one cannot speak of ice to a summer insect because it is bound by its season; one cannot speak of governance to a parochial scholar because he is drowned in what he has heard. Therefore, substance and refinement, leniency and severity, slowness and speed, activity and stillness—these can be employed in the world, yet they are insufficient by themselves to govern the world. The circumstances of the world may be compared to a person's body. One who is good at regulating the body is careful with food and rest and moderates desires and cravings, so that the toxins of cold, heat, and the seven emotions cannot violate its interior. When they happen to find an opening and enter, a physician will necessarily diagnose the symptoms of depletion and repletion, urgency and remission, root and branch, and administer a prescription accordingly; this is the constant rule of method. Yet if someone like Yi He 醫和 or Bian Que 扁鵲 examines the patient—observing the complexion and inspecting the finest hairs to see the obstructions in the viscera and bowels, and discerning the strength or weakness of the will and vital energy—he might cut open the chest and replace the heart, and whatever he administers never fails to take immediate effect. The essential point is to prevent blockage and obstruction, fortifying the primordial qi and harmonizing the nutritive and defensive qi; this is comprehending the deeper meaning with divine insight without being fettered by set rules. The sage cannot keep circumstances from changing, just as the human body cannot be free from illness; illuminating the cycles of waxing and waning and penetrating the transformations of decline and growth are just like the clarity of seeing into the viscera and bowels and discerning the will and vital energy. Analyzing the subtle springs of action in the bud, initiating instruction in the minute and subtle, holding fast or letting go, closing or opening, with a wave of the hand or a point of the finger, the people of the four…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
方之民莫不俱至者此豈有炫奇飾幻之
術哉天下之弊起於民之有厭倦之心而
其爲患莫大於德不足而求勝其民當其
未厭也雖商君愚之以徙木驅之以實塞
而不能箝秦民不便之口及其旣厭也則
沛公以崛起草創之約能使全秦之父老
怊怊乎若嬰兒之入於慈母之懷而惟恐
失之何者曲防而障者難爲功順風而吹
者易爲力天下之情方燋然爽惑而求解
===
矣吾因其情而爲之振湯火於衽席之上
則趨之如響赴及其久也人情狃於治安
而其巧無所洩狡者思詐强者思暴德不
足以返民之性情則將出於智力以求勝
之上以智力勝其下則下亦以智力勝其
上未有上下交相勝而能治者也故自古
聖人之爲天下因其固然不敢恃一己之
智力以勝之觸而後應迫而後動不得已
而後起要於使天下忘其厭倦之心欣然
punctuated: 方之民莫不俱至者，此豈有炫奇飾幻之術哉？天下之弊，起於民之有厭倦之心；而其爲患，莫大於德不足而求勝其民。當其未厭也，雖商君愚之以徙木，驅之以實塞，而不能箝秦民不便之口；及其旣厭也，則沛公以崛起草創之約，能使全秦之父老，怊怊乎若嬰兒之入於慈母之懷，而惟恐失之。何者？曲防而障者難爲功，順風而吹者易爲力。天下之情，方燋然爽惑而求解矣，吾因其情而爲之振湯火於衽席之上，則趨之如響赴。及其久也，人情狃於治安，而其巧無所洩，狡者思詐，强者思暴。德不足以返民之性情，則將出於智力以求勝之。上以智力勝其下，則下亦以智力勝其上，未有上下交相勝而能治者也。故自古聖人之爲天下，因其固然，不敢恃一己之智力以勝之。觸而後應，迫而後動，不得已而後起，要於使天下忘其厭倦之心，欣然
translation_en: …the people of the four quarters all rally together without exception—how could this come from any technique of flaunting marvels or dressing up illusions? The abuses of the realm arise when the people harbor a sense of weariness and fatigue, and no calamity is greater than when virtue is insufficient and yet the ruler seeks to get the better of his people. When they have not yet grown weary, even though Lord Shang (Shang Yang 商鞅) fooled them by moving a wooden pole and drove them to populate the frontier garrisons, he could not gag the mouths of the people of Qin who spoke of the inconvenience. Yet once they had grown utterly weary, the Duke of Pei (Peigong 沛公, i.e., Liu Bang 劉邦), with a rough-and-ready compact forged in his sudden rise, was able to make the elders of all Qin feel as wistfully attached as an infant entering the embrace of a loving mother, fearing only to lose him. Why is this? Because erecting crooked dikes to block the flow makes it hard to achieve results, whereas blowing with the wind makes it easy to exert force. When the feelings of the world are scorched, bewildered, and begging for relief, if we follow those feelings and rescue the people from boiling water and fire to place them upon a comfortable mat, they will hasten to us like an echo answering a sound. But when a long time has passed, human feelings grow accustomed to peace and order, and their cleverness has no outlet: the cunning think of deceit, and the strong think of violence. When virtue is insufficient to restore the people's nature and feelings, the ruler will resort to wit and force in an effort to get the better of them. If superiors use wit and force to get the better of their inferiors, then inferiors will likewise use wit and force to get the better of their superiors; never has there been a case where superiors and inferiors vied to get the better of one another and good governance was achieved. Therefore, from antiquity, when the sages governed the realm, they followed what was naturally so and did not dare rely on their own personal wit and force to overcome it. Only when touched did they respond; only when pressed did they move; only when there was no alternative did they rise to act. The essential point was to make the world forget its sense of weariness and fatigue, and joyfully…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
思戴其君上而莫測其所以然質文在我
如甘苦之相和而成味繪素之相錯而成
章也遲速在我如泰豆造父氏行乎獨木
之塗内得於中心而外合於馬志也寬猛
在我如大弦濁以春溫小弦廉折以清克
諧以鳴而不相害也動靜在我如三十輻
共轉於一轂當其無有車之用也行而無
迹事而無傳故功蓋天下而似不己出化
貸萬物而民莫得名又何紛紛乎繩約膠
===
漆以固結天下為哉雖然此非聖人之所
為天之所設也天之道運而無所積照臨
者為日月沾濡者為雨露鼓動震撼者為
雷霆孰主張是其太極之默運而不能自
止者乎聖人之道以無私為主以無為為
常窅然空然精神四達無施而不得彼其
眎習尚之隆汚理道之沿革如造化之相
代乎吾前而吾不知其所以為之者洋洋
乎遠撫而長駕德閎而恩博豈人力也哉
punctuated: 思戴其君上，而莫測其所以然。質文在我，如甘苦之相和而成味，繪素之相錯而成章也；遲速在我，如泰豆、造父氏行乎獨木之塗，内得於中心，而外合於馬志也；寬猛在我，如大弦濁以春溫，小弦廉折以清，克諧以鳴，而不相害也；動靜在我，如三十輻共轉於一轂，當其無，有車之用也。行而無迹，事而無傳，故功蓋天下而似不己出，化貸萬物而民莫得名，又何紛紛乎繩約膠漆以固結天下為哉！雖然，此非聖人之所為，天之所設也。天之道，運而無所積：照臨者為日月，沾濡者為雨露，鼓動震撼者為雷霆。孰主張是？其太極之默運而不能自止者乎！聖人之道，以無私為主，以無為為常，窅然空然，精神四達，無施而不得。彼其眎習尚之隆汚、理道之沿革，如造化之相代乎吾前，而吾不知其所以為之者。洋洋乎遠撫而長駕，德閎而恩博，豈人力也哉！
translation_en: …long to support and revere their sovereign above, without being able to fathom why it is so. Substance and refinement rest with oneself, just as sweetness and bitterness blend together to create flavor, and painted colors and plain silk alternate to form a pattern; slowness and speed rest with oneself, just as Taidou 泰豆 and Zaofu 造父 drove along a single-log path, grasping it inwardly in their hearts while outwardly matching the will of the horses; leniency and severity rest with oneself, just as the great string is deep and warm like spring, and the small string is sharp-featured and clear—able to sound in harmony without harming one another; movement and stillness rest with oneself, just as thirty spokes turn together around a single hub, where it is in its empty space that the usefulness of the carriage lies. One acts without leaving a trace and accomplishes affairs without handing down a record; therefore, one's achievements cover the world yet seem not to have come from oneself, and one's transforming influence bestows itself upon the myriad things while the people have no way to name it. What need is there, then, to busily resort to cords and glue to bind the empire fast! Even so, this is not the doing of the sage, but the arrangement of Heaven. The Way of Heaven revolves without accumulation: what shines down from above are the sun and moon; what moistens and bedews are rain and dew; what stirs and shakes are thunder and lightning. Who directs all this? Is it not the silent operation of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji 太極), which cannot stop of itself? The Way of the sage takes selflessness as its master and non-action as its constant norm—profound and empty, his spirit reaches in all four directions, and nothing he applies fails to succeed. He regards the rise and decline of customs and the continuity and change of principles of governance as if the operations of nature were succeeding one another before his eyes, without knowing how they come to be done. Vast and boundless, pacifying afar and driving on at length, with expansive virtue and wide-ranging grace—how could this be mere human strength!

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
昔帝虞氏言天王之用心曰天德而出寧
日月照而四時行若晝夜之有經雲行而
雨施矣斯德之盛而古之極也列禦寇氏
不得其說乃謂聖人以智籠羣愚猶籠眾
狙也抑何枝辭琢正之甚哉管蠡之見惟
執事試詳擇焉
第五問
陳貴科
同考試官教諭梁批粵西大務夷獠與土司竝
===
而土司又患在內者是作情態備陳駕馭得體而末
歸于得人尤爲根極之論匪直留心世務而已售士
佳士
考試官教諭朱批造語暢雄叙事詳覈
考試官教授李批處置周詳鑿有實用
國家之柔遠也以德而利用在威人臣之靖
邊也以才而利用在信德以濟威則威聾
而裔夷慕義才以布信則信立而異類嚮
風二者要在審勢達變而吾之操縱不失
punctuated:
昔帝虞氏言天王之用心曰：「天德而出寧，日月照而四時行，若晝夜之有經，雲行而雨施矣。」斯德之盛而古之極也。列禦寇氏不得其說，乃謂聖人以智籠羣愚，猶籠眾狙也，抑何枝辭琢正之甚哉！管蠡之見，惟執事試詳擇焉。

第五問
陳貴科
同考試官教諭梁批：粵西大務，夷獠與土司竝，而土司又患在內者。是作情態備陳，駕馭得體，而末歸于得人，尤爲根極之論。匪直留心世務而已，售士、佳士。
考試官教諭朱批：造語暢雄，叙事詳覈。
考試官教授李批：處置周詳，鑿有實用。

國家之柔遠也以德，而利用在威；人臣之靖邊也以才，而利用在信。德以濟威，則威聾而裔夷慕義；才以布信，則信立而異類嚮風。二者要在審勢達變，而吾之操縱不失
translation_en:
In antiquity, Emperor Shun spoke of the mind of the Heavenly King, saying: "Through heavenly virtue he goes forth in tranquility; the sun and moon shine and the four seasons proceed, just as day and night have their regular courses, and the clouds move and the rain is bestowed." This is the culmination of virtue and the ultimate standard of antiquity. Lie Yukou 列禦寇 (Liezi) failed to grasp this teaching and instead claimed that the sage uses cleverness to ensnare the foolish masses just as one cages a troop of monkeys—how extreme are such digressive words in hacking away at what is upright! Such are my narrow,管-and-gourd views; I beg Your Excellency to examine and select from them with care.

Fifth Policy Question
Chen Guike 陳貴科
Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Liang: Among the great affairs of Guangxi, the non-Chinese tribes (Yiliao) and the native chieftains (tusi) stand side by side, yet the native chieftains are an internal affliction. This essay sets forth their circumstances and attitudes in full detail and proposes appropriate methods for their control, while concluding with the imperative of obtaining the right men—an argument that truly gets to the root of the matter. He is not merely someone who pays attention to worldly affairs; a successful candidate, a fine scholar!
Comment by Examiner County Director of Studies Zhu: The phrasing is fluent and vigorous; the exposition of affairs is detailed and well-verified.
Comment by Examiner Prefectural Director of Studies Li: The proposed dispositions are comprehensive and thorough, possessing concrete practical utility.

The state pacifies distant peoples through virtue, yet its effective application lies in majesty; a minister calms the frontiers through talent, yet its effective application lies in trustworthiness. When virtue tempers majesty, majesty overawes [? 聾, for 聳/懾] and the border tribes yearn for righteousness; when talent spreads trustworthiness, trustworthiness is established and alien peoples turn toward our civilizing influence. For both, the essential point lies in assessing the situation and adapting to changing circumstances, so that our power togrant or withhold control is never lost…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
焉耳若夫刼之以勢而威益褻籠之以詐
而術愈窮馴至于體統凌夷法令隔閡釁
端滋萌師徒數起欲以振頽綱而收長策
惠中國以綏要荒難矣故善理國者不徒
吾德之足以懷而尤恃吾威之不可犯善
馭夷者不患吾力之不足以懾而患吾信
之不足孚知此則百粤之事可得而言矣
執事策諸生而以夷官下詢大
聖朝無外之治垂遠夷世守之經甚遐算也請
===
先陳其狀而後及制馭之方執事試垂聽
焉夫自有西南夷以來即有夷官爲之藩
籬屏蔽其種類最夥其盤據最遼雜習蠻
風脫略漢法徵兵不俟合符慮囚無煩覆
讞出非甲冑不行入非扃鍵不居其俗也
棄禮義上首功勇于公戰怯于私闘苟有
利焉不顧其後其于父子兄弟禽獸耳貪
而嗜殺其性也毒弩長矛强弓利劔茂林
叢箐疾于走兔扳崖躡蹬捷于升猱探穴
punctuated:
焉耳。若夫刼之以勢而威益褻，籠之以詐而術愈窮，馴至于體統凌夷，法令隔閡，釁端滋萌，師徒數起，欲以振頽綱而收長策，惠中國以綏要荒，難矣。故善理國者，不徒吾德之足以懷，而尤恃吾威之不可犯；善馭夷者，不患吾力之不足以懾，而患吾信之不足孚。知此，則百粤之事可得而言矣。
執事策諸生，而以夷官下詢，大聖朝無外之治，垂遠夷世守之經，甚遐算也。請先陳其狀，而後及制馭之方，執事試垂聽焉。夫自有西南夷以來，即有夷官爲之藩籬屏蔽。其種類最夥，其盤據最遼。雜習蠻風，脫略漢法，徵兵不俟合符，慮囚無煩覆讞，出非甲冑不行，入非扃鍵不居，其俗也；棄禮義，上首功，勇于公戰，怯于私闘，苟有利焉，不顧其後，其于父子兄弟，禽獸耳，貪而嗜殺，其性也；毒弩長矛，强弓利劔，茂林叢箐，疾于走兔，扳崖躡蹬，捷于升猱，探穴
translation_en:
… is lost. If, however, one coerces them through raw power so that prestige is increasingly profaned, or ensnares them through deceit so that stratagems are ever more exhausted—gradually leading to the deterioration of the institutional hierarchy, the obstruction of laws and ordinances, the proliferation of causes for conflict, and the frequent mobilization of troops—then wishing to revive the decaying order and secure a long-term strategy, to bring favor to the Central State and pacify the distant borderlands, will be difficult indeed. Therefore, those skilled at governing the state do not rely merely on our virtue being sufficient to cherish them, but rely even more on our majesty being inviolable; those skilled at controlling the non-Chinese tribes do not worry that our strength is insufficient to overawe them, but worry that our trustworthiness is insufficient to win their confidence. Once this is understood, the affairs of the Hundred Yue (Guangdong and Guangxi) may be discussed.

Your Honor has posed a policy question to us students, inquiring specifically about the native chieftain officials (yi guan 夷官) in order to magnify the all-encompassing governance of our Sacred Dynasty and hand down a permanent standard for the hereditary tenure of distant tribes—this is a most far-reaching plan. Allow me first to set forth their condition, and afterward touch upon the methods for controlling them; may Your Honor condescend to listen.

Ever since there have been Southwestern tribes, there have been native chieftain officials to serve as a protective hedge and screen. Their tribal varieties are most numerous, and the territories they occupy are most vast. They mix in barbaric customs and disregard Chinese laws; when levying troops they do not wait for the matching of tallies, and when reviewing prisoners they do not bother with appellate review; when going out they do not travel without armor and helmets, and when coming in they do not reside without bolted locks—such are their customs. They cast aside ritual and righteousness and prize the taking of heads; they are brave in public warfare and timid in private brawls, yet if there is profit to be had, they disregard the consequences; toward fathers, sons, and elder and younger brothers, they are mere beasts; greedy and fond of killing—such is their nature. With poisoned crossbows and long spears, strong bows and sharp swords, through dense forests and thick bamboo groves they move faster than running hares, and scaling cliffs and treading stone ledges they are nimbler than climbing apes; probing lairs …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
則風雨經旬搜伏則瘴癘累日其長技也
谿峒夷獠所在充斥夷之畏狼如貍捕鼠
以故積威所劫未戰先怖惟死與走無敢
拒敵者鼓行而前所向披靡其先聲也堅
甲利兵雖資桿禦而狼貪麋獷未易擾馴
軍令不遵點閱不服虛數實支受賄縱賊
而所過荆榛不減于寇其虐焰也尺布斗
粟我無所養而朝令夕集彼謂當然有事
則出而應伍鋒鏑不辭無事則歸而力耕
===
繇賦薄貢此中國之所資也地廣官高習
兵擅利生齒益繁財貨益廣詐以謀成罪
以功解種憂釀禍蔑玩內地此中國之所
虞也前代乍叛乍臣姑置不論
明興二祖開基神武振世天戈所指雲附景從
百夷之長皆席藁俟俘納款乞宥海涵天
覆待以不死乃因地置官任土効貢俾世
掌故部爲我外藩卽周人疆以戎索之意
約法疎簡要示羈縻而已然繼及之際令
punctuated: 則風雨經旬，搜伏則瘴癘累日，其長技也。谿峒夷獠，所在充斥，夷之畏狼，如貍捕鼠，以故積威所劫，未戰先怖，惟死與走，無敢拒敵者，鼓行而前，所向披靡，其先聲也。堅甲利兵，雖資桿禦，而狼貪麋獷，未易擾馴，軍令不遵，點閱不服，虛數實支，受賄縱賊，而所過荆榛，不減于寇，其虐焰也。尺布斗粟，我無所養，而朝令夕集，彼謂當然，有事則出而應伍，鋒鏑不辭，無事則歸而力耕，繇賦薄貢，此中國之所資也。地廣官高，習兵擅利，生齒益繁，財貨益廣，詐以謀成，罪以功解，種憂釀禍，蔑玩內地，此中國之所虞也。前代乍叛乍臣，姑置不論。明興，二祖開基，神武振世，天戈所指，雲附景從，百夷之長，皆席藁俟俘，納款乞宥，海涵天覆，待以不死，乃因地置官，任土効貢，俾世掌故部，爲我外藩，卽周人疆以戎索之意，約法疎簡，要示羈縻而已。然繼及之際，令…
translation_en: … they endure wind and rain for ten days at a stretch; in flushing out ambushes, they brave miasmic pestilence for days on end—such are their special skills. The non-Chinese Liao tribes of the mountain streams and valleys swarm everywhere, yet these tribesmen fear the “wolf troops” (langbing) just as mice fear a wildcat catching them. Intimidated by this accumulated dread, they are terrified before battle is even joined; with no choice left to them but death or flight, none dare resist the enemy. Thus, when the wolf troops beat their drums and advance, all before them are swept away—such is their daunting reputation. Yet although their strong armor and sharp weapons are relied upon for defense, they are as rapacious as wolves and as wild as elks, and not easily tamed. They disobey military orders, refuse muster and inspection, pad their rosters while drawing full rations, take bribes to let bandits go, and reduce the places they pass through to brambles and thorns, no less than the bandits themselves—such is their ferocious cruelty. We do not support them with a single foot of cloth or a peck of grain, yet if an order goes out in the morning they assemble by evening, taking this as a matter of course. In times of crisis they come forth to fill the ranks without shrinking from blades and arrows; in times of peace they return home to work the fields, rendering labor service, taxes, and modest tribute—this is what China relies upon them for. On the other hand, their territories are vast and their official ranks high; they are practiced in warfare and monopolize local profits. As their populations grow ever more numerous and their wealth ever more extensive, their deceitful schemes succeed and their crimes are absolved through military merit, planting the seeds of sorrow, brewing disaster, and treating the interior lands with contempt—this is what China fears from them. How in former dynasties they alternately rebelled and submitted we may leave aside for now. With the rise of the Ming, our Two Progenitors (Taizu and Taizong) laid the foundations of the dynasty, their divine martial prowess shaking the world. Wherever the heavenly halberds pointed, people gathered like clouds and followed like shadows. The chieftains of the hundred barbarian tribes all sat on straw mats awaiting capture, offering submission and begging pardon. With magnanimity as vast as the sea and all-encompassing as heaven, the emperors spared their lives; they then established offices in accordance with local conditions and had them present tribute suited to their lands, allowing them to govern their former tribes hereditarily as our outer bulwark. In the very spirit of the Zhou dynasty demarcating lands according to Rong tribal customs, the laws applied to them were kept broad and simple, meant in essence merely to hold them under loose rein (jimi). Yet on occasions of hereditary succession, the statutory ordinances…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
甲具昭或獻劍馬或貢方物萬里赴
闕仰首請
命蓋
朝廷假之官秩以固邊圉土酋藉
國寵靈以長醜類貽謀之遠經制之周秦漢
而下所未有也天順八年上
兩宮徽號
詔許繳呈勘奏即給冠裳成化十五年因方隅
旱灾
===
詔令輸粟濟邊即許沿襲于是經制既卑規取
愈陋乃至介使末將威福自恣戎心日玩
驕悍漸啓矣
孝宗末年發憤釐革正德間旋復隳廢
世宗始曲爲條約稍復
國初之舊大抵創始者多遠圖喜事者輒厭
故建白日煩紛更愈甚其究也綱紀瀾渙
處置乖方察察汶汶罔上遂私迨乎逆節
犯順干戈相尋叱咤徒勤獼薙失策竭膏
punctuated: 甲具昭，或獻劍馬，或貢方物，萬里赴闕，仰首請命。蓋朝廷假之官秩以固邊圉，土酋藉國寵靈以長醜類，貽謀之遠、經制之周，秦、漢而下所未有也。天順八年，上兩宮徽號，詔許繳呈勘奏，即給冠裳。成化十五年，因方隅旱灾，詔令輸粟濟邊，即許沿襲。于是經制既卑，規取愈陋，乃至介使末將，威福自恣，戎心日玩，驕悍漸啓矣。孝宗末年，發憤釐革，正德間旋復隳廢。世宗始曲爲條約，稍復國初之舊。大抵創始者多遠圖，喜事者輒厭故。建白日煩，紛更愈甚，其究也綱紀瀾渙，處置乖方，察察汶汶，罔上遂私。迨乎逆節犯順，干戈相尋，叱咤徒勤，獼薙失策，竭膏
translation_en:
… the foremost statutes were clearly set forth: whether presenting swords and horses or offering local products in tribute, they traveled ten thousand li to the palace gates, raising their heads to petition for investiture. Indeed, the court granted them official ranks so as to secure the frontier defenses, while the native chieftains relied on the prestige and majesty of the dynasty to rule over their kindred tribes. Such far-sighted counsel for posterity and such comprehensive institutional regulations had never been seen since the Qin and Han dynasties.

In the eighth year of Tianshun (1464), upon the bestowal of honorific titles on the Two Empresses Dowager, an imperial decree permitted them, upon submitting an verified memorial of investigation, to be granted official caps and robes forthwith. In the fifteenth year of Chenghua (1479), owing to drought and famine in the region, an imperial decree ordered that those who transported grain to relieve the frontier would immediately be permitted hereditary succession. Thereupon, as the institutional regulations grew debased, the means of exaction became ever more sordid, to the point that even petty envoys and minor commanders arrogated to themselves the power to reward and punish at will. The hearts of the tribesmen grew daily more contemptuous, and arrogance and truculence gradually arose.

In the final years of Emperor Xiaozong (r. 1487–1505), he roused himself to reform these abuses, yet during the Zhengde reign (1506–1521) they were soon neglected and abandoned once more. It was only under Emperor Shizong (r. 1521–1567) that detailed regulations were carefully established, somewhat restoring the old system of the beginning of the dynasty. In general, those who found institutions mostly plan for the distant future, whereas those who delight in meddling readily tire of established ways. As proposals grew daily more numerous and disorderly alterations ever more extreme, the ultimate result was that state discipline dissolved and administrative measures went awry; alternating between petty scrutiny and muddled obscurity, officials deceived their superiors and pursued private gain. By the time rebellious conduct violated allegiance and armed conflicts followed one after another, angry bluster was exerted in vain and campaigns of eradication missed the mark, exhausting the lifeblood…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
血于邊氓貽憂勤于
廷議是故大而逞逆則爲琱狫濬猛小而作
孽則爲蘇受楷寰師老財費而剿撫莫施
日蔓月滋而恩威竝爽當事諸臣蓋與有
責矣可盡責之夷裔者流哉夫輪轂不運
甚者必起而易轍乃可駕也琴瑟不調甚
者必起而改絃乃可鼓也今欲使之俯首
聽
命先讋伏其野心而交臂請纓能盡得其死
===
力土酋獲首領之安而
國家免尾大之慮其道豈有他哉吾所以自
治者有四一曰信賞罰二曰慎名器三曰
定經界四曰嚴勘襲而重事權則內治之
本也我之所以爲彼謀者亦有四一曰申
降削二曰暴罪過三曰孤黨與四曰禁撥
置而體夷情則駕馭之要也何謂信賞罰
土酋調發全藉
國威而威令之行全賴賞罰邇來徵兵禦宄
punctuated: 血于邊氓，貽憂勤于廷議。是故大而逞逆，則爲琱、狫、濬、猛；小而作孽，則爲蘇、受、楷、寰。師老財費，而剿撫莫施；日蔓月滋，而恩威竝爽。當事諸臣，蓋與有責矣，可盡責之夷裔者流哉！夫輪轂不運甚者，必起而易轍，乃可駕也；琴瑟不調甚者，必起而改絃，乃可鼓也。今欲使之俯首聽命，先讋伏其野心；而交臂請纓，能盡得其死力。土酋獲首領之安，而國家免尾大之慮，其道豈有他哉？吾所以自治者有四：一曰信賞罰，二曰慎名器，三曰定經界，四曰嚴勘襲；而重事權，則內治之本也。我之所以爲彼謀者亦有四：一曰申降削，二曰暴罪過，三曰孤黨與，四曰禁撥置；而體夷情，則駕馭之要也。何謂信賞罰？土酋調發，全藉國威，而威令之行，全賴賞罰。邇來徵兵禦宄，
translation_en: … [exhausting the lifeblood] of the frontier people and bequeathing anxious toil to the deliberations at Court. For this reason, on a large scale, those who indulged in rebellion were men like Cen Diao, Cen Lao, Cen Jun, and Cen Meng; on a small scale, those who wrought mischief were men like Lu Su, Wang Shou, Cen Kai, and Cen Huan. The armies grew weary and wealth was squandered, yet neither extermination nor pacification could be effectively carried out; spreading day by day and multiplying month by month, both grace and authority failed together. The various officials in charge truly share in the responsibility for this—how can the blame be placed entirely upon the likes of these non-Chinese border tribes! Now, when wheels and hubs fail to turn altogether, one must rise and change the tracks before the carriage can be driven; when zithers are completely out of tune, one must rise and restring them before they can be played. If today we wish to make them bow their heads and obey commands, we must first cow their wild ambitions into submission; and to have them fold their arms in allegiance and volunteer for service, we must be able to win their utmost, unto-death efforts. So that the native chieftains may preserve the safety of their own heads and the State may be spared the worry of tails grown too big to wag—how could the way to achieve this lie in anything else? There are four measures by which we govern ourselves: the first is to make rewards and punishments trustworthy, the second is to be circumspect with official titles and insignia, the third is to fix territorial boundaries, and the fourth is to strictly investigate hereditary succession; while giving weight to executive authority is the root of internal governance. There are also four measures by which we plan for them: the first is to reiterate the rules of demotion and deprivation, the second is to expose their crimes and transgressions, the third is to isolate their factions and partisans, and the fourth is to prohibit instigators; while understanding the conditions of the non-Chinese tribes is the essential key to controlling them. What is meant by making rewards and punishments trustworthy? The requisitioning and deployment of native chieftains relies entirely upon the prestige of the State, and the enforcement of prestigious commands depends entirely upon rewards and punishments. In recent times, when requisitioning troops to defend against bandits, …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
甘言誘之罷役論功靦然食約以故兵出
如借師行如寇若奉驕子置不敢問賞既
不信罰安從施哉宜申舊章明賞格獲級
者立驗轅門頒金紀籍擾民者按治戲下
請劍行誅夫啗之以財貨則羣然樂趨督
之以威刑則凜然服役緩急有令彼亦無
所藉口以干後至者矣何謂慎名器故事
土人有功惟優賞賚邇因邊方財詘始議
官階彼本猴冠既難俛伏更加虎翼益肆
===
憑陵曩時單騎入郭屏息階下今則輿皁
充擁比跡漢官簾近堂卑冠下履上此其
漸不可長也自今鵰勦常勞惟多金帛大
征殊績始議品銜庶等威辨而覬覦消名
分嚴而激勸著何謂定經界夷漢櫛比疆
域易淆川谷星羅畦畛無別力强則蠶食
無厭勢弱則蝟縮受侵宜先之文告各守
舊封繼之丈勘一清兼并分圖畫界勒石
垂盟其挾眾仇鄰爭疆啓釁者廉其屈直
punctuated:
甘言誘之，罷役論功，靦然食約。以故兵出如借，師行如寇，若奉驕子，置不敢問。賞既不信，罰安從施哉？宜申舊章，明賞格，獲級者立驗轅門，頒金紀籍；擾民者按治戲下，請劍行誅。夫啗之以財貨，則羣然樂趨；督之以威刑，則凜然服役。緩急有令，彼亦無所藉口以干後至者矣。
何謂慎名器？故事，土人有功，惟優賞賚；邇因邊方財詘，始議官階。彼本猴冠，既難俛伏，更加虎翼，益肆憑陵。曩時單騎入郭，屏息階下；今則輿皁充擁，比跡漢官。簾近堂卑，冠下履上，此其漸不可長也。自今鵰勦常勞，惟多金帛；大征殊績，始議品銜。庶等威辨而覬覦消，名分嚴而激勸著。
何謂定經界？夷漢櫛比，疆域易淆；川谷星羅，畦畛無別。力强則蠶食無厭，勢弱則蝟縮受侵。宜先之文告，各守舊封；繼之丈勘，一清兼并。分圖畫界，勒石垂盟。其挾眾仇鄰、爭疆啓釁者，廉其屈直，
translation_en:
… entice them with sweet words, yet when the campaign is over and merits are evaluated, shamelessly go back on promises. Consequently, calling out their troops is like begging for a loan, and their armies march like bandits; they are treated like spoiled children whom one dares not question. Since rewards are not trustworthy, how can punishments be enforced? We should reaffirm the old statutes and clarify the scale of rewards: those who take enemy heads should have them verified immediately at the camp gate, be awarded silver, and have their merits recorded in the registers; those who harass the populace should be investigated and punished beneath the commander's banner, requesting the imperial sword to carry out executions. If we lure them with wealth and goods, they will flock to serve with eagerness; if we supervise them with awe-inspiring punishments, they will submit to duty in fearful respect. When orders are issued in times of urgency, they will have no excuse to incur the penalty for arriving late.

What is meant by being circumspect with official titles and insignia? According to precedent, when native chieftains achieved merit, they were only generously rewarded with gifts. Recently, because financial resources on the frontier have been exhausted, we have begun conferring official ranks upon them. They are by nature like monkeys in human caps, already difficult to make bow in submission; adding wings to a tiger only makes them more unbridled in their arrogance and encroachment. In former times, they entered the city walls on a single horse and held their breath at the foot of the steps; nowadays, they are surrounded by throngs of carriage attendants and runners, placing themselves on an equal footing with Chinese officials. When the screen is close, the hall is made low; when the cap is below, the shoes are above—this is a tendency that must not be allowed to grow. Henceforth, for routine service in swift raids, we should only increase rewards of gold and silk; only for extraordinary achievements in grand campaigns should we deliberate on conferring official rank and title. In this way, hierarchical distinctions of prestige will be clarified and presumptuous ambitions dispelled; status obligations will be strictly maintained and incentives made manifest.

What is meant by fixing boundaries? Native tribes and Chinese populations live side by side like the teeth of a comb, so their territories are easily confused; rivers and valleys are scattered like stars, without clear borders between fields. Those who are strong encroach upon others like silkworms eating leaves without satiation, while those who are weak curl up like hedgehogs and suffer invasion. We should first issue proclamations ordering each to guard their old territories, and follow this with land surveys and inspections to completely clear up annexations. We should divide the maps, demarcate the boundaries, and engrave stones to hand down covenants. As for those who rely on their numbers to feud with neighbors and contest borders to provoke hostilities, we should investigate who is in the wrong and who is in the right, …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
奸戒諭不省今已裂裳罷秩正我典刑覆
轍不遠尔毋效尤彼酋聞之有不消阻閉
藏瞿然改行以兾復舊物者乎何謂禁撥
置土人椎魯戅于理道不敢吾抗者有文
法以牽制之也邇來無良亡命竄名其間
外煽內訌因緣為奸利宜詗其舞文用事
者治之五方流徙投夷有禁土目占恡法
與同科則奸宄不容徑竇自塞何謂孤黨
與力小則易使以義國小則無邪心今土
===
酋大者提封千里擁眾數萬鴟張鷙擊莫
敢誰何顧其御下少恩骨肉最忌一觸法
網人懷異圖俟其難作吾從中劈畫之或
裂地授官或分兵自部一寸之土一旅之
眾我無所利焉凡以定制耳夫勢分難合
息朋奸掉臂之謀地小易制絕恃強跋扈
之患孰肯發首難而貽利他人者由前四
事是我之所自治者也而重事權為急蓋
百粤夷獠帖然聽令者惟督撫耳自襄毅
punctuated: 奸，戒諭不省，今已裂裳罷秩，正我典刑。覆轍不遠，尔毋效尤。」彼酋聞之，有不消阻閉藏、瞿然改行，以兾復舊物者乎？何謂禁撥置？土人椎魯，戅于理道，不敢吾抗者，有文法以牽制之也。邇來無良亡命，竄名其間，外煽內訌，因緣為奸利。宜詗其舞文用事者治之；五方流徙投夷有禁，土目占恡法與同科。則奸宄不容，徑竇自塞。何謂孤黨與？力小則易使以義，國小則無邪心。今土酋大者，提封千里，擁眾數萬，鴟張鷙擊，莫敢誰何。顧其御下少恩，骨肉最忌，一觸法網，人懷異圖。俟其難作，吾從中劈畫之，或裂地授官，或分兵自部，一寸之土、一旅之眾，我無所利焉，凡以定制耳。夫勢分難合，息朋奸掉臂之謀；地小易制，絕恃強跋扈之患。孰肯發首難而貽利他人者？由前四事，是我之所自治者也，而重事權為急。蓋百粤夷獠帖然聽令者，惟督撫耳。自襄毅
translation_en:
… treachery, and when admonished and warned he did not repent; now his robes of office have been torn away and he has been stripped of his rank, suffering the full weight of our statutory punishment. The overturned cart is not far ahead—do not follow his bad example!" When those chieftains hear this, will there be any among them who do not shrink back and hide away, startled into reforming their conduct in hopes of recovering their former possessions?

What is meant by prohibiting instigators? The native peoples are simple and obtuse, ignorant of moral principles; the reason they dare not defy us is that there are legal regulations to hold them in check. Recently, unscrupulous fugitives have concealed their names among them, stirring up trouble outside and sowing dissension within, seizing opportunities for illicit profit. We ought to spy out those who manipulate the written law and wield power among them, and punish them. There should be prohibitions against vagrants from all quarters defecting to the barbarians, and native headmen who harbor and refuse to surrender them should be punished with the same penalty under the law. Then villains and traitors will not be tolerated, and their illicit pathways and loopholes will naturally be blocked.

What is meant by isolating their partisans? When their strength is small, they are easily employed through righteousness; when their domains are small, they harbor no wicked ambitions. Today, the greatest of the native chieftains control territories of a thousand li and command tens of thousands of followers, spreading their wings like owls and striking like birds of prey, with no one daring to challenge them. Yet they treat their subordinates with little grace, and among their own flesh and blood there is the deepest jealousy; once they run afoul of the net of the law, everyone harbors ulterior schemes. Waiting until trouble breaks out among them, we can intervene to divide and reorganize them—either carving up their lands and conferring offices, or dividing their troops into separate commands. From a single inch of their land or a single brigade of their troops, we seek no profit for ourselves; all of it is simply to establish control. When their power is divided and hard to reunite, it puts an end to plots of colluding in villainy and swaggering defiance; when their territories are small and easy to control, it cuts off the menace of relying on force to act with arrogant truculence. Who then would be willing to initiate a rebellion only to leave the profits to others?

Following the preceding four measures is how we govern ourselves, and among these, strengthening executive authority is the most urgent. Indeed, the reason the barbarian tribes of the Hundred Yue submit docilely and obey orders is solely because of the Supreme Commander and Grand Coordinator. Ever since Xiangyi [Han Yong 韓雍]…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
韓雍討平之後而所竄餘孽弘示包荒自
文成王守仁經略之餘而至今遺言尚謂
姑息故曩時赴調恐後今則催督或煩曩
時報兵必實今則名數多冒襲替廢置
朝廷雖假閫外之權而伸縮弛張臣子尚牽
域外之議自今震疊之威必行于土官土
官之命盡制于幕府一切便宜不從中制
則賞罰可信名器可慎經界可定勘襲可
嚴而中國威令常伸如震霆矣由後四事
===
是我之所爲彼謀也而體夷情爲急今夫
父兄之于子弟苟役使煩勞且不能無厭
況夷獷之性歲歲調發奔走道途不得顧
其室家治其田里其能無倦且怨乎及事
平則功歸于上而彼一無所與僨帥墨吏
又往往視爲奇貨其能無怒且慢乎既倦
且怨又慢且怒始而徵調違期既而空文
逃罪上嫉下憤月積日深當事者不惟開
誠之圖而直恃籠絡之術以故諭之益梗
punctuated: 韓雍討平之後，而所竄餘孽，弘示包荒；自文成王守仁經略之餘，而至今遺言，尚謂姑息。故曩時赴調恐後，今則催督或煩；曩時報兵必實，今則名數多冒。襲替廢置，朝廷雖假閫外之權，而伸縮弛張，臣子尚牽域外之議。自今震疊之威，必行于土官；土官之命，盡制于幕府。一切便宜，不從中制，則賞罰可信，名器可慎，經界可定，勘襲可嚴，而中國威令常伸如震霆矣。由後四事，是我之所爲彼謀也，而體夷情爲急。今夫父兄之于子弟，苟役使煩勞，且不能無厭；況夷獷之性，歲歲調發，奔走道途，不得顧其室家，治其田里，其能無倦且怨乎？及事平，則功歸于上，而彼一無所與，僨帥墨吏又往往視爲奇貨，其能無怒且慢乎？既倦且怨，又慢且怒，始而徵調違期，既而空文逃罪。上嫉下憤，月積日深。當事者不惟開誠之圖，而直恃籠絡之術，以故諭之益梗，
translation_en:
… Han Yong (韓雍, posthumous title Xiangyi 襄毅) campaigned and pacified them, broadly displaying magnanimity toward the surviving remnants who had fled; and since Wang Shouren (王守仁, posthumous title Wencheng 文成) completed his military planning, lingering talk to this day still calls his approach overly indulgent. Thus, whereas in the past they answered troop requisitions for fear of being late, nowadays urging and pressing them can be troublesome; whereas in the past the troop numbers they reported were always accurate, nowadays the rosters are full of padded names. Regarding hereditary succession and deposition, although the court grants autonomous authority to commanders in the field, in advancing or retreating, tightening or relaxing control, officials are still hampered by criticisms from outside the region. From now on, awe-inspiring authority must be enforced upon the native officials, and the fate of the native officials must be completely controlled by the Supreme Commander's headquarters. If all discretionary actions are not directed from the central court, then rewards and punishments can be trusted, titles and insignia can be guarded with care, boundaries can be settled, and investigations into hereditary succession can be made strict—so that China's majestic commands will always extend like a thunderbolt.

As for the latter four measures, they are what we plan on their behalf, and among them, sympathizing with the circumstances of the non-Chinese tribes is the most urgent. Now then, even when fathers and elder brothers employ their sons and younger brothers, if the tasks are burdensome and exhausting, they cannot help growing weary of them. How much more so with the fierce nature of these tribesmen! Year after year they are requisitioned and dispatched, rushing along the roads, unable to look after their families or tend their fields and villages—how could they not become both weary and resentful? And when the affair is pacified, the merit goes to their superiors while they have no share in it at all; moreover, disgraced commanders and corrupt officials often treat them as a rare commodity to exploit—how could they not become both angry and defiant? Being already weary and resentful, and furthermore defiant and angry, at first they miss the deadlines when requisitioned, and later they use empty documents to evade punishment. Superiors grow hateful and subordinates indignant, accumulating month by month and deepening day by day. Those in charge do not contemplate plans of sincere openness, but merely rely on the tricks of manipulation; therefore, the more one instructs them, the more obstinate they become, …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
撫之益疑卒至禍亂相尋而不解也故平
居無事則布信懷恩有事出征則宣威仗
義芻糗必豐毋使客兵一而當土兵五可
也功級必賞毋以冒死所得而穰之將校
可也廉朘刻之吏平爭鬭之端則降削可
申罪過可暴黨與可孤廢置可禁而土夷
中心誠服若腐鼠矣雖然愚生猶有說焉
漢得一谷永守鬱林而烏滸內屬唐得一
李靖撫嶺南而遠夷安堵我
===
明沐英守雲南而滇酋効順黃福治安南而交
人寢謀是故先王慎擇邊吏重于內地講
求曠度略于曲防寧使化理稍塞倔強一
隅毋俾輿圖廣收貽憂萬姓惟夫吏好蓄
積政多解弛或遠嫌自潔或求勝喜功則
遐陬日以多故耳故遠方之官非有為不
足以戡亂非有守不足以服人非久事任
無以諳土俗非重權力無以專責成誠得
其人而任之寬其約束優以寵榮即滿考
punctuated: 撫之益疑，卒至禍亂相尋而不解也。故平居無事則布信懷恩，有事出征則宣威仗義。芻糗必豐，毋使客兵一而當土兵五，可也；功級必賞，毋以冒死所得而穰之將校，可也。廉朘刻之吏，平爭鬭之端，則降削可申，罪過可暴，黨與可孤，廢置可禁，而土夷中心誠服，若腐鼠矣。雖然，愚生猶有說焉。漢得一谷永守鬱林，而烏滸內屬；唐得一李靖撫嶺南，而遠夷安堵；我明沐英守雲南，而滇酋効順；黃福治安南，而交人寢謀。是故先王慎擇邊吏，重于內地；講求曠度，略于曲防。寧使化理稍塞，倔強一隅，毋俾輿圖廣收，貽憂萬姓。惟夫吏好蓄積，政多解弛，或遠嫌自潔，或求勝喜功，則遐陬日以多故耳。故遠方之官，非有為不足以戡亂，非有守不足以服人，非久事任無以諳土俗，非重權力無以專責成。誠得其人而任之，寬其約束，優以寵榮，即滿考
translation_en:
…and the more one attempts to pacify them, the more suspicious they become, until finally disasters and rebellions follow one after another without resolution. Therefore, in peaceful times when there is no trouble, one should spread trust and foster gratitude; when emergencies arise and campaigns are launched, one should project majesty and uphold righteousness. Forage and rations must be abundant—do not let the provisioning of one regular guest soldier equal that of five native soldiers. Meritorious heads taken must be rewarded—do not allow what they have won by braving death to be stolen away [?] by regular commanders and officers. Investigate and ferret out extortionate and harsh officials, and settle the causes of their feuds; then demotions and reductions of territory can be enforced, offenses and faults can be exposed, factions and cliques can be isolated, and arbitrary depositions and installations can be prohibited—whereupon the native tribesmen will sincerely submit in their hearts and become as harmless as a rotten rat.

Even so, this humble student still has more to say. When the Han dynasty found a single Gu Yong 谷永 to govern Yulin 鬱林, the Wuhu 烏滸 tribes submitted as inner subjects; when the Tang dynasty found a single Li Jing 李靖 to pacify Lingnan 嶺南, the distant tribes lived in peace; in our own Ming dynasty, when Mu Ying 沐英 guarded Yunnan 雲南, the chieftains of Dian 滇 offered allegiance, and when Huang Fu 黃福 governed Annam 安南, the people of Jiaozhi 交趾 abandoned their plots. For this reason, the former kings chose frontier officials with even greater care than those for the interior, and cultivated broad-minded magnanimity while paying less heed to petty precautions. Better that transformative governance be slightly obstructed and a few remain stubbornly defiant in a corner, than that we broadly annex territory onto the map only to bequeath sorrow to the myriad common people. It is only because officials are fond of hoarding wealth and administration is largely lax—or else they keep aloof from suspicion merely to preserve their own purity, or strive for victory and delight in military exploits—that the distant frontiers grow daily more troubled.

Therefore, as for officials in distant regions: without capability for action, they cannot quell rebellions; without moral integrity, they cannot win people's submission; without long tenure in office, they have no way to master local customs; and without weighty authority, there is no way to hold them solely responsible for results. If we truly find the right men and entrust them with office, relax the restrictions upon them, treat them generously with favor and honor, and even when their term of assessment is completed…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
不代豈惟兩江土酋可繫頸而制命將百
粤夷獠亦伏喙而寒心矣復
祖宗之憲章而正夷夏之大分壯
國家之神氣而垂嶺海之久安要不出此語
曰明王有道守在四夷内治之謂也又曰
閫外之事一以付之任人之謂也敢以復
于執事
punctuated: 不代，豈惟兩江土酋可繫頸而制命，將百粤夷獠亦伏喙而寒心矣。復祖宗之憲章，而正夷夏之大分；壯國家之神氣，而垂嶺海之久安，要不出此。語曰：「明王有道，守在四夷。」内治之謂也。又曰：「閫外之事，一以付之。」任人之謂也。敢以復于執事。
translation_en: … not replacing them, then not only could the native chieftains of the Two Rivers (Liangjiang) be bound by the neck and have their lives placed at our command, but the non-Chinese tribes and Liao peoples across all of the Hundred Yue (Baiyue) would also hold their tongues in submission and tremble at heart. To restore the statutory institutions of our Imperial Ancestors and rectify the great distinction between non-Chinese and Chinese; to strengthen the vital spirit of the Dynastic State and hand down lasting peace across the mountain ranges and southern seas—in essence, nothing goes beyond this. As the saying goes: "When an enlightened king possesses the Way, his defense lies among the Four Barbarians." This refers to internal governance. Another saying goes: "Affairs beyond the threshold of the gate are entrusted entirely to him." This refers to entrusting responsibility to the right men. I venture to offer this in reply to Your Excellency.

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
主上楙峻德章洪業深惟太平之
原右文賓賢以風寓內寓內
士無問遐逖靡不刮磨灑濯
軌策前塗以待登選是歲丙
子秋廣西鄉試事竣旣已得
士之雋者而籍
===
奏之矣故事信亮宜有言綴末
簡竊惟勳華之世道化郅隆
七旬格苗兩階舞干文德敷
於遐阻聲敎訖于要荒萬邦
黎獻共惟帝臣而徯帝舉抑
何盛也迺其知而舉之也則
敷納以言焉爾稽九德稽載
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序

主上楙峻德，章洪業，深惟太平之原，右文賓賢，以風寓內。寓內士無問遐逖，靡不刮磨灑濯，軌策前塗，以待登選。是歲丙子秋，廣西鄉試事竣，旣已得士之雋者而籍奏之矣。故事，信亮宜有言綴末簡。竊惟勳華之世，道化郅隆，七旬格苗，兩階舞干，文德敷於遐阻，聲敎訖于要荒，萬邦黎獻共惟帝臣，而徯帝舉，抑何盛也！迺其知而舉之也，則敷納以言焉爾，稽九德、稽載…
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

His Majesty cultivates lofty virtue and manifests his great enterprise. Reflecting deeply upon the foundations of supreme peace, he exalts civil culture and welcomes worthy men as guests, so as to inspire the entire realm. Throughout the realm, scholars—regardless of how distant or remote they may be—all polish and purify themselves, urging their carriages along the path ahead as they await selection and advancement. In the autumn of this bingzi year [1576], the affairs of the Guangxi Provincial Examination were brought to completion, and the most outstanding scholars had already been selected, registered, and presented in a memorial to the throne. By precedent, I, Xinliang, ought to offer some words to be appended to the final pages. I humbly reflect that in the ages of Yao [Fangxun] and Shun [Chonghua], moral transformation reached the pinnacle of flourishing. In seventy days the Miao were won over as dances with shields were performed between the two staircases; civil virtue spread to distant and rugged lands, and the prestige of moral teaching reached to the domains of Restraint and the Wilds. The numerous worthy men of the myriad states all served together as servants of the Emperor and awaited the Emperor's elevation of them—how magnificent indeed! Yet in coming to know and elevate them, it was simply a matter of receiving their words widely, and of examining the Nine Virtues and examining their…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
采焉爾而科條簡闊不少概
見亡其所用者不必所養乎
比攷命官之詞勞來匡直輔
翼以振新其德者如此其備
故當其時士皆有常言罔攸
伏而孔子獨稱唐虞爲盛際
有繇也廣西距
===
京圻萬里古百粵地我
明統一區宇
文命誕敷武功丕振士之涵濡
衣被旣久屬者醜類蕩夷四
郊新去湯火圭蓽奧渫之儒
摶心揖志益以脩其故業而
曏閑疏邈未皇暇庠序之事
punctuated: 采焉爾，而科條簡闊，不少概見，亡其所用者不必所養乎？比攷命官之詞，勞來匡直輔翼，以振新其德者，如此其備。故當其時，士皆有常，言罔攸伏，而孔子獨稱唐虞爲盛際，有繇也。廣西距京圻萬里，古百粵地。我明統一區宇，文命誕敷，武功丕振，士之涵濡衣被旣久。屬者醜類蕩夷，四郊新去湯火，圭蓽奧渫之儒，摶心揖志，益以脩其故業，而曏閑疏邈未皇暇庠序之事
translation_en: …their deeds, that is all, while formal regulations were simple and broad and scarcely seen in detail—could it be that those whom they employed were not necessarily those whom they had nurtured? Yet when one examines the words spoken in commissioning officials—encouraging them to come, setting them straight, assisting and supporting them, so as to rouse and renew their virtue—their provision was as thorough as this. Therefore, in that era, scholars all had constancy, no worthy words lay hidden, and there was good reason that Confucius uniquely praised the age of Tang and Yu as a flourishing epoch. Guangxi lies ten thousand li from the capital region and was in antiquity the land of the Hundred Yue. Since our Ming unified the realm, civil teachings have been broadly spread and military achievements greatly displayed, so that scholars have long been steeped in and clothed by this influence. Recently, the vile bandits have been swept away and pacified, and the surrounding countryside has newly escaped boiling water and fire. Confucian scholars from humble homes and obscure, lowly stations concentrate their minds and compose their wills to cultivate their former studies all the more, while those who previously were blocked off, distant, and had no leisure for the business of schools…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者今皆為置學官弟子獲耀
闇眢于光明𦘕𥟖舒而聲文
闡視敷文舞干之世詎非越
千載而再覿哉
皇上天縱聖神雅嚮儒術頃慮士
習漸窳特
俞輔臣之請取儒林要束而更飭
===
之俾視學者奉以靡軼真堯
舜振德
盛心也諸士躬際
昌期祗服
睿訓其所感奮踔厲者豈不烝烝
然景附嚮應愈益思乘時自
効哉乃今擷所為文觀之言
punctuated: 者，今皆為置學官弟子，獲耀闇眢于光明，𦘕𥟖舒而聲文闡，視敷文舞干之世，詎非越千載而再覿哉！皇上天縱聖神，雅嚮儒術，頃慮士習漸窳，特俞輔臣之請，取儒林要束而更飭之，俾視學者奉以靡軼，真堯、舜振德盛心也。諸士躬際昌期，祗服睿訓，其所感奮踔厲者，豈不烝烝然景附嚮應，愈益思乘時自効哉！乃今擷所為文觀之，言
translation_en:
… now all have had Confucian Schools established and students appointed for them, gaining the chance to shed light on their dark ignorance and bring it into brilliance; as the glow of cultural refinement unfolds and the renown of letters is made manifest, compared to the ancient age when civil virtue was spread and shields were danced, is this not witnessing it once again across the span of a thousand years?

His Majesty, endowed by Heaven with sage divinity, has long inclined toward Confucian learning. Recently, concerned that the habits of scholars were gradually deteriorating, He specially approved the request of the Grand Secretaries to take the regulations for the Confucian community and renew their enforcement, so that Education Intendants would uphold them without lapse. This is truly the grand heart of Yao and Shun in rousing virtue! As the scholars personally encounter this flourishing era and reverently submit to His sagely instructions, in being moved and roused to vigorous effort, how could they not advance in great numbers to follow like shadows and respond like echoes, thinking ever more of seizing the moment to exert themselves in service? Now, gathering the essays they have composed and examining them, although the words…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
卽人人殊大都根極理道揚
扢今往刋華芟粃闡發本實
彬彬乎質而文也敻逸疇曩
方寓內士且凌駕之作而嘆
曰斯非
主上德化所曁及者耶是可以言
揚矣雖然虞廷之知人匪獨
===
言焉爾已行有九德於是乎
徵故三六具而浚亮茂也今
諸士言之洵有文矣第令指
九者之德而數之而不能盡
讎其文空言之謂何古之君
子身所實有則言以宣之言
所自許則信以成之是以衷
punctuated: 卽人人殊，大都根極理道，揚扢今往，刋華芟粃，闡發本實，彬彬乎質而文也！敻逸疇曩，方寓內士且凌駕之。作而嘆曰：「斯非主上德化所曁及者耶？是可以言揚矣！」雖然，虞廷之知人，匪獨言焉爾已；行有九德，於是乎徵，故三六具而浚亮茂也。今諸士言之洵有文矣，第令指九者之德而數之，而不能盡讎其文，空言之謂何？古之君子，身所實有，則言以宣之；言所自許，則信以成之。是以衷
translation_en: …though each person's words differ, on the whole they are rooted in the ultimate principles and the Way, discussing and evaluating past and present, paring away showiness and weeding out chaff, and elucidating fundamental substance. How admirably balanced in both substance and literary refinement! Far surpassing those of former days, they are even about to outstrip the scholars within the central realms. I rose and sighed, saying: "Is this not what the Sovereign's moral transformation has reached? By these words they may well be raised up and recommended!" Even so, in knowing men at the court of Yu [Shun], it was not by words alone; their conduct possessed the Nine Virtues, which were verified therein, and thus when those of three and six virtues were fully employed, governance was deeply bright and flourishing. Now the words of these scholars are truly refined in literary form; yet if we were to point to the Nine Virtues and reckon them, and they could not fully match their literary compositions in practice, what would be the use of empty words? As for the gentlemen of antiquity, what they truly possessed in their own persons, they used words to declare; what they pledged in their words, they used trustworthiness to fulfill. Therefore, inside…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
外篤懿文行光融爲世誦美
信亮方執此以鏡考諸士而
諸士亦曷以成其信乎夫吞
舟之鱗不游潐垂天之翼不
控榆枋其志遠也辟閭巨闕
不以割驊騮騄駬不以捕鼠
其用巨也故尚友匹休所以
===
明志植德砥行所以利用諸
士誠能羽括鏃礪遠而志巨
而用無論以九見即有二三
于玆亦足爲彥士使攝尺寸
之柄亢聲騰茂允無負
堯舜之世矣不者靜言庸違
帝世將棄之且以不適訛主司亦
punctuated: 外篤懿，文行光融，爲世誦美。信亮方執此以鏡考諸士，而諸士亦曷以成其信乎？夫吞舟之鱗，不游潐；垂天之翼，不控榆枋，其志遠也。辟閭、巨闕，不以割；驊騮、騄駬，不以捕鼠，其用巨也。故尚友匹休，所以明志；植德砥行，所以利用。諸士誠能羽括鏃礪，遠而志、巨而用，無論以九見，即有二三于玆，亦足爲彥士。使攝尺寸之柄，亢聲騰茂，允無負堯舜之世矣。不者，靜言庸違，帝世將棄之，且以不適訛主司，亦
translation_en: … both internally and externally, they were steadfast and admirable; their literary expression and moral conduct shone forth harmoniously and were praised as exemplary by the world. I, Xinliang, am now holding fast to this standard as a mirror by which to examine the scholars—so how then will the scholars fulfill their trustworthiness? Now, a fish large enough to swallow a boat does not swim in shallow puddles, and wings that hang like clouds across the sky do not alight upon elm and sappanwood trees, because their ambitions are far-reaching. The famous swords Pilü and Juque are not used for petty carving, and the fine steeds Hualiu and Lu'er are not used to catch mice, because their utility is vast. Therefore, befriending the ancients and matching their splendor is the means to clarify one's ambition; planting virtue and whetting one's conduct is the means to sharpen one's utility. If the scholars can truly fletch their arrow-nocks and grind their arrowheads, making their ambitions far-reaching and their utility vast, then regardless of whether they manifest all nine virtues, even if they possess only two or three of them here, they will still suffice to be outstanding men of worth. Should they be given even a foot or an inch of authority, their lofty reputation and burgeoning excellence will truly not disappoint an age of Yao and Shun. Otherwise, if they speak smoothly when quiescent but act perversely when employed, the imperial age will cast them aside; moreover, by failing to measure up, they will bring reproach upon the examiners, and how…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
安所傅其谷也昔齊宣好竽
而南郭處士廩食者數百人
迨一一聽之有抱竽而走耳
諸士拔自倫比褒然續食縣
次信亮私幸其無濫吹也繼
自今上春官將有一一而聽
者在焉其尚和其聲以善鳴
===
也哉
浙江紹興府上虞縣儒學教
諭朱信亮謹序
punctuated:
安所傅其谷也？昔齊宣好竽，而南郭處士廩食者數百人；迨一一聽之，有抱竽而走耳。諸士拔自倫比，褒然續食縣次，信亮私幸其無濫吹也。繼自今上春官，將有一一而聽者在焉，其尚和其聲以善鳴也哉！
浙江紹興府上虞縣儒學教諭朱信亮謹序。
translation_en:
…how could one attach any praise to it [?]? In antiquity, King Xuan of Qi loved the yu mouth organ, and Scholar Nanguo was among several hundred men who drew stipends to play it; when the time came to listen to them one by one, he could only clutch his instrument and flee. You gentlemen have been selected from among your peers and will proceed with distinction to be provisioned along the post stages by the counties; I, Xinliang, privately rejoice that there are no impostors playing in the ensemble among you. Hereafter, as you go up to the Ministry of Rites for the Metropolitan Examination, there will be those who listen to you one by one—may you harmonize your voices and sound forth well!
Respectfully prefaced by Zhu Xinliang 朱信亮, Instructor of the Confucian School of Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄序
萬曆丙子秋八月天下復大
比士于鄉惟
今天子稟首出之資接萬年之統
聖學日新
皇猷遐鬯稽古禮文之事靡不脩
飭邇者
===
詔禮官議行釋奠驛召闕里之裔
如
京觀禮乃以是月令日
法駕臨幸太學文武大吏扈
蹕以從儒臣學士執經勸講方領
矩步之徒圜集於橋門皇皇
哉儒林之極觀
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄序
萬曆丙子秋八月，天下復大比士于鄉。惟今天子稟首出之資，接萬年之統，聖學日新，皇猷遐鬯，稽古禮文之事，靡不脩飭。邇者，詔禮官議行釋奠，驛召闕里之裔如京觀禮。乃以是月令日，法駕臨幸太學，文武大吏扈蹕以從，儒臣學士執經勸講，方領矩步之徒，圜集於橋門。皇皇哉！儒林之極觀，
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn of the bingzi year of the Wanli era (1576), the empire once again held the great triennial examination of scholars in the provinces. Now our reigning Son of Heaven, endowed with preeminent natural gifts and succeeding to the line of ten thousand years, renews his sagely learning day by day and extends his imperial plans far and wide; there is no matter of ancient precedent or ritual observance that he has not put in order. Recently, he issued a decree ordering the ritual officials to deliberate on performing the shidian sacrifice to Confucius, and summoned the descendants of Queli by post relay to come to the capital to observe the ceremony. Then, on an auspicious day in this very month, the imperial carriage graced the Directorate of Education (Taixue) in person, with high civil and military officials attending the imperial cortege, Confucian ministers and academicians holding the Classics to expound and lecture, and scholars in square-collared robes and measured gait gathering in a ring around the bridged gates. How magnificent! It is the supreme spectacle of the Confucian world, …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
帝王之盛節也會冇司貢士適當
其期
首善之化自
畿甸曁于海宇秀艾烝烝驩欣
鼓舞咸切利見之思維廣以
西則巡按監察御史陸萬鍾
祗
===
命監臨奉
至尊休德百度益以庀毖總督兩
廣軍務兵部左侍郎兼右僉
都御史凌雲翼節鉞載臨肅
清嶺海巡撫廣西都察院右
副都御史吳文華綏服貞敎
興起譽髦之達等以前巡按
punctuated: 帝王之盛節也！會冇司貢士適當其期，首善之化自畿甸曁于海宇，秀艾烝烝，驩欣鼓舞，咸切利見之思。維廣以西，則巡按監察御史陸萬鍾祗命監臨，奉至尊休德，百度益以庀毖。總督兩廣軍務、兵部左侍郎兼右僉都御史凌雲翼，節鉞載臨，肅清嶺海；巡撫廣西、都察院右副都御史吳文華，綏服貞敎，興起譽髦。之達等以前巡按
translation_en: … and the grand ceremony of Emperors and Kings! It happened that the relevant authorities' presentation of tribute scholars fell precisely at this time. The transforming influence from the place of preeminent goodness extended from the imperial domain to the farthest corners of the empire. Outstanding and mature scholars surged forward in great numbers, rejoicing and inspired, all eagerly harboring thoughts of the advantage of seeing the great man. In the region west of Guangdong, Regional Investigating Censor Lu Wanzhong 陸萬鍾 reverently received the imperial command to serve as Supervising Official. Upholding the Sovereign'ssplendid virtue, he prepared and cautioned all measures with even greater care. Supreme Commander of Military Affairs of Liangguang, Left Vice Minister of War and concurrent Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Ling Yunyi 凌雲翼 arrived once more bearing the tally and battle-axe, bringing order and peace to the mountain ranges and seas. Grand Coordinator of Guangxi and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate Wu Wenhua 吳文華 pacified the region with upright instruction, rousing and encouraging men of renown and talent. I, [Guo] Zhida 之達, and my colleagues, having been invited by the former Regional Investigating…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
御史李采菲聘至則之達及
敎諭朱信亮爲考試敎諭梁
肇脩單文盛許渙王寵麟劉
萃同考試左布政使高察右
叅政朱奎司提調按察使吳
椿副使彭文質司監試諸執
事咸遴選以充旣鎖闈合提
===
學副使高則益所柬士一千
五百有奇三試之遵
制額拔五十五人爲錄以
獻之達謹稽首而序曰之達文
質無所底濫職文學嘗稽載
籍觀成周選士之制考德藝
興賢能賓禮隆重所藉以隸
punctuated: 御史李采菲聘至，則之達及敎諭朱信亮爲考試，敎諭梁肇脩、單文盛、許渙、王寵麟、劉萃同考試，左布政使高察、右叅政朱奎司提調，按察使吳椿、副使彭文質司監試，諸執事咸遴選以充。旣鎖闈，合提學副使高則益所柬士一千五百有奇，三試之，遵制額拔五十五人，爲錄以獻。之達謹稽首而序曰：之達文質無所底，濫職文學，嘗稽載籍，觀成周選士之制，考德藝、興賢能，賓禮隆重，所藉以隸
translation_en:
… Regional Investigating Censor Li Caifei 李采菲, upon arriving, I, Zhida, and Instructor Zhu Xinliang 朱信亮 were made Examiners, and Instructors Liang Zhaoxiu 梁肇脩, Shan Wensheng 單文盛, Xu Huan 許渙, Wang Chonglin 王寵麟, and Liu Cui 劉萃 were made Associate Examiners. Left Administration Commissioner Gao Cha 高察 and Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zhu Kui 朱奎 took charge as Proctors, while Surveillance Commissioner Wu Chun 吳椿 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Peng Wenzhi 彭文質 took charge of monitoring the examination. All the other functionaries were carefully selected to fill their posts. Once the examination compound was locked, we gathered the more than one thousand five hundred scholars selected by Education-intendant Surveillance Vice Commissioner Gao Zeyi 高則益, tested them in three sessions, and, in compliance with the quota set by imperial decree, selected fifty-five men, compiling this record to present to the throne.

I, Zhida, respectfully bow my head to the ground and write in preface: I have achieved nothing of note in either literary refinement or solid substance, yet I unworthily hold a post in education. I have examined the historical records and observed the system of selecting scholars in the flourishing Zhou dynasty, which evaluated moral conduct and the arts, promoted the worthy and the capable, and treated them with grand ceremonial hospitality as guests. What it relied upon to attach…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
社稷庇蒸黎者甚厚
明興紹天闡繹偃武陳常睠隆
周之大寧監賓士之遺意著
之令甲網羅儁髦雖遐荒疏
俗黌塾棊置文治焞然勃興
垂二百餘禩士由此塗著勛
名于春秋者與成周埒顧科
===
目之制取士以文始未嘗不
樸茂後稍浸淫也〔之達〕竊莊
誦
高皇之訓有曰明道理通世物無
事華藻於乎美哉始基之矣其
時士敦本質辭不偭于法度
而致用皆効實故足術也弘
punctuated: 社稷、庇蒸黎者甚厚。明興，紹天闡繹，偃武陳常，睠隆周之大寧，監賓士之遺意，著之令甲，網羅儁髦。雖遐荒疏俗，黌塾棊置，文治焞然勃興，垂二百餘禩，士由此塗著勛名于春秋者，與成周埒。顧科目之制，取士以文，始未嘗不樸茂，後稍浸淫也。〔之達〕竊莊誦高皇之訓，有曰：「明道理，通世物，無事華藻。」於乎美哉！始基之矣。其時士敦本質，辭不偭于法度，而致用皆効實，故足術也。弘
translation_en: …the altars of soil and grain and shelter the multitude of the common people was profound indeed. When the Ming arose, it succeeded to Heaven's mandate and unfolded its grand design, laying down arms and setting forth the constant norms. Looking back fondly upon the great peace of the flourishing Zhou, and taking as a model its enduring intent in treating scholars as honored guests, the dynasty inscribed this into the statutory codes so as to gather in all outstanding talents. Even in distant wilds with rustic customs, schools were arrayed like pieces on a gaming board, and civil governance blazed forth in vigorous rise. For over two hundred years, the scholars who by this path have inscribed their meritorious names in the annals have rivaled those of the flourishing Zhou. Yet under the system of examination categories, in selecting scholars through literary composition, at the outset the writing was never anything less than unadorned and lush, though later it gradually grew extravagant. I, [Zhi Da], have in humble reverence recited the instructions of the Exalted Emperor [Hongwu], which state: "Illuminate moral principles and comprehend worldly affairs, having no use for flowery embellishment." Oh, how admirable! This laid the very foundation. At that time, scholars cultivated fundamental substance, their words did not turn away from proper standards, and in practical application they all yielded genuine results; thus their way is worthy of being followed. Prior to the Hong…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
治而前此道未沫裔玆以降
靡麗之漸人久矣迺今
主上德懋淵懿秉恭儉以先天下
二三碩輔相與矢精白而斡
旋之一時經生學子頓剗華
琱還師古始已駸駸乎
國初之舊焉矧又
===
勸學興禮以風之哉廣右介居
西南垂山川盤鬱毓爲人文
多鴻龐敦固之士其擢制科
登膴仕鏗鉤霳煜爲世所稱
頌者繹繹相望始之達遵岳
麓而西也涉洮湘靈渠陟降
于堯山桂嶺之間而盱衡于
punctuated: 治而前，此道未沫。裔玆以降，靡麗之漸人久矣。迺今主上德懋淵懿，秉恭儉以先天下；二三碩輔，相與矢精白而斡旋之。一時經生學子，頓剗華琱，還師古始，已駸駸乎國初之舊焉，矧又勸學興禮以風之哉！廣右介居西南垂，山川盤鬱，毓爲人文，多鴻龐敦固之士。其擢制科、登膴仕，鏗鉤霳煜，爲世所稱頌者，繹繹相望。始之達遵岳麓而西也，涉洮、湘、靈渠，陟降于堯山、桂嶺之間，而盱衡于
translation_en:
… Prior to the Hongzhi era (1488–1505), this Way had not yet faded. From that time onward, however, florid and ornate styles gradually steeped into people's minds for a long while. Yet now our Sovereign, whose virtue is abundant, profound, and admirable, upholds reverence and frugality to lead the realm; and two or three great chief ministers together pledge pure integrity to redirect the trend. All at once, classical scholars and students have abruptly stripped away flowery carving and returned to emulating the ancient beginnings, already rapidly approaching the old ways of the founding of the dynasty—how much more so when learning is encouraged and rites are promoted to inspire them!

Guangxi lies on the southwestern frontier. Its winding and lush mountains and rivers nurture human talent, producing many scholars of grand, simple, earnest, and steadfast character. Those who have been selected through the civil service examinations and ascended to prominent office, ringing with fame and shining with brilliance as objects of the world's praise, have followed one another in an unbroken succession. When I, Zhi Da 之達, first traveled west along Mount Yuelu, crossing the Tao and Xiang rivers and the Ling Canal, ascending and descending between Mount Yao and the Guiling ranges, and surveying the…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
黨巷則見物力侵而土風儉
寠無芬華綺麗之觀旣入簾
縱閱諸士所爲文類皆含英
茹荄惣微說約不騖精于棘
猴雕龍而闡晰經術敷陳今
古悉中肯綮自非涵泳
主德靡然顧化何能及此以故之
達等于諸士亟收之誠欲得
眞才以裨實用非徒貴其華
也昔孔子侍于魯君君賜之
桃與黍黍以雪桃也乃孔子
則先飯黍而後啗桃蓋黍者
五穀之長祭爲上盛桃雖華
而悅人其實不登于廟先後
punctuated: 黨巷，則見物力侵而土風儉寠，無芬華綺麗之觀。旣入簾，縱閱諸士所爲文，類皆含英茹荄，惣微說約，不騖精于棘猴雕龍，而闡晰經術、敷陳今古，悉中肯綮。自非涵泳主德，靡然顧化，何能及此？以故之達等于諸士亟收之，誠欲得眞才以裨實用，非徒貴其華也。昔孔子侍于魯君，君賜之桃與黍，黍以雪桃也，乃孔子則先飯黍而後啗桃。蓋黍者，五穀之長，祭爲上盛；桃雖華而悅人，其實不登于廟。先後
translation_en: … the neighborhoods and lanes, I saw that material resources were straitened [?] and local customs were frugal and poor, with no sights of luxurious splendor or ornate beauty. Once I entered the examination compound, I read extensively through the essays composed by the various scholars. For the most part, they all held within them the finest blossoms and nourished the deepest roots, synthesizing subtleties and expressing them with concision. They did not expend their energies pursuing the flashy artistry of carving monkeys on thorn-tips or "carving dragons," yet in elucidating classical scholarship and setting forth matters of past and present, they hit the crucial points in every case. Had they not been steeped in the Sovereign's virtue and swept along in willing transformation, how could they have attained this? For this reason, I, Zhida, and my colleagues eagerly selected these scholars, truly wishing to obtain genuine talent to aid in practical use, rather than merely prizing superficial華 (ornamentation). In antiquity, when Confucius was in attendance upon the ruler of Lu, the ruler bestowed upon him a peach and glutinous millet—the millet being intended to wipe clean the fuzz of the peach. Yet Confucius ate the millet first and only afterward ate the peach. This was because millet is the chief of the five grains and serves as the highest vessel-offering in sacrifices; whereas the peach, though showy and pleasing to people, is a fruit that is not presented in the ancestral temple. The sequence of first and last…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
殊用貴賤之義也樹人者毋
抑是類乎故士之工言而不
中于仁不如訥之愿也縟儀
而不協于禮不如野之朴也
勇往而不準于經不如退之
讓也炫明而不適于用不如
晦之藏也今諸士惇本實遘
===
昌明應
右文之盛際袪骯髒之陋習第
藉令奉其所有一比之于道
出而副有司之求猶之嘉穀
秀實升豆籩而薦清廟行必
資之矣是在諸士知所自樹
而主司者不藉有樹人之慶
punctuated: 殊用，貴賤之義也。樹人者毋抑是類乎？故士之工言而不中于仁，不如訥之愿也；縟儀而不協于禮，不如野之朴也；勇往而不準于經，不如退之讓也；炫明而不適于用，不如晦之藏也。今諸士惇本實，遘昌明，應右文之盛際，袪骯髒之陋習。第藉令奉其所有，一比之于道，出而副有司之求，猶之嘉穀秀實，升豆籩而薦清廟，行必資之矣。是在諸士知所自樹，而主司者不藉有樹人之慶…
translation_en: …differ in their uses, reflecting the principle of what is noble and what is base. Is not the cultivation of talent also like this? Therefore, a scholar who is skillful in speech yet does not accord with benevolence is not as good as one who is slow of speech yet sincere; one who has elaborate manners yet does not conform to ritual propriety is not as good as one who is rustic yet simple; one who advances boldly yet does not measure up to the constant norms is not as good as one who retreats and yields; one who flaunts his brilliance yet is unsuited for practical use is not as good as one who conceals his light in obscurity. Now the gentlemen hold fast to fundamental substance and have encountered an era of flourishing enlightenment; responding to this splendid age that esteems civil culture, they cast off coarse and unrefined habits. If only they take what they possess and align it wholly with the Way, going forth to fulfill the expectations of the authorities, they will be like fine grain that has flowered and ripened: raised up in sacrificial vessels and offered in the pure ancestral temple, it will certainly be relied upon in practice. This rests upon the gentlemen knowing how to establish themselves—and will the chief examiners not thereby share in the joy of having cultivated men of talent…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
哉是舉也清戎監察御史李
頤肅憲維風總兵官征蠻將
軍署都督同知李錫詰戎鎮
遠右布政使李鳳右叅政管
副使事沈子木副使吳善徐
作左叅議秦舜翰右叅議陳
應春僉事李一迪王一卿皆
脩秩于外叅將王瑞倪中化
亦孔昭王德懋署都指揮僉
事夏尚忠黃允中皆防範于
外按察使仍管叅政事吳一
介副使顧章志以入
賀行左叅議劉應峯以遷秩行
皆與襄始事刑部署員外郎
punctuated: 哉！是舉也，清戎監察御史李頤肅憲維風；總兵官、征蠻將軍、署都督同知李錫詰戎鎮遠；右布政使李鳳，右叅政管副使事沈子木，副使吳善、徐作，左叅議秦舜翰，右叅議陳應春，僉事李一迪、王一卿皆脩秩于外；叅將王瑞、倪中化、亦孔昭、王德懋，署都指揮僉事夏尚忠、黃允中皆防範于外；按察使仍管叅政事吳一介，副使顧章志以入賀行，左叅議劉應峯以遷秩行，皆與襄始事；刑部署員外郎
translation_en:
… [would those presiding not thereby share in the joy of cultivating men]?!

In this undertaking, Military-Purification Investigating Censor Li Yi 李頤 enforced discipline and upheld moral customs; Regional Commander, General for Subjugating the Southern Barbarians, and Acting Vice Commissioner-in-Chief Li Xi 李錫 kept the military in order and pacified distant regions; Right Administration Commissioner Li Feng 李鳳, Right Administration Vice Commissioner managing the affairs of a Surveillance Vice Commissioner Shen Zimu 沈子木, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Wu Shan 吳善 and Xu Zuo 徐作, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Qin Shunhan 秦舜翰, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Chen Yingchun 陳應春, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Li Yidi 李一迪 and Wang Yiqing 王一卿 all attended to their official duties on the outside; Assistant Regional Commanders Wang Rui 王瑞, Ni Zhonghua 倪中化, Yi Kongzhao 亦孔昭, and Wang Demao 王德懋, along with Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Xia Shangzhong 夏尚忠 and Huang Yunzhong 黃允中, all maintained security on the outside. Surveillance Commissioner still managing the affairs of an Administration Vice Commissioner Wu Yijie 吳一介 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Gu Zhangzhi 顧章志, who departed to present congratulations at Court, and Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Liu Yingfeng 劉應峯, who departed upon promotion to another post, all helped assist in the initial arrangements; and Acting Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
朱湘以讞獄至則遹觀厥成
者也法得竝書
福建興化府儒學教授李之
達謹序
punctuated:
朱湘以讞獄至，則遹觀厥成者也，法得竝書。
福建興化府儒學教授李之達謹序。
translation_en:
…Zhu Xiang 朱湘, who arrived to adjudicate legal cases, was on hand to witness its completion. By custom, all of their names are duly recorded together.
Respectfully prefaced by Li Zhida 李之達, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian.
