title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
夫子聖者與何其多能也子貢曰固天縱
之將聖又多能也子聞之曰大宰知我
乎吾少也賤故多能鄙事君子多乎哉
不多也
郊社之禮所以事上帝也
聖人人倫之至也欲爲君盡君道欲爲臣
盡臣道二者皆法堯舜而已矣
===
易
大有柔得尊位大中而上下應之曰大有
其德剛健而文明應乎天而時行是以
元亨
九二貞吉象曰九二貞吉以中也
夫乾其靜也專其動也直是以大生焉夫
坤其靜也翕其動也闢是以廣生焉廣
大配天地
臨觀之義或與或求
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「夫子聖者與？何其多能也！」子貢曰：「固天縱之將聖，又多能也。」子聞之，曰：「大宰知我乎！吾少也賤，故多能鄙事。君子多乎哉？不多也。」
郊社之禮，所以事上帝也。
聖人，人倫之至也。欲爲君，盡君道；欲爲臣，盡臣道。二者皆法堯、舜而已矣。

易
《大有》，柔得尊位大中，而上下應之，曰《大有》。其德剛健而文明，應乎天而時行，是以元亨。
九二，貞吉。《象》曰：「九二貞吉」，以中也。
夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉。夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉。廣大配天地。
《臨》、《觀》之義，或與或求。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

"Is the Master a sage? How is it that he has so many abilities?" Zigong 子貢 said, "Indeed, Heaven has endowed him so that he is a great sage, and moreover he has many abilities." The Master heard of it and said, "Does the Grand Minister (Taizai 大宰) know me? When I was young, I was of humble station, and therefore I acquired many abilities in menial matters. Does the gentleman have many such abilities? No, he does not." (Analects 9.6)

The ceremonies of the suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth are those by which one serves the Lord on High (Shangdi 上帝). (Doctrine of the Mean 19)

The sage is the culmination of human relationships. Wishing to be a ruler, one fulfills the Way of a ruler; wishing to be a minister, one fulfills the Way of a minister. In both cases, one simply models oneself on Yao 堯 and Shun 舜, and nothing more. (Mencius 4A.2)

Book of Changes (Yi 易)

"Possession in Great Measure (Dayou 大有): the yielding obtains the honored position in the great center, and those above and below respond to it; hence it is called Possession in Great Measure. Its virtue is firm and vigorous, yet civilized and bright; it responds to Heaven and acts in accordance with the time, and therefore there is supreme success." (Hexagram 14, Dayou, Commentary on the Decision)

"Nine in the second place: perseverance brings good fortune. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang 象) says: 'Nine in the second place: perseverance brings good fortune'—because it is in the central position." (Hexagram 19, Lin, or Hexagram 33, Dun, or Hexagram 58, Dui, second line)

"As for the Creative (Qian 乾), in its stillness it is concentrated, and in its movement it is straight; therefore it generates on a great scale. As for the Receptive (Kun 坤), in its stillness it is closed, and in its movement it opens; therefore it generates on a broad scale. In breadth and greatness, they match Heaven and Earth." (Great Commentary, Part I, Chapter 6)

"In the meaning of Approach (Lin 臨) and Contemplation (Guan 觀), some give and some seek." (Commentary on the Mixed Hexagrams, Zagua 雜卦)

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
書
文命敷于四海祗承于帝曰后克艱厥后
臣克艱厥臣政乃乂黎民敏德
終始愼厥與惟明明后
其爾典常作之師
一人有慶兆民賴之其寧惟永
詩
羔羊之皮素絲五紽退食自公委蛇委蛇
禾易長畝終善且有曾孫不怒農夫克敏
===
曾孫之稼如茨如梁曾孫之庾如坻如
京乃求千斯倉乃求萬斯箱黍稷稻粱
農夫之慶
之綱之紀燕及朋友百辟卿士媚于天子
不解于位民之攸墍
紹庭上下陟降厥家
春秋
晉人敗狄于箕僖公三十有三年十有二
月乙丑季孫行父及晉郤犨盟于扈成
punctuated:

「終始愼厥與，惟明明后。」
「其爾典常作之師。」
「一人有慶，兆民賴之，其寧惟永。」
《詩》
「羔羊之皮，素絲五紽。退食自公，委蛇委蛇。」
「禾易長畝，終善且有。曾孫不怒，農夫克敏。曾孫之稼，如茨如梁；曾孫之庾，如坻如京。乃求千斯倉，乃求萬斯箱。黍稷稻粱，農夫之慶。」
「之綱之紀，燕及朋友。百辟卿士，媚于天子。不解于位，民之攸墍。」
「紹庭上下，陟降厥家。」

translation_en:
Book of Documents (Shu):
"His civilizing mandates were spread throughout the Four Seas, and he reverently responded to the Sovereign. He said: 'If the sovereign can appreciate the difficulty of being a sovereign, and the minister can appreciate the difficulty of being a minister, government will be well ordered, and the black-haired people will be quick to cultivate virtue.'"
"From beginning to end carefully choose those with whom you associate—this marks the truly illustrious sovereign."
"Take your constant statutes as your standard and teacher."
"When the One Man has goodness, the millions of people rely on him, and the peace they enjoy will be everlasting."

Book of Odes (Shi):
"Lambskins and sheep's pelts, with five braidings of white silk. Retiring from court to take their meal, how self-possessed and composed they are!"
"The grain is well-cultivated all along the acres, and in the end will be good and abundant. The descendant does not show anger; the husbandmen are diligent. The descendant's standing grain is thick as thatch and high as a bridge; the descendant's unroofed stacks are like islands and like mounds. He shall seek a thousand granaries; he shall seek ten thousand carts. Broomcorn and panicled millet, rice and spiked millet, are the blessing of the husbandmen."
"Giving law and order to all, he brings peace and joy to his friends. The hundred lords and ministers show their devotion to the Son of Heaven; never remiss in their positions, in them the people find rest."
"Continuing to walk in the court above and below, ascending and descending in his house."

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
〔公十有六年〕
宋人齊人楚人盟于鹿上〔僖公二十有一年〕
三月公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男
曹伯盟于牡丘 遂次于匡 公孫敖
帥師及諸侯之大夫救徐〔僖公十有五年〕
六月公會單子晉侯宋公衛侯鄭伯
莒子邾子齊世子光已未同盟于雞澤
陳侯使袁僑如會 戊寅叔孫豹及
===
諸侯之大夫及陳袁僑盟〔襄公三年〕
八月晉荀吳帥師滅陸渾之戎〔昭公十有七年〕
禮記
天子乃命將帥選士厲兵簡練桀俊專任
有功以征不義詰誅暴慢以明好惡順
彼遠方
故自郊社祖廟山川五祀義之脩而禮之
藏也
punctuated:
〔公十有六年〕
宋人、齊人、楚人盟于鹿上。〔僖公二十有一年〕
三月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯盟于牡丘，遂次于匡。公孫敖帥師及諸侯之大夫救徐。〔僖公十有五年〕
六月，公會單子、晉侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光，已未，同盟于雞澤。陳侯使袁僑如會。戊寅，叔孫豹及諸侯之大夫及陳袁僑盟。〔襄公三年〕
八月，晉荀吳帥師滅陸渾之戎。〔昭公十有七年〕

《禮記》
天子乃命將帥，選士厲兵，簡練桀俊，專任有功，以征不義，詰誅暴慢，以明好惡，順彼遠方。
故自郊社、祖廟、山川、五祀，義之脩而禮之藏也。
translation_en:
… [Sixteenth year of Duke Cheng].

Men of Song, men of Qi, and men of Chu made a covenant at Lushang [Twenty-first year of Duke Xi].

In the third month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao, and made a covenant at Muqiu; thereupon they halted at Kuang. Gongsun Ao led a force to join the great officers of the feudal lords in relieving Xu [Fifteenth year of Duke Xi].

In the sixth month, the Duke met with the Viscount of Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and Guang, Heir Apparent of Qi; on the yiwei [jiwei] day, they made a joint covenant at Jize. The Marquis of Chen sent Yuan Qiao to attend the meeting. On the wuyin day, Shusun Bao, together with the great officers of the feudal lords, made a covenant with Yuan Qiao of Chen [Third year of Duke Xiang].

In the eighth month, Xun Wu of Jin led a force and extinguished the Rong of Luhun [Seventeenth year of Duke Zhao].

Record of Rites (Liji)

"The Son of Heaven then commands the generals and commanders to select warriors and sharpen weapons, to choose and drill heroes and men of outstanding talent, and to give exclusive responsibility to those of proven merit, in order to punish the unrighteous, to interrogate and execute the violent and insolent, thereby making clear what is favored and what is hated, and bringing obedience from those in distant quarters."

"Therefore, from the suburban sacrifices and the altar of the soil, the ancestral temples, the mountains and rivers, to the five household sacrifices, these are the cultivation of righteousness and the repository of ritual."

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
樂者敦和率神而從天禮者別宜居鬼而
從地故聖人作樂以應天制禮以配地
禮樂明備天地官矣
臣下竭力盡能以立功於國君必報之以
爵祿故臣下皆務竭力盡能以立功是
以國安而君寧
第貳場
論
正心爲天下萬事之本
===
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢賜天下今年田租之半詔文帝二年
擬唐以李靖等爲黜陟大使分行天下誥
貞觀八年
擬輔臣疏內外文武臣工職名於屏風恭
進
御覽表萬曆二年
判語五條
官員赴任過限
punctuated:
樂者，敦和，率神而從天；禮者，別宜，居鬼而從地。故聖人作樂以應天，制禮以配地，禮樂明備，天地官矣。
臣下竭力盡能以立功於國，君必報之以爵祿；故臣下皆務竭力盡能以立功，是以國安而君寧。

第貳場
論
正心爲天下萬事之本。

詔、誥、表內科一道
擬漢賜天下今年田租之半詔（文帝二年）
擬唐以李靖等爲黜陟大使分行天下誥（貞觀八年）
擬輔臣疏內外文武臣工職名於屏風恭進御覽表（萬曆二年）

判語五條
官員赴任過限
translation_en:
"Music deepens harmony, leads the spirits, and follows Heaven; ritual distinguishes what is appropriate, settles the ghosts, and follows Earth. Therefore, the sages created music to respond to Heaven and instituted ritual to match Earth. When ritual and music are clear and complete, Heaven and Earth fulfill their proper functions."

"When ministers and subordinates exhaust their strength and abilities to establish merit for the state, the ruler must reward them with noble ranks and emoluments; therefore, ministers and subordinates all strive to exhaust their strength and abilities to establish merit, and thus the state is secure and the ruler is at peace."

Second Session

Discourse:
"Rectifying the mind is the foundation of the ten thousand affairs under Heaven."

Imperial Edict (zhao), Mandate (gao), or Memorial (biao) (examinees choose one):
Imitation of the Han Dynasty imperial edict granting the empire a reduction of half of this year's land tax (2nd year of Emperor Wen, 178 BCE).
Imitation of the Tang Dynasty mandate appointing Li Jing 李靖 and others as Grand Commissioners for Evaluating Merits (chuzhi dashi) to tour the empire in circuits (8th year of the Zhenguan era, 634 CE).
Imitation of a memorial by the Grand Secretaries inscribing the official titles and names of civil and military officials inside and outside the capital upon a folding screen and reverently presenting it for Imperial inspection (2nd year of the Wanli era, 1574).

Five Legal Judgments:
Officials exceeding the time limit in proceeding to their posts…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
丁夫差遣不平
禁止師巫邪術
邊境申索軍需
失時不脩隄防
第叄塲
策五道
問帝王之興中天地為綱常主繫於民彝
世教至重也是故治莫先於明倫倫莫
大於君親古今言忠孝者至虞舜周公
===
極矣載在傳記鑿鑿可攷孝經一書說
者以為成於曽子門人之手明順教孝
為世所宗迨漢有擬作忠經十八篇者
篇中意旨又若不專為人臣訓不知與
孝經可相表裏否洪惟
太祖高皇帝開天立極人紀肇脩貽謨垂範至
宏且遠
成祖文皇帝闡烈綏猷製為
聖學心法一書其於臣道子道蓋縷縷言之
punctuated:
丁夫差遣不平
禁止師巫邪術
邊境申索軍需
失時不脩隄防

第叄塲
策五道

問：帝王之興，中天地為綱常主，繫於民彝世教至重也。是故治莫先於明倫，倫莫大於君親。古今言忠孝者，至虞舜、周公極矣，載在傳記，鑿鑿可攷。《孝經》一書，說者以為成於曽子門人之手，明順教孝，為世所宗。迨漢有擬作《忠經》十八篇者，篇中意旨又若不專為人臣訓，不知與《孝經》可相表裏否？洪惟太祖高皇帝開天立極，人紀肇脩，貽謨垂範，至宏且遠。成祖文皇帝闡烈綏猷，製為《聖學心法》一書，其於臣道、子道，蓋縷縷言之，
translation_en:
Unfair assignment of adult male corvée laborers
Prohibiting shamans and heterodox arts
Frontier requisitions for military supplies
Failing to repair dikes at the proper season

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: When emperors and kings arise, they stand between Heaven and Earth as the masters of the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues; their bearing upon the moral norms of the people and the teachings of the age is of the utmost weight. Therefore, in governance nothing takes precedence over clarifying human relationships, and among human relationships none is greater than those toward ruler and parent. From antiquity to the present, discussions of loyalty and filial piety reached their ultimate expression in Yu Shun and the Duke of Zhou; recorded in traditions and histories, these are supported by clear and verifiable evidence. As for the Book of Filial Piety (Xiaojing), commentators hold that it was completed by the hands of Zengzi's disciples; in elucidating compliance and teaching filial piety, it has been revered as a standard by the world. By the Han dynasty, someone composed in imitation the Classic of Loyalty (Zhongjing) in eighteen chapters, yet the purport within its chapters seems not to serve exclusively as instruction for ministers and subjects; one wonders whether it can stand as the counterpart and complement to the Book of Filial Piety? We reflect with awe upon how Grand Progenitor Emperor Gao (Taizu Gaohuangdi) opened up Heaven and established the supreme standard, initiating the rectification of human moral order and handing down counsels and setting forth models that were supremely vast and far-reaching. Accomplished Ancestor Emperor Wen (Chengzu Wenhuangdi) illuminated these meritorious achievements and gave tranquility to the dynastic plan; he composed the book Methods of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa), in which he spoke in great detail of the way of the minister and the way of the son, …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
孝順事實紀孝行甚具
宣宗章皇帝思古明良之盛
製歷代臣鑑其叙臣事甚詳又
命儒臣編輯
五倫書頒布中外即古之誕告多方訓迪百
官何以加焉二百餘年敦叙興行百司
憲度庶民歸極有繇然也
皇上稟睿纂曆諸所陳之象魏宣之渙汗者無
不討
===
累朝故實而脩明之祗若
列祖敬事
兩宮以孝治先天下二三喆輔精白承休庶幾
與重華元聖比隆矣
上益銳於理
宸翰飛灑頒賜臣工直以古良弼望諸輔佐至
部臺講讀之臣並加
寵勸所以作忠者又何惓也
明良相遇千載一時薄海內外有不躍然思奮
punctuated: 《孝順事實》紀孝行甚具。宣宗章皇帝思古明良之盛，製《歷代臣鑑》，其叙臣事甚詳；又命儒臣編輯《五倫書》，頒布中外，即古之誕告多方、訓迪百官，何以加焉！二百餘年敦叙興行，百司憲度，庶民歸極，有繇然也。皇上稟睿纂曆，諸所陳之象魏、宣之渙汗者，無不討累朝故實而脩明之；祗若列祖，敬事兩宮，以孝治先天下，二三喆輔精白承休，庶幾與重華、元聖比隆矣。上益銳於理，宸翰飛灑，頒賜臣工，直以古良弼望諸輔佐；至部臺、講讀之臣，並加寵勸，所以作忠者又何惓也！明良相遇，千載一時，薄海內外，有不躍然思奮
translation_en:
…and the Factual Accounts of Filial Piety and Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi), which records filial deeds in great detail. Emperor Xuanzong Zhang, reflecting on the flourishing of enlightened rulers and worthy ministers in antiquity, composed the Mirror of Ministers Through the Ages (Lidai chenjian), which recounts the deeds of ministers most thoroughly; he also commanded Confucian officials to compile the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) and promulgate it within the court and throughout the realm. Even the grand proclamations to the myriad regions and the instruction and guidance of the hundred officials in antiquity—how could they surpass this! That for over two hundred years the social order has been fostered and virtuous conduct promoted, the hundred offices have taken the laws as their model, and the common people have returned to the standard of perfection, truly has its cause in this.

His Majesty, endowed with sagely wisdom, has succeeded to the throne. In all that is posted at the palace gates and proclaimed in his imperial edicts, there is nothing in which he does not examine the precedents of successive reigns to cultivate and clarify them. Reverently following the imperial ancestors and respectfully serving the Two Palaces [the Empresses Dowager], he leads the world through governance by filial piety, while two or three wise Grand Secretaries uphold his grace with pure devotion, nearly rivaling the splendor of Chonghua [Emperor Shun] and the Great Sage [Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou]. His Majesty grows ever more ardent in governance: his imperial calligraphy flows forth and is bestowed upon his officials, directly expecting of his chief ministers the stature of the good coadjutors of antiquity; even down to the officials of the Ministries and the Censorate, and the Lecturers and Readers-in-waiting, all alike receive his favored encouragement. How earnest indeed is that whereby he inspires loyalty! This meeting of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers is a moment that comes once in a thousand years; within and beyond the four seas, is there anyone who does not leap with eagerness to exert…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者乎諸生抱經待問茲移孝為忠之日
也將安所報稱哉其悉陳所蘊
問記有之帝入太學承師而問道則視學
之典所從來久矣然天子曰辟雝而又
曰成均于義何居釋奠禮也而又曰釋
菜于制何別抑可言其大較否鎬京辟
雝四方咸服炳乎莫可尚已漢而後有
詔諸生雅吹擊磬盡日乃罷者有會諸
儒執經問難正坐自講者有召博士發
===
春秋題者有詔祭酒講孝經者有命講
周易泰卦與說命三篇者有令說論語
因閱東序三禮圖者豈皆有得于承師
問道之意否歟洪惟我
皇上梃明悊之資執粹清之道
踐阼以來
儲思聽納
典學緝熈
篤禮儒賢頻開
punctuated:
者乎？諸生抱經待問，茲移孝為忠之日也，將安所報稱哉？其悉陳所蘊。

問：《記》有之，帝入太學，承師而問道。則視學之典，所從來久矣。然天子曰辟雝，而又曰成均，于義何居？釋奠，禮也，而又曰釋菜，于制何別？抑可言其大較否？鎬京辟雝，四方咸服，炳乎莫可尚已。漢而後，有詔諸生雅吹擊磬、盡日乃罷者；有會諸儒執經問難、正坐自講者；有召博士發《春秋》題者；有詔祭酒講《孝經》者；有命講《周易》〈泰〉卦與〈說命〉三篇者；有令說《論語》，因閱東序《三禮圖》者。豈皆有得于承師問道之意否歟？洪惟我皇上梃明悊之資，執粹清之道，踐阼以來，儲思聽納，典學緝熈，篤禮儒賢，頻開
translation_en:
… [Is there anyone within and beyond the four seas who would not eagerly aspire to rouse themselves] to action? You students have embraced the Classics while awaiting examination; today is the day to transform filial piety into loyalty. How, then, will you reciprocate and prove worthy of your charge? Set forth in full what you have stored in your minds.

Question: It is recorded in the Record of Rites (Liji) that when the Sovereign enters the Imperial Academy, he honors his teachers and inquires into the Way. Thus, the ceremony of inspecting the Academy is of long standing. Yet for the Son of Heaven it is called Biyong (Jade-Ring Moat), and it is also called Chengjun (Perfect Harmony)—what is the meaning behind these names? The Shidian (Sacrificial Offering of Libations and Food) is a ritual, yet there is also the Shicai (Offering of Vegetables)—how do they differ in institutional regulation? Can you state their general outlines? At the Biyong in the capital of Hao, the four quarters all submitted in allegiance; how resplendent it was, unsurpassable indeed! From the Han dynasty onward, there was one [ruler] who decreed that the students play elegant wind instruments and strike the musical stones, concluding only at the end of the day; there was one who assembled the Confucian scholars to hold the Classics and pose difficult questions while he sat upright and lectured in person; there was one who summoned the Erudites to propound themes from the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); there was one who decreed that the Libationer lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety (Xiaojing); there was one who commanded lectures on the Tai hexagram of the Book of Changes (Zhouyi) and the three chapters of the "Charge to Yue" ("Yueming") [in the Book of Documents]; and there was one who ordered an exposition of the Analects (Lunyu) and thereupon inspected the Illustrated Three Rituals (Sanli tu) in the Eastern Wing. Did all of these indeed grasp the true meaning of honoring teachers and inquiring into the Way, or not?

We humbly reflect that Our Emperor is endowed with brilliant and wise qualities and holds fast to the pure and unsullied Way. Since ascending the throne, He has focused His thoughts on heeding and accepting counsel, applied Himself to continuous and luminous study, earnestly treated Confucian worthies with ritual courtesy, and frequently opened…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
講幄爍哉
聖德侔往初矣乃者
車駕幸太學釋奠
先師因
御彝倫堂
命儒臣進講
盛節駿聲渙揚寓內學士大夫交口而姼頌
之諸生身遊膠庠雖在萬里外亦靡不
借爲色澤然
===
皇上脩問道閎摹而爲臣子者不能將盛美以
効靖獻謂
今日何倘欲闡道術要眇仰裨
聖學宥密其說何繇執事者願有聞也
問王政莫大于明時授時莫先于治曆羲
氏和氏之法載在堯典其詳不得盡聞
然以閏月定四時所以成歲功也後世
增入歲差之說不知昉之者誰歟豈置
閏之外復有所謂差歟古今改曆者無
punctuated:
講幄，爍哉！聖德侔往初矣。乃者車駕幸太學，釋奠先師，因御彝倫堂，命儒臣進講。盛節駿聲，渙揚寓內，學士大夫交口而姼頌之。諸生身遊膠庠，雖在萬里外，亦靡不借爲色澤。然皇上脩問道閎摹，而爲臣子者不能將盛美以効靖獻，謂今日何？倘欲闡道術要眇，仰裨聖學宥密，其說何繇？執事者願有聞也。
問：王政莫大于明時，授時莫先于治曆。羲氏、和氏之法載在《堯典》，其詳不得盡聞，然以閏月定四時，所以成歲功也。後世增入歲差之說，不知昉之者誰歟？豈置閏之外，復有所謂差歟？古今改曆者無
translation_en:
… the lecture tent. How resplendent! His sage virtue matches that of early antiquity. Recently, the Imperial Carriage visited the Directorate of Education to offer a sacrifice of libation and food to the Former Teacher, and thereupon His Majesty took His seat in the Hall of Moral Principles (Yiluntang) and commanded the Confucian officials to advance and lecture. This grand ceremony and exalted renown have spread throughout the realm, and scholars and officials vie with one another in praising its beauty [?]. As government students studying in the state schools, even though you are ten thousand li away, there is none among you who does not share in the luster of this occasion. Yet when His Majesty cultivates the grand plan of inquiring into the Way, if those who are His subjects and sons cannot advance His splendid virtue and offer their loyal devotion, what would that say of today? Should you wish to expound the profound subtleties of the Way and its arts so as to reverently assist the tranquil depth of His sage learning, from what basis would your explanations proceed? This presiding official wishes to hear what you have to say.

Question: In kingly governance, nothing is greater than clarifying the seasons, and in granting the seasons, nothing takes precedence over regulating the calendar. The methods of the Xi and He clans are recorded in the Canon of Yao (Yaodian); although their details cannot be heard in full, determining the four seasons by means of an intercalary month was how they brought the work of the year to completion. Later generations added the theory of the precession of the equinoxes (suicha); it is unclear who first initiated this. Could it be that beyond the insertion of intercalary months, there is also this so-called discrepancy? From antiquity to the present, those who have reformed the calendar number no …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
慮數十家自黃帝訖秦末改者凡六由
西漢訖東漢改者凡五由魏訖隋末改
者凡十三由唐訖周末改者凡十六由
宋太祖訖宋末改者凡十八由金訖元
改者凡三其詳可得陳歟就中推驗之
精後代莫能外者有三家今尚有可尋
歟夫一曆之改非偶合億中也兼綜羣
議考測圖影思無遺智法無遺術宜其
永久不變也即歷代長于曆者不數歲
===
而輒差其故何歟我
朝承運以來三曆協于五紀二統徵諸七政
堯欽舜敕不是過矣然曆雖以大統為
名而積分猶授時之數年遠數盈漸差
天度臺官建議欲隨時脩改者屢矣不
知果有定見歟占天象者不過擬諸日
月之交食耳漢魏以前日食俱在朔以
後或在晦又何歟班固作漢志明治曆
不可不擇者有三今求而應者有若人
punctuated: 慮數十家：自黃帝訖秦末，改者凡六；由西漢訖東漢，改者凡五；由魏訖隋末，改者凡十三；由唐訖周末，改者凡十六；由宋太祖訖宋末，改者凡十八；由金訖元，改者凡三。其詳可得陳歟？就中推驗之精，後代莫能外者有三家，今尚有可尋歟？夫一曆之改，非偶合億中也。兼綜羣議，考測圖影，思無遺智，法無遺術，宜其永久不變也。即歷代長于曆者，不數歲而輒差，其故何歟？我朝承運以來，三曆協于五紀，二統徵諸七政，堯欽舜敕不是過矣。然曆雖以《大統》為名，而積分猶《授時》之數，年遠數盈，漸差天度，臺官建議欲隨時脩改者屢矣，不知果有定見歟？占天象者，不過擬諸日月之交食耳。漢、魏以前，日食俱在朔，以後或在晦，又何歟？班固作《漢志》，明治曆不可不擇者有三，今求而應者有若人
translation_en: …no fewer than several dozen schools: from the Yellow Emperor down to the end of the Qin, it was revised six times in all; from the Western Han down to the Eastern Han, it was revised five times in all; from the Wei down to the end of the Sui, it was revised thirteen times in all; from the Tang down to the end of the Later Zhou, it was revised sixteen times in all; from Emperor Taizu of the Song down to the end of the Song, it was revised eighteen times in all; and from the Jin down to the Yuan, it was revised three times in all. Can the details of these be set forth? Among them, for precision in calculation and verification, there are three schools beyond which later generations could not go—can they still be traced today? Now, the revision of a calendar is not a matter of chance coincidence or guesswork. It brings together the discussions of all, examines and measures diagrams and gnomon shadows, leaves no wisdom unexhausted in thought and no technique unexhausted in method, so it ought to remain permanently unchanged. Yet even with those in successive dynasties who excelled in calendrical science, before many years had passed discrepancies would promptly arise—what is the reason for this? Since Our Dynasty received the Mandate, the three calendars have harmonized with the Five Regulators, and the two systems have been verified by the Seven Governors; the reverent respect of Yao and the ordenariness of Shun did not surpass this. Yet although the calendar bears the name Great Concordance (Datong), its accumulated fractions still follow the figures of the Season-Granting (Shoushi) calendar. As the years grow distant and the numbers fill out, it gradually diverges from the celestial degrees. Officials of the Directorate of Astronomy have repeatedly submitted proposals wishing to revise and correct it in accordance with the times, yet we do not know whether they truly possess a settled view? Those who observe celestial phenomena do no more than gauge them by the eclipses at the conjunctions of the sun and moon. Why is it, moreover, that prior to the Han and Wei, solar eclipses all occurred on the first day of the month (shuo), whereas afterward they sometimes occurred on the last day of the month (hui)? When Ban Gu 班固 composed the Treatise in the History of the Han (Hanzhi), he made clear that in regulating the calendar there are three types of men who must be selected; if we seek them today, are there such men who would respond…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
歅諸士冥搜博考必有達天人之際者
願究言之將以轉告于太史
問自古論治者貴識體識其大也甞稽載
籍因時立政代有損益大都不越質文
遲速寛猛動靜之變耳昔周監二代孔
子致美於郁郁之文矣他日乃曰虞夏
之道寡怨於民商周之道不勝其弊胡
軒輕不同若此也伯禽治魯三年而報
政周公曰何遲也魯後世其北面事齊
===
矣太公治齊五月而報政周公曰何疾
也孔子顧不與之以為必一變而後至
魯夫速者可與圖功而其俗乃不魯若
遲者可以近古而策其受命於霸將何
適而可歟寛一也黃霸用之潁川而大
治子太叔用之鄭國而多盜嚴一也孔
明用之治蜀而興嚴延年用之東海而
敗何趣舍同類而收效殊科也宓子賤
身不下堂彈琴而理單父巫馬期以星
punctuated:
歅？諸士冥搜博考，必有達天人之際者，願究言之，將以轉告于太史。

問：自古論治者貴識體，識其大也。甞稽載籍，因時立政，代有損益，大都不越質文、遲速、寛猛、動靜之變耳。昔周監二代，孔子致美於「郁郁之文」矣；他日乃曰：「虞、夏之道，寡怨於民；商、周之道，不勝其弊。」胡軒輕不同若此也？伯禽治魯，三年而報政，周公曰：「何遲也？魯後世其北面事齊矣！」太公治齊，五月而報政，周公曰：「何疾也？」孔子顧不與之，以為必一變而後至魯。夫速者可與圖功，而其俗乃不魯若；遲者可以近古，而策其受命於霸。將何適而可歟？寛一也，黃霸用之潁川而大治，子太叔用之鄭國而多盜；嚴一也，孔明用之治蜀而興，嚴延年用之東海而敗。何趣舍同類而收效殊科也？宓子賤身不下堂，彈琴而理單父；巫馬期以星
translation_en:
… [Note: 歅 here is a graphic variant of 歟, completing the sentence from the previous page: "…are there such men today who can respond when sought?"] You scholars have searched deeply and examined broadly; among you there must be those who understand the correlation between Heaven and man. I wish you to speak of this exhaustively, so that it may be reported to the Grand Scribe (Taishi 太史).

Question: Since antiquity, those who discuss governance have valued understanding the essential body of rule—that is, understanding what is great. When we examine the historical records, in establishing governance according to the times, each era had its additions and subtractions, yet generally they did not go beyond the alternations of substance and refinement, slowness and swiftness, leniency and severity, action and quiescence. In the past, the Zhou looked back upon the two preceding dynasties, and Confucius praised its "resplendent refinement" (yuyu zhi wen 郁郁之文). Yet on another day he said: "The Way of Yu and Xia aroused little resentment among the people; the Way of Shang and Zhou could not overcome its own defects." Why did his relative valuation differ like this? When Boqin 伯禽 governed Lu 魯, he reported on his administration after three years. The Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公) said: "Why so slow? In future generations Lu will surely face north to serve Qi 齊!" When Taigong 太公 governed Qi, he reported on his administration after five months, and the Duke of Zhou said: "Why so swift?" Yet Confucius did not favor Qi, holding that Qi would have to undergo one transformation before it could reach the level of Lu. Now, the swift approach allows one to plan for achievements, yet its customs did not match those of Lu; the slow approach allows one to be close to antiquity, yet it was foretold that it would take orders from a hegemon. Which course should one follow for it to be right? Leniency is one and the same: Huang Ba 黃霸 used it in Yingchuan 潁川 and achieved great order, whereas Zi Taishu 子太叔 used it in the state of Zheng 鄭 and brigands proliferated. Severity is one and the same: Kongming 孔明 (Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮) used it to govern Shu 蜀 and flourished, whereas Yan Yannian 嚴延年 used it in Donghai 東海 and met with ruin. Why is it that their choices of approach were of the same kind, yet the results they reaped were so different in category? Fu Zijian 宓子賤 did not descend from the hall, playing his zither while putting Shanfu 單父 in order; Wuma Qi 巫馬期 went out by the stars…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
出以星入單父亦理將服勤之績顧不
若優游之驗與易言聖人通其變使民
不倦意其所用𠯁綱紀振作者固自有
道歟二三子學古入官講於當世之務
熟矣其悉心折衷以對
問夏典要荒周官蕃鎮夷官之設其來尚
矣
明興平定百粤諸酋納款因而官之俾世掌
其土比封建之遺焉惟時
===
二祖開天皇稜大抗夷裔之長重足疊跡以待
徴令繼及之際或獻馬貢方物萬里赴
闕請
命最謹嗣後凞恬世際詳近略遠諸酋稍稍越
法馴至于今威令漸弛驕蹇時肆徵調
愆期什伍虛冒侵疆逋賦嫡孽稱兵西
南之間幾成尾大說者謂繳勘授官始
于天順之
詔輸粟給劄起于成化之中然歟否歟又謂二
punctuated:
出，以星入，單父亦理，將服勤之績顧不若優游之驗與？《易》言「聖人通其變，使民不倦」，意其所用𠯁綱紀、振作者，固自有道歟？二三子學古入官，講於當世之務熟矣，其悉心折衷以對。

問：夏典要荒，周官蕃鎮，夷官之設，其來尚矣。明興，平定百粤，諸酋納款，因而官之，俾世掌其土，比封建之遺焉。惟時二祖開天，皇稜大抗，夷裔之長，重足疊跡以待徴令。繼及之際，或獻馬貢方物，萬里赴闕，請命最謹。嗣後凞恬世際，詳近略遠，諸酋稍稍越法。馴至于今，威令漸弛，驕蹇時肆，徵調愆期，什伍虛冒，侵疆逋賦，嫡孽稱兵，西南之間，幾成尾大。說者謂繳勘授官，始于天順之詔；輸粟給劄，起于成化之中，然歟否歟？又謂二
translation_en:
… went out [by starlight] and returned by starlight, and Shanfu was likewise well governed. Is the achievement of diligent labor really inferior to the efficacy of leisurely ease? The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "The sages comprehend the changes and enable the people not to grow weary." Could it be that what they used to establish order and rouse action inherently had its own way? You gentlemen study antiquity in preparation for entering officialdom and have thoroughly discussed the affairs of the present age; devote your whole minds to weighing these matters and reply.

Question: The zones of constraint and the wilds in the institutions of Xia, and the frontier domains and defense commands in the offices of Zhou—the establishment of native officials among the non-Chinese tribes is of great antiquity. When the Ming arose and pacified the Hundred Yue, the various chieftains offered submission; accordingly, they were granted official posts and allowed to govern their lands hereditarily, comparable to a vestige of the feudal system. At that time, the Two Progenitors founded the empire, and the imperial awe was greatly exalted; the leaders of the distant border tribes stood in fearful trepidation awaiting summonses and commands. Upon occasions of succession, they would present horses and tribute of local products, traveling ten thousand li to the imperial court to request investiture with the utmost reverence. Thereafter, during an era of peace and tranquility, close attention was paid to what was near while what was distant was neglected, and the various chieftains gradually transgressed the laws. Gradually down to the present, authority and ordinances have grown lax, and arrogance and insubordination are frequently indulged: troop requisitions miss their deadlines, military ranks are padded with false names, borders are encroached upon and taxes evaded, and legitimate heirs and concubines' sons take up arms against one another, so that in the southwest it has nearly become a case of the tail growing too large to wag. Commentators say that conferring office upon the submission of verification documents began with the edict of the Tianshun era (1457–1464), and that issuing commissions in exchange for deliveries of grain arose in the middle of the Chenghua era (1465–1487); is this so or not? They also say that the two…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣威力全藉土兵一切釁瑕向示包荒
不盡漢法將何以善其後歟茲欲振舉
頹綱收綜長策不納侮不黷兵內寧而
無外憂其要安在諸生比境連壤耳目
睹記最真不可謂細故也願詳言制馭
之略
punctuated: 廣威力全藉土兵，一切釁瑕，向示包荒，不盡漢法，將何以善其後歟？茲欲振舉頹綱，收綜長策，不納侮，不黷兵，內寧而無外憂，其要安在？諸生比境連壤，耳目睹記最真，不可謂細故也。願詳言制馭之略。
translation_en: …the military strength of the Two Guang provinces relies entirely on native troops (tubing), and all their offenses and flaws have hitherto been met with magnanimous tolerance rather than the full application of Chinese law—how, then, is this situation to be satisfactorily managed in the future? Now, if we wish to revive decaying discipline and gather together far-sighted policies, so as neither to invite insult nor to engage in wanton warfare, ensuring domestic tranquility without external worries, wherein lies the essential key? You students live on neighboring borders and adjoining lands; what you have seen and heard with your own eyes and ears is most authentic, and this cannot be called a trifling matter. I hope you will set forth in detail the strategies for controlling and managing them.

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
夫子聖者與何其多能也子貢曰固天縱
之將聖又多能也子聞之曰大宰知我
乎吾少也賤故多能鄙事君子多乎哉
不多也
金輝漢
同考試官教諭單批孔子之聖不在多能此作
理明意盡皆本色語宜錄以式
===
考試官教諭朱批發揮明淨
考試官教授李批精瑩透徹
聖人因人兩擬以聖而執藝以示其意焉夫聖
非藝之可名也大宰昧而不知賢者知而未盡
聖人述所能以示其意也有以哉且夫聖者道
之至而天所成也能者道之緒而聖所該也大
宰徒見聖之能而不見聖之聖故問於子貢曰
夫子聖者與何其多能也執聞見之知而疑聖
之得名者在是淺之乎觀聖矣子貢則見聖之
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「夫子聖者與？何其多能也？」子貢曰：「固天縱之將聖，又多能也。」子聞之曰：「大宰知我乎！吾少也賤，故多能鄙事。君子多乎哉？不多也。」

金輝漢

同考試官教諭單批：孔子之聖不在多能，此作理明意盡，皆本色語，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭朱批：發揮明淨。
考試官教授李批：精瑩透徹。

聖人因人兩擬以聖，而執藝以示其意焉。夫聖，非藝之可名也。大宰昧而不知，賢者知而未盡，聖人述所能以示其意也，有以哉！且夫聖者，道之至而天所成也；能者，道之緒而聖所該也。大宰徒見聖之能，而不見聖之聖，故問於子貢曰：「夫子聖者與？何其多能也？」執聞見之知，而疑聖之得名者在是，淺之乎觀聖矣！子貢則見聖之
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

[Topic:] "Is the Master a sage? How is it that he has so many abilities?" Zigong的子貢 said: "Indeed Heaven has endowed him so that he is a great sage, and moreover he has many abilities." The Master heard of it and said: "Does the Grand Minister (Taizai 大宰) know me? When I was young, I was of humble station, and therefore I acquired many abilities in menial matters. Does the gentleman have many abilities? No, he does not." [Analects 9.6]

[Author:] Jin Huihan 金輝漢

Comment by Associate Examiner, County Director of Schools (jiaoyu 教諭) Shan 單: The sagehood of Confucius 孔子 does not lie in having many abilities. In this composition the principles are clear and the meaning is fully expressed, all in authentic language; it should be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner, County Director of Schools Zhu 朱: The exposition is clear and clean.
Comment by Examiner, Prefectural Director of Schools (jiaoshou 教授) Li 李: Refined, lustrous, and thoroughgoing.

Because two people likened him to a sage, the Sage held to his practical skills in order to show his intent. Now, sagehood is not something that can be named on the basis of practical skills. The Grand Minister wasin the dark and did not know; the worthy [Zigong] knew, yet not exhaustively. That the Sage recounted his abilities in order to show his intent—there was good reason for it! Moreover, sagehood is the ultimate of the Way and that which Heaven brings to completion; ability is the餘緒 [peripheral thread / byproduct] of the Way and that which the sage encompasses. The Grand Minister merely saw the Sage's abilities without seeing the Sage's sagehood, and so he asked Zigong: "Is the Master a sage? How is it that he has so many abilities?" Clinging to knowledge gained from hearing and seeing, and suspecting that what earns a sage his name lies therein—how shallow was his view of the Sage! Zigong, on the other hand, saw the Sage's…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖而亦見聖之能故告於大宰曰固天縱之將
聖又多能也本聰明之盡而意藝之兼能者在
是智足以知聖矣然聖則孔子不居也多能亦
非君子所尚也夫子乃聞而嘆曰世莫我知也
已大宰其知我乎我之多能非如賜之所謂天
縱而無不能也吾少也賤未獲効用于當時多
能鄙事因以博習于名物耳夫君子豈其能之
多云乎哉守吾心之體要不徇象以弊其精神
執天下之易簡不徧物以窮其耳目道本至一
===
君子亦一之而已吾方學君子而未能焉若謂
之聖則豈敢哉是知聖者德也多能藝也德成
而藝自涵焉局于藝矣即無所不能不過竊君
子之餘德者本也藝者末也本立而末自裕焉
得其本矣即有所未能亦不失君子之實夫子
直述已之多能而推不多于君子厥旨深哉噫
德藝一理也博約一事也博而寡要是無本也
逐藝遺德是玩物也不然周公稱才美畢公勤
小物寧獨藝乎哉無言之訓一貫之傳學者合
punctuated: 聖，而亦見聖之能，故告於大宰曰：「固天縱之將聖，又多能也。」本聰明之盡，而意藝之兼能者在是，智足以知聖矣。然聖則孔子不居也，多能亦非君子所尚也。夫子乃聞而嘆曰：「世莫我知也已，大宰其知我乎？我之多能，非如賜之所謂天縱而無不能也。吾少也賤，未獲効用于當時，多能鄙事，因以博習于名物耳。夫君子豈其能之多云乎哉？守吾心之體要，不徇象以弊其精神；執天下之易簡，不徧物以窮其耳目。道本至一，君子亦一之而已。吾方學君子而未能焉，若謂之聖，則豈敢哉！」是知聖者，德也；多能，藝也。德成而藝自涵焉，局于藝矣，即無所不能，不過竊君子之餘。德者，本也；藝者，末也。本立而末自裕焉，得其本矣，即有所未能，亦不失君子之實。夫子直述已之多能，而推不多于君子，厥旨深哉！噫！德藝一理也，博約一事也。博而寡要，是無本也；逐藝遺德，是玩物也。不然，周公稱才美，畢公勤小物，寧獨藝乎哉？無言之訓、一貫之傳，學者合
translation_en: …sagehood, while also seeing the sage's abilities. Therefore, he told the Grand Steward (Taizai): "Certainly Heaven has endowed him generously so that he is a sage, and furthermore he has many abilities." Grounding his view in the perfection of innate intelligence while supposing that comprehensive skill in the arts also followed from this, Zigong's wisdom was sufficient to recognize a sage. Yet Confucius did not claim sagehood for himself, nor is having many abilities what the superior man esteems. Hearing of this, the Master sighed and said: "The world does not know me! Does the Grand Steward know me? My having many abilities is not, as Ci [Zigong] says, a matter of being generously endowed by Heaven so that there is nothing I cannot do. When I was young, I was of humble station and unable to be of service to my age; thus I acquired many abilities in menial matters, thereby practicing widely in names and things. Does the superior man need to have so many abilities? He guards the essential substance of his mind and does not pursue outward appearances to the exhaustion of his spirit; he holds fast to the ease and simplicity of the world and does not range over every object to the depletion of his ears and eyes. The Way is fundamentally supreme unity, and the superior man simply unifies himself with it. I am just now striving to learn to be a superior man and have not yet succeeded—as for calling me a sage, how would I dare!" From this we know that sagehood is virtue, while having many abilities is skill in the arts. When virtue is perfected, the arts are naturally encompassed within it; if one is confined to the arts, even if there is nothing one cannot do, one merely appropriates the leftover traces of the superior man. Virtue is the root; the arts are the branches. When the root is established, the branches naturally flourish; if one attains the root, even if there are things one cannot do, one still does not lose the substance of a superior man. How profound was the Master's meaning when he straightforwardly recounted his own many abilities while attributing few to the superior man! Alas! Virtue and the arts are of one principle; breadth of learning and restraint are of one affair. To be broad in learning yet lacking in essentials is to have no root; to chase after the arts while neglecting virtue is to dally with things. Otherwise, when the Duke of Zhou was praised for the beauty of his talents, and the Duke of Bi was diligent in small matters, was that merely skill in the arts? The teaching of "speaking no words" and the transmission of the "one thread binding all"—if the student combines…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而觀之孔門傳受心法可識矣
郊社之禮所以事上帝也
陳貴科
同考試官教諭梁批因郊社以明達孝措語不
繁而意義融貫傑作也
考試官教諭朱批體認精到
考試官教授李批筆力雄渾
觀聖人之所以享帝而制禮之精見矣夫惟仁
人為能享帝也禮行於郊社而上帝所由享焉
===
其義不既精乎中庸贊武周之達孝蓋曰聖人
之制禮也其用意也遠故其取義也精我觀周
禮而知武周之為達孝也已何則迎陽氣之始
復而升中于天禮行于郊也泰壇之奉非徒將
享之彌文而已順陰氣之始萌而告虔于澤禮
行于社也泰折之舉非徒裸獻之飾節而已然
其義何居乃所以事上帝耳體辨於兩儀而祭
以時行將以報其施生之德制隆於昭代而禮
縁義起用以酬其廣大之功司覆司載本至尊
punctuated:
而觀之，孔門傳受心法可識矣。

郊社之禮，所以事上帝也。
陳貴科
同考試官教諭梁批：因郊社以明達孝，措語不繁，而意義融貫，傑作也。
考試官教諭朱批：體認精到。
考試官教授李批：筆力雄渾。

觀聖人之所以享帝，而制禮之精見矣。夫惟仁人為能享帝也，禮行於郊社，而上帝所由享焉，其義不既精乎？《中庸》贊武、周之達孝，蓋曰：聖人之制禮也，其用意也遠，故其取義也精。我觀周禮，而知武、周之為達孝也已。何則？迎陽氣之始復，而升中于天，禮行于郊也，泰壇之奉，非徒將享之彌文而已；順陰氣之始萌，而告虔于澤，禮行于社也，泰折之舉，非徒裸獻之飾節而已。然其義何居？乃所以事上帝耳。體辨於兩儀，而祭以時行，將以報其施生之德；制隆於昭代，而禮縁義起，用以酬其廣大之功。司覆司載，本至尊
translation_en:
…and examine them together, the mind-method transmitted within the Confucian school can be understood.

"By the ceremonies of the sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, they served God."
Chen Guike
Associate Examiner Instructor Liang comments: Drawing upon the sacrifices to Heaven and Earth to elucidate far-reaching filial piety, the phrasing is not wordy, yet the meaning is thoroughly coherent—a masterpiece.
Examiner Instructor Zhu comments: His personal comprehension of the text is precise and thorough.
Examiner Instructor Li comments: The vigor of his brush is bold and grand.

When we observe that by which the sages made offerings to the Lord on High, the subtlety of their institution of rites becomes manifest. Indeed, only a humane man is able to make offerings to the Lord on High; when the rites are performed at the suburban and earth altars, it is through them that the Lord on High receives the offerings—is their meaning not subtle indeed? In praising the far-reaching filial piety of King Wu and the Duke of Zhou, the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) says in effect: When the sages instituted the rites, their intentions were far-reaching, and therefore the meanings they adopted were subtle. Looking at the rites of Zhou, I know that King Wu and the Duke of Zhou possessed far-reaching filial piety indeed. Why is this? Greeting the initial return of the yang vital force and sending up the burnt offering to Heaven is the rite performed at the suburban altar; the service at the Great Altar (Taitan) is not merely the elaborate ornament of presenting offerings. Following the initial sprouting of the yin vital force and announcing reverence at the marsh is the rite performed at the altar of the earth; the ceremony at the Great Square Mound (Taizhe) is not merely the decorative formality of libations and presentations. Yet wherein does their meaning lie? It is that by which one serves the Lord on High. Their forms are distinguished according to the Two Modes [Heaven and Earth], and the sacrifices are performed according to the seasons, in order to repay Their virtue in bestowing life; the institution was exalted in that illustrious age, and the rites arose on the basis of righteousness, in order to requite Their vast and great achievements. Presiding over covering all and presiding over bearing up all, They are originally supreme in dignity…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而無尚也然元后萬民之父母其位有相為對
越者夫是以明禋舉焉而上帝是祗禮自不嫌
于僭矣惟玄惟默若至幽而難假也然大君天
地之宗子其氣有相為流通者夫是以殷薦行
焉而上帝是皇禮自不病其瀆矣是蓋本事親
之心因推之為事天之典所謂享帝之仁人者
在是卽事天之仁益顯其為事親之孝所謂純
天之翼子者在是我周郊社之禮而豈徒哉吁
聖人制作之精也如此謂之達孝固宜抑有虞
===
氏禘黃帝而郊嚳則郊社之禮自古志之矣夫
子何亟稱于周耶蓋尊尊親親周道大備而達
孝錫類非武周繼述之善未能也先儒有曰舜
為人道之極萬世仰之不可加周為王制之備
萬世由之莫能易信哉
聖人人倫之至也欲為君盡君道欲為臣
盡臣道二者皆法堯舜而已矣
孫夢熊
同考試官教諭劉 批 筆力簡勁講法堯舜處尤
punctuated:
而無尚也。然元后，萬民之父母，其位有相為對越者。夫是以明禋舉焉而上帝是祗，禮自不嫌于僭矣。惟玄惟默，若至幽而難假也。然大君，天地之宗子，其氣有相為流通者。夫是以殷薦行焉而上帝是皇，禮自不病其瀆矣。是蓋本事親之心，因推之為事天之典，所謂享帝之仁人者在是；卽事天之仁，益顯其為事親之孝，所謂純天之翼子者在是。我周郊社之禮，而豈徒哉！吁！聖人制作之精也如此，謂之達孝，固宜。抑有虞氏禘黃帝而郊嚳，則郊社之禮自古志之矣，夫子何亟稱于周耶？蓋尊尊親親，周道大備，而達孝錫類，非武周繼述之善未能也。先儒有曰：「舜為人道之極，萬世仰之不可加；周為王制之備，萬世由之莫能易。」信哉！
聖人人倫之至也。欲為君，盡君道；欲為臣，盡臣道。二者皆法堯、舜而已矣。
孫夢熊
同考試官教諭劉批：筆力簡勁，講「法堯、舜」處尤
translation_en:
…and have nothing above them. Yet the great sovereign is the father and mother of the myriad people, and his position corresponds directly to Theirs. Therefore, when the pure sacrifice is performed to revere the Lord on High, the rites are naturally free from any suspicion of usurpation. Dark and silent, They seem utterly abstruse and difficult to approach. Yet the great ruler is the eldest son of Heaven and Earth, and his vital breath circulates in communion with Theirs. Therefore, when the grand offerings are carried out to magnify the Lord on High, the rites are naturally free from the fault of profanation. This is because, rooted in the heart that serves one's parents, one extends it to become the canon for serving Heaven—what is meant by "the humane man who makes offerings to the Lord" lies here; and through the humanity of serving Heaven, one further manifests the filiality of serving one's parents—what is meant by "the reverent son who is pure before Heaven" lies here. How could the suburban and altar sacrifices of our Zhou dynasty be in vain! Ah! Such is the refinement of the sages' institutions; to call this "far-reaching filial piety" is truly fitting. Yet the Lord of Yu performed the ancestral *di* sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor and the suburban *jiao* sacrifice to Ku, so the rites of the suburban and altar sacrifices had been recorded since antiquity; why did the Master so earnestly praise the Zhou? It is because in honoring the honorable and loving one's kin, the Way of Zhou was grandly complete, and such far-reaching filial piety that bestows its kind upon all could not have been achieved without the excellence of King Wu and the Duke of Zhou in continuing and carrying forward their predecessors' work. A former Confucian scholar said: "Shun was the ultimate of the human way, whom ten thousand generations look up to without being able to add anything; Zhou was the perfection of kingly institutions, which ten thousand generations follow without being able to change." Truly it is so!

"The sage is the culmination of human relationships. Either as a ruler, wishing to fulfill the way of a ruler, or as a minister, wishing to fulfill the way of a minister, in both cases one need only model oneself on Yao and Shun."

Sun Mengxiong

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Liu: The brushwork is concise and vigorous; the discussion of "modeling oneself on Yao and Shun" especially…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
得本旨取之
考試官教諭朱批洗盡塵語
考試官教授李批詞明理順
大賢論惟聖盡倫而因舉君臣所當法者焉夫
倫盡於聖而堯舜君臣之極也然則欲盡道者
舍是其奚法哉孟子勉當時之意若曰立人之
道莫大於倫盡倫之極莫過於聖蓋天敘有典
本斯民所共由也然由之而未盡者不可以言
至矣聖人者智本夙成一心而契天經地義之
===
懿德由天縱一身而會民彝物則之全本達德
以行乎達道析之極其精也而天下之軌範立
於此矣由至誠以經綸大經合之盡其大也而
萬世之標準建於此矣是其盡倫也誠無異於
規矩之盡物也而有志於惇倫者將安所取法
哉是故上焉者有君道當盡也如知爲君之難
而欲盡其道亦法堯而已矣下焉者有臣道當
盡也如知爲臣之不易而欲盡其道亦法舜而
已矣爲平章爲協和大哉堯之爲君也萬世稱
punctuated:
得本旨，取之。
考試官教諭朱批：洗盡塵語。
考試官教授李批：詞明理順。

大賢論惟聖盡倫，而因舉君臣所當法者焉。夫倫盡於聖，而堯舜，君臣之極也，然則欲盡道者，舍是其奚法哉？孟子勉當時之意若曰：立人之道，莫大於倫；盡倫之極，莫過於聖。蓋天敘有典，本斯民所共由也，然由之而未盡者，不可以言至矣。聖人者，智本夙成，一心而契天經地義之懿；德由天縱，一身而會民彝物則之全。本達德以行乎達道，析之極其精也，而天下之軌範立於此矣；由至誠以經綸大經，合之盡其大也，而萬世之標準建於此矣。是其盡倫也，誠無異於規矩之盡物也，而有志於惇倫者，將安所取法哉？是故上焉者，有君道當盡也，如知爲君之難，而欲盡其道，亦法堯而已矣；下焉者，有臣道當盡也，如知爲臣之不易，而欲盡其道，亦法舜而已矣。爲平章，爲協和，大哉堯之爲君也，萬世稱
translation_en:
…grasps the fundamental purport; selected.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Zhu comments: Washed clean of mundane expressions.
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Li comments: The wording is clear and the reasoning flows smoothly.

The great worthy discusses how only the sage fulfills human relationships, and consequently cites those whom rulers and ministers ought to take as models. Now, human relationships find their ultimate fulfillment in the sage, and Yao and Shun were the supreme culmination of rulers and ministers; if so, then for those who wish to fulfill the Way, setting these two aside, whom else should they take as their model? The meaning with which Mencius exhorted his contemporaries was to say: In establishing the Way of humanity, nothing is greater than human relationships; in reaching the ultimate fulfillment of human relationships, none surpasses the sage. For Heaven's arrangement has its constant norms, which are fundamentally what the people all follow together; yet if one follows them without fulfilling them completely, one cannot be said to have reached the ultimate. As for the sage, his wisdom is innately mature from an early age, and with a single mind he tallies with the beauty of the constant principles of Heaven and Earth; his virtue is unleashed by Heaven, and in a single person he gathers the entirety of the people's normal nature and the rules of things. Grounded in universal virtue to practice the universal Way, when analyzed, it reaches the utmost subtlety, and the model for all under Heaven is established herein; proceeding from utmost sincerity to order and regulate the great invariable relations, when synthesized, it exhausts the utmost greatness, and the standard for ten thousand generations is erected herein. Thus, his fulfillment of human relationships is truly no different from how the compass and square exhaust the forms of things; for those who aspire to earnestly cultivate human relationships, where else shall they take their model? Therefore, for one in a superior position, there is the Way of the ruler that ought to be fulfilled; if he knows the difficulty of being a ruler and wishes to fulfill his Way, he need only take Yao as his model. For one in a subordinate position, there is the Way of the minister that ought to be fulfilled; if he knows that being a minister is not easy and wishes to fulfill his Way, he need only take Shun as his model. Regulating and distinguishing the百官 and bringing harmony to the myriad states—great indeed was Yao as a ruler! Ten thousand generations praise him as…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖焉今思仁心仁政無忝於高位之履必去其
不如堯者以就其如堯者爲愼徽爲時敘巍乎
舜之爲臣也萬世稱聖焉今思責難陳善而效
其恭敬之實必去其不如舜者以就其如舜者
法堯則君之倫至矣法舜則臣之倫至矣殆猶
規矩設而天下之爲方圓者不能外乎吁孟子
此言其所以責望當時之君臣者意獨切矣嗟
夫聖人非絕德堯舜與人同耳故聖人此心吾
人亦此心也盡此心以治民卽堯矣盡此心以
===
事君卽舜矣苟不惟其心惟其迹則慕唐虞者
不免漢其治於道乎何有是以論治者貴善事
其心
易
九二貞吉象曰九二貞吉以中也
文體循
同考試官教諭劉批專認本題詞簡意精他日
必善處壯者
考試官教諭朱批發正中意眞切有餘味
punctuated:
聖焉。今思仁心仁政，無忝於高位之履，必去其不如堯者，以就其如堯者。爲愼徽、爲時敘，巍乎舜之爲臣也，萬世稱聖焉。今思責難陳善，而效其恭敬之實，必去其不如舜者，以就其如舜者。法堯則君之倫至矣，法舜則臣之倫至矣，殆猶規矩設而天下之爲方圓者不能外乎！吁！孟子此言，其所以責望當時之君臣者，意獨切矣。嗟夫！聖人非絕德，堯舜與人同耳。故聖人此心，吾人亦此心也。盡此心以治民，卽堯矣；盡此心以事君，卽舜矣。苟不惟其心，惟其迹，則慕唐虞者，不免漢其治，於道乎何有？是以論治者貴善事其心。

易

「九二：貞吉。象曰：九二貞吉，以中也。」

文體循
同考試官教諭劉批：專認本題，詞簡意精，他日必善處壯者。
考試官教諭朱批：發正中意眞切，有餘味。
translation_en:
…as a sage. Now, if one wishes to have a benevolent heart and benevolent governance so as not to bring shame upon the high position one occupies, one must cast aside whatever is unlike Yao in order to attain what is like Yao. In carefully displaying the five virtues and bringing the百揆 [official tasks] into timely order, how lofty was Shun as a minister! Ten thousand generations have praised him as a sage. Now, if one wishes to urge difficult achievements upon one's ruler, set forth what is good, and offer the substance of reverence and respect, one must cast aside whatever is unlike Shun in order to attain what is like Shun. By modeling oneself on Yao, the human relationship of the ruler reaches its perfection; by modeling oneself on Shun, the human relationship of the minister reaches its perfection—just as once the compass and square are set up, no one in the world who makes squares and circles can depart from them! Alas! In speaking these words, how earnestly Mencius held high expectations for the rulers and ministers of his time! Ah, the sages did not possess unattainable virtue; Yao and Shun were the same as other men. Therefore, the sages had this mind, and we too have this mind. To fully realize this mind in governing the people is to be Yao; to fully realize this mind in serving the ruler is to be Shun. If one attends not to their mind but only to their outward traces, then even those who admire Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] will inevitably end up with governance no better than that of the Han—what does that have to do with the Way? Therefore, those who discuss governance value cultivating their minds well.

Book of Changes (Yi)

"Nine in the second place: Perseverance brings good fortune. The Commentary on the Images says: 'Nine in the second place: Perseverance brings good fortune,' because it is central."

Wen Tixun
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Liu comments: He focuses squarely on the assigned theme; the language is concise and the meaning precise. In the future he will surely be one who knows how to conduct himself well in a state of Great Vigor (Zhuang).
Examiner and County Director of Studies Zhu comments: He brings out the meaning of correctness and centrality with genuine incisiveness and lingering resonance.

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授李批通篇剴切讀之凜然
二聖於壯爻與其事之善而原其心之純焉夫
處壯莫善於貞而中其本也九二以之宜二聖
交發其義與且君子之處壯非正無以保其盛
非中無以裕其原卦之九二居陰失正而所處
得中是故周公係爻慮其有用壯之失也而戒
以貞吉焉蓋大壯利貞時則然也故當其時者
不可以過壯也是必以天下之公理行天下之
公事動有關于君德則爲之而弗過于激也政
===
有裨于民瘼則爲之而弗失于驟也觀其所發
一天地正大之情焉惟正可以懾羣邪而彼之
伺隙乘釁者皆不得撓吾剛動之謀矣此正道
行而吉之所以大來乎孔子傳象本其有得正
之心也而原其以中焉蓋因中求正理則然也
故事之正者不容以襲取也由其以天下之公
道秉天下之公心上攄其忠以格君之心爲心
也下宣其猷以惠民之心爲心也察其所存一
天地受中之懿焉惟中可以貫萬事而措之行
punctuated:
考試官教授李批：通篇剴切，讀之凜然。

二聖於壯爻，與其事之善，而原其心之純焉。夫處壯莫善於貞，而中其本也。九二以之，宜二聖交發其義與！且君子之處壯，非正無以保其盛，非中無以裕其原。卦之九二，居陰失正，而所處得中。是故周公係爻，慮其有用壯之失也，而戒以「貞吉」焉。蓋大壯利貞，時則然也，故當其時者，不可以過壯也。是必以天下之公理，行天下之公事：動有關于君德，則爲之而弗過于激也；政有裨于民瘼，則爲之而弗失于驟也。觀其所發，一天地正大之情焉。惟正可以懾羣邪，而彼之伺隙乘釁者，皆不得撓吾剛動之謀矣。此正道行而吉之所以大來乎！孔子傳《象》，本其有得正之心也，而原其「以中」焉。蓋因中求正，理則然也，故事之正者，不容以襲取也。由其以天下之公道，秉天下之公心：上攄其忠，以格君之心爲心也；下宣其猷，以惠民之心爲心也。察其所存，一天地受中之懿焉。惟中可以貫萬事，而措之行…
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Li's comment: The entire piece is incisive and pertinent; reading it inspires awe.

Regarding the line of Great Vigor (Dazhuang), the two sages approve the goodness of its deeds and trace the purity of its mind. Now, in dwelling in a time of vigor, nothing is better than firmness and correctness (zhen), and centrality (zhong) is its root. Nine in the Second Place embodies this, so is it not fitting that the two sages mutually elucidated its meaning?

Moreover, when a gentleman dwells in a time of vigor, without correctness he has no means to preserve his flourishing state, and without centrality he has no means to enrich its source. Nine in the Second Place of the hexagram occupies a yin position and thus lacks correctness of place, yet where it dwells attains centrality. Therefore, when the Duke of Zhou appended the line statement, concerned lest it suffer the fault of relying recklessly on vigor, he admonished/pronounced "firmness and correctness bring good fortune." For in Great Vigor it is advantageous to be firm and correct; the time makes it so. Thus, those who find themselves in such a time must not be excessively vigorous. They must carry out the public affairs of the world according to the public principles of the world: if an action pertains to the ruler's virtue, they undertake it without being overly strident; if a policy remedies the people's distress, they implement it without erring into haste. Observing what they manifest, it is entirely the upright and great disposition of Heaven and Earth. Only correctness can overawe the pack of wicked men, so that those who watch for openings and exploit rifts are all unable to obstruct our resolute and active plans. Is this not how the right Way prevails and good fortune arrives in full measure?

When Confucius composed the Commentary on the Images (Xiang), he grounded it in Nine in the Second's possessing a mind that attains correctness, and traced its source to its being "because of centrality." For seeking correctness through centrality is the natural principle of things; thus correctness in affairs cannot be seized through mere external imitation. It comes from holding fast to the public mind of the world through the public Way of the world: above, pouring forth one's loyalty, taking the rectification of the ruler's mind as one's own mind; below, spreading forth one's wise plans, taking the benefiting of the people as one's own mind. Examining what is preserved within, it is entirely the admirable virtue of centrality received from Heaven and Earth. Only centrality can thread together the myriad affairs, and when applied to conduct…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
已立朝者悉有以閑夫非禮之履矣此中心純
而貞之所以獲吉乎合而觀之聖人爲吾道慶
也深矣而其爲君子謀也至矣雖然是道也必
君臣合德而後可蓋中以行正者臣道也而中
心無爲以守至正君道也君以中正爲大壯之
主則有孚攣如而中正之臣咸得乘時以自効
是謂上下交而泰道長也何壯之不可保耶此
二聖未發之旨玩易者不可不知
夫乾其靜也專其動也直是以大生焉夫
===
坤其靜也翕其動也闢是以廣生焉廣
大配天地
呂興周
同考試官教諭劉 批 直說題旨脫去浮詞非苟作者
考試官教諭朱 批 雅淡可以爲式
考試官教授李 批 醇正典切
大傳推易之廣大本於天地而配之也夫德妙
動靜天地之所以廣大也觀天地而易之廣大
punctuated:
已、立朝者，悉有以閑夫非禮之履矣。此中心純而貞之所以獲吉乎！合而觀之，聖人爲吾道慶也深矣，而其爲君子謀也至矣。雖然，是道也，必君臣合德而後可。蓋中以行正者，臣道也；而中心無爲以守至正，君道也。君以中正爲《大壯》之主，則有孚攣如，而中正之臣咸得乘時以自効，是謂上下交而《泰》道長也，何壯之不可保耶？此二聖未發之旨，玩《易》者不可不知。

「夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉。夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉。廣大配天地。」
呂興周
同考試官教諭劉 批：直說題旨，脫去浮詞，非苟作者。
考試官教諭朱 批：雅淡，可以爲式。
考試官教授李 批：醇正典切。

《大傳》推《易》之廣大，本於天地而配之也。夫德妙動靜，天地之所以廣大也；觀天地而《易》之廣大，
translation_en:
… personal conduct and standing at court will all serve to guard against treading where propriety forbids. Is this not why purity of heart in one's center leads to the good fortune of firm correctness! Viewing these together, how deeply the Sages rejoiced for our Way, and how thoroughly they took counsel for the noble man! Even so, this Way can be realized only when ruler and minister unite in virtue. For to enact rectitude through centrality is the way of the minister, whereas to preserve supreme rectitude through non-action at the center of the heart is the way of the ruler. When the ruler presides over "Great Vigor" (Dazhuang) with centrality and rectitude, there is sincere trust binding all together, and ministers of centrality and rectitude are all able to seize the moment to devote their service. This is what is meant by above and below communicating and the Way of "Peace" (Tai) growing—what vigor could then fail to be preserved? This is the unspoken import of the two Sages, which those who study the Changes (Yi) must not fail to understand.

"As for Qian, in its stillness it is concentrated, and in its movement it is straight; therefore great things are produced from it. As for Kun, in its stillness it is closed, and in its movement it is open; therefore vast things are produced from it. In vastness and greatness it matches heaven and earth."

Lü Xingzhou 呂興周

Associate Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉 comments: It states the import of the topic directly and sheds empty verbiage; not the work of a careless writer.
Examiner and Instructor Zhu 朱 comments: Refined and understated; it can serve as a model.
Examiner and Professor Li 李 comments: Pure, orthodox, classical, and apt.

The Great Commentary (Dazhuan) traces how the vastness and greatness of the Changes originate in heaven and earth and match them. Indeed, virtue wondrously manifest in movement and stillness is whereby heaven and earth are vast and great; observing heaven and earth, as for the vastness and greatness of the Changes…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
夫何間耶今夫易之爲書也通逺邇焉塞兩間
焉人知其廣矣大矣抑孰知其原于天地乎夫
乾天也天以一氣運于上而有動靜焉靜則專
一而不貳動則直遂而不撓一專一直交而萬
物胥此乎始矣此乾之所以大也易以效天也
大不于是而生乎夫坤地也地以一氣承乎天
而有動靜焉靜則翕聚而有常動則發舒而不
匱一翕一闢交而萬物胥此乎成矣此坤之所
以廣也易以法地也廣不于是而生乎夫惟天
爲大而易有天道焉是天之理盡于易也而易
之大而無外者足以配乎天矣大而至于配天
則遠近上下莫有出於天者而何一之不備耶
惟地爲廣而易有地道焉是地之理盡於易也
而易之廣而無方者足以配乎地矣廣而至于
配地則遠近上下莫有出於地者而何一之不
該耶信乎易與天地準而凡變通之宜與夫隂
陽之義易簡之善皆自此而包括之矣善言易
者其亦求端于天地乎抑論天地者象形也易
punctuated: 夫何間耶？今夫《易》之爲書也，通逺邇焉，塞兩間焉，人知其廣矣、大矣，抑孰知其原于天地乎？夫乾，天也。天以一氣運于上而有動靜焉。靜則專一而不貳，動則直遂而不撓。一專一直交，而萬物胥此乎始矣，此乾之所以大也。《易》以效天也，大不于是而生乎？夫坤，地也。地以一氣承乎天而有動靜焉。靜則翕聚而有常，動則發舒而不匱。一翕一闢交，而萬物胥此乎成矣，此坤之所以廣也。《易》以法地也，廣不于是而生乎？夫惟天爲大，而《易》有天道焉，是天之理盡于《易》也，而《易》之大而無外者足以配乎天矣。大而至于配天，則遠近上下莫有出於天者，而何一之不備耶？惟地爲廣，而《易》有地道焉，是地之理盡於《易》也，而《易》之廣而無方者足以配乎地矣。廣而至于配地，則遠近上下莫有出於地者，而何一之不該耶？信乎《易》與天地準，而凡變通之宜與夫隂陽之義、易簡之善，皆自此而包括之矣。善言《易》者，其亦求端于天地乎？抑論天地者，象形也；《易》
translation_en:
…how could there be any gap between them?

Now, as for the Book of Changes (Yi), it penetrates what is distant and near, and fills the space between Heaven and Earth. People know that it is vast and great, yet who knows that it originates in Heaven and Earth?

Qian is Heaven. Heaven revolves above with a single vital force (qi) and possesses movement and stillness. In stillness, it is concentrated and undivided; in movement, it goes straight forward and unbent. As this concentration and straightness alternate, the myriad things all take their beginning from this. This is why Qian is great. The Changes emulates Heaven; does not its greatness arise from this?

Kun is Earth. Earth receives from Heaven with a single vital force and possesses movement and stillness. In stillness, it gathers in and maintains constancy; in movement, it opens out and is inexhaustible. As this gathering and opening alternate, the myriad things all reach their completion through this. This is why Kun is vast. The Changes models itself on Earth; does not its vastness arise from this?

Indeed, only Heaven is great, and the Changes contains the Way of Heaven; thus the principle of Heaven is fully expressed in the Changes, and the boundlessness of the greatness of the Changes is sufficient to match Heaven. Being so great as to match Heaven, nothing far or near, above or below, goes beyond Heaven—so what single thing is not provided for within it? Only Earth is vast, and the Changes contains the Way of Earth; thus the principle of Earth is fully expressed in the Changes, and the limitlessness of the vastness of the Changes is sufficient to match Earth. Being so vast as to match Earth, nothing far or near, above or below, goes beyond Earth—so what single thing is not encompassed within it?

Truly, the Changes is on a par with Heaven and Earth, and all the appropriateness of change and continuity, together with the meaning of yin and yang and the goodness of easy and simple action, are all encompassed from this. Those who are skilled at discussing the Changes—should they not also seek its beginnings in Heaven and Earth?

Yet if we discuss them further: Heaven and Earth are images and forms; the Changes…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者奇偶也以象形視天地則有迹矣以奇偶視
易則有文矣文者道之顯也迹者道之著也以
道而觀則象形無迹也奇偶無文也道會于吾
心也學者致吾心之廣大而天地易理以一心
而涵之矣故曰神而明之存乎其人
書
其爾典常作之師
吳懋昭
同考試官教諭單批法典守官不難措詞而鋪
叙圓融略無斧鑿是有手段者允宜高薦
考試官教諭朱批淘煉精純
考試官教授李批舂容可誦
===
賢王之訓治官惟守當代之法而已夫周之典
常法之盡善者也有治官之責者可不以是爲
師哉成王訓迪百官及此意曰王制以時爲大
臣子以趨時爲忠凡我有官君子學古而裁度
之固可以適治矣然豈但已哉我周之法創立
本於文武制作成於周公固一代之典常而入
punctuated:
者，奇偶也。以象形視天地，則有迹矣；以奇偶視《易》，則有文矣。文者，道之顯也；迹者，道之著也。以道而觀，則象形無迹也，奇偶無文也，道會于吾心也。學者致吾心之廣大，而天地《易》理以一心而涵之矣。故曰：「神而明之，存乎其人。」

《書》：其爾典常作之師。
吳懋昭
同考試官教諭單批：法典守官，不難措詞，而鋪叙圓融，略無斧鑿，是有手段者，允宜高薦。
考試官教諭朱批：淘煉精純。
考試官教授李批：舂容可誦。

賢王之訓治官，惟守當代之法而已。夫周之典常，法之盡善者也，有治官之責者，可不以是爲師哉？成王訓迪百官及此，意曰：王制以時爲大，臣子以趨時爲忠。凡我有官君子，學古而裁度之，固可以適治矣，然豈但已哉？我周之法，創立本於文、武，制作成於周公，固一代之典常，而入
translation_en:
… operates through odd and even numbers. If one views heaven and earth through images and forms, then there are physical traces; if one views the Book of Changes (Yi) through odd and even numbers, then there are written patterns. Written patterns are the manifestation of the Way; physical traces are the display of the Way. Yet if one observes them from the standpoint of the Way itself, then images and forms leave no traces, odd and even numbers have no written patterns, and the Way converges within our own mind. When a scholar brings the vastness and greatness of his mind to the utmost, heaven, earth, and the principles of the Changes are all encompassed within a single mind. Therefore it is said: "To apprehend it with spirit-like insight and illuminate it depends upon the person himself."

Book of Documents (Shu): "Take for your teacher the regular laws [of our dynasty]."
By Wu Maozhao 吳懋昭.
Associate Examiner Instructor Shan 單 comments: On the theme of statutory laws and officials keeping to their duties, it is not difficult to find words, yet his exposition is well-rounded and harmonious, without the slightest trace of forced carving. This is someone of real skill, who truly deserves a high recommendation.
Examiner Instructor Zhu 朱 comments: Sifted and refined to pure perfection.
Examiner Professor Li 李 comments: Measured and dignified, worthy of recitation.

When a worthy king instructs his governing officials, he bids them only to uphold the laws of the reigning dynasty. Now, the regular laws of the Zhou are laws of complete perfection; how could those who bear the responsibility of governing officials not take them as their teacher? When King Cheng 成王 instructed and guided the hundred officials and touched upon this, his meaning was as follows: Royal institutions take timeliness as paramount, and subjects take keeping pace with the times as loyalty. When all you gentlemen who hold office study antiquity and measure your actions accordingly, you can indeed adapt to governance; yet how could it stop merely at that? The laws of our Zhou dynasty were founded at their root by King Wen 文王 and King Wu 武王, and brought to completion in their institutions by the Duke of Zhou 周公; they are truly the regular laws of our age, and upon entering…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
官者所當師也爾其仰王制之昭垂而欽之焉
攸司者務守乎明徵之範思聖謨之定保而慎
之焉出令者毋忘乎佑啓之方監二代而損益
法何備也于是師其法焉之綱之紀遵成憲以
攸行更三聖而經綸意何精也于是師其意焉
一弛一張奉舊章以時措為天子論思之臣燮
理寅亮其職也廟謨國體具於先世之所規畫
者其道本可繼惟善繼之而已矣為天子分猷
之臣率屬倡牧其責也吏治民瘼見於昭代之
===
所講明者其事本可述惟善述之而已矣蓋前
王之謨烈徵諸庶民即萬邦猶作孚矣況在位
之君子耶周官之法度垂諸后昆即萬世猶永
賴矣況今日之臣工耶信能以是為師則入官
者不惟學古而且師今行政者不必更化而可
善治所以敬厥職者其道得矣噫周王之訓迪
厥官其有得於制治保邦之要乎抑於是而知
成王守成之令主也自古創業之君典則所貽
至深且遠繼體者能世守而勿失雖至今存可
punctuated: 官者所當師也。爾其仰王制之昭垂而欽之焉，攸司者務守乎明徵之範；思聖謨之定保而慎之焉，出令者毋忘乎佑啓之方。監二代而損益，法何備也，于是師其法焉，之綱之紀，遵成憲以攸行；更三聖而經綸，意何精也，于是師其意焉，一弛一張，奉舊章以時措。為天子論思之臣，燮理寅亮其職也，廟謨國體具於先世之所規畫者，其道本可繼，惟善繼之而已矣；為天子分猷之臣，率屬倡牧其責也，吏治民瘼見於昭代之所講明者，其事本可述，惟善述之而已矣。蓋前王之謨烈徵諸庶民，即萬邦猶作孚矣，況在位之君子耶？周官之法度垂諸后昆，即萬世猶永賴矣，況今日之臣工耶？信能以是為師，則入官者不惟學古而且師今，行政者不必更化而可善治，所以敬厥職者，其道得矣。噫！周王之訓迪厥官，其有得於制治保邦之要乎！抑於是而知成王守成之令主也。自古創業之君，典則所貽，至深且遠，繼體者能世守而勿失，雖至今存可
translation_en: …entering office ought to take as their model. You should look up to the illustrious transmission of the royal regulations and revere them, so that those in charge of specific duties strive to abide by the standards that have been clearly verified; reflect upon how the sagely counsels secure peace and stability and be cautious regarding them, so that those who issue commands never forget the methods that assist and enlighten us. Having surveyed the two preceding dynasties to make reductions and additions, how complete the laws are! Taking these laws as your model, in both overarching principles and minor details, follow the established statutes in all that you do. Having passed through three sages in their statecraft and ordering, how refined the underlying intent is! Taking this intent as your model, whether relaxing or tightening, uphold the old canons and implement them according to the times. For the ministers who deliberate and reflect for the Son of Heaven, harmonizing and reverently brightening the governance is their duty; since the counsels of the court and the fundamental structure of the state are fully present in what was planned by earlier generations, their Way can inherently be continued—one need only be good at continuing it! For the ministers who share in the plans of the Son of Heaven, leading their subordinates and guiding the regional pastors is their responsibility; since the administration of officials and the sufferings of the people are evident in what has been elucidated by our illustrious dynasty, their affairs can inherently be carried forward—one need only be good at carrying them forward! Indeed, the counsels and achievements of the former kings have been verified among the common people, so that even the myriad states place their trust in them—how much more so the noble men holding office? The laws and regulations of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) have been handed down to later descendants, so that even ten thousand generations will forever rely on them—how much more so the ministers and officials of today? If they can truly take these as their model, then those entering office will not only study antiquity but also take the present as their teacher, and those administering governance will not need to alter the system in order to achieve good rule; thus, the Way of reverently fulfilling their duties will be attained. Ah! In instructing and guiding his officials, did the King of Zhou not grasp the essentials of regulating governance and securing the state? Moreover, from this we know that King Cheng was an admirable sovereign of consolidation. Since antiquity, the canons and rules bequeathed by founding rulers have been most profound and far-reaching; if those who succeed to the throne can guard them from generation to generation without losing them, even down to the present day they could endure…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
矣成王繼序不忘既以法典嚴諸巳至是又嚴
諸臣其慮淵哉雖然基命宥密祗勤于德則又
法典之本也願治者其圖之
一人有慶兆民賴之其寧惟永
金輝漢
同考試官教諭單批敬刑獲福勸勉之意溢于
言表他日服政必能以欽恤為心者敬服敬服
考試官教諭朱批文思雋永
考試官教授李批格調雅馴
===
賢王期君民獲福之遠勉諸侯之敬刑也夫刑
者所用𠯁資治安者也君慶民賴而極於永寧
非敬刑何𠯁致之哉穆王訓同姓諸侯也蓋曰
人臣之典獄也所職者惟持天下之平故所用
者足綏天下之福爾能敬五刑以成三德其效
果何如耶彼上而一人以恤刑為心者也茲則
刑措而慶集焉予政罔干樂觀化中之盛也從
欲以治坐致垂拱之休也始之奉我一人者至
是而斂福於一人矣不有慶乎下而兆民以懷
punctuated:
矣。成王繼序不忘，既以法典嚴諸巳，至是又嚴諸臣，其慮淵哉！雖然，基命宥密，祗勤于德，則又法典之本也。願治者其圖之。

「一人有慶，兆民賴之，其寧惟永。」
金輝漢
同考試官教諭單批：敬刑獲福，勸勉之意，溢于言表。他日服政，必能以欽恤為心者，敬服！敬服！
考試官教諭朱批：文思雋永。
考試官教授李批：格調雅馴。

賢王期君民獲福之遠，勉諸侯之敬刑也。夫刑者，所用𠯁資治安者也。君慶民賴，而極於永寧，非敬刑何𠯁致之哉？穆王訓同姓諸侯也，蓋曰：人臣之典獄也，所職者惟持天下之平，故所用者足綏天下之福。爾能敬五刑以成三德，其效果何如耶？彼上而一人，以恤刑為心者也。茲則刑措而慶集焉。予政罔干，樂觀化中之盛也；從欲以治，坐致垂拱之休也。始之奉我一人者，至是而斂福於一人矣，不有慶乎？下而兆民，以懷
translation_en:
… indeed. King Cheng succeeded to the royal line without forgetting his predecessors; having already applied the legal canons strictly to himself, at this point he also applied them strictly to his ministers—how profound was his foresight! Even so, establishing the Mandate in quietude and stillness and being reverently diligent in virtue are in turn the foundation of the legal canons. Let those who desire good governance take heed of this.

"The One Man shall enjoy felicity, the millions of people will depend on him, and the tranquility he brings will be everlasting."
By Jin Huihan.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Shan: Being reverent toward punishments brings blessings; the spirit of exhortation overflows beyond the words. In days to come when he takes up administration, he will surely be one who takes reverent compassion to heart. Respectful admiration, respectful admiration!
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhu: His literary thoughts are rich and enduring.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Li: The style is elegant and refined.

The worthy king looks forward to the ruler and the people obtaining far-reaching blessings, and thus exhorts the feudal lords to be reverent in their use of punishments. Now, punishments are employed sufficiently to aid in securing order and peace. That the ruler enjoys felicity and the people depend on him, culminating in everlasting tranquility—without reverence for punishments, how could this be achieved? When King Mu instructed the feudal lords of the royal surname, he said in effect: When a minister is in charge of criminal cases, his sole duty is to maintain fairness throughout the realm, and therefore what he employs is sufficient to secure the blessings of the realm. If you are able to be reverent toward the Five Punishments so as to accomplish the Three Virtues, what will the effect be? Above, the One Man takes compassion in punishments to heart. Now, punishments are set aside and felicities gather. With no interference in my governance, I joyfully behold the flourishing of those who are being transformed; governing in accordance with desires, I effortlessly attain the blessings of ruling with robes hanging down and hands folded. Those who at first served me, the One Man, have by this point gathered blessings upon the One Man—is there not felicity? Below, the millions of people take bearing…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
刑爲分者也玆則刑清而咸賴焉民日遠罪有
所藉以全生也家用平康有所倚以立命也始
之天齊于民者至是而造福於民矣不有賴乎
君而有慶是君寧於上也民而咸賴是民寧於
下也豈特于今爲然哉太和之氣洽朝野以交
孚自衍爲永終之祜大順之風合中外以交暢
自篤爲永綏之祥繼今而爲君者非一世也深
仁所培足以爲長我王國之本則蒙成業者世
世此有慶焉宗社寧謐之祉不愈遠而有光乎
===
繼今而爲民者非一世也厚澤所被足以爲保
我黎民之基則承餘庇者世世此永賴焉海宇
寧一之休不愈久而弗替乎夫慶在一人而賴
及兆民安在一時而垂及後世敬刑成德之化
其所貽者遠矣必如是而後見日勤之效也爾
同姓諸侯其尚欽念之哉抑刑者成也一成而
不變故君子盡心焉心者天下萬世之所繫命
也呂刑之作雖云誥四方以權宜一時之急然
一篇之中惓惓於敬刑多懼之戒其藹然惻怛
punctuated:
刑爲分者也，玆則刑清而咸賴焉。民日遠罪，有所藉以全生也；家用平康，有所倚以立命也。始之天齊于民者，至是而造福於民矣，不有賴乎？君而有慶，是君寧於上也；民而咸賴，是民寧於下也。豈特于今爲然哉？太和之氣，洽朝野以交孚，自衍爲永終之祜；大順之風，合中外以交暢，自篤爲永綏之祥。繼今而爲君者，非一世也。深仁所培，足以爲長我王國之本，則蒙成業者，世世此有慶焉，宗社寧謐之祉，不愈遠而有光乎？繼今而爲民者，非一世也。厚澤所被，足以爲保我黎民之基，則承餘庇者，世世此永賴焉，海宇寧一之休，不愈久而弗替乎？夫慶在一人而賴及兆民，安在一時而垂及後世，敬刑成德之化，其所貽者遠矣，必如是而後見日勤之效也。爾同姓諸侯，其尚欽念之哉！

抑刑者，成也，一成而不變，故君子盡心焉。心者，天下萬世之所繫命也。《呂刑》之作，雖云誥四方以權宜一時之急，然一篇之中，惓惓於敬刑多懼之戒，其藹然惻怛
translation_en:
… fearing punishments as their lot; now, as punishments become pure, all rely upon them. As the people daily distance themselves from crime, they have something to depend upon to preserve their lives; as their households enjoy peace and tranquility, they have something to lean upon to establish their destinies. That by which Heaven originally brought uniformity to the people now creates blessings for the people—is there not reliance in this? When the ruler has felicity, the ruler is at peace above; when the people all rely on it, the people are at peace below. Yet how could this be so only in the present? The vital energy of supreme harmony pervades court and countryside in mutual trust, naturally extending into everlasting blessings; the wind of great compliance unites the inner and outer realms in mutual flourishing, naturally consolidating into an auspicious sign of eternal tranquility. Those who succeed to the throne after today will not be of a single generation. What is cultivated by deep benevolence suffices to serve as the foundation for prolonging our royal state; thus those who inherit the accomplished work will generation after generation possess this felicity—will not the blessings of a tranquil ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain shine all the brighter the further they reach? Those who live as the people after today will not be of a single generation. What is overspread by generous grace suffices to serve as the basis for protecting our black-haired people; thus those who receive the remaining shelter will generation after generation eternally rely on this—will not the excellence of a peaceful and unified realm endure all the longer without decline? Indeed, when felicity rests with the One Man and reliance extends to the millions of people, when peace exists in a single era and is handed down to later generations, the transforming influence of revering punishments to complete the virtues leaves a legacy that reaches far indeed! Only when it is like this can the efficacy of daily diligence be seen. May you feudal lords of the royal surname reverently bear this in mind!

Moreover, punishment means that which is settled; once settled, it cannot be changed, and therefore the noble man exhausts his heart-and-mind in it. The heart-and-mind is that upon which the lives of the world and ten thousand generations depend. Although the composition of the "Punishments of Lü" (Lü xing) is said to have been an announcement to the four quarters as an expedient for the urgency of the moment, throughout the entire chapter it is earnestly devoted to the admonition of revering punishments with much apprehension; its gentle and compassionate…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之意成康忠厚之澤千載而下猶可想見矣吁
此孔子所以有取而錄之也歟
詩
禾易長畝終善且有曾孫不怒農夫克敏
曾孫之稼如茨如梁曾孫之庾如坻如
京乃求千斯倉乃求萬斯箱黍稷稻粱
農夫之慶
莫若知
同考試官教諭梁批有周以農事為首務是作
發明上下一體之情渾見盛時氣象宜錄以式
考試官教諭朱批義意含蓄
考試官教授李批簡潔而盡
公卿於農事致民之力而不居其功焉甚矣公
卿之重農也下不愛其力而上不有其功其眞
一體而無間者哉此詩述公卿力農奉祭而作
也意謂明君以稼穡為務未始不以有年為祥
然力則欲其出於民也功則惡其歸諸己也我
公卿殆有以辨此乎彼禾之弗治有秋未可必
punctuated:
之意，成、康忠厚之澤，千載而下猶可想見矣。吁！此孔子所以有取而錄之也歟？

《詩》
「禾易長畝，終善且有。曾孫不怒，農夫克敏。曾孫之稼，如茨如梁；曾孫之庾，如坻如京。乃求千斯倉，乃求萬斯箱。黍稷稻粱，農夫之慶。」
莫若知
同考試官教諭梁批：有周以農事為首務，是作發明上下一體之情，渾見盛時氣象，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭朱批：義意含蓄。
考試官教授李批：簡潔而盡。

公卿於農事，致民之力而不居其功焉。甚矣，公卿之重農也！下不愛其力，而上不有其功，其眞一體而無間者哉！此詩述公卿力農奉祭而作也。意謂：明君以稼穡為務，未始不以有年為祥，然力則欲其出於民也，功則惡其歸諸己也。我公卿殆有以辨此乎？彼禾之弗治，有秋未可必
translation_en:
… intent, and the loyal and generous beneficence of Kings Cheng and Kang, can still be envisioned a thousand years later. Ah! Is this not why Confucius found value in it and recorded it?

Book of Odes (Shijing)
"The grain is well-cultivated all along the acres, and in the end will be good and abundant. The distant descendant is not angry; the husbandmen are able to be diligent. The crops of the distant descendant are thick as thatch and curved as carriage-beams; the stacks of the distant descendant are like islands and like mounds. He will seek a thousand granaries; he will seek ten thousand carts. Millet, panicled millet, rice, and sorghum are the felicitation of the husbandmen." [Ode "Fu Tian" 甫田]
Mo Ruozhi 莫若知
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Liang: The Zhou dynasty took agriculture as its foremost task. This composition elucidates the sentiment of superiors and inferiors forming a single body, fully revealing the spirit of a flourishing age. It is fitting to record it as a model.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhu: The meaning and purport are rich and restrained.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Li: Concise yet exhaustive.

In agricultural matters, the dukes and high ministers elicit the strength of the people without claiming the merit for themselves. Profound indeed is the importance that the dukes and high ministers attach to agriculture! Those below do not spare their strength, while those above do not take possession of the merit—truly they form a single body without any gap between them! This ode was composed to recount how the dukes and high ministers devoted themselves to agriculture in order to present sacrifices. Its meaning is that an enlightened ruler takes sowing and reaping as his central duty and never fails to regard a bountiful year as an auspicious sign; yet as for the labor, he wishes it to come from the people, and as for the merit, he dislikes having it attributed to himself. Do our dukes and high ministers not understand this well? If those crops are not properly tended, an autumn harvest cannot be counted upon…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也國有惰農且貽曾孫之戚矣自今觀之禾皆
易治無遺力焉竟畝如一無遺利焉則終善且
有適愜祈年之願而曾孫之若殆與田畯之喜
相協矣然農夫以曾孫之悅為悅者也莫不曰
服田力穡我農人之職也曾孫不怒凡以其敏
耳吾何敢自愛焉感上心之懌豫益相率而從
事矣其諸悅以先民而民忘其勞者乎稼之弗
登穡人罔成功也君有違欲亦非田野之利矣
自今觀之如茨如梁稼何盛也如坻如京庾何
===
盛也則千倉萬箱誠裕十千之取而黍稷稻粱
殆與善有之占相符矣然曾孫以農夫之慶為
慶者也必將曰自天降康雖明神之貺也百穀
用登凡以為農耳吾何力之有焉念小民之勤
動將歸其功而不居矣其諸以美利利天下而
不言所利者乎吁盡勸相之道而下不弛其勞
獲順成之休而上不專其美君民一體之情藹
然於田事之際盛世氣象不可想見哉抑自古
有年非天時適然亦和氣有以召之公卿惟致
punctuated: 也；國有惰農，且貽曾孫之戚矣。自今觀之，禾皆易治，無遺力焉；竟畝如一，無遺利焉。則終善且有，適愜祈年之願，而曾孫之若，殆與田畯之喜相協矣。然農夫以曾孫之悅為悅者也，莫不曰：「服田力穡，我農人之職也。曾孫不怒，凡以其敏耳，吾何敢自愛焉？」感上心之懌豫，益相率而從事矣，其諸悅以先民而民忘其勞者乎！稼之弗登，穡人罔成功也；君有違欲，亦非田野之利矣。自今觀之，如茨如梁，稼何盛也；如坻如京，庾何盛也。則千倉萬箱，誠裕十千之取，而黍稷稻粱，殆與善有之占相符矣。然曾孫以農夫之慶為慶者也，必將曰：「自天降康，雖明神之貺也，百穀用登，凡以為農耳，吾何力之有焉？」念小民之勤動，將歸其功而不居矣，其諸以美利利天下而不言所利者乎！吁！盡勸相之道，而下不弛其勞；獲順成之休，而上不專其美。君民一體之情，藹然於田事之際，盛世氣象，不可想見哉！抑自古有年，非天時適然，亦和氣有以召之。公卿惟致…
translation_en:
… [that an autumn harvest cannot be guaranteed]; and if the state has lazy farmers, it will moreover leave grief to the Great-grandson. Viewing it now, the grain is all well-tended, with no effort spared; across the whole acre it is uniform, with no benefit left uncultivated. Thus in the end it is both good and abundant, fittingly fulfilling the wish of the prayer for a good year, and the Great-grandson's approval is well in harmony with the joy of the Inspector of the Fields. Yet the farmers are those who take the Great-grandson's pleasure as their own pleasure, and there is none who does not say: "Working the fields and toiling at the harvest is our duty as farmers. That the Great-grandson is not angry is entirely because of our diligence—how dare we spare ourselves?" Moved by the gladness in their superior's heart, they lead one another on all the more to apply themselves to their tasks. Is this not what is meant by leading the people through joy so that the people forget their toil!

If the grain does not ripen, the harvesters achieve no success; and if the ruler's wishes are thwarted, neither is it to the benefit of the countryside. Viewing it now, like thatch and like a bridge, how flourishing is the grain in the fields; like an islet and like a mound, how flourishing are the open-air stacks! Thus a thousand granaries and ten thousand carts truly enrich the taking of ten thousand measures, and the glutinous millet, panicled millet, rice, and fine millet well correspond with the auspicious divination of a good and abundant harvest. Yet the Great-grandson is one who takes the farmers' celebration as his own celebration, and he will surely say: "That peace and abundance are sent down from Heaven, though it is the gift of the bright spirits, that the hundred grains are thereby harvested is all because of the farmers—what effort of mine is there in this?" Mindful of the common people's diligent labor, he will attribute the merit to them and not claim it for himself. Is this not what is meant by benefiting the world with admirable benefits without speaking of what he has benefited!

Ah! He exhausts the way of encouragement and assistance, and those below do not slacken in their labor; he obtains the blessing of a favorable and completed harvest, and he above does not monopolize its glory. The feeling of ruler and people being of one body is warm and harmonious in the midst of fieldwork—can the atmosphere of a flourishing age not be envisioned in this! Moreover, since antiquity, a bountiful year has not been a mere coincidence of heaven's seasons, but is also summoned by a harmonious ethos. Only because the dukes and ministers devote…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
力於民者盡故民竭力以事其上惟不自有其
功故民亦忘帝力於何有也是以民和而神降
之福海內稱極治焉使仁不足以成民則德馨
不脩神且吐之國與民將何賴耶是故君子先
成民而後致力於神
紹庭上下陟降厥家
馬千官
同考試官教諭梁批成王體道之密模寫殆盡
是深於詩者宜錄以式
===
考試官教諭朱批義精句煉讀之灑然
考試官教授李批詞㫖瑩徹
隨在述先王之事嗣王體道之勤見矣蓋先王
之事即道也于庭于家而紹之道其有不得者
哉成王朝廟延訪羣臣作也蓋曰先王之治本
於道先王之道見于行維予小子方判渙之難
就而值多難之未堪所以敷求先王者可但已
耶誠以清明開一統之業昭考所當上下以聽
外治者有庭也朕今踐其位既不能就其道矣
punctuated:
力於民者盡，故民竭力以事其上；惟不自有其功，故民亦忘帝力於何有也。是以民和而神降之福，海內稱極治焉。使仁不足以成民，則德馨不脩，神且吐之，國與民將何賴耶？是故君子先成民而後致力於神。

紹庭上下，陟降厥家。
馬千官
同考試官教諭梁批：成王體道之密，模寫殆盡，是深於《詩》者，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭朱批：義精句煉，讀之灑然。
考試官教授李批：詞㫖瑩徹。

隨在述先王之事，嗣王體道之勤見矣。蓋先王之事即道也，于庭于家而紹之，道其有不得者哉？成王朝廟，延訪羣臣作也。蓋曰：先王之治本於道，先王之道見于行。維予小子，方判渙之難就，而值多難之未堪，所以敷求先王者，可但已耶？誠以清明開一統之業，昭考所當上下以聽外治者，有庭也。朕今踐其位，既不能就其道矣，
translation_en:
…devoted their efforts completely to the people, so the people exhausted their strength in serving their superiors; only because they did not claim the merit as their own did the people likewise forget what the ruler's power even had to do with them. Therefore, the people were harmonious and the spirits sent down blessings upon them, and all within the seas acclaimed it as the pinnacle of good governance. If benevolence were insufficient to bring the people to completion, then the fragrant virtue would not be cultivated, the spirits would even spurn the offerings, and what would the state and the people have to rely upon? For this reason, the noble man first brings the people to completion and afterwards devotes his efforts to the spirits.

"Continuing at court above and below, ascending and descending in his house."
Ma Qianguan 馬千官
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Liang comments: King Cheng's meticulousness in embodying the Way is depicted almost to perfection. This is someone deeply versed in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing), and his essay should be recorded as a model.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Zhu comments: The meaning is refined and the phrasing polished; reading it is refreshing.
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Li comments: The diction and purport are crystal clear.

By following and continuing the affairs of the former king everywhere, the successor king's diligence in embodying the Way becomes evident. Indeed, the affairs of the former king are none other than the Way; by continuing them in the court and in the household, how could the Way fail to be attained? This was composed when King Cheng attended the ancestral temple and received his assembled ministers to seek their counsel. It is as if to say: The governance of the former king was rooted in the Way, and the Way of the former king was manifested in his actions. Now I, the little child, just as what is scattered and dispersed is difficult to bring together and at a time when many hardships are more than I can bear—how could my广泛 seeking of the former king's example simply cease? Truly, in founding the enterprise of great unification through pure brightness, the place where my illustrious father went above and below [?] to attend to external governance was the court. Now that I occupy his position, since I am not yet able to achieve his Way…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而可無紹于此乎貽謀垂燕翼之規昭考所甞
陟降以正內治者有家也朕今承其家旣不能
就其道矣而可無紹于此乎于是本國典之宜
昭而不愆不忘求副承辟之重守家法之明備
而以似以續克盡纘服之心一上一下頒紀法
于朝廷者憲章具在也吾其講求先王之治迹
而端冕凝旒之際一周旋而不敢忘焉一陟一
降垂彞範于宫壼者典則具存也吾其彷彿先
王之身敎而宵衣旰食之圖一歩趨而不敢違
===
===
焉雖執競之德用爲經綸之本者不能窺其微
矣卽其所以正百官正萬民者而求之庶幾道
同于繼治不至悠遠而難及耳羣臣皆有對揚
王庭之忠者將何以助我乎雖敬勝之衷用爲
正始之原者不能探其蘊矣卽其所以脩于身
齊于家者而求之庶幾道顯于繩武不至判渙
而難合耳羣臣咸有克定厥家之責者將何以
益我乎夫道不可見則述諸事事有可紹則藉
其休成王之體道勤而咨訪至矣其纘先烈而
