punctuated: 而可無紹于此乎？貽謀垂燕翼之規，昭考所甞陟降以正內治者，有家也；朕今承其家，旣不能就其道矣，而可無紹于此乎？于是本國典之宜昭，而不愆不忘，求副承辟之重；守家法之明備，而以似以續，克盡纘服之心。一上一下，頒紀法于朝廷者，憲章具在也，吾其講求先王之治迹，而端冕凝旒之際，一周旋而不敢忘焉；一陟一降，垂彞範于宫壼者，典則具存也，吾其彷彿先王之身敎，而宵衣旰食之圖，一歩趨而不敢違焉。雖執競之德用爲經綸之本者，不能窺其微矣，卽其所以正百官、正萬民者而求之，庶幾道同于繼治，不至悠遠而難及耳。羣臣皆有對揚王庭之忠者，將何以助我乎？雖敬勝之衷用爲正始之原者，不能探其蘊矣，卽其所以脩于身、齊于家者而求之，庶幾道顯于繩武，不至判渙而難合耳。羣臣咸有克定厥家之責者，將何以益我乎？夫道不可見，則述諸事；事有可紹，則藉其休。成王之體道勤而咨訪至矣，其纘先烈而
translation_en:
…yet how can I fail to carry on his work here? And by bequeathing counsels to hand down a plan for the comfort and protection of his descendants, that wherein my glorious late father used to ascend and descend to rectify the internal governance is the royal household. Now that I have inherited his household, since I am already unable to attain his Way, how can I fail to carry on his work here?

Thereupon, grounding myself in the state statutes that ought to be made bright, without erring and without forgetting, I seek to live up to the weighty responsibility of succeeding to the sovereign's rule; guarding the clear and complete family laws, by resembling him and continuing after him, I am able to fulfill my heart's devotion to carrying on his great undertaking. In every movement up and down, as he promulgated discipline and laws in the royal court, the constitutional models are all present; I shall carefully study the traces of the former king's governance, and when wearing the ceremonial cap with its hanging pendants, in every turn and movement I shall not dare to forget them. In every ascent and descent, as he handed down constant norms within the palace quarters, the canons and rules are all preserved; I shall strive to emulate the former king's personal instruction, and in my plans made while dressing before dawn and eating after dusk, in every step and stride I shall not dare to violate them.

Even if I cannot fathom the subtlety of that resolute and vigorous virtue which served as the foundation of his statecraft, if I seek it right in that whereby he rectified the hundred officials and rectified the myriad people, then perhaps my Way will be one with his in continuing the governance, and it will not be so distant as to be unreachable. All you ministers possess the loyalty to respond to and extol the royal court—how will you assist me? Even if I cannot plumb the depths of that reverent and self-mastering heart which served as the source of his rectifying the beginnings, if I seek it right in that whereby he cultivated his person and regulated his household, then perhaps the Way will be made manifest in following his footsteps, and it will not be so scattered and dispersed as to be impossible to unite. All you ministers share the responsibility of being able to settle the royal household—how will you benefit me?

Now, when the Way cannot be seen, one follows it in deeds; when deeds can be carried on, one relies upon their blessings. King Cheng's embodiment of the Way was diligent, and his consultation and inquiry were utmost! That he carried on the former achievements and…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
保鴻業者厥有由哉抑世德作求子道也虛已
求言君道也有成王之訪落而後有周召之弼
違有周召之弼違而後有鳧鷖之治化日就月
將緝熈典學其覲光而揚烈也有自來矣此固
萬世守文者之法
春秋
三月公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男
曹伯盟于牡丘遂次于匡公孫敖
帥師及諸侯之大夫救徐僖公十有五
===
年六月公會單子晉侯宋公衛侯鄭伯
莒子邾子齊世子光巳未同盟于雞澤
陳侯使袁僑如會戊寅叔孫豹及
諸侯之大夫及陳袁僑盟襄公三年
馬中化
同考試官教諭王批春秋之義重於謹權故溴
梁不得與牡丘雞澤例書也是作得之宜錄以
式
考試官教諭朱批詞義嚴整
punctuated:
保鴻業者，厥有由哉！抑世德作求，子道也；虛已求言，君道也。有成王之《訪落》，而後有周、召之弼違；有周、召之弼違，而後有《鳧鷖》之治化。日就月將，緝熈典學，其覲光而揚烈也有自來矣。此固萬世守文者之法。

《春秋》
「三月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯，盟于牡丘，遂次于匡。公孫敖帥師及諸侯之大夫救徐。」（僖公十有五年）「六月，公會單子、晉侯、宋公、衛公、鄭伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光。巳未，同盟于雞澤。陳侯使袁僑如會。戊寅，叔孫豹及諸侯之大夫及陳袁僑盟。」（襄公三年）
馬中化
同考試官教諭王批：《春秋》之義，重於謹權，故溴梁不得與牡丘、雞澤例書也。是作得之，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭朱批：詞義嚴整。
translation_en:
… preserve the great enterprise indeed had its reasons! Furthermore, seeking to emulate the ancestral virtues of generations is the way of a filial son; humbling oneself to seek counsel is the way of a ruler. Only because there was King Cheng's consultation at the start of his reign ("Fangluo" 訪落) was there the corrective assistance of the Dukes of Zhou and Shao; and only because there was the corrective assistance of the Dukes of Zhou and Shao was there the transformative governance celebrated in "Wild Ducks and Widgeons" ("Fuyi" 鳧鷖). With daily accomplishment and monthly progress, and continuing the radiant devotion to classical learning, his manifesting the glory and exalting the achievements of his predecessors truly had its origin. This is assuredly the model for ten thousand generations of rulers who maintain the civil order.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In the third month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao, and made a covenant at Muqiu; thereupon they halted at Kuang. Gongsun Ao led a force and, together with the great officers of the feudal lords, went to relieve Xu." (Fifteenth year of Duke Xi) "In the sixth month, the Duke met with Viscount Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Duke of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and Guang, Heir Apparent of Qi. On the jisi [jiwei] day, they made a common covenant at Jize. The Marquis of Chen sent Yuan Qiao to come to the meeting. On the wuyin day, Shusun Bao, together with the great officers of the feudal lords and Yuan Qiao of Chen, made a covenant." (Third year of Duke Xiang)

By Ma Zhonghua 馬中化.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Wang: The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals places great weight on carefully guarding authority; therefore, the covenant at XiuLiang could not be recorded in the same manner as those at Muqiu and Jize. This composition grasps this point and ought to be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhu: The diction and meaning are rigorous and well-ordered.

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授李批跌宕不羣
春秋紀兵信而名有所繫見權之統于上也夫
權不可以下移也牡丘雞澤之役而皆統於諸
侯焉聖人繫之以名宜哉且禮樂征伐人君之
大權也權以統分分以辨名名以守禮諸侯保
有其國者恃此耳觀於桓悼之事而溴梁之盟
抑何戾哉牡丘之會齊桓以救徐合而諸侯同
次於匡矣乃率師以往救者則公孫敖與諸大
夫也聖人書曰諸侯之大夫者何蓋救灾卹患
===
征伐之權係焉次而救桓其有怠心乎然創伯
之君英明之烈尚存而七國從之以遏楚鋒以
紓徐困命由諸侯制也則夫仗鉞臨戎以為同
惡之恤者大夫特承命以從事耳孰敢奸大權
以徼寵耶經故繫以諸侯見救徐之大夫猶統
於牡丘之諸侯也雞澤之會晋悼為懼楚合而
諸侯業已同盟矣乃許成以盟陳者則叔孫豹
與諸大夫也聖人書曰諸侯之大夫者何蓋講
信脩睦禮樂之權係焉恊而盟悼其有戒心乎
punctuated:
考試官敎授李批：跌宕不羣。

《春秋》紀兵信而名有所繫，見權之統于上也。夫權不可以下移也，牡丘、雞澤之役，而皆統於諸侯焉，聖人繫之以名，宜哉！且禮樂征伐，人君之大權也。權以統分，分以辨名，名以守禮，諸侯保有其國者，恃此耳。觀於桓、悼之事，而溴梁之盟抑何戾哉！牡丘之會，齊桓以救徐合，而諸侯同次於匡矣；乃率師以往救者，則公孫敖與諸大夫也。聖人書曰「諸侯之大夫」者，何？蓋救灾卹患，征伐之權係焉。次而救，桓其有怠心乎？然創伯之君，英明之烈尚存，而七國從之，以遏楚鋒，以紓徐困，命由諸侯制也。則夫仗鉞臨戎，以為同惡之恤者，大夫特承命以從事耳，孰敢奸大權以徼寵耶？《經》故繫以「諸侯」，見救徐之大夫猶統於牡丘之諸侯也。雞澤之會，晋悼為懼楚合，而諸侯業已同盟矣；乃許成以盟陳者，則叔孫豹與諸大夫也。聖人書曰「諸侯之大夫」者，何？蓋講信脩睦，禮樂之權係焉。恊而盟，悼其有戒心乎？
translation_en:
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Li's comment: Bold, free-flowing, and peerless.

When the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records military actions and interstate pledges of good faith, its designations are explicitly subordinated to show that authority is unified at the top. Now, authority must never shift downward. In the campaigns of Muqiu and Jize, everything remained under the control of the feudal lords; how fitting it was that the Sage subordinated the designations to them! Moreover, rites, music, and punitive expeditions are the great prerogatives of the ruler. Authority governs hierarchical status, status distinguishes designations, and designations preserve ritual propriety—it is solely upon this that the feudal lords rely to preserve their states. When we look at the affairs of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Dao of Jin, how perverse by contrast was the covenant at Xiuliang! At the meeting of Muqiu, Duke Huan of Qi assembled the states to rescue Xu, and the feudal lords halted together at Kuang; yet those who actually led the troops forward to the rescue were Gongsun Ao and the various grand masters. Why did the Sage write "the grand masters of the feudal lords"? Because relieving disaster and succoring distress are matters in which the authority over punitive expeditions is bound up. By halting first and only then sending relief, did Duke Huan perhaps harbor a slackening of resolve? Even so, as the ruler who founded the霸 (hegemony), his heroic and brilliant vigor still endured, and seven states followed him to check the sharp advance of Chu and relieve the plight of Xu—the commands were formulated by the feudal lords. Thus, ingrasping the battle-axe and going to the front to succor a fellow state against a common enemy, the grand masters were merely receiving commands to carry out the affair; who among them would dare usurp supreme authority to court favor? The Classic therefore subordinated them to "the feudal lords," showing that the grand masters who rescued Xu were still controlled by the feudal lords at Muqiu. At the meeting of Jize, Duke Dao of Jin assembled the states out of fear of Chu, and the feudal lords had already sworn a covenant together; yet those who granted peace and swore a covenant with Chen were Shusun Bao and the various grand masters. Why did the Sage write "the grand masters of the feudal lords"? Because cultivating good faith and promoting harmony are matters in which the authority over rites and music is bound up. By uniting and swearing a covenant, did Duke Dao perhaps harbor a cautious apprehension?…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
然復伯之君剛明之氣方揚而八國從之以伐
楚謀以通吳好令自諸侯出也則夫刑牲歃血
以爲明神之要者大夫特奉令以共讀耳孰敢
竊大權以私交耶經亦繫以諸侯見盟陳之大
夫猶統於雞澤之諸侯也若夫溴梁之會荀偃
怒而高厚貳列侯在而諸臣盟君若贅旒大夫
張矣宜春秋特書大夫以示謹禮之意歟雖然
事常積於至微謀多忽於未兆徐之救親往可
也而命大夫袁僑之至無盟可也而命大夫則
===
溴梁專盟謂非馴致之漸乎要之司馬司盟天
子之權出于諸侯罪也桓悼伯功去王事遠矣
於晉平又何尤焉此聖人作經必嚴王伯之辨
八月晉荀吳帥師滅陸渾之戎〔昭公十有七年〕
蔣守迪
同考試官敎諭王 批 遷戎於內地晉與有責荀
吳滅之僅足以贖故春秋無褒貶耳是作能明
書法錄之
punctuated:
然復伯之君，剛明之氣方揚，而八國從之，以伐楚謀，以通吳好，令自諸侯出也。則夫刑牲歃血，以爲明神之要者，大夫特奉令以共讀耳，孰敢竊大權以私交耶？經亦繫以諸侯，見盟陳之大夫猶統於雞澤之諸侯也。若夫溴梁之會，荀偃怒而高厚貳，列侯在而諸臣盟，君若贅旒，大夫張矣，宜《春秋》特書大夫，以示謹禮之意歟！雖然，事常積於至微，謀多忽於未兆。徐之救，親往可也，而命大夫；袁僑之至，無盟可也，而命大夫。則溴梁專盟，謂非馴致之漸乎？要之，司馬、司盟，天子之權，出于諸侯，罪也。桓、悼伯功，去王事遠矣，於晉平又何尤焉？此聖人作經，必嚴王伯之辨。
八月，晉荀吳帥師滅陸渾之戎。〔昭公十有七年〕
蔣守迪
同考試官敎諭王批：遷戎於內地，晉與有責。荀吳滅之，僅足以贖，故《春秋》無褒貶耳。是作能明書法，錄之。
translation_en:
Yet for the ruler who was restoring the hegemony, his resolute and clear-sighted spirit was just rising, and eight states followed him to thwart Chu’s schemes and establish friendly relations with Wu; orders thus issued from the feudal lords. Therefore, as for slaughtering the sacrificial victim and smearing its blood on the lips to form a covenant before the bright spirits, the grandees were merely obeying orders to recite the oath together—who would dare usurp great authority to enter into private dealings? Thus the Classic also attaches "the feudal lords" to them, showing that the grandees who covenanted with Chen were still subordinate to the feudal lords at Jize. As for the meeting atouliang (Xiuliang), Xun Yan was enraged and Gao Hou was duplicitous; the feudal lords were present, yet their ministers made the covenant. The rulers were like useless appendages, and the grandees had grown arrogant! Is it not fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) specially wrote "the grandees" to show the intent of strictly guarding ritual propriety? Even so, affairs always accumulate from the most minute beginnings, and plans are often neglected before signs appear. For the relief of Xu, going in person would have been proper, yet grandees were commanded to go; when Yuan Qiao arrived, having no covenant would have been proper, yet grandees were commanded to make one. Can the unauthorized covenant at Xiuliang, then, be said not to have been the gradual result of this progression? In sum, the offices of the Minister of War (Sima) and the Director of Covenants (Simeng) belonged to the authority of the Son of Heaven; for them to issue from the feudal lords was already a transgression. The hegemonic achievements of Dukes Huan and Dao were already far removed from true kingly governance—what further blame can be laid upon Duke Ping of Jin? This is why when the Sage composed the Classic, he strictly distinguished between the Kingly Way and the Hegemonic Way.

"In the eighth month, Xun Wu of Jin led a force and extinguished the Rong of Luhun." [Seventeenth year of Duke Zhao]

Jiang Shoudi

Comment (pi) by Associate Examiner and Instructor (Jiaoyu) Wang: For relocating the Rong into the interior, Jin shared the responsibility. Xun Wu's extinguishing of them was barely enough to atone for the fault, and therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals offers neither praise nor blame. This composition is able to elucidate the principles of historiography; let it be recorded.

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭朱批辭達氣昌
考試官教授李批格嚴語勁
春秋紀伯臣靖華之兵而平詞以示義焉夫夷
不可以亂華也荀吳於陸渾而滅之近乎義矣
春秋所以無貶與且陸渾之戎睦於楚而爲中
國患久矣滅之者晉荀吳也斯與潞氏甲氏之
滅等耳春秋舉其名氏異於林父士會之書何
哉蓋以洛邑爲天地之中帝王所自立也固非
裔夷之可窺王畿爲都會之區臣民所歸往也
===
亦非醜類所可雜維兹陸渾本以允姓之戎徙
居伊雒之地夷夏大防蕩然潰矣有安攘之慮
者固宜滅此而後朝食也何幸晉之有是舉耶
因其貳楚而肆伐以兵既得夫執言之利數其
亂華而盡驅其族庶幾乎敵愾之師屠蒯將命
蓄謀若甚秘也然志在膺戎即有棘津之涉而
非以爲詐矣祭史用牲聲威若甚震也然事在
舉義即有甘鹿之逐而非以爲暴矣容容之猛
萇弘料之膚公奏於雒社華夏之氣以紓赫赫
punctuated:
考試官教諭朱批：辭達氣昌。
考試官教授李批：格嚴語勁。
《春秋》紀伯臣靖華之兵，而平詞以示義焉。夫夷不可以亂華也，荀吳於陸渾而滅之，近乎義矣，《春秋》所以無貶與！且陸渾之戎睦於楚，而爲中國患久矣。滅之者，晉荀吳也，斯與潞氏、甲氏之滅等耳。《春秋》舉其名氏，異於林父、士會之書，何哉？蓋以洛邑爲天地之中，帝王所自立也，固非裔夷之可窺；王畿爲都會之區，臣民所歸往也，亦非醜類所可雜。維兹陸渾，本以允姓之戎，徙居伊、雒之地，夷夏大防蕩然潰矣。有安攘之慮者，固宜滅此而後朝食也，何幸晉之有是舉耶！因其貳楚而肆伐以兵，既得夫執言之利；數其亂華而盡驅其族，庶幾乎敵愾之師。屠蒯將命，蓄謀若甚秘也，然志在膺戎，即有棘津之涉，而非以爲詐矣。祭史用牲，聲威若甚震也，然事在舉義，即有甘鹿之逐，而非以爲暴矣。容容之猛，萇弘料之，膚公奏於雒社，華夏之氣以紓，赫赫
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Zhu's comment: The diction is lucid and the vigor flourishing.
Examiner and Professor Li's comment: The structure is rigorous and the phrasing forceful.

The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records the campaign by which a minister of the Hegemon pacified the Chinese heartland, using neutral wording to manifest righteousness. Now, barbarians must not be permitted to throw China into disorder. That Xun Wu 荀吳 destroyed the Rong at Luhun 陸渾 approaches righteousness; is this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals withholds censure?

Moreover, the Rong of Luhun were on friendly terms with Chu 楚 and had long been a menace to the Central States. The one who destroyed them was Xun Wu of Jin 晉—an act comparable to the destruction of the Lushi 潞氏 and Jiashi 甲氏 tribes. Why then does the Spring and Autumn Annals record his clan and personal name, differing from the way it records Xun Linfu 荀林父 and Shi Hui 士會? It is because Luoyi 洛邑 is the center of Heaven and Earth, the place where emperors and kings establish themselves; it is certainly not a place for frontier barbarians to spy upon. The royal domain is the metropolitan region toward which subjects and people turn in allegiance; it is likewise not a place where vile kind may intermingle. Yet these Luhun, originally Rong of the Yun 允 surname, were relocated to dwell in the region of the Yi 伊 and Luo 雒 rivers, whereby the great barrier between barbarian and Chinese utterly collapsed. Anyone concerned with pacifying the interior and repelling the exterior ought surely to destroy them before eating breakfast! How fortunate that Jin undertook this action!

Seizing upon their duplicity with Chu to launch a punitive expedition by force of arms, Jin gained the advantage of a justifiable pretext; denouncing them for throwing China into disorder and driving out their entire tribe, this came close to being an army animated by shared righteous indignation against the king's enemy. Tu Kuai 屠蒯 conveyed the mission, and the plot laid seemed deeply secretive; yet because the intent was to smite the Rong, even though there was the crossing at Jijin 棘津, it was not deemed deceitful. The sacrificial scribe employed victims, and the display of might seemed deeply awe-inspiring; yet because the affair was a righteous rising, even though there was the pursuit at Ganlu 甘鹿, it was not deemed tyrannical. Their unruly ferocity was foreseen by Chang Hong 萇弘; great merit was reported at the altar of the Luo, the spirit of China was thereby relieved, and majestic…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
宗周不將胥此而廓清乎授戎之夢宣子徵之
俘馘獻於文宫腥穢之風以殄翼翼京邑不將
由是而底定乎此荀吳之師雖未足語夫柔服
之道而視彼淫逞以圖彊覇者則有間矣故春
秋不以罪林父士會者罪之也獨舉其名氏而
紀以平詞纔免於貶耳亦非以為褒也滅戎而
猶無褒則虚內事外者在所禁矣聖人謹於用
兵固如此哉雖然荒服之制裁於周官膺懲之
訓垂於魯頌戎何人也而可使入中國邇王都
===
哉被髮野祭辛有已有隱憂晉為大國乃不能
脩尊奬攘卻之職而與秦共遷之始謀不臧厲
階由作向非荀吳之師其不胥而為夷者幾希
吁後之議徙戎者無亦得於春秋之旨乎
禮記
天子乃命將帥選士厲兵簡練桀俊專任
有功以征不義詰誅暴慢以明好惡順
彼遠方
張正蒙
punctuated:
宗周，不將胥此而廓清乎？授戎之夢，宣子徵之。俘馘獻於文宫，腥穢之風以殄；翼翼京邑，不將由是而底定乎？此荀吳之師，雖未足語夫柔服之道，而視彼淫逞以圖彊覇者，則有間矣。故《春秋》不以罪林父、士會者罪之也。獨舉其名氏而紀以平詞，纔免於貶耳，亦非以為褒也。滅戎而猶無褒，則虚內事外者在所禁矣。聖人謹於用兵，固如此哉！雖然，荒服之制，裁於《周官》；膺懲之訓，垂於《魯頌》。戎何人也，而可使入中國、邇王都哉？被髮野祭，辛有已有隱憂；晉為大國，乃不能脩尊奬攘卻之職，而與秦共遷之。始謀不臧，厲階由作。向非荀吳之師，其不胥而為夷者幾希！吁！後之議徙戎者，無亦得於《春秋》之旨乎！
《禮記》
「天子乃命將帥，選士厲兵，簡練桀俊，專任有功，以征不義，詰誅暴慢，以明好惡，順彼遠方。」
張正蒙
translation_en:
… ancestral Zhou—would it not through this be swept clear? The dream of the Rong being delivered up was verified by Xuanzi (Xun Yin 荀寅 /韓起 Han Qi, Xuanzi of Jin). When the captives and severed ears were presented at the Temple of Duke Wen (Wengong 文宮), the foul and defiling customs were eradicated; would not the reverent royal capital thereby be brought to stability? Thus, although this campaign of Xun Wu 荀吳 is not worthy of being spoken of in terms of the Way of pacifying through gentleness, compared to those who indulged in reckless aggression to scheme for hegemony by force, there is indeed a difference. Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) does not condemn him as it condemned Linfu 林父 (Xun Linfu 荀林父) and Shi Hui 士會. Yet by singly recording his personal and clan names and chronicling the event in plain terms, it merely spares him from censure, and does not take it as praise either. If even annihilating the Rong receives no praise, then depleting the interior to pursue external affairs is clearly among the things forbidden. How cautious indeed was the Sage in the use of arms! Even so, the system of the荒服 (wilderness dependency zone, huangfu) was laid down in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), and the precept of smiting and chastising was handed down in the Sacrificial Odes of Lu (Lusong). What sort of people were the Rong, that they should be allowed to enter the Central States and draw near to the royal capital? Seeing someone with unbound hair sacrificing in the wilds, Xin You 辛有 already harbored secret sorrow; yet Jin, being a great state, was unable to fulfill its duty of honoring and upholding the royal house and repelling the barbarians, and instead joined with Qin in relocating them there. Because the initial counsel was unsound, the steps to disaster were thereby created. Had it not been for the army of Xun Wu, how close all would have come to sinking into barbarism together! Alas! Did not those of later times who argued for relocating the Rong (such as Jiang Tong 江統) also grasp this from the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals?

Record of Rites (Liji)

"The Son of Heaven then commands the generals and commanders to select warriors and sharpen weapons, to choose and train men of outstanding talent, and to give exclusive responsibility to those of proven merit, in order to march against the unrighteous, to interrogate and punish the violent and insolent, thereby making clear what is loved and what is hated, and bringing compliance to those in distant quarters."

Zhang Zhengmeng 張正蒙

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭許批題意重在征不義以明惡
此作得之宜冠多士
考試官教諭朱批詞雅瑩而意聯絡可以式
矣
考試官教授李批以古調發揮征令讀之雄
心
王者命將奮武而因以服乎遠焉夫遠方觀化
者也王者欲明好惡以順之得不命將而示之
武歟且聖王所以昭大順于四方者在以義正
===
天下而已故時維孟秋天地之義氣始顯王者
之義師由興乃于是有將帥之命焉以士則選
之而材官之悉具以兵則屬之而戎器之是除
桀俊之士簡練以先乎衆有功之將推誠以任
之專夫卒服習器用利而又簡能任功若此者
凡以為師出計也而其稱斯師也則謂之何亦
曰征不義而已明王之世惟民從義固無有下
殘上慢以干我天誅者一或有之不義孰甚焉
張薄伐之威而聲其罪以致討整徂征之旅而
punctuated:
同考試官教諭許批：題意重在「征不義」以「明惡」，此作得之，宜冠多士。
考試官教諭朱批：詞雅瑩而意聯絡，可以式矣。
考試官教授李批：以古調發揮征令，讀之雄心。

王者命將奮武，而因以服乎遠焉。夫遠方，觀化者也；王者欲明好惡以順之，得不命將而示之武歟？且聖王所以昭大順于四方者，在以義正天下而已。故時維孟秋，天地之義氣始顯，王者之義師由興，乃于是有將帥之命焉。以士則選之，而材官之悉具；以兵則屬之，而戎器之是除。桀俊之士，簡練以先乎衆；有功之將，推誠以任之專。夫卒服習，器用利，而又簡能任功若此者，凡以為師出計也。而其稱斯師也，則謂之何？亦曰「征不義」而已。明王之世，惟民從義，固無有下殘上慢以干我天誅者；一或有之，不義孰甚焉？張薄伐之威，而聲其罪以致討；整徂征之旅，而
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Instructor Xu's comment: The meaning of the topic lays stress on "punishing the unrighteous" in order to "make clear what is hated." This composition grasps it and deserves to top the multitude of scholars.
Examiner and Instructor Zhu's comment: The diction is refined and limpid while the ideas are well-connected; it can serve as a model.
Examiner and Instructor Li's comment: Expounding the command for a punitive expedition in an ancient style—reading it stirs a heroic spirit.

The true king commands his generals to rouse martial vigor, and thereby brings distant lands into submission. Now, those in distant regions are observers of transformative influence; when the true king wishes to make clear what he likes and hates so as to bring them into obedience, how could he not command his generals and display martial might to them? Moreover, the means by which the sage king manifests great obedience throughout the four quarters lies simply in rectifying the realm with righteousness. Therefore, when the season is the first month of autumn, the righteous vital energy of Heaven and Earth begins to manifest, and the righteous army of the true king is thereby raised; thereupon, the command is given to the generals and commanders. As for the troops, he selects them so that skilled soldiers are all complete; as for the weapons, he Sharpens [? 屬 for 厲] them so that the implements of war are put in order. Men of outstanding talent are chosen and trained to lead the multitude; generals of proven merit are extended sincere trust and given exclusive responsibility. Now, that the soldiers are accustomed to service, the implements and equipment are sharp, and moreover the capable are selected and the meritorious are entrusted in such a manner—all this is done as preparation for sending forth the army. And in naming this army, what is it called? It is simply called "punishing the unrighteous." In the age of an enlightened king, the people follow only righteousness, and naturally there are none who brutalize those below or are insolent toward those above so as to provoke our heavenly punishment; yet if by chance there is even one such person, what unrighteousness could be greater than this? Extending the majesty of a punitive strike, he proclaims their crimes to carry out the chastisement; arraying the battalions of the advancing expedition, he…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
正其罪以脩刑是誅暴也非黷武也蓋不義之
暴天下有同惡焉王者與天下同其惡故爲天
下除其殘所惡在此所好在彼而遠方之心志
于是乎一矣是誅慢也非勤兵也蓋不義之慢
斯世有公惡焉王者與斯世公其惡故爲斯世
除其害即所用惡知所用好而遠方之觀聽于
是乎新矣威振殊俗而畏威以効順者翕如也
孰敢有犯所惡而爲不義者乎德洽窮荒而懷
德以即敘者忻如也孰有違所好而不慕義者
===
乎夫禁虐戢亂武之善經服遠安民王之善政
先王之因時命將也有以夫於乎兵者聖人不
得已而用之也天無所不覆王者體天之心亦
無所不愛迨暴慢之亂作雖聖人有不能自遂
其愛而征伐興焉卒之好惡明而遠方自服則
仁覆之治又無不曁是義也乃所以成其仁也
聖人豈樂于觀兵哉故天道先春而後秋王道
先仁而後義
樂者敦和率神而從天禮者別宜居鬼而
punctuated:
正其罪以脩刑，是誅暴也，非黷武也。蓋不義之暴，天下有同惡焉。王者與天下同其惡，故爲天下除其殘。所惡在此，所好在彼，而遠方之心志于是乎一矣。是誅慢也，非勤兵也。蓋不義之慢，斯世有公惡焉。王者與斯世公其惡，故爲斯世除其害。即所用惡，知所用好，而遠方之觀聽于是乎新矣。威振殊俗，而畏威以効順者翕如也，孰敢有犯所惡而爲不義者乎？德洽窮荒，而懷德以即敘者忻如也，孰有違所好而不慕義者乎？夫禁虐戢亂，武之善經；服遠安民，王之善政。先王之因時命將也，有以夫！於乎！兵者，聖人不得已而用之也。天無所不覆，王者體天之心，亦無所不愛。迨暴慢之亂作，雖聖人有不能自遂其愛，而征伐興焉。卒之好惡明而遠方自服，則仁覆之治又無不曁。是義也，乃所以成其仁也。聖人豈樂于觀兵哉？故天道先春而後秋，王道先仁而後義。
樂者，敦和率神而從天；禮者，別宜居鬼而
translation_en:
… rectify their crimes in order to carry out punishment—this is executing the violent, not wantonly engaging in warfare. For toward the violence of unrighteousness, all under Heaven share a common hatred. The true king shares his hatred with all under Heaven, and therefore eliminates the cruel on behalf of all under Heaven. When what is hated lies here and what is loved lies there, the minds and wills of distant regions are thereby unified. This is executing the insolent, not exhausting the troops. For toward the insolence of unrighteousness, this age holds a public hatred. The true king shares this public hatred with the age, and therefore eliminates harm on behalf of this age. From that to which hatred is applied, people know that to which love is applied, and the sights and hearings of distant regions are thereby renewed. When awe shakes foreign customs, those who fear his awe and offer submission gather harmoniously; who would dare offend against what he hates and commit unrighteousness? When virtue saturates the farthest wilds, those who cherish his virtue and come to take their proper place in the order rejoice; who would go against what he loves and fail to admire righteousness? Now, prohibiting cruelty and quelling disorder are the good principles of martial power; bringing distant peoples to submission and giving peace to the people are the good governance of a true king. That the former kings appointed generals in accordance with the season indeed had its reason! Alas! Weapons are instruments that the sage uses only when he has no alternative. Heaven shelters everything without exception; the true king embodies the heart of Heaven and likewise loves everything without exception. Yet when disorders of violence and insolence arise, even a sage cannot fulfill his love on his own, and so punitive expeditions are launched. In the end, when loves and hatreds are made clear and distant regions submit of their own accord, then the governance of benevolent shelter once again reaches everywhere. This righteousness is precisely the means by which his benevolence is brought to completion. How could the sage take pleasure in displaying military might? Therefore, the Way of Heaven puts spring first and autumn after; the Way of the True King puts benevolence first and righteousness after.

Music deepens harmony, leads the spirits, and follows Heaven; ritual distinguishes what is fitting, settles the ghosts, and…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
從地故聖人作樂以應天制禮以配地
禮樂明備天地官矣
丘九疇
同考試官教諭許批能發明禮樂之用是知禮
樂之本者
考試官教諭朱批瑩徹可錄
考試官教授李批精健
觀禮樂合造化之用而聖人因有以成其能也
蓋禮樂有自然之功用也聖人盡制作以官天
===
地固其所哉且夫論禮樂者不惟遡其效法之
原尤當要其成功之極故周流同化顯之爲作
長之仁是天地之和也而斯樂之成有以敦厚
之然和非他也卽陽之伸爲神而天由之以生
物者也樂惟敦和有不達其氣之伸而與天竝
運乎高下散殊凝之爲斂藏之義是天地之宜
也而斯禮之成有以區別之然宜非他也卽陰
之屈爲鬼而地由之以成物者也禮惟別宜有
不斂其氣之屈而與地同流乎夫禮樂之用合
punctuated:
從地。故聖人作樂以應天，制禮以配地。禮樂明備，天地官矣。」
丘九疇
同考試官教諭許批：能發明禮樂之用，是知禮樂之本者。
考試官教諭朱批：瑩徹，可錄。
考試官教授李批：精健。
觀禮樂合造化之用，而聖人因有以成其能也。蓋禮樂有自然之功用也，聖人盡制作以官天地，固其所哉！且夫論禮樂者，不惟遡其效法之原，尤當要其成功之極。故周流同化，顯之爲作長之仁，是天地之和也，而斯樂之成有以敦厚之。然和非他也，卽陽之伸爲神，而天由之以生物者也。樂惟敦和，有不達其氣之伸，而與天竝運乎？高下散殊，凝之爲斂藏之義，是天地之宜也，而斯禮之成有以區別之。然宜非他也，卽陰之屈爲鬼，而地由之以成物者也。禮惟別宜，有不斂其氣之屈，而與地同流乎？夫禮樂之用合
translation_en:
… conforms to Earth. Therefore, the sages created music to respond to Heaven and instituted ritual to match Earth. When ritual and music are clear and complete, Heaven and Earth fulfill their proper functions."

Qiu Jiuchou 丘九疇

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Xu 許 comments: Capable of elucidating the function of ritual and music; this is one who understands the fundamental basis of ritual and music.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Zhu 朱 comments: Lucid and penetrating; worthy of selection.
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Li 李 comments: Precise and vigorous.

When we observe how ritual and music accord with the operations of creative transformation, we see how the sages thereby brought their capacities to completion. Indeed, ritual and music possess a natural efficacy and function; that the sages exhausted their efforts in instituting and creating them so that Heaven and Earth fulfill their proper functions is truly a matter of course! Moreover, those who discuss ritual and music should not merely trace back the origin of what they model themselves upon, but must especially grasp the ultimate perfection of their accomplished work. Thus, circulating everywhere and harmonizing transformations, manifesting as the benevolence of origination and growth—this is the harmony of Heaven and Earth, and the completion of this music serves to thicken and enrich it. Yet harmony is nothing other than the expansion of yang becoming shen (expansive spirit), through which Heaven gives birth to all things. Since music thickens harmony, how could it fail to extend this expansion of vital energy and move in tandem with Heaven? High and low dispersed in their distinctness, coalescing as the righteousness of gathering and storing—this is the appropriateness of Heaven and Earth, and the completion of this ritual serves to differentiate and distinguish it. Yet appropriateness is nothing other than the contraction of yin becoming gui (contractive spirit), through which Earth brings all things to completion. Since ritual distinguishes appropriateness, how could it fail to gather in this contraction of vital energy and flow together with Earth? Now, the functions of ritual and music accord…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
乎造化如此聖人法其和而樂作焉以從天者
上應乎天而平中之雅若于乾知大始有幽賛
矣法其宜而禮制焉以從地者下配乎地而儀
則之陳若于坤作成物有默相矣是禮非強制
所以配地而至序之寓于經緯者何其明且備
也樂非徒作所以應天而太和之寓于播比者
何其明且備也制作善而敦和別宜之功顯則
天地位而氣覆形載之職全陽一噓而萬物以
作以長天得其所以為天也陰一吸而萬物以
===
斂以藏地得其所以為地也向微聖人應天之
樂配地之禮疇能致之哉吁禮樂之道大矣始
之者天地終之者聖人也夫聖人胡能以禮樂
官天地耶蓋通性命可與議禮樂推位育必本
之中和惟聖人達性命之原建中和之極所以
舉禮樂而天地為昭也儀文鍾律云乎任制作
者當思其本矣
第貳場
論
punctuated:
乎造化如此。聖人法其和而樂作焉，以從天者上應乎天，而平中之雅，若于乾知大始有幽賛矣；法其宜而禮制焉，以從地者下配乎地，而儀則之陳，若于坤作成物有默相矣。是禮非強制，所以配地，而至序之寓于經緯者，何其明且備也；樂非徒作，所以應天，而太和之寓于播比者，何其明且備也。制作善而敦和別宜之功顯，則天地位而氣覆形載之職全。陽一噓而萬物以作以長，天得其所以為天也；陰一吸而萬物以斂以藏，地得其所以為地也。向微聖人應天之樂、配地之禮，疇能致之哉？吁！禮樂之道大矣，始之者天地，終之者聖人也。夫聖人胡能以禮樂官天地耶？蓋通性命可與議禮樂，推位育必本之中和。惟聖人達性命之原，建中和之極，所以舉禮樂而天地為昭也。儀文鍾律云乎？任制作者當思其本矣。

第貳場
論
translation_en:
…with the creative transformations of nature is like this. The sages modeled themselves on its harmony and created music; by following Heaven they corresponded above with Heaven, and the elegance of equilibrium and centrality was as if secretly assisting Qian in knowing the great beginning. They modeled themselves on its appropriateness and instituted rites; by following Earth they matched below with Earth, and the setting forth of ceremonial rules was as if silently aiding Kun in bringing things to completion. Thus, rites are not forcibly instituted: they are that whereby one matches Earth, and how bright and complete is the utmost order lodged in their warp and woof! Music is not made in vain: it is that whereby one corresponds with Heaven, and how bright and complete is the supreme harmony lodged in its performance and arrangement! When the institutions and creations are good and the achievements of thickening harmony and distinguishing appropriateness are made manifest, then Heaven and Earth take their proper places and the functions of vital energy overarching and physical form supporting are complete. Yang breathes out once and the myriad things thereby arise and grow—Heaven attains that whereby it is Heaven. Yin breathes in once and the myriad things thereby contract and are stored away—Earth attains that whereby it is Earth. Had it not been for the sages' music that corresponds with Heaven and rites that match Earth, who could have brought this about?

Ah! Great indeed is the Way of rites and music! That which begins it is Heaven and Earth; he who completes it is the sage. Yet how is the sage able to govern the functions of Heaven and Earth by means of rites and music? It is because only when one comprehends human nature and heavenly decree can one discuss rites and music, and extending the establishment of order and the nurturing of things must be rooted in equilibrium and harmony. Only the sage penetrates the source of human nature and heavenly decree and establishes the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony; therefore, when he raises up rites and music, Heaven and Earth are made luminous. Is it merely a matter of ceremonial forms and pitch-pipes and bells? Those who bear the responsibility of instituting rites and creating music ought to reflect upon their fundamental root.

Second Session
Discourse

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
正心爲天下萬事之本
陳貴科
同考試官教諭梁批君心萬化之原是作援證
古今根極體要末歸本心學具見忠愛佳士也
考試官教諭朱批有議論有風骨
考試官教授李批雅渾正大
論曰治天下有幾焉人君欲致治于天下不可
不識其幾而圖之幾者何心也人君以一身寄
之巍巍之上爲天地民物之主庶務于我乎裁
===
决家國天下于我乎觀嚮百官萬民于我乎拱
手而待命六合之內孰非吾事也苟不得其所
謂幾者而握之而欲事事而爲之理將以彌綸
天地材官萬物總人羣而成治功也不亦勞且
艱哉人君知其然是故不求治于治而求治于
心蓋誠見夫此心正否理亂關焉是天下之大
幾也幾在我而化在天下有莫知所以然者是
天下之大順也握大幾成大順則身佚而事治
上可以帝中可以王是人主之大要也正心爲
punctuated:
正心爲天下萬事之本
陳貴科
同考試官教諭梁批：君心，萬化之原。是作援證古今，根極體要，末歸本心學，具見忠愛，佳士也。
考試官教諭朱批：有議論，有風骨。
考試官教授李批：雅渾正大。
論曰：治天下有幾焉，人君欲致治于天下，不可不識其幾而圖之。幾者何？心也。人君以一身寄之巍巍之上，爲天地民物之主，庶務于我乎裁决，家國天下于我乎觀嚮，百官萬民于我乎拱手而待命，六合之內，孰非吾事也？苟不得其所謂幾者而握之，而欲事事而爲之理，將以彌綸天地、材官萬物、總人羣而成治功也，不亦勞且艱哉！人君知其然，是故不求治于治，而求治于心。蓋誠見夫此心正否，理亂關焉，是天下之大幾也。幾在我而化在天下，有莫知所以然者，是天下之大順也。握大幾，成大順，則身佚而事治，上可以帝，中可以王，是人主之大要也。「正心爲…
translation_en:
"Rectifying the Mind Is the Foundation of the Myriad Affairs of the World"

Chen Guike 陳貴科

Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Liang 梁 comments: The ruler's mind is the source of the myriad transformations. This composition cites evidence from past and present, getting down to the fundamental essentials, and at the end brings it back to the learning of the mind—fully revealing his loyalty and affection. A fine scholar!

Examiner, County Director of Studies Zhu 朱 comments: Possesses substantive argument and strength of character.

Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Li 李 comments: Refined,渾 [well-rounded/profound], upright, and grand.

The discourse reads: In governing the world there is a pivotal spring. When a ruler wishes to bring about good governance in the world, he cannot fail to recognize its pivotal spring and attend to it. What is this pivotal spring? It is the mind. The ruler places his single person upon the lofty heights above as master of Heaven, Earth, the people, and all things. The multitude of affairs depend on him for decision; the family, the state, and the world look to him for direction; the hundred officials and the myriad people fold their hands before him and await his commands. Within the six directions of the universe, what is not his affair? If he does not grasp what is called the pivotal spring and hold fast to it, yet wishes to put every single affair in order one by one—intending thereby to encompass Heaven and Earth, employ the myriad things according to their capacities, bring together human society, and accomplish the work of governance—would that not be toilsome and difficult indeed! The ruler knows that this is so; therefore, he does not seek good governance in governance itself, but seeks good governance in the mind. For he truly sees that upon whether this mind is rectified or not hinges order and disorder: this is the great pivotal spring of the world. When the pivotal spring lies within oneself and transformation takes place throughout the world without anyone knowing how it comes to be so, this is the great natural compliance of the world. To grasp the great pivotal spring and achieve the great natural compliance so that one's person is at ease while affairs are well governed—whereby at the highest level one may become an August Emperor and at the middle level a True King—this is the great essential of the sovereign. "Rectifying the mind is…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天下萬事之本旨哉朱子之言其善于論治者
乎今夫人之一身耳聽目視手持足行四者之
不相借官也而心寔統之故心曰天君蘊之爲
性發之爲情而措之則爲事禮樂異制刑政異
施慶賞威罰異用斂之不盈一掬極之可以配
天地横四海皆是心也吾心之體廓然太公粹
然至正其初本如是而或失其體者物欲撓之
耳不觀諸水乎止錯勿動可燭鬚眉湛濁一淆
莫辨妍醜心亦若是矣故冥冥而行者見寢石
===
以爲伏虎見植木以爲後人也冥冥蔽其明也
醉者越百歩之溝以爲蹞歩之澮俯而出城門
以爲小之閨也湎亂其神也慾之撓心爲蔽爲
亂又有不可勝言者且人君尊居九重其權無
不可致凡天下之可喜可好雜然于吾前者皆
足以誘吾心而爲之蠱是故身安曲房口御五
齊命之曰損心之鴆毒耳極曼淫目備佳冶命
之曰伐心之斧斤佞幸當先宵人在側命之曰
賊心之蟊蠹人主之心關於天下甚重而攻之
punctuated: 天下萬事之本。」旨哉，朱子之言！其善于論治者乎！今夫人之一身，耳聽、目視、手持、足行，四者之不相借官也，而心寔統之，故心曰「天君」。蘊之爲性，發之爲情，而措之則爲事。禮樂異制，刑政異施，慶賞威罰異用，斂之不盈一掬，極之可以配天地、横四海，皆是心也。吾心之體，廓然太公，粹然至正，其初本如是；而或失其體者，物欲撓之耳。不觀諸水乎？止錯勿動，可燭鬚眉；湛濁一淆，莫辨妍醜，心亦若是矣。故冥冥而行者，見寢石以爲伏虎，見植木以爲後人也，冥冥蔽其明也；醉者越百歩之溝，以爲蹞歩之澮，俯而出城門，以爲小之閨也，湎亂其神也。慾之撓心，爲蔽爲亂，又有不可勝言者。且人君尊居九重，其權無不可致，凡天下之可喜可好，雜然于吾前者，皆足以誘吾心而爲之蠱。是故身安曲房，口御五齊，命之曰「損心之鴆毒」；耳極曼淫，目備佳冶，命之曰「伐心之斧斤」；佞幸當先，宵人在側，命之曰「賊心之蟊蠹」。人主之心，關於天下甚重，而攻之
translation_en: … the root of the myriad affairs of the world." How profound are the words of Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹)! Truly, he was adept at discussing governance! Now, in a person's single body, the ears hear, the eyes see, the hands grasp, and the feet walk. These four do not borrow one another's functions, yet the mind actually governs them all; therefore, the mind is called the "Heavenly Ruler." Stored within, it is human nature; expressed outwardly, it is emotion; and when put into practice, it becomes affairs. Rites and music have different institutions, punishments and administration have different applications, and rewards and penalties have different uses. Yet when gathered in, it does not fill a single handful; when extended to the utmost, it can match Heaven and Earth and span the Four Seas—all of this is the mind. The substance of our mind is vast and utterly impartial, pure and supremely rectified. In the beginning, it is originally like this; that it sometimes loses its substance is simply because material desires disturb it. Have you not observed water? When it rests still and unmoving, it can reflect one's beard and eyebrows; once clear and turbid are mixed together, one cannot distinguish beauty from ugliness. The mind is also like this. Thus, one who walks in the dark sees a lying stone and takes it for a crouching tiger, or sees a standing tree and takes it for a person following behind—because the darkness obscures his sight. A drunken man leaps over a ditch a hundred paces wide, taking it for a half-pace drain, or stoops to go out a city gate, taking it for a small side-door—because intoxication confuses his spirit. When desires disturb the mind, causing obscuration and confusion, the effects are even more beyond description. Moreover, the ruler of men dwells in the exalted Ninefold Palace, and there is nothing his power cannot obtain. All the delightful and pleasing things in the world that are arrayed mingled before him are enough to entice his mind and bewitch it. Therefore, when his body takes comfort in secluded chambers and his mouth partakes of the five kinds of wine, these are called "deadly poisons that harm the mind." When his ears indulge to the utmost in alluring and licentious sounds and his eyes are supplied with exquisite and seductive beauties, these are called "axes and hatchets that hew down the mind." When sycophants and favorites stand in the forefront and petty men are at his side, these are called "pests and wood-borers that ruin the mind." The mind of the ruler of men is of the utmost importance to the world, yet those that attack it …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者其衆又如此若遂聽其攻而不爲制至使四
肢百骸得以役吾心而吾心爲萬化之本原者
反洸洋儻蕩莫之持檢則庶務之所取裁者何
如家國天下之所觀嚮者何如百官萬民之所
拱手待命于我者何如而顧可以是不正之心
應之乎甚哉人君之不可不正其心也君心者
表也表直而景直表枉而景枉君心者槃也槃
圓而水圓槃方而水方故採山探淵所以爲富
也上好貨則臣下百吏乘是而興利于游于田
===
所以爲適也上好逸則臣下百吏乘是而偷窺
建章甘泉所以爲觀也上好土木則臣下百吏
乘是而恠侈入海登岱所以爲奇也上好長生
則臣下百吏乘是而誕謾闢疆服遠所以爲大
也上好黷武則臣下百吏乘是而喜功興利之
人出而民力殫矣偷窺之人出而百度隳矣恠
侈之人出而天下隨風靡矣誕謾之人出而天
下爭騖于怪矣喜功之人出而大荒窮塞之外
日多事矣其幾始于一心而其流弊乃應于天
punctuated: 者，其衆又如此。若遂聽其攻而不爲制，至使四肢百骸得以役吾心，而吾心爲萬化之本原者，反洸洋儻蕩，莫之持檢，則庶務之所取裁者何如？家國天下之所觀嚮者何如？百官萬民之所拱手待命于我者何如？而顧可以是不正之心應之乎？甚哉，人君之不可不正其心也！君心者，表也，表直而景直，表枉而景枉；君心者，槃也，槃圓而水圓，槃方而水方。故採山探淵，所以爲富也，上好貨，則臣下百吏乘是而興利；于游于田，所以爲適也，上好逸，則臣下百吏乘是而偷窺；建章、甘泉，所以爲觀也，上好土木，則臣下百吏乘是而恠侈；入海、登岱，所以爲奇也，上好長生，則臣下百吏乘是而誕謾；闢疆、服遠，所以爲大也，上好黷武，則臣下百吏乘是而喜功。興利之人出，而民力殫矣；偷窺之人出，而百度隳矣；恠侈之人出，而天下隨風靡矣；誕謾之人出，而天下爭騖于怪矣；喜功之人出，而大荒窮塞之外日多事矣。其幾始于一心，而其流弊乃應于天
translation_en: … [that which] assail it are moreover so numerous as this. If one simply lets them assail it without imposing restraint, to the point of allowing the four limbs and hundred bones to enslave one's mind—while one's mind, which is the fundamental source of all transformations, instead becomes boundless and unbridled, with nothing to hold it in check—then what will become of the myriad affairs that look to it for judgment? What will become of the state and the empire that look to it for direction? What will become of the hundred officials and the myriad people who fold their hands and await commands from us? And can one really respond to them with this unrectified mind? Imperative indeed is it that a ruler must rectify his mind! The ruler's mind is a gnomon: when the gnomon is straight, the shadow is straight; when the gnomon is crooked, the shadow is crooked. The ruler's mind is a basin: when the basin is round, the water is round; when the basin is square, the water is square. Therefore, mining the mountains and plumbing the depths are means to achieve wealth; if the ruler loves wealth, then his subjects and the hundred officials will take advantage of this to pursue profit. Roaming and hunting are means to achieve pleasure; if the ruler loves ease, then his subjects and the hundred officials will take advantage of this to shirk and scheme [?]. The Jianzhang and Ganquan palaces were built for spectacle; if the ruler loves construction projects, then his subjects and the hundred officials will take advantage of this to indulge in bizarre extravagance. Entering the sea and ascending Mount Tai were done in pursuit of the marvelous; if the ruler loves longevity, then his subjects and the hundred officials will take advantage of this to practice absurd deceptions. Expanding territory and subjugating distant lands are means to achieve greatness; if the ruler loves militarism, then his subjects and the hundred officials will take advantage of this to crave martial exploits. When men who pursue profit emerge, the strength of the people is exhausted; when men who shirk and scheme emerge, all institutional standards are ruined; when men of bizarre extravagance emerge, the empire is swept along in their wake; when men of absurd deception emerge, the empire vies in rushing after the strange; when men who crave martial exploits emerge, beyond the great wilderness and remote frontiers there is more trouble by the day. title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
下吁豈不大可畏哉是故人君知吾之心不可
有嗜好也一有嗜好則天下爭以其好者中吾
之欲而吾心旣中於欲卽方寸之地渙然而莫
爲之主其所以權衡萬事而推行之者日見其
諄謬蹠盭而治愈不可幾于是乎有正心之道
焉然心之正未易言也必有洞察幾微之明而
後能正其心必有果確無難之勇而後能正其
心必有專一不貳之誠而後能正其心蓋吾之
心本公而無私也中而匪偏也正而匪邪也與
===
接焉構日以心闚則公者鑿而私矣中正者漓
而偏而邪矣幾微之介是故宜用察也非至明
不能也黜其私以全公也克其偏以用中也祛
其邪以歸正也凜若馭馬兢若執盈非至勇不
能也廓乎公不以私間渾乎中不以偏間純乎
正不以邪間天精天粹萬物作類非至誠不能
也故宴安珍御不極口體所以防此心之毒曼
聲冶色不快耳目所以閑此心之伐佞幸宵人
屏于左右所以剔此心之蠹如是者心正貨賄
punctuated: 下。吁！豈不大可畏哉！是故人君知吾之心不可有嗜好也。一有嗜好，則天下爭以其好者中吾之欲；而吾心旣中於欲，卽方寸之地渙然而莫爲之主，其所以權衡萬事而推行之者，日見其諄謬蹠盭，而治愈不可幾。于是乎有正心之道焉。然心之正未易言也：必有洞察幾微之明，而後能正其心；必有果確無難之勇，而後能正其心；必有專一不貳之誠，而後能正其心。蓋吾之心本公而無私也，中而匪偏也，正而匪邪也；與接焉構，日以心闚，則公者鑿而私矣，中正者漓而偏而邪矣。幾微之介，是故宜用察也，非至明不能也；黜其私以全公也，克其偏以用中也，祛其邪以歸正也，凜若馭馬，兢若執盈，非至勇不能也；廓乎公不以私間，渾乎中不以偏間，純乎正不以邪間，天精天粹，萬物作類，非至誠不能也。故宴安珍御不極口體，所以防此心之毒；曼聲冶色不快耳目，所以閑此心之伐；佞幸宵人屏于左右，所以剔此心之蠹。如是者心正？貨賄
translation_en: … world. Alas! Is this not greatly to be feared? Therefore, a ruler knows that his mind must not harbor fond desires. Once he has a fond desire, the whole empire will vie to cater to his cravings with what he favors; and once his mind is struck by desire, that square inch within him becomes dissipated and lacks a master. Consequently, in his weighing of the myriad affairs and putting them into practice, one sees daily more perversity, error, and transgression [? 諄謬 for 悖謬], and good governance becomes ever more out of reach. Thus there is the Way of rectifying the mind. Yet the rectification of the mind is not easily spoken of: one must possess the clarity to discern subtle incipient tendencies before one can rectify one's mind; one must possess resolute and unflinching courage before one can rectify one's mind; and one must possess single-minded and undivided sincerity before one can rectify one's mind. For our mind is originally impartial and without selfishness, balanced and not one-sided, upright and not crooked. When it comes into contact and engages with things, and people daily spy upon the ruler's mind, what was impartial is chipped away and becomes selfish, and what was balanced and upright becomes thinned out, turning one-sided and crooked. At the threshold of subtle incipient tendencies, one ought therefore to exercise discernment—and without the utmost clarity, one cannot do so. Rejecting selfishness to preserve impartiality, overcoming one-sidedness to employ the mean, and dispelling crookedness to return to uprightness—trembling as if driving horses with rotten reins, cautious as if holding a vessel filled to the brim—without the utmost courage, one cannot do so. Expansively impartial without selfishness intervening, wholly balanced without one-sidedness intervening, purely upright without crookedness intervening—with heavenly essence and heavenly purity, becoming the counterpart to the myriad things—without the utmost sincerity, one cannot do so. Thus, not indulging palate and body to the extreme with ease and rare delicacies is the means to guard against the poison of this mind; not gratifying ears and eyes with seductive music and alluring beauty is the means to bar the despoiling of this mind; banishing flatterers, favorites, and petty men from one's side is the means to weed out the vermin of this mind. Is the mind rectified by doing just this? As for wealth and bribes, …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
游畋懼其汨吾心也我則慎之土木長生懼其
蕩吾心也我則杜之窮兵黷武懼其暴吾心也
我則誡之如是者心正未也書史所以明此心
也吾何可廢開卷之益學問所以存此心也吾
何可替就將之勤賢人君子所以輔養此心也
吾何可乏啓沃之助而師保疑丞三公四輔日
與之稽古正學無爲以守至正可也如是者心
正猶未也負扆端黻此心矣瞽御承接亦此心
焉享帝格廟此心矣深宮燕閒亦此心焉寡欲
===
以培之主靜以凝之蜎蜎蠖濩弗忘也廣廈細
旃弗肆也如是者心正吾心既正則萬事之大
本大原皆自我而握其幾矣由此以宰制天下
如戶之有樞如車之有輪將隨吾所闔闢運旋
而罔不宜者唯公也故能通天下唯中也故能
一天下唯正也故能齊天下以禮樂則脩明以
刑政則振舉以慶賞威罰則足以勸善而懲奸
由是帷帘有徽音綴衣皆常吉而宮闈正由是
藝極陳風聲樹而朝廷正由是大臣法小臣廉
punctuated: 游畋懼其汨吾心也，我則慎之；土木長生懼其蕩吾心也，我則杜之；窮兵黷武懼其暴吾心也，我則誡之：如是者，心正。未也。書史所以明此心也，吾何可廢開卷之益；學問所以存此心也，吾何可替就將之勤；賢人君子所以輔養此心也，吾何可乏啓沃之助。而師、保、疑、丞，三公、四輔，日與之稽古正學，無爲以守至正可也：如是者，心正。猶未也。負扆端黻，此心矣；瞽御承接，亦此心焉。享帝格廟，此心矣；深宮燕閒，亦此心焉。寡欲以培之，主靜以凝之；蜎蜎蠖濩弗忘也，廣廈細旃弗肆也：如是者，心正。吾心既正，則萬事之大本大原，皆自我而握其幾矣。由此以宰制天下，如戶之有樞，如車之有輪，將隨吾所闔闢運旋而罔不宜者。唯公也，故能通天下；唯中也，故能一天下；唯正也，故能齊天下。以禮樂則脩明，以刑政則振舉，以慶賞威罰則足以勸善而懲奸。由是帷帘有徽音，綴衣皆常吉，而宮闈正；由是藝極陳，風聲樹，而朝廷正；由是大臣法，小臣廉，
translation_en: …and hunting trips, fearing that they may submerge my mind, I exercise caution toward them; grand construction projects and quests for immortality, fearing that they may unsettle my mind, I shut them out; exhausting military force and wantonly waging war, fearing that they may make my mind violent, I guard against them. When it is like this, the mind is rectified. Yet this is still not all. Books and histories are the means to illuminate this mind—how could I abandon the benefit of opening a scroll? Learning and inquiry are the means to preserve this mind—how could I slacken in the diligence of advancing day by day? Worthy men and gentlemen are the means to assist and nourish this mind—how could I lack the aid of their enlightening counsel? And with the Preceptor, Guardian, Averter of Faults, and Coadjutor—the Three Dukes and Four Assistants—to daily examine antiquity and rectify learning with them, practicing non-action in order to hold fast to supreme rectitude, will suffice. When it is like this, the mind is rectified. Yet even this is still not all. Standing before the斧-screen in ceremonial robes and cap, it is this mind; when blind musicians and attendants wait upon me, it is also this mind. Making sacrificial offerings to the Supreme Lord and approaching the ancestral temple, it is this mind; in the leisure of the deep palace, it is also this mind. By lessening desires to cultivate it, and holding to tranquility to consolidate it—never forgetting it even amid the deepest seclusion, nor indulging oneself in spacious halls upon fine felt rugs—when it is like this, the mind is rectified. Once my mind is rectified, the great foundation and great source of the myriad affairs are all grasped in their subtle springs by me. From this, to govern and regulate the world is like a door having its pivot, or a carriage having its wheels: they will follow whatever I open or close, turn or revolve, without anything being improper. Only because it is impartial can it connect the whole world; only because it is balanced can it unify the whole world; only because it is rectified can it bring order to the whole world. Applied to rites and music, they are cultivated and made brilliant; applied to punishments and governance, they are invigorated and raised up; applied to rewards and awesome punishments, they suffice to encourage goodness and chastise wickedness. From this, behind the curtains of the inner quarters there is virtuous renown, the Keepers of the Robes are all men of constant goodness, and the palace interior is rectified; from this, the standard of perfection is set forth, a moral example is established, and the court is rectified; from this, the great ministers abide by the law, the lesser officials are incorruptible,…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而百官正由是智不詐愚衆不暴寡勇不苦怯
而萬民莫敢不正其有奇袤而不治者則微矣
此順之至也化之極也聖帝明王之治由此其
選也豈非正心之明驗歟當舜之世庶政乂而
黎民敏德矣乃其命禹則曰人心惟危道心惟
微惟精惟一允執厥中湯以天錫勇智表正萬
邦而仲虺所以勗之者曰懋昭大德建中于民
以義制事以禮制心夫虞商豈不稱極治哉而
其相授受相告勉尤惓惓于心學如此君人者
===
欲襲迹帝王之盛亦足以稽矣於乎斯道也乃
千聖傳心之宗旨而亦萬世言治者之準的也
然下必有格心之臣而後能進此言上必有純
心之主而後可以此言進故漢之時董仲舒嘗
以對武帝矣卒無能格其多慾之蔽唐文皇弓
矢之喻若有解于正心者而不能不塵十漸之
陳誠則以其心之未純故也朱子接洙泗淵源
倡明理學于有宋之季而正心誠意之說所以
為脩齊治平之本者尤三復不置焉噫此豈直
punctuated: 而百官正；由是智不詐愚，衆不暴寡，勇不苦怯，而萬民莫敢不正。其有奇袤而不治者，則微矣。此順之至也，化之極也，聖帝明王之治，由此其選也，豈非正心之明驗歟？當舜之世，庶政乂而黎民敏德矣，乃其命禹則曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。」湯以天錫勇智，表正萬邦，而仲虺所以勗之者曰：「懋昭大德，建中于民，以義制事，以禮制心。」夫虞、商豈不稱極治哉？而其相授受、相告勉，尤惓惓于心學如此，君人者欲襲迹帝王之盛，亦足以稽矣。於乎！斯道也，乃千聖傳心之宗旨，而亦萬世言治者之準的也。然下必有格心之臣，而後能進此言；上必有純心之主，而後可以此言進。故漢之時，董仲舒嘗以對武帝矣，卒無能格其多慾之蔽；唐文皇弓矢之喻，若有解于正心者，而不能不塵十漸之陳，誠則以其心之未純故也。朱子接洙、泗淵源，倡明理學于有宋之季，而正心誠意之說，所以為脩、齊、治、平之本者，尤三復不置焉。噫！此豈直
translation_en:
…and the hundred officials are rectified; from this, the wise do not deceive the foolish, the many do not tyrannize the few, the brave do not torment the timid, and none among the myriad people dare not be rectified. Those who remain perverse and unmanageable will be few indeed. This is the utmost of harmony and the pinnacle of transformation; the governance of sage emperors and enlightened kings takes its model from this. Is this not clear proof of the rectification of the mind?

In the age of Shun, the numerous affairs of state were well-ordered and the black-haired people were diligent in virtue; yet when he charged Yu, he said: "The human mind is precarious, the mind of the Way is subtle; be discerning, be undivided, and sincerely hold fast the Mean." Tang, endowed by Heaven with valor and wisdom, stood as a standard to rectify all states, yet Zhonghui exhorted him by saying: "Strive to illustrate your great virtue, establish the Mean among the people, regulate affairs by righteousness, and regulate your mind by propriety." Did not the eras of Yu [Shun] and Shang [Tang] represent the pinnacle of good governance? Yet in handing down the succession to one another and in mutually counseling and encouraging one another, they were thus earnestly devoted to the learning of the mind. Those who rule over others and wish to follow in the footsteps of the flourishing age of the emperors and kings have sufficient basis here for examination.

Alas! This Way is the central tenet transmitted from mind to mind by a thousand sages, and the standard for all who speak of governance for ten thousand generations. Yet below, there must first be ministers capable of rectifying the ruler's mind before such words can be presented; above, there must first be a sovereign of pure mind before such words can be received. Thus, in Han times, Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 once presented this in reply to Emperor Wu, yet in the end he was unable to correct the blindness of the Emperor's many desires. Emperor Wen of Tang [Taizong], with his metaphor of the bow and arrow, seemed to have some understanding of rectifying the mind, yet he could not avoid giving rise to the remonstrance on the "Ten Gradual Declines"; truly, this was because his mind was not yet pure. Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] continued the fountainhead of the Zhu and Si rivers [Confucianism], championing and elucidating the Learning of Principle (lixue) during the late Song dynasty; and as for the doctrine of rectifying the mind and making the intentions sincere as the root of cultivating the person, regulating the family, ordering the state, and bringing peace to the world, he repeated it over and over without ceasing. Alas! Was this merely…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
爲有宋君臣發哉
表
擬輔臣疏內外文武臣工職名於屏風恭
進
御覽表萬曆二年
金輝漢
同考試官教諭單批結構有體該括不遺
皇上知人安民至意及大臣獻納之忠讀之可想匪徒四六之工已也
健羡健羡
===
考試官教諭朱批蒼然之質淵然之光
考試官教授李批駢麗可則
萬曆二年某月某日輔臣某等謹將所製
內外文武臣工職名
御屏一座上
進者伏以
帝王弘致治之謨安民惟要
聖哲操馭臣之柄課職寔先欲內順外威之兼
隆必文經武緯之共濟敬攄一得奏記千
punctuated:
爲有宋君臣發哉！

表

擬輔臣疏內外文武臣工職名於屏風恭進御覽表（萬曆二年）

金輝漢

同考試官教諭單批：結構有體，該括不遺。皇上知人安民至意，及大臣獻納之忠，讀之可想，匪徒四六之工已也。健羡，健羡！
考試官教諭朱批：蒼然之質，淵然之光。
考試官教授李批：駢麗可則。

萬曆二年某月某日，輔臣某等謹將所製內外文武臣工職名御屏一座上進者。伏以帝王弘致治之謨，安民惟要；聖哲操馭臣之柄，課職寔先。欲內順外威之兼隆，必文經武緯之共濟。敬攄一得，奏記千
translation_en:
…uttered merely for the ruler and ministers of the Song dynasty!

Memorial

A Draft Memorial by the Grand Secretaries Respectfully Presenting for Imperial Inspection a Folding Screen Inscribed with the Titles and Names of Civil and Military Officials Inside and Outside the Capital (Second Year of Wanli [1574])

Jin Huihan 金輝漢

Associate Examiner and Instructor Shan 單 comments: The structure has proper form, and its coverage leaves nothing out. Reading it allows one to envision His Majesty's supreme intention to know men and bring peace to the people, as well as the loyalty of great ministers in offering counsel—it is not merely skillful four-six parallel prose! Truly admirable, truly admirable!
Examiner and Instructor Zhu 朱 comments: Antique in substance, profound in luster.
Examiner and Professor Li 李 comments: Its parallel elegance is worthy of serving as a model.

On a certain day of a certain month in the second year of the Wanli era [1574], Grand Secretary So-and-so and others respectfully present on high an imperial screen that they have had made, inscribed with the titles and names of civil and military officials inside and outside the capital. We humbly reflect that when sovereigns broaden their plans for bringing about order, giving peace to the people is alone essential; when sages and worthies wield the authority of governing their ministers, evaluating the performance of duties truly comes first. If one wishes both internal harmony and external awe to flourish together, civil warp and military woof must mutually assist one another. Respectfully setting forth our humble insight, we submit this record of the thousand…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
官恭製清防仰塵
睿覽具官臣某等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首上言竊
惟執樞運化大君囿六合以爲家列秩宣
猷元首聯百司而同體故虞廷稽載采幽
明類別於肆朝周室肇時巡震疊丕彰於
式序緣籍省觀之徧聿昭慶讓之公醇古
旣還遺風猶在綜名實而覈吏治績紀循
良披輿圖而恢帝紘任專桓赳蒼生軫念
屏書刺史之名紫殿聞言柱寫涇陽之令
===
幷撰廉刑二訓儆貪戾以惠窮簷獨頒軍
戒三篇警威萌以和大衆迹垂往牒事軼
前聞磨礪胥切臣工隆汚有關世道肆我
皇明啓運遏亂略而民困宏紓
聖祖統天端化原而官常載肅
文皇懋遴庶職籍內外姓名於
武英之南廊
仁宗慎簡諸司揭藩臬履歷於
奉天之西序
punctuated: 官，恭製清防，仰塵睿覽。具官臣某等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：竊惟執樞運化，大君囿六合以爲家；列秩宣猷，元首聯百司而同體。故虞廷稽載采，幽明類別於肆朝；周室肇時巡，震疊丕彰於式序。緣籍省觀之徧，聿昭慶讓之公。醇古旣還，遺風猶在。綜名實而覈吏治，績紀循良；披輿圖而恢帝紘，任專桓赳。蒼生軫念，屏書刺史之名；紫殿聞言，柱寫涇陽之令。幷撰《廉》《刑》二訓，儆貪戾以惠窮簷；獨頒《軍戒》三篇，警威萌以和大衆。迹垂往牒，事軼前聞；磨礪胥切臣工，隆汚有關世道。肆我皇明啓運，遏亂略而民困宏紓；聖祖統天，端化原而官常載肅。文皇懋遴庶職，籍內外姓名於武英之南廊；仁宗慎簡諸司，揭藩臬履歷於奉天之西序。
translation_en:
… the myriad officials, respectfully fashioning a clear screen and raising it to sully Your Imperial Gaze.

Your servants [name], holding [official titles], and others, in utmost fear and trepidation, bow our heads to the ground and submit these words:

We humbly reflect that in grasping the pivot and revolving transformation, the Great Sovereign encompasses the six directions as his household; in arraying ranks and proclaiming plans, the Supreme Head joins the hundred offices as a single body. Thus the court of Yu examined recorded achievements, and the distinction between the obscure and the illustrious was differentiated during the four audiences; the house of Zhou initiated seasonal tours of inspection, and awesome dread was grandly manifested in the orderly ranking of the princes. Because inspection by means of registers was comprehensive, the impartiality of rewards and reprimands was thereby made bright.

After pure antiquity passed away, its lingering customs still remained. Synthesizing titles and realities to verify administrative governance, merits were recorded of the dutiful and good; spreading out the map of the realm to expand the imperial cordon, responsibilities were entrusted exclusively to the martial and valiant. With compassionate concern for the common people, the names of Regional Inspectors were inscribed upon a screen; upon hearing words in the Purple Hall, the magistrate of Jingyang's name was written upon a pillar. Furthermore, the two instructions on Integrity and Punishments were composed, warning the greedy and perverse so as to benefit humble cottages; the three chapters of Military Admonitions were specially promulgated, alerting against incipient arrogance so as to harmonize the great multitude. These traces have been handed down in past records, and their deeds surpass what was formerly heard; such honing and whetting touched all officials alike, and their flourishing or decline was bound up with the state of the world.

Thus when our August Ming opened its destiny, it checked rebellious schemes and broadly relieved the distress of the people; the Sacred Ancestor [Emperor Taizu] governed Heaven's realm, rectifying the source of transformation so that official discipline was once again made solemn. The Cultured Emperor [Emperor Chengzu] diligently selected the myriad officials, registering the names of inner and outer officials in the southern corridor of the Wuying Hall; Ancestor Ren [Emperor Renzong] carefully chose the various authorities, posting the service records of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions in the western wing of the Fengtian Hall. …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
用賢求治憂勤不替于
累朝計吏保邦延攬尤殷于
今日玆蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
睿資挺植
聖學緝熈翰灑
宸章煥堯文於
五位
冊尊
===
===
徽號隆舜孝於
兩宮
召對寵
平臺資舟楫鹽梅之助
傳宣頒
禁藥敕銓衡樞筦之司時當大計而
親獎廉能復
允奏除而
躬臨選授縉紳揚采慶元氣之發舒介胄騰權
punctuated: 用賢求治，憂勤不替于累朝；計吏保邦，延攬尤殷于今日。玆蓋伏遇皇帝陛下：睿資挺植，聖學緝熈。翰灑宸章，煥堯文於五位；冊尊徽號，隆舜孝於兩宮。召對寵平臺，資舟楫鹽梅之助；傳宣頒禁藥，敕銓衡樞筦之司。時當大計，而親獎廉能；復允奏除，而躬臨選授。縉紳揚采，慶元氣之發舒；介胄騰權，
translation_en: Employing the worthy to seek good governance, anxious diligence has never slackened across successive reigns; evaluating officials to safeguard the state, the recruiting of talent is especially earnest today. This is because we humbly encounter Your Imperial Majesty: endowed with outstanding sagely qualities, and continuously illuminating your sacred learning. Your brush pours forth imperial compositions, making Yao-like civil radiance shine from the sovereign's position; Your patents confer exalted honorific titles, exalting Shun-like filial piety toward the Two Palaces. Summoning ministers for audiences, You bestow favor at the Platform Hall, relying on the assistance of those who serve as boats and oars or salt and plum; transmitting pronouncements, You distribute medicines from the Forbidden Palace, admonishing the officials in charge of personnel evaluation and military affairs. When the time came for the Great Evaluation, You personally rewarded the incorrupt and capable; furthermore, approving memorialized appointments, You personally attended the selection and conferral of offices. The civil officials display their splendor, celebrating the burgeoning of vital energy; the armored soldiers surge with vigor [reading 歡 for 權?], …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
快
神威之丕振凡此
經綸大政率由
宵旰深惟顧八埏寥邈非摹形制或聞見之
未周庶府森羅不假標題將勸懲之無據
臣等祗承
德意少効贊襄謹屬吏兵總領之臣備採遠邇
職司之隷提綱挈要就簡刪繁自兩京逮
及諸藩由郡守遡之
===
朝著握持鉛槧次第丹青用紀載於監觀奉
神明於坐照
御屏巍聳依稀頫疆域以宅中
黼座時憑左右儼臣鄰之在列置諸
文華後殿庶幾密邇
清光假以
講幄餘閒亦可備延
顧問撫馭具存之掌上搜羅盡在於目前按
籍而妍媸莫逃若冰鑑之昭融羣品試功
punctuated: 快神威之丕振。凡此經綸大政，率由宵旰深惟。顧八埏寥邈，非摹形制，或聞見之未周；庶府森羅，不假標題，將勸懲之無據。臣等祗承德意，少効贊襄，謹屬吏、兵總領之臣，備採遠邇職司之隷，提綱挈要，就簡刪繁，自兩京逮及諸藩，由郡守遡之朝著，握持鉛槧，次第丹青，用紀載於監觀，奉神明於坐照。御屏巍聳，依稀頫疆域以宅中；黼座時憑，左右儼臣鄰之在列。置諸文華後殿，庶幾密邇清光；假以講幄餘閒，亦可備延顧問。撫馭具存之掌上，搜羅盡在於目前。按籍而妍媸莫逃，若冰鑑之昭融羣品；試功
translation_en: …and rejoice in the grand invigoration of Your sacred majesty. All these great affairs of statecraft arise entirely from Your deep contemplation before dawn and after dusk. Yet the eight directions of the realm are vast and distant—without depicting their geographical forms and configurations, what is heard and seen might not be comprehensive; the multitudinous offices are arrayed in dense profusion—without the aid of inscribed headings, encouragement and chastisement would lack a basis. Your servants have reverently received Your virtuous intent and striven to offer some slight assistance. We have respectfully charged the officials exercising general supervision in the Ministries of Personnel and War to gather complete records of the subordinate officeholders near and far. Grasping the main threads and essential points, aiming for conciseness and pruning away prolixity, extending from the Two Capitals down to the various provinces, and tracing from the Grand Governors back up to the court roster, we have taken up lead and wooden tablets to set everything in order with vermilion and green pigments, so as to record them for Your supervisory inspection and serve Your sacred intelligence in effortless illumination. The imperial screen towers loftily, as though looking down upon the territorial domains from the central seat; leaned upon at all times beside the embroidered throne, to the left and right Your ministerial associates appear ranked in solemn order. Placed in the rear hall of the Wenhua Palace (Palace of Literary Brilliance), it may remain in close proximity to Your pure radiance; given the leisure moments following the Classic Colloquium, it may also stand ready to invite Your inquiries and consultations. The means of pacifying and governing the realm are held entirely in the palm of Your hand; the gathering of talents lies wholly before Your eyes. By consulting the register, neither merit nor defect can escape notice, just as an icy mirror clearly reflects all manner of things; by testing achievements…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而黜陟不爽猶璣衡之斟酌四時伏念臣
等質任朴忠功微調燮荷
三朝之知遇報塞惟艱慶
一德之遭逢對揚敢後學雖慙於丹扆義竊
附於諫屏地險周詢倣曾公亮更書別籍
官聯積錄希呂文穆採取夾囊豈云因事
納忠尚冀
知人則哲伏願
皇猷遐鬯
===
帝鑑常明
見萬里於几席間仁覃蔀屋
辨羣才於堂陛下彙拔茹茅奠
二祖
八宗之鴻基
邁五帝三王之駿業
文教揆而武衛奮華夷共戴鞏
社稷於金甌九德事而庶績凝
朝野咸寧熙寰區於玉燭臣等無任瞻
punctuated: 而黜陟不爽，猶璣衡之斟酌四時。伏念臣等質任朴忠，功微調燮；荷三朝之知遇，報塞惟艱；慶一德之遭逢，對揚敢後？學雖慙於丹扆，義竊附於諫屏。地險周詢，倣曾公亮更書別籍；官聯積錄，希呂文穆採取夾囊。豈云因事納忠，尚冀知人則哲。伏願皇猷遐鬯，帝鑑常明。見萬里於几席間，仁覃蔀屋；辨羣才於堂陛下，彙拔茹茅。奠二祖八宗之鴻基，邁五帝三王之駿業。文教揆而武衛奮，華夷共戴，鞏社稷於金甌；九德事而庶績凝，朝野咸寧，熙寰區於玉燭。臣等無任瞻
translation_en: …and demotions and promotions will be without error, just as the armillary sphere measures out the four seasons. We humbly reflect that your servants are by nature simple and loyal, with but slight merit in harmonizing the administration; having received the favor and recognition of three reigns, we find it truly difficult to repay our debt; rejoicing in this encounter with pure and unified virtue, how could we dare fall behind in extolling and responding to Your Majesty's grace? Though our learning puts us to shame before the crimson screen of the throne, in duty we venture to attach ourselves to the screen of remonstrance. Making comprehensive inquiries into strategic terrains, we emulate Zeng Gongliang 曾公亮 in compiling a separate register; cumulatively recording the ranks of officialdom, we aspire to Lü Wenmu 呂文穆 (Lü Mengzheng 呂蒙正) in drawing names from his folder-pouch. How could we claim merely to offer loyalty through the occasion of this task? Rather, we hope to aid in the wisdom of knowing men. We humbly pray that the August Plan may spread far and wide, and the Imperial Mirror remain forever bright; that viewing ten thousand li from between Your table and mat, Your benevolence may extend to the humblest thatched huts; that distinguishing the multitude of talents below the steps of the hall, You may draw them forth together like pulling up cogongrass by its tangled roots; that You may consolidate the grand foundation of the Two Ancestors and Eight Ancestral Emperors, and surpass the magnificent achievements of the Five Emperors and Three Kings; that civil teachings may be measured and military defenses roused, with Chinese and non-Chinese alike sharing in allegiance, securing the altars of soil and grain like a golden urn; and that those of the nine virtues may be employed and the myriad achievements brought to completion, with court and countryside alike in peace, brightening the realm under the jade candle of harmony. Your servants, unable to contain our earnest…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以所製內外文武職名屏
風一座隨
表上
進以
聞
第叁塲
策五道
第一問
===
孫夢熊
同考試官教諭劉批重本惇倫風示在上我
列聖謨訓之昭
皇上繼述之善子能援往陳今鋪張而揚厲之末歸本敬一尤得精髓
之義宜冠多士
考試官教諭朱批上下今古闡析忠孝大義
殆盡讀之令人感奮可以式矣
考試官教授李批敷答詳明矩矱嚴整
聖王所以宰制六合綜理民物置之仁義
punctuated:
天仰聖、激切屏營之至。謹以所製內外文武職名屏風一座，隨表上進以聞。

第叁塲
策五道

第一問
孫夢熊
同考試官教諭劉批：重本惇倫，風示在上。我列聖謨訓之昭，皇上繼述之善，子能援往陳今，鋪張而揚厲之；末歸本敬一，尤得精髓之義，宜冠多士。
考試官教諭朱批：上下今古，闡析忠孝大義殆盡，讀之令人感奮，可以式矣。
考試官教授李批：敷答詳明，矩矱嚴整。

聖王所以宰制六合、綜理民物，置之仁義
translation_en:
… looking up to Heaven and the Sacred Person in the utmost earnestness and trepidation. We reverently present, accompanying this memorial, one standing screen inscribed with the official titles and names of the metropolitan and provincial civil and military officials that we have had made, for the Emperor's information.

Third Session
Five Policy Essays

First Question
Sun Mengxiong 孫夢熊
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Liu 劉: Emphasizing fundamentals and cultivating human relationships depend on moral exemplification from above. You are able to cite the past and set forth the present, elaborating upon and exalting the illustrious counsels and instructions of our successive Sacred Ancestors and the excellence of His Majesty's continuation of their legacy. At the end, tracing the root back to reverence and unity especially captures the quintessential meaning; this essay deserves to top the multitude of scholars.
Comment by Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Zhu 朱: Ranging across antiquity and the present, it elucidates and analyzes the great principles of loyalty and filial piety almost exhaustively. Reading it leaves one moved and inspired; it may serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner Instructor (jiaoshou) Li 李: The exposition in the reply is detailed and clear, and its structural standards are strict and well-ordered.

Whereby the sage kings governed the six directions, comprehensively managed the people and all things, placed them within the realm of benevolence, righteousness, …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
禮樂之域而錫之平康正直之福者豈無
所本哉以脩人極則藹然與天下相熈洽
而萬世之倫紀立焉以扶世教則秩然與
天下相綱維而萬世之謨訓昭焉意之所
眎辨於立的化之所趣疾於偃草是以端
冕垂裳而化行俗美無爲恭巳而物阜民
康德與三五比隆名與天壤俱遠也執事
首發策而以忠孝之說進諸生甚大惠也
今薄海内外承休函祉漸濡我
===
祖宗豐芑之仁
棫樸之化二百餘禩于兹矣
聖天子丕宅君師
神靈睿知以臨之
愷悌敬睦以先之卽含生之倫無不矯首跂
踵慕誼嚮風迪於彝而若於訓況於章縫
之士沐浴
君親闓澤者有不蹶然興起思以臣子大義自
効者乎請陳其說夫人君中天地而立爲
punctuated: 禮樂之域，而錫之平康正直之福者，豈無所本哉？以脩人極，則藹然與天下相熈洽，而萬世之倫紀立焉；以扶世教，則秩然與天下相綱維，而萬世之謨訓昭焉。意之所眎，辨於立的；化之所趣，疾於偃草。是以端冕垂裳，而化行俗美；無爲恭巳，而物阜民康。德與三五比隆，名與天壤俱遠也。執事首發策，而以忠孝之說進諸生，甚大惠也。今薄海内外，承休函祉，漸濡我祖宗豐芑之仁、棫樸之化，二百餘禩于兹矣。聖天子丕宅君師，神靈睿知以臨之，愷悌敬睦以先之，卽含生之倫，無不矯首跂踵，慕誼嚮風，迪於彝而若於訓；況於章縫之士，沐浴君親闓澤者，有不蹶然興起，思以臣子大義自効者乎？請陳其說。夫人君中天地而立，爲
translation_en: …the realm of rites and music, and bestows upon them the blessings of peace, tranquility, and uprightness—how could this lack a foundation? By cultivating the ultimate standard of human conduct, he harmoniously unites with all under Heaven in genial concord, and the moral relations of ten thousand generations are thereby established; by upholding the moral teachings of the age, he systematically binds all under Heaven in orderly governance, and the counsels and instructions for ten thousand generations are thereby made luminous. What his intentions point toward is more distinct than a target set up to view; where his transforming influence tends is swifter than grass bending before the wind. Therefore, he wears the ceremonial cap and lets his robes hang down, yet transformation proceeds and customs become beautified; he practices non-action and reverently composes himself, yet things are abundant and the people are at peace. His virtue rivals the splendor of the Three Dynasties and Five Emperors, and his renown endures as long as Heaven and Earth. For Your Honor to open the first policy question by presenting the scholars with the doctrine of loyalty and filial piety is a great kindness indeed. Today, within and beyond the four seas, all receive blessings and are encompassed by good fortune, steeped in the benevolence of "Abundant Millet" (Fengqi) and the transforming influence of "Luxuriant Scrub Oak" (Yupu) of our Imperial Ancestors for more than two hundred years now. The Sacred Son of Heaven grandly occupies the position of ruler and teacher, presiding over the realm with divine intelligence and sage wisdom, and leading it with graciousness, reverence, and harmony. Even among all living creatures, there are none who do not raise their heads and stand on tiptoe, admiring righteousness and turning toward his moral wind, guided by constant norms and compliant with instructions. How much more so for scholars in ceremonial dress who are bathed in the generous grace of ruler and parent—could any fail to rouse themselves eagerly and think of devoting themselves to the supreme duty of ministers and sons? Allow me to set forth my explanation. Now, the ruler of men stands at the center between Heaven and Earth, serving as…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
綱常之主為紀法之宗臨御寰區陶冶品
庶其望治需澤者至眾也整齊而軌束之
者至無極也然勸率之樞在上不在下轉
移之柄以實不以名上以忠作天下而後
為子者化焉上以忠作天下而後為臣者
勸焉三代之盛其治大順其俗大同卓乎
尚已豈抱寂守默無所為哉亦豈家喻戶
曉為之訓哉書有之天秩有典敕我五典
五惇哉又曰惟皇上帝降衷于下民厥有
===
恒性克綏厥猷惟后自天秩之自我敕之
自帝降之自后綏之立教之本端可識矣
夫典一也而君親為重性一也而事君事
親為本記曰父母生之恩莫大焉君親臨
之厚莫重焉此忠孝之說也舜大聖人也
以玄德君天下者而萬世稱大孝底豫之
化舜之心也而夔夔之形於祗載者不知
也周公大聖人也以顯德相天下而萬世
稱大忠篤棐之忱周公之心也而几几之
punctuated: 綱常之主，為紀法之宗，臨御寰區，陶冶品庶。其望治需澤者至眾也，整齊而軌束之者至無極也。然勸率之樞，在上不在下；轉移之柄，以實不以名。上以忠作天下，而後為子者化焉；上以忠作天下，而後為臣者勸焉。三代之盛，其治大順，其俗大同，卓乎尚已，豈抱寂守默無所為哉？亦豈家喻戶曉為之訓哉？《書》有之：「天秩有典，敕我五典五惇哉！」又曰：「惟皇上帝，降衷于下民，若有恒性，克綏厥猷惟后。」自天秩之，自我敕之；自帝降之，自后綏之，立教之本端可識矣。夫典一也，而君親為重；性一也，而事君、事親為本。《記》曰：「父母生之，恩莫大焉；君親臨之，厚莫重焉。」此忠孝之說也。舜，大聖人也，以玄德君天下者，而萬世稱大孝。底豫之化，舜之心也，而夔夔之形於祗載者不知也。周公，大聖人也，以顯德相天下，而萬世稱大忠。篤棐之忱，周公之心也，而几几之
translation_en: … the master of the cardinal bonds and constant virtues, and the exemplar of laws and institutions, ruling over the realm and molding the multitude of things and people. Those who long for good governance and await his beneficence are vast in number, and the task of ordering and regulating them is boundless. Yet the pivot for encouraging and leading them lies above, not below; the handle for transforming them relies on substance, not on name. When the superior rouses the world with devotion [NOTE: Here the woodblock appears to have printed 忠 'loyalty' twice; context suggests the first should be 孝 'filial piety'], only then are those who are sons transformed; when the superior rouses the world with loyalty, only then are those who are subjects encouraged. In the flourishing era of the Three Dynasties, governance was in great harmony and customs were in great unity—lofty indeed! How could this have been achieved by embracing quietude and keeping silent while doing nothing? Or how could it have been done by going from house to house and door to door to instruct them? The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Heaven orders the social arrangements; let us rightly direct our five social arrangements and give thickness to all five!" It also says: "Great God has conferred even on the inferior people a moral sense, compliance with which would show their nature invariably right. To make them tranquilly pursue the course which it would indicate is the work of the sovereign." Heaven orders them, and we direct them; the Lord on High confers it, and the sovereign makes them tranquilly pursue it—from this the fundamental basis for establishing moral instruction can truly be recognized. Now, the social arrangements are one, yet the ruler and parents are of greatest weight; human nature is one, yet serving the ruler and serving parents are the root. The Record of Rites (Ji) says: "Parents give one life; no grace is greater than this. The ruler personally presides over one; no generosity is weightier than this." Such is the doctrine of loyalty and filial piety. Shun was a great sage who ruled the world through his mysterious virtue, yet ten thousand generations have praised his great filial piety. The transformation that brought his parents to delight was the heart of Shun, whereas the respectful dread manifested in his reverent service was something he was not even conscious of. The Duke of Zhou was a great sage who assisted in governing the world through his illustrious virtue, yet ten thousand generations have praised his great loyalty. The sincerity of his devoted assistance was the heart of the Duke of Zhou, whereas the self-possessed composure…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
形於赤舄者不知也舜孝矣而敘百揆徽
五典以膺堯之統則忠為益純故能成
從欲之治周公忠矣而善繼志善述事以
成文武之德則孝為益達故能成迓衡之
休是二聖為人倫之至而千古頌治功之
極厥有由哉後世乃有孝經一書說者謂
成于曾子門人之手以天子諸侯卿大夫
士庶人為序凡列為十八章當煨燼散逸
之餘雖未必盡出于夫子之言然其教孝
===
章順明生人之大綱不可易也與諸經並
傳可矣忠經一書出於東漢馬融之作以
聖君冢臣百工守宰兆人為序亦擬為十
八章雖篇旨雜出不專為人臣立訓然其
勸忠著教明臣子之大義不可廢也與孝
經相表裏其庶矣顧其書不列于學官義
不講于庠塾至元而斯道晦蝕久矣洪惟
我
太祖高皇帝汛掃腥羶重開寓縣驅一世之椎
punctuated: 形於赤舄者，不知也。舜孝矣，而敘百揆、徽五典，以膺堯之統，則忠為益純，故能成從欲之治；周公忠矣，而善繼志、善述事，以成文、武之德，則孝為益達，故能成迓衡之休。是二聖為人倫之至，而千古頌治功之極，厥有由哉！後世乃有《孝經》一書，說者謂成于曾子門人之手，以天子、諸侯、卿大夫、士、庶人為序，凡列為十八章。當煨燼散逸之餘，雖未必盡出于夫子之言，然其教孝章順，明生人之大綱，不可易也，與諸經並傳可矣。《忠經》一書，出於東漢馬融之作，以聖君、冢臣、百工、守宰、兆人為序，亦擬為十八章。雖篇旨雜出，不專為人臣立訓，然其勸忠著教，明臣子之大義，不可廢也，與《孝經》相表裏，其庶矣。顧其書不列于學官，義不講于庠塾，至元而斯道晦蝕久矣。洪惟我太祖高皇帝汛掃腥羶，重開寓縣，驅一世之椎
translation_en:
…manifested in his red slippers went unnoticed by himself. Shun was filial indeed, yet in ordering the General Administration and glorifying the five constant relationships so as to receive the succession of Yao, his loyalty became all the more pure, and thus he was able to achieve a governance in which the people followed their desires. The Duke of Zhou was loyal indeed, yet in skillfully carrying forward the intentions of his forebears and skillfully continuing their undertakings so as to bring to completion the virtue of Kings Wen and Wu, his filial piety became all the more far-reaching, and thus he was able to achieve the blessing of welcoming peaceful equilibrium. That these two sages stand as the pinnacle of human relationships, and that for a thousand ages their achievements in governance have been praised as the ultimate, surely has its reason!

In later ages there came to be a book, the Classic of Filial Piety (Xiaojing). Commentators say it was completed by the hands of Zengzi's disciples; arranged in sequence from the Son of Heaven, feudal lords, high officials and grandees, servicemen, down to the common people, it is divided into eighteen chapters in all. Coming out of the remnants of the秦 burning of the books and subsequent dispersal, although it may not entirely derive from the words of the Master, its teaching of filial piety and display of compliance illuminate the great guiding principles of human life and cannot be altered; it may well be transmitted alongside the other classics. As for the book the Classic of Loyalty (Zhongjing), it came from the work of Ma Rong 馬融 of the Eastern Han; arranged in sequence from the sage ruler, chief minister, hundred artisans, local governors and magistrates, down to the millions of common people, it too was modeled into eighteen chapters. Although the purport of its sections is miscellaneous and not exclusively framed as instruction for ministers and subjects, its encouragement of loyalty and setting forth of teachings illuminate the great duty of subjects and sons and cannot be discarded; it may well serve as the counterpart to the Classic of Filial Piety. Yet this book was not established in the official schools, nor was its meaning expounded in local academies and village schools, so that by the Yuan dynasty this Way had long been obscured and eclipsed.

I reflect with awe upon how our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gao Huangdi), swept away the foul and rank, reopened the realm, and drove a whole generation of mallet-haired…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
結而冠裳之開天立極功何偉也乃其爲
教則
大誥有諭官之詞明孝之章使人不後君不遺
親而大指在於懲惡
資世通訓有民用前民用後使人報其君親
其親而大指在於勸善洋洋
睿謨昭垂海宇佑啓
神聖至宏遠矣
文皇帝際龍乘之運重燕貽之圖製爲
===
聖學心法綱凡有四目凡三十有一言臣道則
欲其致身効勞匪躬匪懈言子道則欲其
慎行其身不辱父母條分縷析真可以爲
萬世法程謂
新命巳申故習未革非以一有衆也
作孝順事實紀帝王則首舜文紀賢哲則首
參季凡二百有七人爲事不同而教天下
以孝者一何備也
章皇帝繼之謂堂陛相隔明良難逢非以倣有
punctuated: 結而冠裳之，開天立極，功何偉也！乃其爲教，則《大誥》有〈諭官〉之詞、〈明孝〉之章，使人不後君、不遺親，而大指在於懲惡；《資世通訓》有〈民用前〉、〈民用後〉，使人報其君、親其親，而大指在於勸善。洋洋睿謨，昭垂海宇，佑啓神聖，至宏遠矣。文皇帝際龍乘之運，重燕貽之圖，製爲《聖學心法》，綱凡有四，目凡三十有一。言臣道，則欲其致身効勞、匪躬匪懈；言子道，則欲其慎行其身、不辱父母。條分縷析，真可以爲萬世法程。謂新命巳申，故習未革，非以一有衆也，作《孝順事實》。紀帝王則首舜、文，紀賢哲則首參、季，凡二百有七人。爲事不同，而教天下以孝者，一何備也！章皇帝繼之，謂堂陛相隔，明良難逢，非以倣有
translation_en:
… mallet-shaped topknots and dressed them in caps and robes, opening up Heaven and establishing the Supreme Standard—how magnificent were his achievements! As for his moral instruction, the Grand Pronouncements (Da gao) includes the words of “Admonishing Officials” and the section on “Clarifying Filial Piety,” causing people not to put their ruler last and not to abandon their parents, with its main thrust lying in punishing evil; the Comprehensive Instructions for Assisting the World (Zishi tongxun) has “The People's Conduct, Part I” and “The People's Conduct, Part II,” causing people to repay their ruler and love their parents, with its main thrust lying in encouraging good. Vast and overflowing are the imperial counsels, shining down across the realm, aiding and enlightening the sacred and sage successors—most grand and far-reaching indeed!

Emperor Wen [the Yongle Emperor], meeting the destiny of mounting the dragon and valuing the plans left for his descendants, composed the Method of the Mind in Imperial Learning (Shengxue xinfa), which has four main principles in all and thirty-one sub-headings. Speaking of the way of the minister, he desired that they devote their lives and exert their efforts, acting unselfishly and tirelessly; speaking of the way of the son, he desired that they conduct themselves prudently and bring no disgrace upon their parents. Divided into clauses and analyzed in detail, it truly can serve as a standard and model for ten thousand generations. Considering that although the new mandate had already been proclaimed, old habits had not yet been reformed—which was not the way to unify the multitude—he composed the True Records of Filial Piety and Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi). In recording emperors and kings, it begins with Shun and King Wen; in recording worthies and sages, it begins with Zeng Shen and Min Ziqian [?], totaling two hundred and seven persons in all. Though their deeds differed, how thorough it was in instructing the world in filial piety!

Emperor Zhang [the Xuande Emperor] succeeded him. Considering that the palace hall and the steps below are separated from one another and that enlightened rulers and worthy ministers rarely meet—which was not the way to admonish [?] those in…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
位也
作歷代臣鑑善可爲法則始於鄭子產惡可
爲戒則始於漢田蚡凡二百八十餘人爲
事不同而教天下以忠者一何惓也又以
爲言行尚遺紀載未備復
命儒臣編輯
五倫全書頒示中外其叙臣道也始於輔德
終於恬退所以補臣鑒之所未及其叙子
道也始於伯奇終於劉氏所以發事實之
===
所未詳
炳煥日月
昭回雲漢要以明彰癉於既往示懲勸于將
來即古帝王之誕告訓迪蔑以加焉
作述相承
後先一轍是故歷十餘祀而
天眷益隆人紀益勅雖有阻山憑海之虓而
輿圖鞏如磐石雖有佞豎逆藩之孽而
宗社安如泰山以綱常素明而民志素定也
punctuated: 位也，作《歷代臣鑑》。善可爲法，則始於鄭子產；惡可爲戒，則始於漢田蚡。凡二百八十餘人，爲事不同，而教天下以忠者一何惓也！又以爲言行尚遺，紀載未備，復命儒臣編輯《五倫全書》，頒示中外。其叙臣道也，始於輔德，終於恬退，所以補《臣鑒》之所未及；其叙子道也，始於伯奇，終於劉氏，所以發《事實》之所未詳。炳煥日月，昭回雲漢，要以明彰癉於既往，示懲勸于將來，即古帝王之誕告訓迪，蔑以加焉。作述相承，後先一轍。是故歷十餘祀而天眷益隆，人紀益勅。雖有阻山憑海之虓，而輿圖鞏如磐石；雖有佞豎逆藩之孽，而宗社安如泰山，以綱常素明而民志素定也。
translation_en: …those in office, he composed the Mirror of Ministers through the Ages (Lidai chenjian 歷代臣鑑). In recording good conduct that could serve as a model, he began with Zichan 子產 of Zheng 鄭; in recording evil conduct that could serve as a warning, he began with Tian Fen 田蚡 of the Han 漢. In all, it comprised more than two hundred and eighty men; though their deeds differed, how earnest he was in instructing the realm in loyalty! Moreover, considering that worthy words and deeds had still been left out and that the records were not yet complete, they further commanded Confucian officials to compile the Complete Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun quanshu 五倫全書) and promulgated it at court and in the provinces. In setting forth the way of the minister, it begins with assisting in virtue and ends with retiring in contentment, thereby supplementing what the Mirror of Ministers had not reached; in setting forth the way of the son, it begins with Boqi 伯奇 and ends with the Liu 劉 clan, thereby bringing to light what the True Accounts of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi 孝順事實) had not detailed. Shining as brightly as the sun and moon and revolving as radiantly as the Milky Way, in sum these works served to clarify praise of the good and condemnation of the wicked in the past, and to set forth warnings and encouragements for the future—even the grand proclamations and instructional guidance of the ancient emperors and kings could not surpass them. Creation and transmission succeeded one another, earlier and later rulers following the same track. Therefore, over more than ten reigns [?], Heaven's favor has grown ever more abundant, and the human moral order has been ever more firmly regulated.
