Although there have been roaring rebels holding fast to mountains and relying on the seas, the imperial territory has remained as solid as a great rock; although there have been the scourges of treacherous eunuchs and rebellious feudatories, the ancestral temples and altars of the state have remained as secure as Mount Tai—because theThree Bonds and Five Constant Virtues have long been clear and the minds of the people have long been settled.

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
今
皇上稟
上聖之資履盈成之運倚任耆宿
咨諏治理謂奉
先之孝在率舊章則討
累朝故實而脩明之而不獨師其作為之迹
事
親之節在奉
慈闈則承
===
兩宮德意而推廓之而不獨謹其問侍之儀至
其遵
憑几之言而勤學親賢重
山陵之禮而
召見面諭我
皇上之以孝先天下者至矣謂股肱元首一體
相須乃
宸翰寵錫荐及輔佐而部臺講讀之臣亦廑
奎畫之頒內治外嚴兩事兼舉乃
punctuated: 今皇上稟上聖之資，履盈成之運，倚任耆宿，咨諏治理。謂奉先之孝在率舊章，則討累朝故實而脩明之，而不獨師其作為之迹；事親之節在奉慈闈，則承兩宮德意而推廓之，而不獨謹其問侍之儀。至其遵憑几之言而勤學親賢，重山陵之禮而召見面諭，我皇上之以孝先天下者至矣。謂股肱元首一體相須，乃宸翰寵錫，荐及輔佐，而部臺講讀之臣亦廑奎畫之頒；內治外嚴，兩事兼舉，乃
translation_en: Now our reigning Emperor, endowed with the natural gifts of a supreme sage and occupying a cycle of fullness and completion, relies upon seasoned elders and consults them on the principles of governance. Deeming that filial devotion in honoring his ancestors lies in following the established statutes, he examines the precedents of successive reigns to restore and clarify them, rather than merely imitating the outward traces of their actions; deeming that the proper observance of serving his parents lies in revering the Maternal Quarters, he receives and expands upon the virtuous intentions of the Two Empresses Dowager, rather than merely being scrupulous in the ceremonies of inquiring after their health and waiting upon them. As for his obeying the testamentary words delivered when the late Emperor leaned upon the armrest by studying diligently and drawing close to the worthy, and his attaching great weight to the rites of the imperial mausoleums by summoning officials to audience and instructing them in person—in leading the realm through filial piety, our Emperor has reached the utmost perfection! Deeming that the limbs and the head form a single body in mutual dependence, he has repeatedly bestowed the gracious gifts of his imperial calligraphy upon his grand counselors, while ministers of the Ministries and the Censorate, as well as the Classics-mat lecturers and readers-in-waiting, have also been honored by the presentation of his imperial brushwork. Deeming that internal governance and external vigilance are two matters to be pursued together, he has…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
綸音嚴飭首及本兵而臣工考覈之後又奉
更始之
諭若其詧吏治廉能而
宴賞特賜
覽除目奏進而銓選
躬臨
皇上之以忠作天下者至矣合而觀之
祖宗之垂訓言教也言教立故人紀明而天下
一於所向
===
主上之建極身教也身教端故人心正而天下
習於所安
神謨之貽由
今日而丕承丕顯
聖政之美率
成憲而不愆不忘故自
踐阼以來
明良之遇相得益章
天人之交孚契孔固九服仰流百司稟度南越
punctuated: 綸音嚴飭，首及本兵，而臣工考覈之後，又奉更始之諭；若其詧吏治廉能，而宴賞特賜，覽除目奏進，而銓選躬臨：皇上之以忠作天下者至矣。合而觀之，祖宗之垂訓，言教也，言教立，故人紀明而天下一於所向；主上之建極，身教也，身教端，故人心正而天下習於所安。神謨之貽，由今日而丕承丕顯；聖政之美，率成憲而不愆不忘。故自踐阼以來，明良之遇，相得益章；天人之交，孚契孔固。九服仰流，百司稟度，南越
translation_en: … the imperial pronouncements gave stern admonitions, beginning first with the Minister of War, and after the evaluation of officials, they again received a decree for a fresh start. As for inspecting the integrity and ability of local governance and specially bestowing banquets and rewards, or reviewing the submitted lists of appointments and personally attending the personnel selections—His Majesty's rousing of the empire to loyalty has reached the utmost! Viewed together, the instructions handed down by the Imperial Ancestors are teaching by words; because teaching by words was established, human moral bonds were made clear and the empire was unified in its direction. The standard of supreme perfection set up by the reigning Sovereign is teaching by personal example; because teaching by personal example is upright, human minds are rectified and the empire is accustomed to peace. The divine counsels bequeathed to us are, from the present day, grandly inherited and grandly manifested; the excellence of sage governance follows the established statutes without error and without neglect. Therefore, since His Majesty ascended the throne, the encounter between an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers has grown ever more illustrious through mutual reinforcement, and the communion between Heaven and Man has been firmly bound in mutual trust. The Nine Domains look up to his influence, the hundred offices take his standards as their rule, the southern Yue…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
勒名於銅柱北狄解辮於玉關山無鳴鏑
之虞海絕揚波之警蓋前史之所未甞談
而
祖宗時之不數見也一時熈恬氣象豈不與重
華元聖度德比隆哉愚生甞詮伏草野竊
觀
皇上躬行節儉被服孝慈鼓舞臣工尊尚往古
真不世出之
主矣執事者乃復進以移孝為忠之說詎非臣
===
子忠愛無巳之心哉夫枹觸響應言所倡
也行百里者半九十言所竟也今
主上率先忠孝天下亦既翕然景從矣然仁人
孝子其理相通君明臣良其機相感承
祖宗父母之貽而不善推其所欲則孝猶歉於
錫類是仁之未及也故好生之德慎徽之
懿萬世稱仁焉而後舜之孝為不匱今
主上尊養極隆孝友克篤矣然而
宗藩之鱗衛寰宇者皆
punctuated: 勒名於銅柱，北狄解辮於玉關，山無鳴鏑之虞，海絕揚波之警，蓋前史之所未甞談，而祖宗時之不數見也。一時熈恬氣象，豈不與重華、元聖度德比隆哉！愚生甞詮伏草野，竊觀皇上躬行節儉，被服孝慈，鼓舞臣工，尊尚往古，真不世出之主矣。執事者乃復進以移孝為忠之說，詎非臣子忠愛無巳之心哉！夫枹觸響應，言所倡也；行百里者半九十，言所竟也。今主上率先忠孝，天下亦既翕然景從矣。然仁人孝子，其理相通；君明臣良，其機相感。承祖宗父母之貽，而不善推其所欲，則孝猶歉於錫類，是仁之未及也。故好生之德、慎徽之懿，萬世稱仁焉，而後舜之孝為不匱。今主上尊養極隆，孝友克篤矣。然而宗藩之鱗衛寰宇者，皆
translation_en:
… inscribe their names on the bronze pillars, and the northern Di unbraid their queues at the Jade Gate. The mountains are free from the peril of whistling arrows, and the seas are clear of the alarm of rising waves. Indeed, this is what former histories have never spoken of, and what was not often seen even in the times of the imperial ancestors. How could the tranquil and flourishing atmosphere of our age not match in virtue and grandeur that of Shun (Chonghua) and the Duke of Zhou (the Great Sage)! As an ignorant student living in obscurity in the countryside, I have privately observed that His Majesty personally practices frugality, clothes himself in filial piety and benevolence, inspires his officials, and reveres antiquity—truly a sovereign of rare appearance across the ages. Yet you, Sir, now further present the doctrine of transforming filial piety into loyalty; is this not out of the boundless loyalty and affection of a minister and son!

When the drumstick strikes, the sound responds: this speaks of how things are initiated. "Of a hundred-li journey, ninety li is only halfway": this speaks of how things are brought to completion. Today, the Sovereign leads the way in loyalty and filial piety, and all under Heaven already follow in harmonious admiration. Yet the humane man and the filial son share a common principle; the enlightened ruler and the worthy minister move one another through a mutual mechanism. If one inherits the legacy of ancestors and parents, yet fails to skillfully extend what they desired, then filial piety still falls short of "bestowing blessings on one's kind," and benevolence has not yet reached its full extent. Therefore, it was only after his virtue of loving life and his excellence in carefully displaying the five teachings were praised as humane for ten thousand generations that the filial piety of Shun became inexhaustible. Today, the Sovereign honors and nourishes his parents to the utmost degree, and is thoroughly devoted to filial piety and fraternal love. Even so, the imperial clansmen who guard the realm like overlapping scales are all…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
祖宗所欲親睦者也寧無有歌行葦而獻之者
乎天下之鰥寡孤獨顛連無告者皆
祖宗之所欲優恤者也豈無有歌鴻鴈而爰及
者乎仁而及此是能體親之心充吾之愛
而天地萬物無不各得其所矣斯不謂善
推其孝哉重股肱心膂之寄而或未究其
所蘊則忠弗獲以自盡是明之未及也故
明保之資和恒之託萬世稱明焉而後周
公之忠爲益顯今
===
主上
會際明良道隆交泰矣然延納雖勤而補牘
執奏之魏徵折柳必諫之程子豈盡皆和
顏色以受之乎綜覈雖嚴而下考之兒寬
豈盡舉僞增之王成豈盡黜乎明而及此
必能以臣之心爲己之心而効忠宣力之
士無不畢竭其知矣斯不謂善作其忠哉
雖然有本焉敬一是也敬則純而私欲不
雜故能弘至仁以成其孝一則公而賢奸
punctuated: 祖宗所欲親睦者也，寧無有歌《行葦》而獻之者乎？天下之鰥寡孤獨、顛連無告者，皆祖宗之所欲優恤者也，豈無有歌《鴻鴈》而爰及者乎？仁而及此，是能體親之心，充吾之愛，而天地萬物無不各得其所矣，斯不謂善推其孝哉？重股肱心膂之寄，而或未究其所蘊，則忠弗獲以自盡，是明之未及也。故明保之資、和恒之託，萬世稱明焉，而後周公之忠爲益顯。今主上會際明良，道隆交泰矣。然延納雖勤，而補牘執奏之魏徵、折柳必諫之程子，豈盡皆和顏色以受之乎？綜覈雖嚴，而下考之兒寬豈盡舉？僞增之王成豈盡黜乎？明而及此，必能以臣之心爲己之心，而効忠宣力之士無不畢竭其知矣，斯不謂善作其忠哉？雖然，有本焉，敬、一是也。敬則純而私欲不雜，故能弘至仁以成其孝；一則公而賢奸
translation_en:
…those with whom the Imperial Ancestors wished to maintain affectionate harmony; could there be no one to sing the ode "Wayside Reeds" (Xingwei) and present it to the throne? The widowers, widows, orphans, the childless, and those in distress with no one to turn to throughout the realm are all those whom the Imperial Ancestors wished to treat with generous compassion; could there be no one to sing the ode "Wild Geese" (Hongyan) so as to extend relief to them? When benevolence reaches this far, one is able to embody the heart of one's parents and fulfill one's own love, so that there is nothing between heaven and earth and among the myriad things that does not find its proper place—can this not be called skillfully extending one's filial piety?

If the ruler places heavy reliance on ministers who serve as his limbs, heart, and backbone, yet perhaps fails to fathom all that they hold within, then their loyalty cannot be fully realized; this is because his discernment has not yet reached far enough. Thus it was only because of King Cheng's reliance on the Duke of Zhou as an enlightened protector and his entrusting to him the harmonizing and perpetuating of the state—for which ten thousand generations have praised the king's discernment—that the loyalty of the Duke of Zhou became ever more manifest. Today His Majesty meets with an era of enlightened rule and worthy ministers, and the Way flourishes in harmonious communion between ruler and minister. Yet although he is diligent in receiving counsel, when it comes to a Wei Zheng 魏徵 who appends memorials and insists on his remonstrances, or a Master Cheng 程子 (Cheng Yi 程頤) who invariably remonstrates even over the snapping of a willow branch, does he always receive them with a gentle countenance? And although his verification of administrative performance is strict, are men like Ni Kuan 兒寬, who received a low rating in merit evaluations, all promoted? Are men like Wang Cheng 王成, who falsely inflated household registers, all dismissed? When discernment reaches this far, the ruler will surely be able to take the hearts of his ministers as his own heart, and gentlemen who devote their loyalty and exert their strength will all exhaust their wisdom without reserve—can this not be called skillfully inspiring their loyalty?

Even so, there is a fundamental basis for this: reverence and oneness. Through reverence, one is pure and unmixed with selfish desires, and therefore able to broaden utmost benevolence so as to perfect one's filial piety; through oneness, one is impartial and the worthy and the wicked…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
不蔽故能運至明以成其忠昔孟氏論大
孝終身慕父母而五十之慕獨歸之大舜
史稱成王將冠朝祖見諸侯而史雍之頌
獨命于周公繼二聖而作者可以勃然興
矣敢以是爲
聖天子純孝勸忠之助
第二問
馬中化
同考試官教諭王批視學乃君人崇儒重道盛
節我
皇上以冲德肇舉是典風敎丕彰士能愉揚休美式闡雅道末復進以
仁孝尤得勸講至意是抱忠愛之忱者敬服敬服
考試官教諭朱批對揚敷暢悉露忠悃而詞
尤卓雅
考試官教授李批考古揚今義精制備
帝王之御世也以立君師之矩存乎教以
端教化之原本于道夫道術之明必有所
自出是故表章之典宜崇焉崇表章所以
punctuated:
不蔽，故能運至明以成其忠。昔孟氏論大孝，終身慕父母，而五十之慕獨歸之大舜；史稱成王將冠，朝祖見諸侯，而史雍之頌獨命于周公。繼二聖而作者，可以勃然興矣。敢以是爲聖天子純孝勸忠之助。

第二問
馬中化
同考試官教諭王批：視學乃君人崇儒重道盛節。我皇上以冲德肇舉是典，風敎丕彰。士能愉揚休美，式闡雅道，末復進以仁孝，尤得勸講至意，是抱忠愛之忱者。敬服，敬服。
考試官教諭朱批：對揚敷暢，悉露忠悃，而詞尤卓雅。
考試官教授李批：考古揚今，義精制備。

帝王之御世也，以立君師之矩存乎教，以端教化之原本于道。夫道術之明，必有所自出，是故表章之典宜崇焉。崇表章所以
translation_en:
… are not obscured, and therefore one can exercise utmost perspicacity to bring loyalty to completion. In former times, when Mencius (Mengshi 孟氏) discussed great filial piety—yearning for one's parents throughout one's whole life—he attributed yearning at the age of fifty solely to the Great Shun. History records that when King Cheng was about to be capped, he paid court to his ancestors and received the feudal lords, while the eulogy recorded by Scribe Yong was commanded solely by the Duke of Zhou. One who arises in succession to these two sages may well be stirred to flourish! I venture to offer this as an aid to the Sacred Son of Heaven in perfecting filial piety and encouraging loyalty.

Second Question
Ma Zhonghua 馬中化

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies (jiaoyu) Wang comments: Inspecting the Imperial University is a grand ceremonial occasion whereby the ruler honors Confucians and reveres the Way. Our Emperor, in his youthful virtue, has newly inaugurated this canon, and moral teaching has been gloriously manifested. This scholar is able to joyfully extol [? 愉揚, for 揄揚] the splendid virtue and set forth the noble Way; at the close, he further presents counsel on benevolence and filial piety, especially grasping the utmost intent of exhortation and lecturing. Truly he is one who cherishes a heart of loyalty and devotion. Respectful admiration, respectful admiration!

Examiner and County Director of Studies (jiaoyu) Zhu comments: His response in praise of the sovereign is fluent and expansive, fully revealing his loyal sincerity, while his diction is especially lofty and refined.

Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies (jiaoshou) Li comments: Examining antiquity and extolling the present, its meaning is subtle and its structure complete.

When emperors and kings govern the world, establishing the standard of ruler and teacher lies in instruction, and rectifying the source of transformative teaching is rooted in the Way. Now, the illumination of the arts of the Way must have that from which it issues forth; therefore, the canons of honoring and commending ought to be exalted. Exalting such commendation is the means by which …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
敬道也而萬古之聖真愈演迆于不窮教
化之行必有所由始是故首善之風宜樹
焉樹首善所以勸學也而四方之標準自
昭布于無外故興秩節脩殷儀禮之文也
其數可陳也隆道術貞教化禮之實也其
義難知也苟不惟其所以實而直循往襲
故盿曰文具而已焉道化謂何耳於乎知
其義而敬守之非
明天子孰能與于斯且夫道彌綸造化周流六
虛者也洋洋乎大哉人主不可不殫心焉
古之所謂道術者惡乎在曰在于聖人堯
舜以帝焉而聖禹湯文武以王焉而聖周
公以相焉而聖蓋聖人未興天下多得一
曲焉以自好自數聖人作而三極之道管
是矣周室衰而詩書微禮樂缺有間孔子
以聖德遭季世要刪詩書述正禮樂因史
記脩春秋以寓王法後之學者言六藝靡
不折中而數千載綱常之理不少恇恇者
punctuated:
敬道也，而萬古之聖真愈演迆于不窮。教化之行，必有所由始，是故首善之風宜樹焉；樹首善所以勸學也，而四方之標準自昭布于無外。故興秩節、脩殷儀，禮之文也，其數可陳也；隆道術、貞教化，禮之實也，其義難知也。苟不惟其所以實，而直循往襲故，盿曰文具而已焉，道化謂何耳！於乎！知其義而敬守之，非明天子孰能與于斯？

且夫道，彌綸造化、周流六虛者也，洋洋乎大哉，人主不可不殫心焉！古之所謂道術者，惡乎在？曰：在于聖人。堯、舜以帝焉而聖，禹、湯、文、武以王焉而聖，周公以相焉而聖。蓋聖人未興，天下多得一曲焉以自好；自數聖人作，而三極之道管是矣。周室衰而《詩》、《書》微，禮、樂缺有間。孔子以聖德遭季世，要刪《詩》、《書》，述正禮、樂，因史記脩《春秋》以寓王法。後之學者言六藝，靡不折中；而數千載綱常之理不少恇恇者，
translation_en:
… revere the Way, so that the sagely truth of ten thousand ages extends ever further without end. For moral transformation to take effect, there must be a place from which it begins; therefore, a model of supreme goodness at the capital ought to be established. Establishing this model of supreme goodness is the means to encourage learning, so that the standard for the four quarters is naturally proclaimed without limit. Thus, instituting ordered regulations and cultivating grand ceremonies are the outward forms of ritual—their technicalities can be set forth; exalting the art of the Way and rectifying moral transformation are the substance of ritual—their deeper meaning is difficult to know. If one does not reflect upon what constitutes their substance, and merely follows the past and repeats old routines, looking upon them [?] as mere formal trappings, what then becomes of transformation through the Way! Alas! To understand their meaning and reverently uphold it—who but an enlightened Son of Heaven could be capable of this?

Moreover, the Way encompasses and orders creation and circulates throughout the six reaches of space. Vast and boundless, how great it is! A ruler of men cannot fail to devote his whole heart to it. Where did what the ancients called the art of the Way reside? One says: it resided in the sages. Yao and Shun were sages as emperors; Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu were sages as kings; the Duke of Zhou was a sage as a minister. Indeed, before the sages arose, people in the world mostly grasped a single partial aspect and delighted in it for themselves; once these several sages appeared, the Way of the Three Ultimates was encompassed therein. When the House of Zhou declined, the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu) grew obscure, and Rites (Li) and Music (Yue) fell into disrepair for a time. Confucius, possessing sagely virtue yet meeting with a degenerate age, summarized and edited the Odes and Documents, transmitted and rectified the Rites and Music, and, drawing upon historical records, compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) in order to lodge within it the laws of true kingship. Later scholars who spoke of the Six Arts all took him as their standard of judgment; and that for several thousand years the principles of the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues have not in the least been shaken or confused [?] …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皆其作經垂訓之功也自孔子出而數聖
人之道又一是矣所謂儒術之宗萬世之
師非耶在昔隆古莫不有學而祀於學者
載籍無稽焉爰周郅隆兼立四代以舜禹
湯文爲先聖而取左右四聖者爲先師合
饗之至如素王特祀正道大興則昉于炎
漢盛于隋唐釋奠之禮遂爲千百代令典
而世主以垂聲彤管有褒述矣然愚又甞
遡而攷之上庠下庠肇自有虞鄉學國學
===
分於三代辟雝成均孰非天子之學乎顧
總三代而名之則曰辟雝而辟明雍和之
意寓總五帝而名之則曰成均而成行均
習之意存此其義之各有攸在也上丁仲
丁命以樂正先聖先師祭于四時釋奠釋
菜孰非王者之禮乎顧釋奠于禮爲稍隆
而有樂有牲幣釋菜于禮爲甚略而不舞
不授器斯其制之不能無辨也此其大較
也乃若視學之典著于月令詳于世子而
punctuated: 皆其作經垂訓之功也。自孔子出，而數聖人之道又一是矣。所謂儒術之宗、萬世之師，非耶？在昔隆古，莫不有學，而祀於學者，載籍無稽焉。爰周郅隆，兼立四代，以舜、禹、湯、文爲先聖，而取左右四聖者爲先師，合饗之。至如素王特祀，正道大興，則昉于炎漢，盛于隋、唐，釋奠之禮遂爲千百代令典，而世主以垂聲，彤管有褒述矣。然愚又甞遡而攷之，上庠、下庠，肇自有虞；鄉學、國學，分於三代。辟雝、成均，孰非天子之學乎？顧總三代而名之則曰辟雝，而辟明雍和之意寓；總五帝而名之則曰成均，而成行均習之意存，此其義之各有攸在也。上丁、仲丁，命以樂正，先聖、先師，祭于四時。釋奠、釋菜，孰非王者之禮乎？顧釋奠于禮爲稍隆，而有樂有牲幣；釋菜于禮爲甚略，而不舞不授器，斯其制之不能無辨也。此其大較也。乃若視學之典，著于《月令》，詳于《世子》，而
translation_en: …is all due to his merit in composing the Classics and handing down teachings. Since Confucius appeared, the Way of those several sages was once again unified in him. Is he not what is called the patriarch of Confucian learning and the teacher of ten thousand generations? In the flourishing antiquity of old, there was no era without schools, yet as for who was sacrificed to in the schools, there is no record in the texts to verify it. Coming to the supreme flourishing of the Zhou, they concurrently established the schools of the four dynasties, taking Shun, Yu, Tang, and King Wen as the Former Sages, and selecting those who assisted the four sages as the Former Teachers, offering joint sacrifices to them. As for the special sacrifices to the Uncrowned King [Confucius] and the great flourishing of the Orthodox Way, this began in the fiery Han and flourished in the Sui and Tang. The ritual of the Libation Sacrifice (shidian) thereupon became a fine canon for hundreds and thousands of generations, whereby reigning monarchs handed down their renown and the red brushes of female historians recorded praiseworthy accounts. Yet I have also traced back and examined the matter: the Upper School (shangxiang) and Lower School (xiaxiang) originated with Yu [Shun]; the local schools (xiangxue) and capital schools (guoxue) were differentiated in the Three Dynasties. Were not the Circular Moat (biyong) and the Equalizing Academy (chengjun) both schools of the Son of Heaven? However, when naming them collectively across the Three Dynasties, it was called Biyong, wherein the meaning of bright clarity (bi) and harmonious peace (yong) was lodged; when naming them collectively across the Five Emperors, it was called Chengjun, wherein the meaning of perfecting conduct (cheng) and equalizing practice (jun) was preserved. Thus each name had that wherein its significance lay. On the first ding day and the second ding day [of the month], commands were given to the Director of Music (yuezheng), and the Former Sages and Former Teachers were sacrificed to in the four seasons. Were not the Libation Sacrifice (shidian) and the Vegetable Offering (shicai) both rituals of the true king? However, the Libation Sacrifice is somewhat grander in ritual, having music as well as sacrificial animals and silk; the Vegetable Offering is much simpler in ritual, neither performing dances nor handing out ritual implements. In this their institutions cannot be without distinction. This is the general outline. As for the canon of inspecting the Imperial School, it is set forth in the Monthly Ordinances (Yueling), detailed in the King Wen as Heir Apparent (Shizi), and…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
莫備于大戴禮保傅之一篇按古視學大
都主于養老東京而後此禮浸亡而或以
釋奠或以講經則猶承師問道之遺意焉
夫問道于上而所以敎天下者自王都達
之九有若桴觸而響應風行而草偃矣故
古之人一舉事而衆皆喻于敎者此物此
志也鎬京辟廱無思不服說者謂其講學
行禮有以致之烝哉武王誠萬古稱烈矣
歷選羣辟以迄于今若漢之光武親臨觀
===
饗詔諸生雅吹擊磬而盡日乃罷明帝袒
割三雍會諸儒執經問難而正坐自講唐
之高祖幸國學召博士徐文遠發春秋題
而異其占對太宗觀釋奠詔祭酒孔穎達
講孝經而嘉其進頌宋之太宗命李覺孫
奭講泰卦說命各有味于其言仁宗令直
講馬龜符說論語一篇因閱禮圖于東序
之數君者皆一世之英也竝能尊未有之
至聖煥可述之文章豈不舄奕異代聲施
punctuated: 莫備于《大戴禮·保傅》之一篇。按古視學，大都主于養老，東京而後，此禮浸亡。而或以釋奠，或以講經，則猶承師問道之遺意焉。夫問道于上，而所以敎天下者，自王都達之九有，若桴觸而響應，風行而草偃矣。故古之人一舉事而衆皆喻于敎者，此物此志也。「鎬京辟廱，無思不服。」說者謂其講學行禮有以致之。烝哉武王！誠萬古稱烈矣。歷選羣辟，以迄于今，若漢之光武親臨觀饗，詔諸生雅吹擊磬，而盡日乃罷；明帝袒割三雍，會諸儒執經問難，而正坐自講；唐之高祖幸國學，召博士徐文遠發《春秋》題，而異其占對；太宗觀釋奠，詔祭酒孔穎達講《孝經》，而嘉其進頌；宋之太宗命李覺、孫奭講《泰卦》、《說命》，各有味于其言；仁宗令直講馬龜符說《論語》一篇，因閱《禮圖》于東序。之數君者，皆一世之英也，竝能尊未有之至聖，煥可述之文章，豈不舄奕異代，聲施…
translation_en:
…is nowhere more complete than in the "Protector and Tutor" ("Baofu") chapter of the Record of Rites of the Elder Dai (Da Dai Li). Examining the ancient imperial visits to the state school, they were mostly centered on nourishing the aged; after the Eastern Capital [of the Later Han], this ritual gradually died out. Yet whether through the ceremonial libations to the sages or through lecturing on the Classics, they still preserved the lingering intent of honoring teachers and inquiring into the Way. Now, when inquiry into the Way takes place at the top, the means by which all under Heaven is instructed reaches from the royal capital out to the Nine Regions, just as an echo responds to the strike of a drumstick, or as grass bends before the blowing wind. Therefore, that the ancients could undertake a single affair and have the multitude all understand their instruction was due to this very practice and this very intent. "In the capital of Hao, with its Biyong hall, there were none who did not submit in their thoughts." Commentators say that it was through lecturing on learning and performing the rites that this was brought about. Splendid indeed was King Wu! Truly his illustrious achievements are praised for ten thousand generations.

Selecting from among the various sovereigns down to the present: Emperor Guangwu of the Han personally attended to observe the banquet, commanding the students to play elegant wind music and strike the stone chimes, ending only when the day was done; Emperor Ming bared his arm to slice the meat at the Three Halls (Sanyong), assembled the Confucian scholars to hold the Classics and pose difficult questions, and sat upright to lecture himself. Emperor Gaozu of the Tang visited the National University, summoned the Erudite (boshi) Xu Wenyuan to expound on themes from the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), and marveled at his impromptu replies; Emperor Taizong observed the ceremonial libations, ordered the Libationer (jijiu) Kong Yingda to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety (Xiaojing), and praised the panegyric he presented. Emperor Taizong of the Song commanded Li Jue and Sun Shi to lecture on the "Tai" hexagram and the "Charge to Yue" ("Yueming"), finding deep meaning in each of their words; Emperor Renzong ordered the Lecturer (zhijiang) Ma Guifu to explain a chapter of the Analects (Lunyu), and thereupon inspected the Illustrations of the Rites (Litu) in the Eastern Wing (Dongxu). These several rulers were all heroes of their ages; all were able to venerate the unprecedented Supreme Sage and make resplendent a body of culture worthy of transmission. Does not their glory shine across different eras, their renown extending…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
到今哉然意雖媺而出之未醇事足誇而
實則不副篤信讖文始開佛教律以聖人
中正之道則悖矣家法罔正天倫負慙繩
以聖人脩齊之道則咈矣曲宴賦詩釣魚
興詠概以聖人端本之道則逕庭矣即禮
聖于宮墻講業于黌舍要亦脩故事而飾
榮觀耳又何惑其治功之不足軼休三五
乎洪惟我
皇上濬哲夙生
徇齊神授以
茂齡宅丕后纂
二祖
八宗之基緒是堯舜禹湯文武之統也以
至德躬師帥暢九垓八埏之文明是堯舜禹湯
文武周孔之道也
踐阼以來
道化旁皇函夏寧謐海內羣生靡不受祉而
鼓攲于大順是唐虞夏商成周之治也
punctuated:
到今哉？然意雖媺而出之未醇，事足誇而實則不副。篤信讖文，始開佛教，律以聖人中正之道，則悖矣；家法罔正，天倫負慙，繩以聖人脩齊之道，則咈矣；曲宴賦詩，釣魚興詠，概以聖人端本之道，則逕庭矣。即禮聖于宮墻，講業于黌舍，要亦脩故事而飾榮觀耳，又何惑其治功之不足軼休三五乎？
洪惟我皇上，濬哲夙生，徇齊神授。以茂齡宅丕后，纂二祖、八宗之基緒，是堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之統也；以至德躬師帥，暢九垓八埏之文明，是堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武、周、孔之道也。踐阼以來，道化旁皇，函夏寧謐，海內羣生靡不受祉而鼓攲于大順，是唐、虞、夏、商、成周之治也。
translation_en:
…down to the present day? Yet although their intentions were admirable, what issued from them was not pure; although their deeds were worthy of boasting, the reality did not match. Deeply believing in prognosticatory texts and first introducing Buddhism—when judged by the sages' Way of centrality and correctness, this was perverse! Failing to rectify family discipline and bearing shame in natural human relationships—when measured by the sages' Way of self-cultivation and family regulation, this was contrary! Composing poetry at private banquets and chanting verses while fishing—when weighed by the sages' Way of rectifying the fundamental, this was poles apart! Even though they paid ritual homage to the Sage within the precincts of his temple and lectured on scholarship in the school buildings, in sum they were merely performing routine precedents and adorning a glorious spectacle; what wonder is it, then, that their achievements in governance were insufficient to surpass the splendor of the Three Emperors and Five Sovereigns?

Vast indeed is Our Emperor: profound wisdom was his from birth, and swift comprehension was divinely bestowed upon him. Ascending to the great sovereignty in his flourishing youth, he carries on the foundational lineage of the Two Ancestors and Eight Preceding Emperors—this is the succession of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. Leading in person as ruler and teacher through supreme virtue, he spreads civilization throughout the nine heavens and eight extremities of the earth—this is the Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius. Since ascending the throne, his moral transformation has pervaded everywhere, the Chinese realm has been tranquil and at peace, and all living beings within the seas have without exception received blessings and rejoiced in great harmony—this is the governance of Tang, Yu, Xia, Shang, and Perfect Zhou.

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖學日新寒燠靡間公孤晝接注倚彌殷
降諭臣工定百官之準
嘉納圖說勤
乙夜之觀
御製一十二條而儆誡昭
命書四箴六箴而顧諟備迺者
車駕幸大學釋奠
先師
萬乘躬臨增輝俎豆偉儀也張幄橫經儒臣進
===
講文武大吏環侍而拱聽壯觀也
召三氏于闕里
賜師生之
璽書而錫宴錫鏹幣賚予頻蕃
湛恩也隆師重道章教樹風是以功羨于五
帝名冠于三王而漢唐宋諸君方玆褊矣
愚也萬里草澤守窔奧而未睹天庭雖欲
竭精揚厲安知前後而執事乃求所以靖
獻者于鯫生不左計與顧帝王之道集于
punctuated:
聖學日新，寒燠靡間，公孤晝接，注倚彌殷；降諭臣工，定百官之準；嘉納圖說，勤乙夜之觀；御製一十二條，而儆誡昭；命書《四箴》、《六箴》，而顧諟備。迺者，車駕幸大學，釋奠先師。萬乘躬臨，增輝俎豆，偉儀也；張幄橫經，儒臣進講，文武大吏環侍而拱聽，壯觀也；召三氏于闕里，賜師生之璽書，而錫宴、錫鏹幣，賚予頻蕃，湛恩也。隆師重道，章教樹風，是以功羨于五帝，名冠于三王，而漢、唐、宋諸君方玆褊矣。
愚也，萬里草澤，守窔奧而未睹天庭，雖欲竭精揚厲，安知前後？而執事乃求所以靖獻者于鯫生，不左計與？顧帝王之道，集于
translation_en:
His sacred learning is renewed day by day, without interruption through cold or heat, and He receives the Three Dukes and Three Solitaries during the day, relying upon them ever more earnestly; He issues edicts to His officials and functionaries, establishing the standards for the hundred offices; He graciously accepts the Illustrated Explanations (Tushuo), diligently perusing them into the second watch of the night; He has personally composed the Twelve Articles, making admonitions clear; and He has commanded the transcription of the Four Admonitions (Sizhen) and the Six Admonitions (Liuzhen), making constant mindfulness of Heaven's bright mandate complete. Recently, the Imperial Carriage visited the National University to perform the libation sacrifice to the Former Teacher. The Lord of Ten Thousand Chariots attended in person, adding luster to the ritual vessels—a magnificent ceremony! Canopies were spread and the Classics laid open as erudite officials advanced to lecture, while senior civil and military officials stood in attendance around Him and listened with folded hands—a grand spectacle! He summoned the descendants of the three families from Queli, bestowed an imperial letter under the dynastic seal upon the instructors and students, and granted banquets as well as strings of cash and silk, showering them with frequent and abundant gifts—profound grace! By honoring teachers and revering the Way, making education illustrious and establishing moral customs, His achievements surpass those of the Five Emperors and His renown crowns that of the Three Kings, so that in comparison with this, the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties appear narrow indeed.

Ignorant as I am, dwelling in the rustic marshes ten thousand li away, keeping to a humble corner without ever having beheld the Heavenly Court, even if I wished to exhaust my energies in extolling His majesty, how could I know the proper sequence of things? Yet Your Excellency seeks from a petty scholar like me the means to make a loyal offering to the throne—is this not a mistaken calculation? Nevertheless, the Way of the Emperors and Kings was synthesized in…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
孔子而
皇上今日之所嚴事而禮之者爲是道也愚生
甄育
熈世習先聖之術亦知有孔子而已矣無巳
則持此而効之乎何也君道多矣而其大
者能外敬天法祖兩事哉昔孔子嘗以告
魯君曰仁人不過乎物孝子不過乎物是
故事親如事天事天如事親善乎其言之
也夫物實理也實理誠也一誠立而脩身
===
事親知人知天靡不具矣此道術之妙聖
學之要君人者察此故帝王不難侔而治
易幾也
皇上德象重玄孝奉
兩宮
郊祀必親星異虔禱而天變畏脩復史職
躬臨銓授而
祖憲明仁孝之道豈尠于
皇上哉惟設誠于內而致行之則在
punctuated: 孔子，而皇上今日之所嚴事而禮之者，爲是道也。愚生甄育熈世，習先聖之術，亦知有孔子而已矣。無巳，則持此而効之乎！何也？君道多矣，而其大者能外敬天、法祖兩事哉？昔孔子嘗以告魯君曰：「仁人不過乎物，孝子不過乎物。是故事親如事天，事天如事親。」善乎其言之也！夫物，實理也；實理，誠也。一誠立而脩身、事親、知人、知天靡不具矣。此道術之妙，聖學之要。君人者察此，故帝王不難侔而治易幾也。皇上德象重玄，孝奉兩宮，郊祀必親，星異虔禱，而天變畏；脩復史職，躬臨銓授，而祖憲明。仁孝之道，豈尠于皇上哉？惟設誠于內而致行之，則在
translation_en: … Confucius, and what His Majesty today reverently serves and honors with ritual is precisely this Way. Born and nurtured in a prosperous age, and practicing the arts of the former sages, this ignorant student also knows only of Confucius. If I must speak, then let me hold fast to this and offer it up! Why is this? The ways of rulership are many, yet can the greatest of them lie outside the two matters of revering Heaven and modeling oneself on the Ancestors? Long ago, Confucius once told the ruler of Lu: "The humane man does not err with respect to things; the filial son does not err with respect to things. Therefore, serving one's parents is like serving Heaven, and serving Heaven is like serving one's parents." How excellent are these words! Now, "things" means real principle, and real principle is sincerity. Once sincerity is established, cultivating the self, serving one's parents, knowing men, and knowing Heaven are all without exception complete. This is the subtlety of the Way and its arts, and the essence of sage learning. One who rules over men examines this; therefore, it is not difficult to equal the Five Emperors and Three Kings, and good governance is easy to attain. His Majesty's virtue resembles the profound heavens, and he filially serves the Two Palaces [the Empresses Dowager]. He unfailingly attends the suburban sacrifices in person, prays devoutly upon the appearance of celestial anomalies, and stands in awe of the portents of Heaven; he has restored the offices of the court historians, personally attends the selection and appointment of officials, and renders bright the institutions of the Imperial Ancestors. How could the Way of humanity and filial piety be lacking in His Majesty? Yet establishing sincerity within and carrying it out to the utmost rests upon…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖心益加之意爾誠思天之命難諶而涉冰之
懼不輟于慮天之怒易干而戲豫之惕不
替于思天之視聽易忽而若保之懷不弛
于念自出入起居以及命令賞罰常若上
帝臨汝日監在玆焉斯天下之至仁也誠
思
祖宗之德澤不可不培務敦大以成裕
祖宗之法度不可不飭務明作以崇功
祖宗之遺體不可不愛務保身以保民自
===
深宮獨行以至
大庭廣衆常如在于其上在于左右焉斯天
下之至孝也允若時則孔子對君之精蘊
我
皇上潛孚而身體之若挹尼父于千載而與之
相授受講勸不虛誦釋奠非彌文將
天眷永膺
先猷克紹鞏億萬年之
國祚而永固之矣書生之譚無甚高論執事
punctuated: 聖心益加之意爾。誠思天之命難諶，而涉冰之懼不輟于慮；天之怒易干，而戲豫之惕不替于思；天之視聽易忽，而若保之懷不弛于念。自出入起居，以及命令賞罰，常若上帝臨汝，日監在玆焉，斯天下之至仁也。誠思祖宗之德澤不可不培，務敦大以成裕；祖宗之法度不可不飭，務明作以崇功；祖宗之遺體不可不愛，務保身以保民。自深宮獨行，以至大庭廣衆，常如在于其上、在于左右焉，斯天下之至孝也。允若時，則孔子對君之精蘊，我皇上潛孚而身體之，若挹尼父于千載而與之相授受，講勸不虛誦，釋奠非彌文。將天眷永膺，先猷克紹，鞏億萬年之國祚而永固之矣。書生之譚，無甚高論，執事
translation_en: … the Sacred Mind to give them ever greater heed. Truly reflect that the Mandate of Heaven is hard to rely upon, and let the dread of treading upon thin ice never cease in Your deliberations; that the wrath of Heaven is easily provoked, and let vigilance against idle amusement never slacken in Your thoughts; that the sight and hearing of Heaven are easily overlooked, and let the solicitude of caring for the people as if tending an infant never relax in Your mind. From going out, coming in, and daily conduct, to issuing commands, granting rewards, and meting out punishments, always act as though the Supreme Lord were approaching You and daily inspecting You right here—this is the ultimate benevolence in the world. Truly reflect that the virtuous legacy and grace of the Imperial Ancestors must not go uncultivated, striving for generous magnanimity so as to achieve abundance; that the laws and institutions of the Imperial Ancestors must not go unrectified, striving for enlightened exertion so as to exalt achievements; that the body bequeathed by the Imperial Ancestors must not go uncherished, striving to preserve Your person so as to preserve the people. From solitary conduct in the deep palace to appearing before great assemblies in the grand court, always act as though they were above You and at Your left and right—this is the ultimate filial piety in the world. If indeed it be thus, then the profound essence of Confucius's reply to his ruler will be silently comprehended and personally embodied by Our Emperor, as if greeting Father Ni across a thousand years and engaging in mutual transmission and reception with him. The classical lectures and exhortations will not be empty recitations, and the sacrificial offerings to the First Teacher will not be mere ornate formalities. Thus will Heaven's favor be forever received, the plans of the Imperial Ancestors be ably continued, and the dynastic fortune of hundreds of millions of years be consolidated and made eternally secure. The talk of a mere scholar holds no very lofty discourse; Your Excellency …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
能毋以下體否
第三問
金輝漢
同考試官教諭單批天道難知歲差久無定法
此作考究詳明議論精確末歸重于持敬法天尤得
治曆之本宜錄以式
考試官教諭朱批博雅之學精覈之論
考試官教授李批諸家異同剖析明盡
曆法之難言也久矣天道無端惟數可以
===
推其機天道至妙因數可以明其理是故
理因數顯者也數從理出者也理數可相
倚而不可相離者也治曆以正天時因時
以興民事而帝王爲治之先務在是矣何
則日月之運行星辰之次舍凡可推步而
知者亘古今而不變者也日月有盈縮朓
朒之不齊焉星辰有遲留疾伏之不一焉
往來出入于二道之間者雖竭天下之智
巧而不能盡者也于天運有常之中而參
punctuated:
能毋以下體否？
第三問
金輝漢
同考試官教諭單批：天道難知，歲差久無定法。此作考究詳明，議論精確，末歸重于持敬法天，尤得治曆之本，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭朱批：博雅之學，精覈之論。
考試官教授李批：諸家異同，剖析明盡。
曆法之難言也久矣。天道無端，惟數可以推其機；天道至妙，因數可以明其理。是故理因數顯者也，數從理出者也，理數可相倚而不可相離者也。治曆以正天時，因時以興民事，而帝王爲治之先務在是矣。何則？日月之運行，星辰之次舍，凡可推步而知者，亘古今而不變者也。日月有盈縮朓朒之不齊焉，星辰有遲留疾伏之不一焉，往來出入于二道之間者，雖竭天下之智巧而不能盡者也。于天運有常之中，而參
translation_en:
…will Your Excellencies not discard it like the lower roots of a plant?

Third Policy Question
Jin Huihan 金輝漢
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu 教諭) Shan 單: The Way of Heaven is difficult to know, and for the precession of the equinoxes there has long been no fixed method. This essay's investigation is detailed and clear, and its arguments are precise and accurate. At the end, it places prime importance on maintaining reverence and modeling oneself on Heaven, which especially grasps the fundamental basis of regulating the calendar. It should be recorded as a model answer.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhu 朱: Broad and refined learning; precise and verified argumentation.
Comment by Examiner Instructor (jiaoshou 教授) Li 李: The similarities and differences among the various schools are analyzed clearly and exhaustively.

Calendrical methods have long been difficult to speak of. The Way of Heaven has no beginning or end, and only through numbers can one calculate its mechanisms; the Way of Heaven is supremely subtle, and through numbers one can illuminate its principles. Therefore, principle is made manifest through numbers, and numbers emerge from principle; principle and numbers can rely upon each other and cannot be separated from one another. Regulating the calendar to rectify the seasons of Heaven, and following the seasons to promote the affairs of the people—herein lies the foremost task of emperors and kings in governing. Why is this so? The revolutions of the sun and moon and the zodiacal mansions of the stars and constellations—all that can be known through calculation and pacing—remain unchanged from antiquity to the present. Yet the sun and moon have irregularities of acceleration and retardation, and of early and late visibility at the margins of the month; the stars and planets have variations of slowness, stationariness, swiftness, and occultation. Their comings and goings, emerging and entering between the ecliptic and the lunar path, are things that cannot be exhausted even if one expends all the wisdom and ingenuity in the world. Within the constancy of Heaven's movements, to consult…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之隨時變通之術驗之以陰陽寒暑之氣
積之以絲秒毫忽之數其于曆也庶幾乎
自黄帝命羲和占日常儀占月車區占星
象大撓作甲子而容成總其術曆所自始
也少昊使玄鳥氏司分伯趙氏司至青鳥
氏司啟丹鳥氏司閉而鳳鳥氏爲曆正法
所由傳也顓頊命南正仲司天北正黎司
地而建孟春爲元是爲曆宗帝堯使羲仲
叔主春夏和仲叔主秋冬以閏月定四時
===
是爲曆紀舜察璣衡禹衍疇範周官設馮
相保章古之帝王所以奉若天道者其法
雖不盡傳其意固可得而識矣然古未有
閏也至堯命羲和而後置閏閏法立則四
時之氣候不忒矣古未有歲差也至晉虞
喜諸人而後立差差法立則七政之躔度
不爽矣二者相用而不可偏廢者也古人
改曆者無慮數十家由黄帝訖秦來凡六
改惟史官喪紀疇人子弟分散春秋因魯
punctuated:
之隨時變通之術，驗之以陰陽寒暑之氣，積之以絲秒毫忽之數，其于曆也庶幾乎！

自黄帝命羲和占日、常儀占月、車區占星象、大撓作甲子，而容成總其術，曆所自始也。少昊使玄鳥氏司分、伯趙氏司至、青鳥氏司啟、丹鳥氏司閉，而鳳鳥氏爲曆正，法所由傳也。顓頊命南正仲司天、北正黎司地，而建孟春爲元，是爲曆宗。帝堯使羲仲、叔主春夏，和仲、叔主秋冬，以閏月定四時，是爲曆紀。舜察璣衡，禹衍疇範，周官設馮相、保章，古之帝王所以奉若天道者，其法雖不盡傳，其意固可得而識矣。

然古未有閏也，至堯命羲和而後置閏；閏法立，則四時之氣候不忒矣。古未有歲差也，至晉虞喜諸人而後立差；差法立，則七政之躔度不爽矣。二者相用而不可偏廢者也。

古人改曆者無慮數十家。由黄帝訖秦來，凡六改。惟史官喪紀，疇人子弟分散，《春秋》因魯
translation_en:
…with techniques of adapting to the times, verifying them through the vital breaths of yin and yang, cold and heat, and accumulating them by the minute measures of threads, seconds, hairs, and fractions, one comes close indeed to mastering the calendar!

From the time the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi 黄帝) commanded Xihe 羲和 to divine the sun, Changyi 常儀 to divine the moon, Chequ 車區 to divine the stars and constellations, and Danao 大撓 to devise the sexagenary cycle (jiazi 甲子), while Rongcheng 容成 synthesized their techniques—this was where the calendar began. Shaohao 少昊 appointed the Dark Bird Clan (Xuanniao shi 玄鳥氏) to preside over the equinoxes, the Shrike Clan (Bozhao shi 伯趙氏) to preside over the solstices, the Green Bird Clan (Qingniao shi 青鳥氏) to preside over the beginnings of spring and summer, and the Red Bird Clan (Danniao shi 丹鳥氏) to preside over the beginnings of autumn and winter, while the Phoenix Clan (Fengniao shi 鳳鳥氏) served as Director of the Calendar (Lizheng 曆正)—this was how the methods were transmitted. Zhuanxu 顓頊 commanded Zhong 仲, Rector of the South (Nanzheng 南正), to preside over Heaven, and Li 黎, Rector of the North (Beizheng 北正), to preside over Earth, establishing the first month of spring as the beginning of the year—this was the ancestor of calendars. Emperor Yao 堯 appointed Xi Zhong 羲仲 and Xi Shu 羲叔 to take charge of spring and summer, and He Zhong 和仲 and He Shu 和叔 to take charge of autumn and winter, using the intercalary month to fix the four seasons—this was the standard of the calendar. Shun 舜 observed the armillary sphere and sighting tube (jiheng 璣衡), Yu 禹 elaborated the categories of the Great Plan (Choufan 疇範), and the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan 周官) established the Astrologer-Observers (Fengxiang 馮相) and Imperial Astrologers (Baozhang 保章). How the ancient emperors and kings reverently accorded with the Way of Heaven—even if their methods have not been transmitted in full, their intent can certainly be grasped and understood.

Yet in antiquity there was no intercalation; only when Yao commanded Xi and He was intercalation instituted. Once the method of intercalation was established, the seasonal nodes of the four seasons did not err. In antiquity there was no precession of the equinoxes (suicha 歲差); only with Yu Xi 虞喜 and others in the Jin dynasty was precession established. Once the method of precession was established, the orbital degrees of the Seven Regulators (qizheng 七政) did not go astray. The two operate together and neither can be neglected in favor of the other.

Among the ancients, those who reformed the calendar numbered roughly several dozen schools. From the Yellow Emperor down to the Qin dynasty, there were six reforms in all. However, the official historians lost their records, the descendants of the hereditary astronomers scattered, and the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) followed the Lu…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
曆而譏置閏之差秦曆無定法而置閏常
在十月之後是三代至秦巳非黄帝之舊
矣由漢高祖訖漢末凡五改張蒼用顓帝
曆司馬遷作太初曆劉歆作三統曆李梵
作四分曆劉洪作乾象曆可謂備矣而惟
太初爲善蓋其說本于鍾律以黄鍾八十
一分爲日法復自前曆上元推之得閼逢
攝提格之歲爲甲子冬至日月如合璧五
星如連珠而晦朔弦朢不爽毫髮當時一
===
十七家之疏遠者悉罷矣由魏文帝訖隋
末凡十三改由唐高祖訖周末凡十六改
晉有春秋長曆杜預之長慶曆何承天之
元嘉新曆崔浩之五寅元曆馬重績之調
元曆隋劉焯之皇極曆唐高祖有傅仁均
曆高宗有李淳風曆開元有一行大衍曆
代宗有寳應五紀曆徐承嗣有建中正元
曆徐昂有元和宣明曆穆宗時有長慶曆
宗時有景福崇元曆周王朴有欽天曆可
punctuated: 曆而譏置閏之差，秦曆無定法而置閏常在十月之後，是三代至秦，巳非黄帝之舊矣。由漢高祖訖漢末凡五改：張蒼用《顓帝曆》，司馬遷作《太初曆》，劉歆作《三統曆》，李梵作《四分曆》，劉洪作《乾象曆》，可謂備矣，而惟《太初》爲善。蓋其說本于鍾律，以黄鍾八十一分爲日法，復自前曆上元推之，得閼逢攝提格之歲爲甲子冬至，日月如合璧，五星如連珠，而晦朔弦朢不爽毫髮，當時一十七家之疏遠者悉罷矣。由魏文帝訖隋末凡十三改，由唐高祖訖周末凡十六改。晉有《春秋長曆》、杜預之《長慶曆》，何承天之《元嘉新曆》，崔浩之《五寅元曆》，馬重績之《調元曆》，隋劉焯之《皇極曆》，唐高祖有傅仁均曆，高宗有李淳風曆，開元有一行《大衍曆》，代宗有《寳應五紀曆》，徐承嗣有《建中正元曆》，徐昂有《元和宣明曆》，穆宗時有《長慶曆》，宗時有《景福崇元曆》，周王朴有《欽天曆》，可
translation_en: … calendar and criticized the discrepancies in its placement of intercalary months. The Qin calendar lacked a fixed method and consistently placed the intercalary month after the tenth month; thus, from the Three Dynasties down to the Qin, it was already no longer the old system of the Yellow Emperor. From Emperor Gaozu of Han down to the end of the Han, there were five reforms in all: Zhang Cang 張蒼 used the Zhuanxu Calendar (Zhuandi li), Sima Qian 司馬遷 created the Grand Inception Calendar (Taichu li), Liu Xin 劉歆 created the Three Sequences Calendar (Santong li), Li Fan 李梵 created the Quarter-Remainder Calendar (Sifen li), and Liu Hong 劉洪 created the Uranic Manifestation Calendar (Qianxiang li). These could be called comprehensive, yet only the Grand Inception Calendar was considered excellent. This is because its theory was rooted in the pitch-pipes, taking the eighty-one parts of the Yellow Bell (huangzhong) pitch-pipe as the daily denominator (rifa). Calculating back to the High Epoch (shangyuan) of the previous calendars, it obtained the winter solstice on the jiazi day in a year of E'feng Shetige (jia-yin), when the sun and moon were like joined jade disks and the five planets like a string of pearls, and the dark of the moon, new moon, quarter moons, and full moon did not err by a hair's breadth. At that time, the seventeen schools whose calculations were loose and remote were all abolished. From Emperor Wen of Wei down to the end of the Sui, there were thirteen reforms in all; from Emperor Gaozu of Tang down to the end of the Later Zhou, there were sixteen reforms in all. The Jin had the Long Calendar of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu changli) and Du Yu's 杜預 Changqing Calendar [?], along with He Chengtian's 何承天 New Calendar of the Yuanjia Era (Yuanjia xinli), Cui Hao's 崔浩 Five Yin Epoch Calendar (Wuyin yuanli), Ma Chongji's 馬重績 Harmonizing the Epoch Calendar (Tiaoyuan li), and in the Sui, Liu Zhuo's 劉焯 Imperial Ultimate Calendar (Huangji li). Under Emperor Gaozu of Tang there was the calendar of Fu Renjun 傅仁均; under Gaozong there was the calendar of Li Chunfeng 李淳風; in the Kaiyuan era there was Yixing's 一行 Great Expansion Calendar (Dayan li); under Daizong there was the Five Era Calendar of the Baoying Era (Baoying wuji li); Xu Chengsi 徐承嗣 had the Zhengyuan Calendar of the Jianzhong Era (Jianzhong zhengyuan li); Xu Ang 徐昂 had the Xuanming Calendar of the Yuanhe Era (Yuanhe xuanming li); in the time of Muzong there was the Changqing Calendar (Changqing li); in the time of [Zhao]zong [?] there was the Chongyuan Calendar of the Jingfu Era (Jingfu chongyuan li); and in the Later Zhou, Wang Pu 王朴 had the Revering Heaven Calendar (Qintian li). These could…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
謂備矣而惟大衍爲最蓋其說起于蓍策
以卦當歲以爻當月以策當日以天地之
二始位剛柔以天地之二終紀閏餘以卦
氣定七十二候以中星正二十四氣以晦
朔正日月之會以日度正周天之數章蔀
紀元皆合于易而二十三家之曆盡廢矣
由宋太祖訖宋末凡十八改由金熙宗訖
元末凡三改吳昭素衛朴之乾元奉元曆
吳處訥周琮之應天明天曆壽皇之會元
===
曆孝宗之乾道曆史序宋行古之義天崇
天曆皇居卿姚舜輔之觀天占天曆陳得
一之統元曆楊級初之大明曆元許衡之
授時曆耶律楚材之庚午曆皆各有所取
也而惟授時爲近之蓋簡儀仰儀及諸儀
表皆郭守敬創爲之宿度餘分約爲大半
少未得其的乃用二線推測餘分纖微皆
有可考而又當時四海測景之所凡二十
有七東極高麗西極滇池南踰珠崖北盡
punctuated: 謂備矣，而惟《大衍》爲最。蓋其說起于蓍策，以卦當歲，以爻當月，以策當日；以天地之二始位剛柔，以天地之二終紀閏餘；以卦氣定七十二候，以中星正二十四氣；以晦朔正日月之會，以日度正周天之數。章、蔀、紀、元，皆合于《易》，而二十三家之曆盡廢矣。由宋太祖訖宋末，凡十八改；由金熙宗訖元末，凡三改。吳昭素、衛朴之《乾元》、《奉元曆》，吳處訥、周琮之《應天》、《明天曆》，壽皇之《會元曆》，孝宗之《乾道曆》，史序、宋行古之《義天》、《崇天曆》，皇居卿、姚舜輔之《觀天》、《占天曆》，陳得一之《統元曆》，楊級初之《大明曆》，元許衡之《授時曆》，耶律楚材之《庚午曆》，皆各有所取也，而惟《授時》爲近之。蓋簡儀、仰儀及諸儀表，皆郭守敬創爲之。宿度餘分，約爲大半少，未得其的，乃用二線推測，餘分纖微皆有可考。而又當時四海測景之所，凡二十有七：東極高麗，西極滇池，南踰珠崖，北盡
translation_en: …may be called comprehensive, yet the Dayan Calendar (Dayan li 大衍曆) alone was the finest. For its theory originated in the milfoil stalks of divination: matching the hexagrams to the year, the lines to the months, and the stalks to the days; using the two beginnings of Heaven and Earth to position the firm and the yielding, and the two endings of Heaven and Earth to record the intercalary remainder; using the hexagram breaths (guaqi 卦氣) to determine the seventy-two pentads (hou 候), and the culminating stars to rectify the twenty-four solar terms (qi 氣); using the dark of the moon and the new moon to rectify the conjunctions of the sun and moon, and the solar degrees to rectify the number of the celestial circumference. The zhang 章 (19-year cycle), bu 蔀 (76-year cycle), ji 紀 (1,520-year cycle), and yuan 元 (4,560-year cycle) all conformed to the Book of Changes (Yi 易), and the calendars of the twenty-three schools were all discarded. From Emperor Taizu of Song down to the end of the Song, there were eighteen revisions in all; from Emperor Xizong of Jin down to the end of the Yuan, there were three revisions in all. The Qianyuan and Fengyuan Calendars of Wu Zhaosu 吳昭素 and Wei Pu 衛朴, the Yingtian and Mingtian Calendars of Wu Chune 吳處訥 [for Wang Chuna 王處訥] and Zhou Cong 周琮, the Huiyuan Calendar of the Retired Emperor [Emperor Xiaozong, or Guangzong], the Qiandao Calendar of Emperor Xiaozong 孝宗, the Yitian [for Yitian 儀天] and Chongtian Calendars of Shi Xu 史序 and Song Xinggu 宋行古, the Guantian and Zhantian Calendars of Huang Juqing 皇居卿 and Yao Shunfu 姚舜輔, the Tongyuan Calendar of Chen Deyi 陳得一, the Daming Calendar of Yang Jichu 楊級初 [Yang Ji 楊級], the Season-Granting Calendar (Shoushi li 授時曆) of Xu Heng 許衡 in the Yuan, and the Gengwu Calendar of Yelü Chucai 耶律楚材—all had their respective merits, yet the Season-Granting Calendar alone came closest to perfection. This was because the simplified instrument (jianyi 簡儀), the upward-facing instrument (yangyi 仰儀), and the various gnomons and instruments were all newly invented by Guo Shoujing 郭守敬. Previously, the fractional remainders of the degrees of the lunar lodges had been approximated as three-quarters (tai 太 [written 大]), one-half (ban 半), or one-quarter (shao 少), without attaining exactness; he therefore used two threads to measure and deduce them, so that the finest minutiae of the fractional remainders could all be verified. Moreover, at that time the stations for measuring gnomon shadows across the Four Seas numbered twenty-seven in all: reaching as far east as Koryŏ (Gaoli 高麗), as far west as Dianchi 滇池, passing south beyond Zhuya 珠崖, and extending north all the way to…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
鐵勒皆古人所未及爲者其法具載元史
可謂度越前古矣合而觀之隨時更改代
有損益而推驗精密不過三家耳豈皆憑
胸臆以作聰明任智巧以愚耳目爲哉廣
集衆見而周思曲算之無遺博采羣言而
參伍錯綜之不謬然後定而行之宜其推
往知來信今傳後也即歷代長于曆者亦
不數歲而輒差何哉考之堯時冬至躔在
虛一度夏至在柳十四度春分在胃十二
===
===
度秋分在氐十度至唐開元大衍曆冬至
日躔在斗十度夏至在井十度春分在奎
七度秋分在軫十四度宋統元曆冬至在
斗二度夏至在井六度春分在奎初度秋
分在軫七度此歷代之曆可驗者也晉虞
喜覺其差乃以天爲天歲爲歲立差法以
追其變而算之以五十年差一度然失之
太過久而驗之弗合也何承天倍增其數
約以百年差一度而又不及劉焯取二家
punctuated: 鐵勒，皆古人所未及爲者。其法具載《元史》，可謂度越前古矣。合而觀之，隨時更改，代有損益，而推驗精密不過三家耳。豈皆憑胸臆以作聰明，任智巧以愚耳目爲哉？廣集衆見而周思曲算之無遺，博采羣言而參伍錯綜之不謬，然後定而行之，宜其推往知來、信今傳後也。即歷代長于曆者，亦不數歲而輒差，何哉？考之堯時，冬至躔在虛一度，夏至在柳十四度，春分在胃十二度，秋分在氐十度；至唐開元《大衍曆》，冬至日躔在斗十度，夏至在井十度，春分在奎七度，秋分在軫十四度；宋《統元曆》，冬至在斗二度，夏至在井六度，春分在奎初度，秋分在軫七度：此歷代之曆可驗者也。晉虞喜覺其差，乃以天爲天、歲爲歲，立差法以追其變，而算之以五十年差一度，然失之太過，久而驗之弗合也。何承天倍增其數，約以百年差一度，而又不及。劉焯取二家
translation_en: … Tiele—all of which the ancients had never reached or accomplished. Its methods are fully recorded in the History of the Yuan (Yuan shi 元史), and may truly be said to have surpassed all of antiquity. Viewing them together, calendars were altered in accordance with the times, with additions and subtractions in every age, yet those that were precise in their calculations and verifications numbered no more than three schools. Could they all have merely relied on subjective conjectures to feign cleverness, or indulged in ingenious artifice to deceive people's eyes and ears? Rather, they broadly gathered the views of the multitude, thinking them through comprehensively and calculating them in every detail without omission; they widely collected diverse opinions, comparing and cross-checking them without error, and only then established and promulgated them. It is fitting, then, that they could deduce the past and know the future, command credence in the present and be transmitted to posterity. Yet even the work of those across the dynasties who excelled in calendrical science would invariably fall into discrepancy after scarcely a few years—why is this? Examining the time of Yao 堯, at the winter solstice the sun was lodged at the first degree of the lunar mansion Emptiness (Xu 虛), at the summer solstice at the fourteenth degree of Willow (Liu 柳), at the vernal equinox at the twelfth degree of Stomach (Wei 胃), and at the autumnal equinox at the tenth degree of Root (Di 氐). By the time of the Great Expansion Calendar (Dayan li 大衍曆) of the Kaiyuan 開元 era of the Tang, at the winter solstice the sun was lodged at the tenth degree of Dipper (Dou 斗), at the summer solstice at the tenth degree of Well (Jing 井), at the vernal equinox at the seventh degree of Legs (Kui 奎), and at the autumnal equinox at the fourteenth degree of Chariot (Zhen 軫). In the Unified Origin Calendar (Tongyuan li 統元曆) of the Song, the winter solstice was at the second degree of Dipper, the summer solstice at the sixth degree of Well, the vernal equinox at the initial degree of Legs, and the autumnal equinox at the seventh degree of Chariot. These are what can be verified from the calendars of successive dynasties. Yu Xi 虞喜 of the Jin perceived this discrepancy; he therefore treated the celestial revolution as the celestial revolution and the solar year as the solar year, establishing the method of axial precession (chafa 差法) to trace its changes, and calculated it as a shift of one degree every fifty years. However, this erred by being too fast, and when tested over a long period it did not accord. He Chengtian 何承天 doubled that figure, estimating a shift of one degree every hundred years, yet that fell short. Liu Zhuo 劉焯 took the two schools'…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
中數以七十五年爲近之僧一行以大衍
推之得八十三年而差一度久而驗之又
弗合也許衡王恂郭守敬以六十六年而
差一度算已往減一算算將來加一算至
精密矣今據其法歩之又弗合也此歷代
之不可驗者也或者曰四時寒暑無形而
運于下日月星辰有象而見于上二者常
動而不息一有一無出入升降或遲或速
不相爲謀其久不能無差忒者勢使然也
===
夫以歲差而歸之勢其能有合乎哉然其
所以差者由天周有餘日周不足也天周
有餘則天常平運而舒日周不足則日常
内轉而縮天日之差于中星驗焉堯之冬
至初昏昴中而日在虛七度虛者北方之
宿則日行北陸躔于玄枵之子也今之冬
至初昏室中而日在箕三度箕者東方之
宿則日行東陸躔于析木之寅也是去堯
未四千年而差五十度矣古曆之簡易者
punctuated: 中數，以七十五年爲近之；僧一行以《大衍》推之，得八十三年而差一度，久而驗之，又弗合也。許衡、王恂、郭守敬以六十六年而差一度，算已往減一算，算將來加一算，至精密矣，今據其法歩之，又弗合也。此歷代之不可驗者也。或者曰：「四時寒暑，無形而運于下；日月星辰，有象而見于上。二者常動而不息，一有一無，出入升降，或遲或速，不相爲謀，其久不能無差忒者，勢使然也。」夫以歲差而歸之勢，其能有合乎哉？然其所以差者，由天周有餘、日周不足也。天周有餘，則天常平運而舒；日周不足，則日常内轉而縮。天日之差，于中星驗焉。堯之冬至，初昏昴中，而日在虛七度；虛者，北方之宿，則日行北陸，躔于玄枵之子也。今之冬至，初昏室中，而日在箕三度；箕者，東方之宿，則日行東陸，躔于析木之寅也。是去堯未四千年，而差五十度矣。古曆之簡易者，
translation_en:
…the median number, taking seventy-five years as close to it. The monk Yixing 一行 calculated it by the Great Expansion Calendar (Dayan li 大衍曆) and obtained a precession of one degree in eighty-three years; yet when verified over a long time, this too did not match. Xu Heng 許衡, Wang Xun 王恂, and Guo Shoujing 郭守敬 took it to precess one degree in sixty-six years, subtracting one unit [per century] when calculating the past and adding one unit when calculating the future—which was extremely precise; yet now when we pace the heavens according to their method, it again does not match. These are the aspects across the dynasties that could not be verified.

Some say: "The cold and heat of the four seasons operate formlessly below; the sun, moon, and stars appear with visible forms above. Both move constantly without rest—one without form, one with form—emerging and receding, ascending and descending, sometimes slow and sometimes fast, without coordinating with one another. That over a long period they cannot be free of discrepancies is simply brought about by the natural tendency of things." Now, if one attributes the precession of the equinoxes merely to tendency, how could one ever achieve a match?

Yet the reason there is precession is that the circumference of heaven has a surplus while the circuit of the sun falls short. Because the circumference of heaven has a surplus, heaven constantly revolves evenly and stretches out; because the circuit of the sun falls short, the sun constantly turns inward and contracts. The discrepancy between heaven and the sun is verified by the culminating stars. At the winter solstice in the time of Yao 堯, at dusk the Pleiades (Mao 昴) culminated, and the sun was at seven degrees of Emptiness (Xu 虛); Emptiness is a lodge of the northern quadrant, so the sun traveled the northern path, stationed at the zi 子 position of Xuanxiao 玄枵. At the winter solstice today, at dusk Encampment (Shi 室) culminates, and the sun is at three degrees of Winnowing Basket (Ji 箕); Winnowing Basket is a lodge of the eastern quadrant, so the sun travels the eastern path, stationed at the yin 寅 position of Ximu 析木. Thus, in less than four thousand years since Yao, it has shifted by fifty degrees. As for the simplicity of the ancient calendars…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
今安得倣而求之乎或曰定朔之法莫驗
于日月之交食書詩春秋所載日食俱在
朔漢魏以後日食或在晦者蓋日行一度
月行十三度有奇言其平行也二十九日
有奇而會言其經朔也夫日者陽之精也
行南陸則盈行北陸則縮月者陰之精也
近日則行疾遠日則行遲古者止用經朔
故月一大一小日食或在朔二月食或在
朢之前後漢魏以後日食多在晦其弊蓋
===
坐此耳張衡分九道何承天定小餘李淳
風之定朔皆是矣然日躔有自然之度而
以已意附之可乎善乎杜預之言曰陰陽
之運隨動而差差而不已遂與曆錯曆家
者流欲以管窺之見而推合以驗天不知
以有常之理而順天以求合差法何時而
明哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
承乾御極
punctuated: 今安得倣而求之乎？或曰：「定朔之法，莫驗于日月之交食。」《書》、《詩》、《春秋》所載日食，俱在朔；漢、魏以後，日食或在晦者，蓋日行一度，月行十三度有奇，言其平行也；二十九日有奇而會，言其經朔也。夫日者，陽之精也，行南陸則盈，行北陸則縮；月者，陰之精也，近日則行疾，遠日則行遲。古者止用經朔，故月一大一小，日食或在朔二，月食或在朢之前後。漢、魏以後，日食多在晦，其弊蓋坐此耳。張衡分九道，何承天定小餘，李淳風之定朔，皆是矣。然日躔有自然之度，而以已意附之，可乎？善乎杜預之言曰：「陰陽之運，隨動而差，差而不已，遂與曆錯。」曆家者流，欲以管窺之見，而推合以驗天，不知以有常之理，而順天以求合，差法何時而明哉？洪惟我太祖高皇帝承乾御極，
translation_en: …how can we imitate and seek after them today? Some say: "For the method of determining the true new moon (dingshuo), nothing provides clearer verification than the eclipses at the conjunctions of the sun and moon." The solar eclipses recorded in the Book of Documents (Shu), the Book of Odes (Shi), and the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) all occurred on the first day of the month (shuo). From the Han and Wei dynasties onward, solar eclipses sometimes occurred on the last day of the month (hui). This is because saying that the sun moves one degree while the moon moves thirteen degrees and a fraction refers to their mean motion; and saying that they meet after twenty-nine days and a fraction refers to the mean new moon (jingshuo). Now, the sun is the essence of yang: when it travels along the southern path it accelerates (ying), and when it travels along the northern path it decelerates (suo). The moon is the essence of yin: when near the sun it moves rapidly, and when far from the sun it moves slowly. In antiquity, they used only the mean new moon; therefore, months alternated between one long and one short, solar eclipses sometimes occurred on the first or second day of the month, and lunar eclipses sometimes occurred before or after the full moon (wang). From the Han and Wei onward, solar eclipses frequently occurred on the last day of the month—the flaw lay precisely in this. Zhang Heng 張衡 dividing the nine paths of the moon, He Chengtian 何承天 determining the fractional remainder (xiaoyu), and Li Chunfeng 李淳風 establishing the true new moon were all right in this regard. Yet the sun's trajectory has its natural degrees; is it permissible to force one's own subjective notions onto it? Well put were the words of Du Yu 杜預: "The movements of yin and yang shift as they move; shifting without cease, they eventually fall out of step with the calendar." Those of the calendrical school wish to use their narrow, tube-peering views to force a fit in order to test the heavens, not knowing to use constant principles and follow the heavens to seek agreement—when, then, will the method of accounting for discrepancies ever become clear? Looking with awe upon our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gaohuangdi), who received the Mandate of Heaven and ascended the Supreme Throne…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
膺曆授圖數由天悟理本神孚二統相持則
徵諸七政三曆相讎必協于五紀占天有
臺而璿璣之器存造曆有官而羲和之職
舉銅候有儀而推測之法立其積分一授
時之數也其置閏一大易之旨也分至啓
閉卽少昊之所命也春夏秋冬卽陶唐之
所授也敬
天勤民也至矣而執事猶有謂年遠數盈隨時
改曆之說是豈無所本歟嘗考博士元統
===
之議曰曆日之法其來尚矣今曆雖以大
統爲名而積分猶授時之數况授時曆以
至元辛巳爲曆元至洪武甲子積一百四
年以曆法推之得三億七千六百一十九
萬九千七百七十五分經云大約七十年
而差一度每歲差一分五十秒辛巳至今
年遠數溢漸差天度擬合脩改
太祖是其言矣開創未遑也正德十三年五月
己亥朔日食起復弗合員外郎鄭繼之曰
punctuated: 膺曆授圖，數由天悟，理本神孚。二統相持，則徵諸七政；三曆相讎，必協于五紀。占天有臺，而璿璣之器存；造曆有官，而羲和之職舉；銅候有儀，而推測之法立。其積分，一授時之數也；其置閏，一《大易》之旨也。分至啓閉，卽少昊之所命也；春夏秋冬，卽陶唐之所授也。敬天勤民也至矣。而執事猶有謂年遠數盈、隨時改曆之說，是豈無所本歟？嘗考博士元統之議曰：「曆日之法，其來尚矣。今曆雖以《大統》爲名，而積分猶《授時》之數。况《授時曆》以至元辛巳爲曆元，至洪武甲子積一百四年，以曆法推之，得三億七千六百一十九萬九千七百七十五分。《經》云：『大約七十年而差一度，每歲差一分五十秒。』辛巳至今，年遠數溢，漸差天度，擬合脩改。」太祖是其言矣，開創未遑也。正德十三年五月己亥朔，日食起復弗合，員外郎鄭繼之、日
translation_en:
…received the mandate of the calendar and accepted the royal chart; the numerical calculations were comprehended through Heaven, and the principles were rooted in spiritual accord. When the two systems of calendar calculation were held against each other, they were verified by the Seven Regulators (the sun, moon, and five planets); when the three calendars were collated, they had to be harmonized with the Five Arrangers of Time (year, month, day, stars, and calendrical calculations). For observing the heavens there was an observatory, and the armillary sphere instruments were preserved; for compiling the calendar there were officials, and the duties of Xi and He were carried out; for the bronze clepsydras and weather-watching instruments there were standards, and the methods of calculation and observation were established. Its accumulated fractions (jifen) were entirely the numbers of the Season-Granting Calendar (Shoushi li); its placement of intercalary months was entirely the purport of the Great Changes (Yijing). The equinoxes, solstices, and beginnings of seasons were precisely what Shaohao had named; spring, summer, autumn, and winter were precisely what Yao of Taotang had granted. Reverence for Heaven and diligence toward the people reached their utmost!

Yet Your Excellency still mentions the view that as the years grow distant the numbers overflow, so the calendar should be reformed in accordance with the times—could this really be without foundation? I have examined the proposal of the Erudite (boshi) Yuan Tong 元統, who said: "The methods of calendrical calculation are of great antiquity. Although the present calendar is named the Great Concordance (Datong), its accumulated fractions still follow the numbers of the Season-Granting (Shoushi) system. Moreover, the Season-Granting Calendar took the xinsi year of the Zhiyuan era (1281) as its calendrical epoch; down to the jiazi year of the Hongwu era (1384), one hundred and four years have accumulated, which by calendrical calculation yields 376,199,775 fractional units. The Canon says: 'Roughly every seventy years there is a precession of one degree (du), an annual difference of one fen and fifty miao.' From the xinsi year to the present, the years have grown distant and the numbers have overflowed; it gradually deviates from the celestial degrees and ought to be revised." Grand Progenitor (Taizu) approved his words, but amid the founding of the dynasty there was not yet leisure to carry it out. In the thirteenth year of the Zhengde era (1518), on the jihai new-moon day of the fifth month, the beginning and recovery of a solar eclipse failed to match the predictions. Vice Director (yuanwailang) Zheng Jizhi 鄭繼之 and Calendar…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
官周濂請驗交食以更曆元矣
武廟未之行也嘉靖三年正月五星聚營室稱
脩德以應天脩省以承慶少卿樂頀之疏
可考也請登臺測影調元正曆以求未定
之差法少卿華湘之疏可采也諸臣先後
之建白豈無所見而云然哉嘗以赤道考
之勝國至元辛巳改曆天正冬至赤道歲
差一度五十秒今退天三度五十二分五
十秒矣黃道歲差九十二分九十八秒今
===
退天三度二十五分七十四秒矣故距元
辛巳至洪武甲子僅一百四年迄今則二
百九十五年每歲差一分五十秒約七十
年差一度今合差四度餘矣考曆元以坐
致千歲之日授民時以永垂萬年之統者
不有待于
今日哉竊聞之改曆之法有四一曰立元二曰
測候三曰察度四曰定朔夫歲朔又復謂
之元作曆者每以十一月甲子夜半朔旦
punctuated: 官周濂請驗交食以更曆元矣，武廟未之行也。嘉靖三年正月，五星聚營室，稱脩德以應天，脩省以承慶，少卿樂頀之疏可考也；請登臺測影，調元正曆，以求未定之差法，少卿華湘之疏可采也。諸臣先後之建白，豈無所見而云然哉？嘗以赤道考之：勝國至元辛巳改曆，天正冬至赤道歲差一度五十秒，今退天三度五十二分五十秒矣；黃道歲差九十二分九十八秒，今退天三度二十五分七十四秒矣。故距元辛巳至洪武甲子，僅一百四年；迄今則二百九十五年。每歲差一分五十秒，約七十年差一度，今合差四度餘矣。考曆元以坐致千歲之日，授民時以永垂萬年之統者，不有待于今日哉？竊聞之：改曆之法有四：一曰立元，二曰測候，三曰察度，四曰定朔。夫歲朔又復，謂之元。作曆者每以十一月甲子夜半朔旦
translation_en:
…Calendrical Official Zhou Lian 周濂 requested that eclipses be verified in order to establish a new calendrical epoch, yet the Wuzong 武宗 Emperor (Wumiao 武廟) did not carry it out. In the first month of the third year of the Jiajing 嘉靖 reign (1524), when the Five Planets gathered in the Aligning-the-Hall (Yingshi 營室) lodge, the memorial of Vice Minister Yue Hu 樂頀—which urged cultivating virtue to respond to Heaven and practicing self-reflection to receive blessings—may be examined. And the memorial of Vice Minister Hua Xiang 華湘—which requested ascending the observatory platform to measure gnomon shadows, harmonizing the epoch, and rectifying the calendar so as to determine the unsettled method of precession—may be adopted. How could the successive proposals of these various officials have been spoken without any basis in observation?

If we examine it by means of the celestial equator: when the calendar was reformed in the xinsi 辛巳 year of the Zhiyuan 至元 reign (1281) of the conquered [Yuan] dynasty, the equatorial precession at the astronomical winter solstice was one degree and fifty seconds [?], and now it has receded against the heavens by three degrees, fifty-two minutes, and fifty seconds; the ecliptic precession was ninety-two minutes and ninety-eight seconds, and now it has receded against the heavens by three degrees, twenty-five minutes, and seventy-four seconds. Thus, from the xinsi year of the Yuan dynasty to the jiazi 甲子 year of the Hongwu 洪武 reign (1384) was only one hundred and four years, whereas up to the present it has been two hundred and ninety-five years. With an annual precession of one minute and fifty seconds—a discrepancy of roughly one degree every seventy years—the total discrepancy today is more than four degrees. Does not examining the calendrical epoch so as to determine the solstices of a thousand years while sitting at ease, and granting the seasons to the people so as to hand down forever the system of ten thousand years, await our present day?

I have heard it said that there are four methods for reforming the calendar: the first is called establishing the epoch (liyuan 立元); the second is called observational measurement (cehou 測候); the third is called inspecting the degrees (chadu 察度); and the fourth is called fixing the new moon (dingshuo 定朔). Now, when the beginnings of the year and the lunar month coincide again, it is called an epoch. Those who construct calendars always take the midnight at the dawn of the new moon on a jiazi day in the eleventh month…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
冬至為曆元必也用大史公三紀大備之
法本范史紀元之目如大初所謂四千六
百十七歲已盡都無絲髮之餘特起新曆
之第一日則曆元不差後其可久乎是謂
立元馬融謂天體不可測知天之度者惟
有璣衡一事夫璣衡即今之渾儀也歷代
以來其法漸備至郭守敬又加詳焉獨不
可倣而行之乎是謂測候易之革曰澤中
有火革君子以治曆明時夫作曆有常度
===
也惟觀五星以測三垣觀三垣以測二十
八宿觀二十八宿以察中星是謂察度定
朔之法必于交食驗之張何所考皆不能
無差惟郭守敬以辰集時刻所在之日為
定朔此其為最精者是謂定朔治曆之人
有三一曰專門之裔二曰明經之儒三曰
精算之士夫漢之公孫卿壺遂司馬遷請
改正朔矣而不能為算也乃鄧平唐都洛
下閎之徒出然後成大初之曆崔浩之魏
punctuated:
冬至為曆元。必也用大史公三紀大備之法，本范史紀元之目，如《大初》所謂四千六百十七歲已盡，都無絲髮之餘，特起新曆之第一日，則曆元不差，後其可久乎！是謂立元。馬融謂：「天體不可測，知天之度者，惟有璣衡一事。」夫璣衡即今之渾儀也，歷代以來，其法漸備，至郭守敬又加詳焉，獨不可倣而行之乎？是謂測候。《易》之《革》曰：「澤中有火，革；君子以治曆明時。」夫作曆有常度也，惟觀五星以測三垣，觀三垣以測二十八宿，觀二十八宿以察中星，是謂察度。定朔之法，必于交食驗之，張、何所考皆不能無差，惟郭守敬以辰集時刻所在之日為定朔，此其為最精者，是謂定朔。
治曆之人有三：一曰專門之裔，二曰明經之儒，三曰精算之士。夫漢之公孫卿、壺遂、司馬遷請改正朔矣，而不能為算也；乃鄧平、唐都、洛下閎之徒出，然後成《大初》之曆。崔浩之《魏
translation_en:
… winter solstice as the calendrical epoch. Necessarily, one should employ the Grand Astrologer’s (Sima Qian’s) method of the great completion of the Three Eras (sanji), and take as a basis the framework of the Era Epoch (Jiyuan) in Fan Ye’s History of the Later Han—just as the Grand Inception (Taichu) calendar states that when 4,617 years are exhausted, there is not a hair’s breadth of remainder, and one specially initiates the first day of the new calendar. Then the calendrical epoch will not err, and how long-lasting it will be for posterity! This is what is meant by establishing the epoch. Ma Rong 马融 said: "The heavenly body cannot be fathomed; that by which one knows the degrees of heaven is solely the single matter of the armillary sphere and sighting tube (jiheng)." Now, the armillary sphere and sighting tube are simply today’s armillary instrument (hunyi). Down through successive dynasties its method gradually became complete, and when it came to Guo Shoujing 郭守敬 it was made even more detailed; can we not simply imitate and put it into practice? This is what is meant by observational measurement. The "Revolution" (Ge) hexagram of the Book of Changes (Yi) states: "In the midst of the marsh there is fire: Revolution. Thus the superior man regulates the calendar and makes clear the seasons." Now, the making of a calendar has constant degrees: one simply observes the Five Planets to measure the Three Enclosures (sanyuan), observes the Three Enclosures to measure the Twenty-Eight Lunar Lodgings (ershiba xiu), and observes the Twenty-Eight Lunar Lodgings to examine the culminating stars (zhongxing). This is what is meant by examining the degrees. The method of fixing the new moon (dingshuo) must be verified through solar and lunar eclipses. What Zhang [Heng? / Zhouxuan?] and He [Chengtian] investigated could not be without error; only Guo Shoujing took the day on which the exact double-hour and mark of the conjunction of sun and moon (chenji) occurred as the fixed new moon. This is the most precise of them. This is what is meant by fixing the new moon.

There are three kinds of men who regulate the calendar: the first is called descendants of hereditary specialists; the second is called Confucians who understand the Classics; the third is called scholars skilled in mathematical calculation. Now, in the Han dynasty, Gongsun Qing 公孫卿, Hu Sui 壺遂, and Sima Qian 司馬遷 requested to correct the first month of the year and the first day of the month, yet they were unable to perform the calculations; only when men like Deng Ping 鄧平, Tang Du 唐都, and Luoxia Hong 洛下閎 emerged was the Grand Inception calendar finally completed. Cui Hao’s 崔浩 Northern Wei …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
曆稱精矣而惟高允能辨五星聚井之差
程子嘗曰堯夫差法冠絕古今堯夫嘗曰
楊子雲知曆法又知曆理許衡郭守敬王
恂之作曆也窮極四海竭盡心思就晷測
影凌駕百代夫唐都洛下閎鄧平專門之
裔也子雲堯夫許衡明經之儒也高允郭
守敬王恂精算之士也誠得三者之人而
行改曆之法庶可備一代之制而樹未來
之準矣抑猶有說焉書曰惟天聰明惟聖
===
時憲又曰惟王奉若天道又曰聖人有國
則日月不食星辰不動朱子曰王者脩德
行政用賢去奸能使陽盛足以勝陰則月
常避日而不食蓋天子者法天者也法天
者持敬者也持敬以法天則先天而弗違
後天而奉時自與天地合德日月合明四
時合序矣位育叅賛之道燮理弼亮之功
豈假于器數藝術之末者歟愚也惟知三
光全寒暑時焉
punctuated:
曆稱精矣，而惟高允能辨五星聚井之差；程子嘗曰：「堯夫差法，冠絕古今。」堯夫嘗曰：「楊子雲知曆法，又知曆理。」許衡、郭守敬、王恂之作曆也，窮極四海，竭盡心思，就晷測影，凌駕百代。夫唐都、洛下閎、鄧平，專門之裔也；子雲、堯夫、許衡，明經之儒也；高允、郭守敬、王恂，精算之士也。誠得三者之人，而行改曆之法，庶可備一代之制，而樹未來之準矣。

抑猶有說焉。《書》曰：「惟天聰明，惟聖時憲。」又曰：「惟王奉若天道。」又曰：「聖人有國，則日月不食，星辰不動。」朱子曰：「王者脩德行政，用賢去奸，能使陽盛足以勝陰，則月常避日而不食。」蓋天子者，法天者也；法天者，持敬者也。持敬以法天，則先天而弗違，後天而奉時，自與天地合德，日月合明，四時合序矣。位育叅賛之道，燮理弼亮之功，豈假于器數藝術之末者歟？愚也惟知三光全、寒暑時焉，
translation_en:
…calendar was praised for its precision, yet only Gao Yun 高允 was able to discern the error regarding the conjunction of the five planets in the Eastern Well Lodge (Jing). Master Cheng 程子 once said: "Shao Yaofu's 邵堯夫 (Shao Yong 邵雍) method of intercalation and astronomical difference surpasses all, past and present." Yaofu once said: "Yang Ziyun 楊子雲 (Yang Xiong 揚雄) understood both calendrical methods and calendrical principles." When Xu Heng 許衡, Guo Shoujing 郭守敬, and Wang Xun 王恂 compiled their calendar, they extended their investigations to the limits of the Four Seas, exhausted their mental faculties, and measured gnomon shadows on site, surpassing a hundred generations. Now, Tang Du 唐都, Luoxia Hong 洛下閎, and Deng Ping 鄧平 were descendants of hereditary specialists; Ziyun, Yaofu, and Xu Heng were Confucian scholars who illuminated the Classics; and Gao Yun, Guo Shoujing, and Wang Xun were masters of precise calculation. If one truly obtains men of these three types and carries out the methods of calendrical reform, one may perhaps establish the institution for an entire dynasty and set a standard for the future.

Yet there is still more to be said. The Book of Documents (Shu) states: "Heaven alone is all-intelligent and all-discerning; the sage king alone patterns himself on it." Another passage reads: "The king reverently accords with the Way of Heaven." And it is also said: "When a sage possesses the state, the sun and moon do not suffer eclipses, and the stars and constellations do not stray from their courses." Master Zhu 朱子 (Zhu Xi 朱熹) said: "When a true king cultivates virtue, administers government, employs the worthy, and removes the wicked, enabling the yang force to flourish sufficiently to overcome the yin, then the moon constantly avoids the sun and there are no eclipses." Indeed, the Son of Heaven is one who models himself upon Heaven; one who models himself upon Heaven is one who maintains reverence. If he maintains reverence so as to model himself upon Heaven, then when he precedes Heaven, Heaven does not act in opposition to him, and when he follows Heaven, he respects its timing; thus he naturally matches his virtue with Heaven and Earth, his brilliance with the sun and moon, and his order with the four seasons. How could the Way of establishing the proper positions of things, nurturing life, and participating in the transforming and nourishing powers of Heaven and Earth, or the achievement of harmonizing yin and yang and assisting in governance, depend upon the mere incidentals of instruments, numbers, and technical arts? Stupid as I am, I know only that the three luminaries remaining whole and the cold and heat arriving in their proper seasons are…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖人之賜而已何容置喙于其間哉
第四問
張正蒙
同考試官教諭許批因時立政通變宜民爲治
至要也是作于質文遲速寬猛動靜之間參和補救
約之于中非識時知變者不能及也用世之才允宜
高薦
考試官教諭朱批通達治體詞足發意讀之
爽然
===
考試官教授李批條議剴切非徒答問者
爲政者有定體乎非君子所以運天下也
爲政者無定體乎非君子所以一天下也
吾所知者惟其治天下之意而已夫天下
至大也羣生至夥也好惡相疑誕信相攻
愚智相駁不啻如六馬之易驚江河之易
決也治國家而弭人民者非不欲爲法以
盡天下後世之變顧其情狀之伏也兆於
毫芒更於俄忽將有出於吾之所不及逆
punctuated:
聖人之賜而已，何容置喙于其間哉！

第四問
張正蒙
同考試官教諭許批：因時立政，通變宜民，爲治至要也。是作于質文、遲速、寬猛、動靜之間，參和補救，約之于中，非識時知變者不能及也。用世之才，允宜高薦。
考試官教諭朱批：通達治體，詞足發意，讀之爽然。
考試官教授李批：條議剴切，非徒答問者。

爲政者有定體乎？非君子所以運天下也。爲政者無定體乎？非君子所以一天下也。吾所知者，惟其治天下之意而已。夫天下至大也，羣生至夥也，好惡相疑，誕信相攻，愚智相駁，不啻如六馬之易驚、江河之易決也。治國家而弭人民者，非不欲爲法以盡天下後世之變，顧其情狀之伏也，兆於毫芒，更於俄忽，將有出於吾之所不及。逆
translation_en:
… the bestowal of the Sage; how could I presume to interject a word into the matter!

Question Four
Zhang Zhengmeng 張正蒙
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Xu 許: Establishing policies in accordance with the times and adapting to changes so as to suit the people are the most essential principles of governance. Between substance and refinement, slowness and speed, leniency and severity, action and quiescence, this essay blends and remedies them, bringing them back to the mean—something unattainable by anyone who does not understand the times and comprehend change. A talent fit for practical service in the world, he truly deserves high recommendation.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhu 朱: Thoroughly conversant with the fundamentals of governance, with diction sufficient to express its meaning; reading it is refreshing.
Comment by Examiner Professor Li 李: Its point-by-point arguments are incisive and pertinent; he is not someone merely answering the question.

Does governance have a fixed form? That is not how the superior man moves the realm. Does governance have no fixed form? That is not how the superior man unifies the realm. All that I know is simply the underlying intention in governing the realm. Now, the realm is vast indeed, and the multitude of living beings is numerous indeed. Likes and dislikes breed mutual suspicion, falsehood and good faith attack one another, and folly and wisdom clash—no less than six horses easily startled or great rivers easily breached. Those who govern the state and pacify the people do not lack the desire to establish laws that exhaustively cover all the changes of the world and future generations. Yet the latent conditions and circumstances first appear in the finest hair's breadth and shift in an instant, so that things will arise beyond what we can reach. If one anticipates …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其形而預爲之待虞其巧而曲爲之防事
日益新則智日益出而物之變日益滋智
不足以勝物則天下之情將脊脊棼棼而
無所底止而勢於是乎始窮古之君子觀
風會之淳漓而乗其運洞物情之向背而
握其機抑淫詭暢澹漠其創始而化之因
弊而易之也以其意運量乎天下而不示
其所以化之易之之道天下之人化上之
意而不知其所以整齊改革之由王道之
===
行也其庶矣乎愚生伏處奧渫非通達國
體者也雖然竊嘗窺陳編而櫽桼其槩矣
粤自堯舜禹之相授守一道也其化蕩蕩
其俗于于無捄弊之政也大禹之言政自
養民之外無費詞也夏后氏以還風氣開
而世變日繁聖君賢相始相與反其所敝
而捄其所不足故康王之命畢公曰道有
升降政由俗革則因時之政當時講之詳
矣俗革者法也養民者意也得其意斯得
punctuated:
其形而預爲之待，虞其巧而曲爲之防。事日益新，則智日益出，而物之變日益滋；智不足以勝物，則天下之情將脊脊棼棼而無所底止，而勢於是乎始窮。古之君子，觀風會之淳漓而乗其運，洞物情之向背而握其機，抑淫詭，暢澹漠。其創始而化之、因弊而易之也，以其意運量乎天下，而不示其所以化之易之之道；天下之人，化上之意，而不知其所以整齊改革之由。王道之行也，其庶矣乎！
愚生伏處奧渫，非通達國體者也。雖然，竊嘗窺陳編而櫽桼其槩矣。粤自堯、舜、禹之相授，守一道也，其化蕩蕩，其俗于于，無捄弊之政也。大禹之言政，自養民之外無費詞也。夏后氏以還，風氣開而世變日繁，聖君賢相始相與反其所敝，而捄其所不足。故康王之命畢公曰：「道有升降，政由俗革。」則因時之政，當時講之詳矣。俗革者，法也；養民者，意也。得其意，斯得
translation_en:
… their manifestations and prepare for them in advance, or worry about their cunning and devise intricate defenses against them. As affairs grow daily more novel, cleverness emerges ever more abundantly, and the mutations of things multiply day by day. When cleverness is no longer sufficient to master things, the conditions of the world will become confused and tangled without end, and at that point the course of affairs reaches an impasse. The gentlemen of antiquity observed whether the prevailing ethos was pure or thin and rode upon its momentum; they penetrated the inclinations and aversions of human sentiment and grasped their pivotal mechanisms, suppressing the licentious and deceitful while promoting the tranquil and unassuming. In initiating transformations and altering things in response to abuses, they used their underlying intent to measure and guide the world, without displaying the specific methods by which they transformed and altered it. The people of the world were transformed by the intent of their superiors without knowing the means by which they had been ordered and reformed. In this way, the implementation of the Kingly Way came close to perfection!

As a foolish student living in obscurity and humble circumstances, I am not one who thoroughly comprehends the principles of statecraft. Even so, I have ventured to peer into old texts and gauge their general outlines. From the time when Yao, Shun, and Yu handed down the succession to one another, they held to a single Way; their transforming influence was vast and boundless, their customs were carefree and contented, and there was no governance aimed merely at remedying abuses. When the Great Yu spoke of governance, he wasted no words beyond the nourishing of the people. From the Xia dynasty onward, as cultural sensibilities opened up and worldly changes grew daily more complex, sage rulers and worthy ministers first began to work together to reverse what had decayed and remedy what was deficient. Thus, when King Kang charged the Duke of Bi, he said: "The Way has its ascents and descents; governance is reformed in accordance with customs." Clearly, governance that adapts to the times was already discussed in detail in that era. What is reformed in accordance with customs is the law; what nourishes the people is the intent. Once one grasps the intent, one thereby grasps …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其法矣今之論治者曰質文狃於尚也遲
速拘於趣也寬猛岐於術也動靜局於形
也若是乎其樊然殽亂也卽聖人欲為一
切之聰明以要束之亦難矣愚則曰聖人
不能違時也能不失時而已是故有改制
之名無變道之實質文異尚其宜一也遲
速異趣其情均也寬猛異術其用兼也動
靜異形其器豫也昔者夏之政忠忠之弊
小人以野商人承之以質質之弊小人以
鬼周人承之以文三王之道若循環然逮
於周而天下之變極矣先進禮樂庶幾乎
彬彬君子哉及其弊也暴孽情飾淫志文
武周公之德其衰矣夫子傷周道而追思
虞夏旣雕旣琢其將復歸於朴乎然則從
周者從其文質之得中者也為下不倍之
義也感周道之弊者憂文勝之趨如水之
日流於下而不可返也斟酌四代之意也
故曰質文殊而其宜一也齊魯之興也伯
punctuated: 其法矣。今之論治者曰：質文狃於尚也，遲速拘於趣也，寬猛岐於術也，動靜局於形也。若是乎其樊然殽亂也！卽聖人欲為一切之聰明以要束之，亦難矣。愚則曰：聖人不能違時也，能不失時而已。是故有改制之名，無變道之實。質文異尚，其宜一也；遲速異趣，其情均也；寬猛異術，其用兼也；動靜異形，其器豫也。昔者夏之政忠，忠之弊，小人以野；商人承之以質，質之弊，小人以鬼；周人承之以文。三王之道若循環然。逮於周而天下之變極矣。先進禮樂，庶幾乎彬彬君子哉！及其弊也，暴孽情，飾淫志，文、武、周公之德其衰矣。夫子傷周道而追思虞、夏，旣雕旣琢，其將復歸於朴乎！然則從周者，從其文質之得中者也，為下不倍之義也；感周道之弊者，憂文勝之趨如水之日流於下而不可返也，斟酌四代之意也。故曰：質文殊而其宜一也。齊、魯之興也，伯
translation_en: … the methods as well. Those who discuss governance today say: substance and refinement are habituated to what is valued; slowness and speed are bound to inclinations; leniency and severity diverge in technique; action and quiescence are confined by form. How tangled and confused they are! Even if a sage wished to exercise all-encompassing intelligence to bind them together, it would be difficult. Yet I say: a sage cannot go against the times; he can only avoid missing the opportune moment. Therefore, there is the name of reforming institutions, but not the reality of altering the Way. Substance and refinement differ in what they value, yet their appropriateness is one; slowness and speed differ in inclination, yet their underlying reality is equal; leniency and severity differ in technique, yet their applications complement each other; action and quiescence differ in form, yet their instruments are prepared in advance. In antiquity, the governance of the Xia dynasty prized loyalty, and the abuse of loyalty was that petty men became rustic; the Shang people succeeded it with substance [reverence], and the abuse of substance was that petty men became superstitious; the Zhou people succeeded it with refinement. The Way of the Three Kings was like a cycle. By the time of the Zhou, the transformations of the world had reached their extreme. In the rites and music of the men of former times, how close they were to being cultivated gentlemen in whom substance and refinement were in due proportion! Yet when abuses set in, people exposed perverse passions and adorned licentious ambitions, and the virtue of King Wen, King Wu, and the Duke of Zhou declined. The Master [Confucius] lamented the Way of the Zhou and fondly recalled the Yu [Shun] and Xia: having been carved and polished, should things not return to unadorned simplicity? That being so, his following the Zhou meant following that in which its refinement and substance attained the mean—this was the principle of a subject not rebelling against his ruler; whereas his being moved by the abuses of the Way of the Zhou meant worrying that the trend toward excessive refinement was like water flowing downward day by day, never to be turned back—this was his intention in weighing and selecting from the four dynasties. Thus it is said: substance and refinement differ, yet their appropriateness is one. At the rise of Qi and Lu, Bo…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
禽變其俗革其禮三年而報政可謂遲矣
太公簡其君臣禮從其俗五月而報政可
謂疾矣方二公以宿德巍勳肇基啓宇豈
非聖人之遺化好禮樂之國哉然疾者近
於强而不可與持久遲者近於弱而其教
可長存蓋其積漸然也周公之嘆睹微而
推其著也孔子之論由今而反諸古也要
之勢窮則變變則通使魯公能循方冊以
復文武之舊必不至積弱而折入於齊桓
===
===
公敬仲能惇信明義以脩太公之遺烈則
田氏安得竊齊國而代之惟其衰而莫爲
之捄或捄之而不得其道是以其勢日趨
於極重而不可反耳非其始爲政者之過
也故曰遲速殊而其情均也黃霸施寬和
於綜覈之日乗强之勢者利用惠而法固
未嘗弛也若鄭俗之淫未殄餘風子太叔
一朝反其舊而呴濡之銜扼既解則羣馬
竊轡矣此非寬之失也不善用寬者之咎
punctuated: 禽變其俗，革其禮，三年而報政，可謂遲矣；太公簡其君臣禮，從其俗，五月而報政，可謂疾矣。方二公以宿德巍勳，肇基啓宇，豈非聖人之遺化、好禮樂之國哉？然疾者近於强，而不可與持久；遲者近於弱，而其教可長存，蓋其積漸然也。周公之嘆，睹微而推其著也；孔子之論，由今而反諸古也。要之，勢窮則變，變則通。使魯公能循方冊以復文、武之舊，必不至積弱而折入於齊；桓公、敬仲能惇信明義以脩太公之遺烈，則田氏安得竊齊國而代之？惟其衰而莫爲之捄，或捄之而不得其道，是以其勢日趨於極重而不可反耳，非其始爲政者之過也。故曰：遲速殊而其情均也。黃霸施寬和於綜覈之日，乗强之勢者利用惠，而法固未嘗弛也；若鄭俗之淫未殄餘風，子太叔一朝反其舊而呴濡之，銜扼既解，則羣馬竊轡矣。此非寬之失也，不善用寬者之咎
translation_en: …qin [Boqin 伯禽] changed their customs and reformed their rites, reporting on his governance only after three years—this may be called slow. The Grand Duke [Taigong 太公] simplified the rites between ruler and minister and followed their existing customs, reporting on his governance after five months—this may be called swift. When the two dukes, with their venerable virtue and towering merit, first laid the foundations and opened up their territories, were these not states blessed by the enduring transformative influence of the sages and fond of rites and music? Yet what is swift verges on strength, though it cannot be sustained over the long term; what is slow verges on weakness, yet its teachings can endure for a long time. This is because of how they gradually accumulate. The sigh of the Duke of Zhou [Zhougong 周公] was a case of perceiving the subtle and inferring its manifest outcome; the judgment of Confucius [Kongzi 孔子] was a case of proceeding from the present to trace back to antiquity. In sum, when a tendency reaches its limit, it changes; having changed, it finds a way through. Had the dukes of Lu been able to follow the wooden tablets and bamboo slips of the records to restore the old ways of King Wen and King Wu, Lu would surely not have accumulated weakness to the point of being broken and absorbed by Qi.
