Had Duke Huan [Huangong 桓公] and Jingzhong [敬仲, i.e., Guan Zhong 管仲] been able to cultivate trustworthiness and clarify righteousness so as to renew the splendid legacy of the Grand Duke, how could the Tian [田] clan have usurped the state of Qi and replaced its ruling house? It was only because, in their decline, no one came to their rescue—or those who tried to rescue them failed to find the proper way—that the momentum daily hastened toward an extreme gravity that could not be reversed; it was not the fault of those who first instituted their governance. Therefore it is said: slowness and swiftness differ, yet their underlying reality is the same. Huang Ba [黃霸] practiced leniency and harmony in an age of stringent verification; riding a momentum of strength, he profitably employed kindness, while the laws were certainly never relaxed. By contrast, when the licentiousness of Zheng's customs had not yet been eradicated of its lingering trends, Zi Taishu [子太叔] all of a sudden reversed the old strict policies and coddled the people; once the bit and yoke were loosened, the herd of horses stole away with the reins. This was not a failure of leniency itself, but the fault of one who did not know how to use leniency well…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也諸葛孔明承劉璋闇懦之後乗弱之勢
者利用威而惠固未甞壅也若嚴延年之
鷙烈則馬力竭而猶求焉靡不敗矣此非
嚴之失也不善用嚴者之咎也至矣哉大
舜與孔子乎御衆以寬矣而不捐四裔之
罰寬則得衆矣而不徐徐於兩觀之誅苟
有大舜孔子之心則刑罰者皆至仁之作
用也會何病於寬乎故曰寬猛殊而其用
兼也宓子賤之宰單父也穆穆乎彈琴而
===
理其逸若此矣巫馬期爲之非見星出入
則不能治其勞若彼焉非獨其才不同其
器之深淺異也凡器之所受者大則以我
待物而有餘所畜者隘則以物博我而不
足以單父之褊乃有賢於不齊者五人子
賤事之而稟度順之而行所無事焉居靜
以制動者也巫馬期智巧果敢之列也攖
其神以役於物知有動焉耳祗勞形怵心
索然而無餘味矣宓子之所爲巫馬氏非
punctuated:
也。諸葛孔明承劉璋闇懦之後，乗弱之勢者利用威，而惠固未甞壅也。若嚴延年之鷙烈，則馬力竭而猶求焉，靡不敗矣。此非嚴之失也，不善用嚴者之咎也。至矣哉大舜與孔子乎！御衆以寬矣，而不捐四裔之罰；寬則得衆矣，而不徐徐於兩觀之誅。苟有大舜、孔子之心，則刑罰者皆至仁之作用也，會何病於寬乎？故曰寬猛殊而其用兼也。

宓子賤之宰單父也，穆穆乎彈琴而理，其逸若此矣；巫馬期爲之，非見星出入則不能治，其勞若彼焉。非獨其才不同，其器之深淺異也。凡器之所受者大，則以我待物而有餘；所畜者隘，則以物博我而不足。以單父之褊，乃有賢於不齊者五人，子賤事之而稟度，順之而行所無事焉，居靜以制動者也。巫馬期，智巧果敢之列也，攖其神以役於物，知有動焉耳，祗勞形怵心，索然而無餘味矣。宓子之所爲，巫馬氏非
translation_en:
… [those who do not know how to employ leniency]. Zhuge Kong明 (諸葛孔明, Zhuge Liang) succeeded the benighted and weak rule of Liu Zhang (劉璋); riding a trend of weakness, he found it advantageous to employ awe-inspiring severity, yet his kindness was certainly never obstructed. As for the fierce harshness of Yan Yannian (嚴延年), it was like demanding still more from horses whose strength is already exhausted—none fail to collapse. This is not the fault of severity itself, but the blame of one who does not know how to employ severity well. How supreme were Great Shun and Confucius! Shun governed the multitude with leniency, yet he did not abandon the punishments of banishment to the four frontier regions; Confucius said that by leniency one wins the multitude, yet he did not hesitate in the execution beneath the twin watchtowers. If only one possesses the mind of Great Shun and Confucius, then punishments and penalties are all the functioning of supreme benevolence—how could they be any detriment to leniency? Therefore it is said: leniency and severity differ, yet their functions are combined.

When Fuzi Jian (宓子賤, Fu Buqi) governed Shanfu (單父), in serene dignity he played his zither and the district was well-ordered—such was his ease! When Wuma Qi (巫馬期) governed it, unless he went out and returned by starlight he could not bring about order—such was his toil! This was not merely because their talents were different, but because the depth and shallowness of their capacities were distinct. Whenever the capacity of a vessel to receive is great, one responds to external things from within oneself and has plenty to spare; when what it holds is narrow, external things overwhelm oneself and one falls short. Narrow as Shanfu was, there were five men there worthier than Buqi (不齊) himself; Zijian (子賤) served them and took his measures from them, following their lead and acting without ado—he was one who abided in stillness in order to control movement. Wuma Qi belonged to the class of theclever, adroit, and resolute; he agitated his spirit in servitude to external things, knowing only how to be in motion, which merely wearied his body and distressed his mind, leaving him depleted and without any lingering savor. What Master Fu did, Wuma…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
不欲爲之也顧才可竭而器不可强耳故
曰動靜殊而其器豫也嗟夫天下之變其
具可熟數於前矣夫膠柱不可以鼓瑟者
滯於音也夏蟲不可以語氷者篤於時也
曲士不可以語治者溺於聞也故夫質文
也寬猛也遲速也動靜也可用於天下而
不足以用天下天下之勢譬諸人之一身
然善理身者謹食息節嗜欲使寒暑七情
之毒不能奸其中其適乘間而入也爲醫
===
===
師者必診其虛實急緩標本之候而投之
劑此法之常也有和扁者視之察色觀毫
而見臟腑之癥結辨志氣之强弱則剖胸
易心隨其所投靡不立效要於勿壅勿閼
固其元氣而調其榮衛此神明其意而不
牽於法者也聖人不能使勢之不變猶人
身之不能無疾也燭盈虛之紀達消長之
化猶之視臟腑辨志氣之明也析幾於萌
芽起教於微眇操縱闔闢手撓指顧而四
punctuated: 不欲爲之也，顧才可竭而器不可强耳。故曰：動靜殊而其器豫也。嗟夫！天下之變，其具可熟數於前矣。夫膠柱不可以鼓瑟者，滯於音也；夏蟲不可以語氷者，篤於時也；曲士不可以語治者，溺於聞也。故夫質文也、寬猛也、遲速也、動靜也，可用於天下，而不足以用天下。天下之勢，譬諸人之一身然。善理身者，謹食息，節嗜欲，使寒暑七情之毒不能奸其中；其適乘間而入也，爲醫師者必診其虛實、急緩、標本之候而投之劑，此法之常也。有和、扁者視之，察色觀毫而見臟腑之癥結，辨志氣之强弱，則剖胸易心，隨其所投，靡不立效，要於勿壅勿閼，固其元氣而調其榮衛，此神明其意而不牽於法者也。聖人不能使勢之不變，猶人身之不能無疾也；燭盈虛之紀，達消長之化，猶之視臟腑、辨志氣之明也。析幾於萌芽，起教於微眇，操縱闔闢，手撓指顧，而四
translation_en:
… did not wish to do so; rather, talent can be exhausted, whereas capacity cannot be forced. Therefore it is said: activity and stillness differ, and one's capacity is prepared beforehand.

Alas! Amid the changes of the world, the means to address them can be thoroughly enumerated from past precedents. Now, that one cannot play the zither with glued pegs is because one is bogged down in a single tone; that one cannot speak of ice to a summer insect is because it is bound by its season; that one cannot speak of governance to a parochial scholar is because he is drowned in his limited learning. Therefore, simplicity and refinement, leniency and severity, slowness and speed, activity and stillness—these can be employed in the world, yet they are insufficient by themselves to govern the world.

The dynamics of the world may be compared to a person's body. One who is skilled at tending the body is careful in eating and resting and moderates his desires, so that the toxins of cold and heat and the seven emotions cannot violate his interior. Should they happen to seize an opening and enter, the physician must diagnose the symptoms of deficiency and excess, urgency and remission, root and branch, and administer medicine accordingly; this is the constant rule of method. Yet when someone like Physician He (醫和) or Bian Que (扁鵲) examines him—observing the complexion and inspecting the finest hairs to see the obstructions in the internal organs, and discerning the strength or weakness of the will and vital breath—he may cut open the chest and replace the heart, and whatever he administers never fails to take immediate effect. The essential point is that there be neither blockage nor stagnation, fortifying the primordial vitality and harmonizing the nutritive and defensive energies; this is grasping the spirit of the principle with divine insight rather than being fettered by fixed methods.

That the sage cannot prevent circumstances from changing is just as the human body cannot be entirely free of illness; his illuminating the cycles of fullness and emptiness and comprehending the transformations of waning and waxing are just like the clear discernment of inspecting the internal organs and distinguishing the will and vital breath. Analyzing the subtle springs of action in their very buds, initiating instruction from the finest minutiae, tightening and relaxing, closing and opening, merely flexing the hand and pointing the finger while the people of the four…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
方之民莫不俱至者此豈有炫奇飾幻之
術哉天下之弊起於民之有厭倦之心而
其爲患莫大於德不足而求勝其民當其
未厭也雖商君愚之以徙木驅之以實塞
而不能箝秦民不便之口及其既厭也則
沛公以崛起草創之約能使全秦之父老
怊怊乎若嬰兒之入於慈母之懷而惟恐
失之何者曲防而障者難爲功順風而吹
者易爲力天下之情方燋然爽惑而求解
===
===
矣吾因其情而爲之振湯火於衽席之上
則趨之如響赴及其久也人情狃於治安
而其巧無所洩狡者思詐强者思暴德不
足以返民之性情則將出於智力以求勝
之上以智力勝其下則下亦以智力勝其
上未有上下交相勝而能治者也故自古
聖人之爲天下因其固然不敢恃一己之
智力以勝之觸而後應迫而後動不得已
而後起要於使天下忘其厭倦之心欣然
punctuated: 方之民莫不俱至者，此豈有炫奇飾幻之術哉？天下之弊，起於民之有厭倦之心；而其爲患，莫大於德不足而求勝其民。當其未厭也，雖商君愚之以徙木，驅之以實塞，而不能箝秦民不便之口；及其既厭也，則沛公以崛起草創之約，能使全秦之父老怊怊乎若嬰兒之入於慈母之懷，而惟恐失之。何者？曲防而障者難爲功，順風而吹者易爲力。天下之情，方燋然爽惑而求解矣，吾因其情而爲之振湯火於衽席之上，則趨之如響赴。及其久也，人情狃於治安，而其巧無所洩，狡者思詐，强者思暴。德不足以返民之性情，則將出於智力以求勝之。上以智力勝其下，則下亦以智力勝其上，未有上下交相勝而能治者也。故自古聖人之爲天下，因其固然，不敢恃一己之智力以勝之。觸而後應，迫而後動，不得已而後起，要於使天下忘其厭倦之心，欣然
translation_en: … [that the people of the four] quarters all come together without exception—could this really be due to any art of displaying oddities or embellishing illusions? The abuses of the empire arise from the people having hearts of weariness and fatigue, and its greatest peril lies in having insufficient virtue while seeking to get the better of one's people. When they are not yet weary of the old order, even though Lord Shang (Shangjun) duped them with moving the wooden pole and drove them to populate the frontier garrisons, he could not silence the mouths of the people of Qin complaining of the inconvenience. Yet once they had grown thoroughly weary of it, the Lord of Pei (Peigong), with the rudimentary, newly improvised तीन-article covenant of his sudden rise, was able to make the elders of all Qin feel as wistfully attached as an infant entering the embrace of a loving mother, fearing only to lose him. Why is this? Building crooked dikes to dam a stream makes it hard to succeed, whereas blowing with the wind makes it easy to exert force. When the feelings of the world are distressed, bewildered, and seeking relief, if we follow along with their feelings and rescue them from boiling water and fire to place them upon comfortable mats, they will hasten to us like an echo answering a sound. When a long time has passed, however, human feelings grow accustomed to peace and order, and their cleverness has no outlet: the cunning think of deceit, and the strong think of violence. If virtue is insufficient to restore the nature and feelings of the people, then rulers will resort to intelligence and force in seeking to get the better of them. When superiors use intelligence and force to get the better of their inferiors, inferiors likewise use intelligence and force to get the better of their superiors; never has there been a case where superiors and inferiors vied to get the better of one another and good governance was achieved. Therefore, since antiquity, when the sages governed the empire, they followed what was naturally so and dared not rely on their own personal intelligence and force to get the better of it. They responded only when touched, moved only when pressed, and rose only when they had no choice—the essential point being to make the empire forget its heart of weariness and fatigue, and gladly…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
思戴其君上而莫測其所以然質文在我
如甘苦之相和而成味繪素之相錯而成
章也遲速在我如泰豆造父氏行乎獨木
之塗内得於中心而外合於馬志也寛猛
在我如大弦濁以春溫小弦廉折以清克
諧以鳴而不相害也動靜在我如三十輻
共轉於一轂當其無有車之用也行而無
迹事而無傳故功蓋天下而似不已出化
貸萬物而民莫得名又何紛紛乎繩約膠
===
漆以固結天下爲哉雖然此非聖人之所
爲天之所設也天之道運而無所積照臨
者爲日月沾濡者爲雨露鼓動震撼者爲
雷霆孰主張是其太極之默運而不能自
止者乎聖人之道以無私爲主以無爲爲
常窅然空然精神四達無施而不得彼其
眡習尚之隆汚理道之沿革如造化之相
代乎吾前而吾不知其所以爲之者洋洋
乎遠撫而長駕德閎而恩博豈人力也哉
punctuated: 思戴其君上，而莫測其所以然。質文在我，如甘苦之相和而成味，繪素之相錯而成章也；遲速在我，如泰豆、造父氏行乎獨木之塗，内得於中心而外合於馬志也；寛猛在我，如大弦濁以春溫，小弦廉折以清，克諧以鳴而不相害也；動靜在我，如三十輻共轉於一轂，當其無，有車之用也。行而無迹，事而無傳，故功蓋天下而似不已出，化貸萬物而民莫得名，又何紛紛乎繩約膠漆以固結天下爲哉？雖然，此非聖人之所爲，天之所設也。天之道運而無所積，照臨者爲日月，沾濡者爲雨露，鼓動震撼者爲雷霆，孰主張是？其太極之默運而不能自止者乎！聖人之道，以無私爲主，以無爲爲常，窅然空然，精神四達，無施而不得。彼其眡習尚之隆汚、理道之沿革，如造化之相代乎吾前，而吾不知其所以爲之者。洋洋乎遠撫而長駕，德閎而恩博，豈人力也哉？
translation_en: … long to honor and support their sovereign above, without fathoming why it is so. Substance and refinement rest with me, just as sweetness and bitterness blend to form flavor, and painted colors and plain silk alternate to form a pattern. Slowness and speed rest with me, just as Taidou and Zaofu drove along a track the width of a single log, grasping it inwardly in their hearts while outwardly matching the will of their horses. Leniency and severity rest with me, just as the thick strings sound deep and warm like spring, and the thin strings sound sharp and clear—able to resonate in harmony without impairing one another. Activity and stillness rest with me, just as thirty spokes turn together around a single hub, where it is in its empty space that the utility of the carriage lies. Moving without leaving a trace, acting without passing down a record—thus his achievements cover the world yet seem not to issue from himself; his transforming influence bestows itself upon the myriad things yet the people cannot name it. Why then go to all the trouble of using cords, bonds, glue, and lacquer to bind the world fast? Even so, this is not the doing of the sage, but the arrangement of Heaven. The Way of Heaven revolves without accumulation: what shines down from above are the sun and moon; what moistens and enriches are rain and dew; what rouses and shakes are thunder and lightning. Who directs all this? Is it not the silent operation of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji), which cannot halt of itself! The Way of the sage takes selflessness as its foundation and non-purposive action (wuwei) as its constant rule. Profound and empty, his spirit reaches in all directions, and nothing he applies fails to succeed. He views the rise and decline of customs and the continuities and changes in principles of governance just as the transformations of nature succeed one another before our eyes, without our knowing how they are brought about.Vast and boundless, pacifying distant lands and guiding the realm from afar, with magnificent virtue and wide-reaching grace—how could this be achieved by human strength alone?

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
昔帝虞氏言天王之用心曰天德而出寧
日月照而四時行若晝夜之有經雲行而
雨施矣斯德之盛而古之極也列禦寇氏
不得其說乃謂聖人以智籠羣愚猶籠眾
狙也抑何枝辭琢正之甚哉管蠡之見惟
執事試詳擇焉
第五問
陳貴科
同考試官教諭梁批粵西大務夷獠與土司並
===
而土司又患在內者是作情態備陳駕馭得體而末
歸于得人尤爲根極之論匪直留心世務而已佳士
佳士
考試官教諭朱批造語暢雄敘事詳覈
考試官教授李批處置周詳鑿有實用
國家之柔遠也以德而利用在威人臣之靖
邊也以才而利用在信德以濟威則威讋
而裔夷慕義才以布信則信立而異類嚮
風二者要在審勢達變而吾之操縱不失
punctuated:
昔帝虞氏言天王之用心曰：「天德而出寧，日月照而四時行，若晝夜之有經，雲行而雨施矣。」斯德之盛而古之極也。列禦寇氏不得其說，乃謂聖人以智籠羣愚，猶籠眾狙也，抑何枝辭琢正之甚哉！管蠡之見，惟執事試詳擇焉。

第五問
陳貴科
同考試官教諭梁批：粵西大務，夷獠與土司並，而土司又患在內者。是作情態備陳，駕馭得體，而末歸于得人，尤爲根極之論，匪直留心世務而已。佳士！佳士！
考試官教諭朱批：造語暢雄，敘事詳覈。
考試官教授李批：處置周詳，鑿有實用。

國家之柔遠也以德，而利用在威；人臣之靖邊也以才，而利用在信。德以濟威，則威讋而裔夷慕義；才以布信，則信立而異類嚮風。二者要在審勢達變，而吾之操縱不失
translation_en:
In antiquity, Emperor Yu spoke of the mind of the Heavenly King, saying: "With heavenly virtue he comes forth in tranquility; the sun and moon shine and the four seasons proceed, just as day and night have their regular course, and clouds move and rain is bestowed." This is the culmination of virtue and the ultimate standard of antiquity. Lie Yukou [Liezi], failing to grasp this doctrine, claimed instead that the sage uses intelligence to ensnare the foolish masses just as one cages a troop of monkeys—how extreme are such trifling words that whittle away at orthodoxy! Such are my narrow, humble views; may Your Excellency examine and select from them with care.

Question Five
Chen Guike
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Liang: In the great affairs of western Yue [Guangxi], the Yi and Liao tribes stand alongside the native chieftains (tusi), yet the native chieftains are an internal affliction. This essay sets forth their conditions and attitudes in full, proposes proper methods for reining them in, and at the end comes back to obtaining the right men—an argument that gets to the very root of the matter, showing far more than a mere attention to worldly affairs. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhu: The phrasing is fluent and vigorous; the account of affairs is detailed and well-verified.
Comment by Examiner Professor Li: The proposed dispositions are comprehensive and thorough, possessing concrete practical utility.

The state pacifies distant peoples through virtue, yet its effective application lies in majesty; a minister calms the frontiers through talent, yet its effective application lies in trustworthiness. When virtue tempers majesty, majesty inspires awe and the border tribes yearn for righteousness; when talent spreads trustworthiness, trust is established and alien peoples turn toward our civilizing influence. For both, the key lies in assessing the situation and adapting to changing circumstances, so that our control over when to tighten and when to relax is never lost…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
焉耳若夫刧之以勢而威益褻籠之以詐
而術愈窮馴至于體統凌夷法令隔閡釁
端滋萌師徒數起欲以振頹綱而收長策
惠中國以綏要荒難矣故善理國者不徒
吾德之足以懷而尤恃吾威之不可犯善
馭夷者不患吾力之不足以懾而患吾信
之不足孚知此則百粤之事可得而言矣
執事策諸生而以夷官下詢大
聖朝無外之治垂遠夷世守之經甚遐筭也請
===
先陳其狀而後及制馭之方執事試垂聽
焉夫自有西南夷以來即有夷官爲之藩
籬屏蔽其種類最夥其盤據最遼雜習蠻
風脫略漢法徵兵不俟合符慮囚無煩覆
讞出非甲冑不行入非扃鍵不居其俗也
棄禮義上首功勇于公戰怯于私鬭茍有
利焉不顧其後其于父子兄弟禽獸耳貪
而嗜殺其性也毒弩長矛强弓利劔茂林
叢箐疾于走兔扳崖躡蹬捷于升猱探穴
punctuated:
焉耳。若夫刧之以勢，而威益褻；籠之以詐，而術愈窮。馴至于體統凌夷，法令隔閡，釁端滋萌，師徒數起，欲以振頹綱而收長策，惠中國以綏要荒，難矣。故善理國者，不徒吾德之足以懷，而尤恃吾威之不可犯；善馭夷者，不患吾力之不足以懾，而患吾信之不足孚。知此，則百粤之事可得而言矣。
執事策諸生，而以夷官下詢，大聖朝無外之治，垂遠夷世守之經，甚遐筭也。請先陳其狀，而後及制馭之方，執事試垂聽焉。夫自有西南夷以來，即有夷官爲之藩籬屏蔽，其種類最夥，其盤據最遼。雜習蠻風，脫略漢法，徵兵不俟合符，慮囚無煩覆讞，出非甲冑不行，入非扃鍵不居，其俗也；棄禮義，上首功，勇于公戰，怯于私鬭，茍有利焉，不顧其後，其于父子兄弟，禽獸耳，貪而嗜殺，其性也；毒弩長矛，强弓利劔，茂林叢箐，疾于走兔，扳崖躡蹬，捷于升猱，探穴
translation_en:
… is not lost. As for coercing them through force, authority only becomes more profaned; ensnaring them through deceit, stratagems only grow more exhausted. Gradually this leads to the deterioration of the system of governance, the obstruction of laws and ordinances, the sprouting of causes for conflict, and the frequent mobilization of troops. To wish under such conditions to revive decayed authority and achieve a long-term strategy, bringing benefit to the central states in order to pacify the distant borderlands, would be difficult indeed. Therefore, those skilled at governing the state do not merely rely on their virtue being sufficient to cherish the people, but especially depend on their majesty being inviolable; those skilled at controlling the non-Chinese tribes do not worry that their strength is insufficient to overawe them, but worry that their trustworthiness is insufficient to win their confidence. Once this is understood, the affairs of the Hundred Yue [Guangdong and Guangxi] can be discussed.

Your Excellency has posed a policy question to us students, inquiring into the matter of native officials (yi guan), so as to magnify our Sacred Dynasty's governance that excludes nothing and to hand down a constant standard for the distant tribes to observe for generations—this is a most far-reaching design. Allow me first to set forth their condition, and then address the methods for controlling them; may Your Excellency deign to listen.

Ever since there have been Southwestern tribes, there have been native officials to serve as a protective hedge and screen. Their types are most numerous, and the territories they occupy are most vast. They mix in barbarian customs and disregard Chinese law; in levying troops they do not wait for matching tallies, and in reviewing prisoners they do not bother with re-examination; when going out they do not travel without armor and helmet, and when entering they do not dwell without bolts and locks—such are their customs. They cast aside ritual and righteousness and prize the taking of heads; they are brave in public warfare and timid in private brawls; so long as there is profit in it, they do not consider the aftermath; in their relations between father and son, or older and younger brother, they are no different from birds and beasts, being greedy and fond of killing—such is their nature. With poisoned crossbows and long spears, strong bows and sharp swords, in dense forests and thick bamboo groves they are swifter than running hares, and in scaling cliffs and treading stone steps they are more agile than climbing apes; when probing caves…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
則風雨經旬搜伏則瘴癘累日其長技也
谿峒夷獠所在充斥夷之畏狼如貍捕鼠
以故積威所劫未戰先怖惟死與走無敢
拒敵者鼓行而前所向披靡其先聲也堅
甲利兵雖資捍禦而狼貪麋獷未易擾馴
軍令不遵點閘不服虛數實支受賄縱賊
而所過荊榛不減于寇其虐焰也尺布斗
粟我無所養而朝令夕集彼謂當然有事
則出而應伍鋒鏑不辭無事則歸而力耕
===
繇賦薄貢此中國之所資也地廣官高習
兵擅利生齒益繁財貨益廣詐以謀成罪
以功解種憂釀禍蔑玩內地此中國之所
虞也前代乍叛乍臣姑置不論
明興二祖開基神武振世天戈所指雲附景從
百夷之長皆席藁俟俘納款乞宥海涵天
覆待以不死乃因地置官任土効貢俾世
掌故部爲我外藩卽周人疆以戎索之意
約法疎簡要示羈縻而已然繼及之際令
punctuated: 則風雨經旬，搜伏則瘴癘累日，其長技也。谿峒夷獠所在充斥，夷之畏狼如貍捕鼠，以故積威所劫，未戰先怖，惟死與走，無敢拒敵者，鼓行而前，所向披靡，其先聲也。堅甲利兵，雖資捍禦，而狼貪麋獷，未易擾馴。軍令不遵，點閘不服，虛數實支，受賄縱賊，而所過荊榛，不減于寇，其虐焰也。尺布斗粟，我無所養，而朝令夕集，彼謂當然；有事則出而應伍，鋒鏑不辭，無事則歸而力耕，繇賦薄貢，此中國之所資也。地廣官高，習兵擅利，生齒益繁，財貨益廣，詐以謀成，罪以功解，種憂釀禍，蔑玩內地，此中國之所虞也。前代乍叛乍臣，姑置不論。明興，二祖開基，神武振世，天戈所指，雲附景從。百夷之長，皆席藁俟俘，納款乞宥，海涵天覆，待以不死。乃因地置官，任土効貢，俾世掌故部，爲我外藩，卽周人「疆以戎索」之意，約法疎簡，要示羈縻而已。然繼及之際，令…
translation_en:
… can endure wind and rain for ten days at a stretch, and in searching out hidden ambushes they can brave miasmic pestilence for days on end—such are their special skills. The tribal peoples (Yi and Liao) of the streams and grottoes fill every quarter, yet these tribesmen fear the "wolf troops" (langbing) just as mice fear a wildcat catching them. For this reason, cowed by their accumulated prestige, the tribesmen are terrified even before battle is joined; their only choices are to die or to flee, none daring to resist the enemy. Advancing to the beat of drums, they sweep away all before them—such is their daunting reputation. Yet although we rely on their strong armor and sharp weapons for defense, they are greedy as wolves and wild as elk, and are not easily tamed. They disobey military orders, refuse to submit to roll calls and inspections, pad their numbers to draw actual rations, take bribes to let bandits go, and leave everywhere they pass reduced to brambles and thorns, no less than the bandits themselves—such is their destructive ferocity. We do not support them with so much as a foot of cloth or a peck of grain, yet if an order is issued in the morning they assemble by evening, taking this as a matter of course; when trouble arises they go forth to fill the ranks without shrinking from blades and arrows, and when peace returns they go home to till the soil with all their strength, rendering labor service, taxes, and modest tribute—this is what China relies upon them for. Yet their territories are vast and their offices high; they are practiced in warfare and monopolize local profits. As their population grows ever more numerous and their wealth ever more extensive, their treacheries succeed through calculation and their crimes are absolved through military merit, planting the seeds of sorrow, brewing disaster, and treating the interior heartland with contemptuous disregard—this is what China fears from them. How in former dynasties they alternately rebelled and submitted, we may set aside without discussion.

With the rise of the Ming, our Two Progenitors (Taizu and Taizong) laid the foundations of the empire, their divine martial prowess shaking the world; wherever the heavenly halberd pointed, people attached themselves like clouds and followed like shadows. The chieftains of the hundred tribes all sat upon straw mats awaiting capture, offering submission and begging for pardon. Encompassing them like the sea and sheltering them like heaven, our emperors spared their lives. Thereupon, offices were established in accordance with local conditions, and tribute was presented according to what the land produced, allowing them to govern their old tribes hereditarily and serve as our outer bulwark. This followed the very principle of the Zhou people in "bounding them according to Rong regulations"—keeping laws and stipulations loose and simple, aiming only to maintain a halter-and-bridle (jimi) control. Yet at the time of hereditary succession, the statutes…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
甲具昭或獻劒馬或貢方物萬里赴
闕印首請
命蓋
朝廷假之官秩以固邊圉土酋藉
國寵靈以長醜類貽謀之遠經制之周秦漢
而下所未有也天順八年上
兩宮徽號
詔許繳呈勘奏即給冠裳成化十五年因方隅
旱灾
===
詔令輸粟濟邊即許沿襲于是經制既卑規取
愈陋乃至介使末將威福自恣戎心日玩
驕悍漸啓矣
孝宗末年發憤釐革正德間旋復隳廢
世宗始曲為條約稍復
國初之舊大抵創始者多遠圖喜事者輒厭
故建白日煩紛更愈甚其究也綱紀瀾渙
處置乖方察察汶汶罔上遂私迨乎逆節
犯順干戈相尋叱咤徒勤獮薙失策竭膏
punctuated: 甲具昭：或獻劒馬，或貢方物，萬里赴闕，印首請命。蓋朝廷假之官秩以固邊圉，土酋藉國寵靈以長醜類，貽謀之遠，經制之周，秦漢而下所未有也。天順八年，上兩宮徽號，詔許繳呈勘奏，即給冠裳。成化十五年，因方隅旱灾，詔令輸粟濟邊，即許沿襲。于是經制既卑，規取愈陋，乃至介使末將威福自恣，戎心日玩，驕悍漸啓矣。孝宗末年，發憤釐革，正德間旋復隳廢。世宗始曲為條約，稍復國初之舊。大抵創始者多遠圖，喜事者輒厭故，建白日煩，紛更愈甚。其究也，綱紀瀾渙，處置乖方，察察汶汶，罔上遂私。迨乎逆節犯順，干戈相尋，叱咤徒勤，獮薙失策，竭膏
translation_en: … statutes were clearly manifest: some offered up swords and horses, while others presented local products as tribute, traveling ten thousand li to the imperial court, bowing their heads [?] to request investiture. Indeed, the court lent them official ranks to secure the frontier defenses, while the native chieftains relied on the dynasty's favor and prestige to rule over their kindred. Such far-reaching counsel for posterity and comprehensive institutional regulations had never been seen since the Qin and Han dynasties. In the eighth year of the Tianshun reign (1464), upon the bestowal of honorable titles on the Two Palaces, an imperial decree permitted them simply to submit verification memorials to be granted official caps and robes immediately. In the fifteenth year of the Chenghua reign (1479), because of drought disasters in the region, an imperial decree ordered that those who transported grain to relieve the frontier would immediately be permitted to inherit their posts. Thereupon, as the institutional regulations became debased and the means of exaction grew ever more sordid, it reached the point where minor envoys and petty commanders arbitrarily dispensed punishments and rewards at will; the hearts of the tribesmen grew daily more contemptuous, and their arrogance and ferocity were gradually unleashed. In the final years of Emperor Xiaozong's reign, he roused himself to reform and rectify these abuses, yet during the Zhengde reign (1506–1521) they soon fell back into ruin and neglect. Only under Emperor Shizong were detailed regulations carefully drawn up, somewhat restoring the old system of the beginning of the dynasty. In general, those who found institutions mostly plan for the distant future, whereas those who delight in meddling readily tire of old ways; as proposals grew daily more numerous, chaotic alterations became ever more extreme. In the end, principles and discipline dissolved, measures were mishandled, and officials were either overly picky or muddled and corrupt, deceiving their superiors to pursue private ends. By the time rebellious elements violated allegiance and warfare followed incessantly, angry bellowing proved mere futile toil and campaigns of extermination missed the mark, exhausting the lifeblood…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
血于邊氓貽憂勤于
廷議是故大而逞逆則爲玵Jh濬猛小而作
孽則爲蘇受楷寰師老財費而勦撫莫施
日蔓月滋而恩威竝爽當事諸臣蓋與有
責矣可盡責之夷裔者流哉夫輪轂不運
甚者必起而易轍乃可駕也琴瑟不調甚
者必起而改絃乃可鼓也今欲使之俯首
聽
命先讋伏其野心而交臂請纓能盡得其死
===
力土酋獲首領之安而
國家免尾大之慮其道豈有他哉吾所以自
治者有四一曰信賞罰二曰慎名器三曰
定經界四曰嚴勘襲而重事權則內治之
本也我之所以爲彼謀者亦有四一曰申
降削二曰暴罪過三曰孤黨與四曰禁撥
置而體夷情則駕馭之要也何謂信賞罰
土酋調發全藉
國威而威令之行全賴賞罰邇來徵兵禦宄
punctuated: 血于邊氓，貽憂勤于廷議。是故大而逞逆，則爲玵Jh濬猛；小而作孽，則爲蘇、受、楷、寰。師老財費而勦撫莫施，日蔓月滋而恩威竝爽。當事諸臣蓋與有責矣，可盡責之夷裔者流哉？夫輪轂不運甚者，必起而易轍乃可駕也；琴瑟不調甚者，必起而改絃乃可鼓也。今欲使之俯首聽命，先讋伏其野心；而交臂請纓，能盡得其死力；土酋獲首領之安，而國家免尾大之慮，其道豈有他哉？吾所以自治者有四：一曰信賞罰，二曰慎名器，三曰定經界，四曰嚴勘襲，而重事權則內治之本也。我之所以爲彼謀者亦有四：一曰申降削，二曰暴罪過，三曰孤黨與，四曰禁撥置，而體夷情則駕馭之要也。何謂信賞罰？土酋調發，全藉國威；而威令之行，全賴賞罰。邇來徵兵禦宄，
translation_en: …blood of the frontier populace and bequeathing anxiety and toil to the deliberations at court. For this reason, on a large scale, when they indulge in rebellion, they become like Cen Jun and Cen Meng [? 玵Jh濬猛]; on a small scale, when they cause trouble, they become like Lu Su, Wang Shou, Cen Kai, and Zhao Huan. The troops grow exhausted and wealth is squandered, yet neither extermination nor pacification can be effectively applied; day by day they spread and month by month they multiply, while both grace and awe fail alike. The various officials in charge surely share in the responsibility for this—how can the blame be placed entirely upon the likes of these native frontier tribes? Now, when wheels and hubs fail badly to turn, one must rise and change the ruts before the carriage can be driven; when zithers are badly out of tune, one must rise and restring them before they can be played. Today, if we wish to make them bow their heads and obey commands, first cowing their untamed ambitions, and then make them fold their arms in submission and request tassels to serve, so that we can fully obtain their service unto death—whereby the native chieftains secure the safety of their own heads and the state is spared the worry of appendages growing too big to wag—is there any other way to achieve this? There are four measures by which we govern ourselves: the first is to make rewards and punishments trustworthy; the second is to be prudent with titles and insignia; the third is to fix territorial boundaries; and the fourth is to strictly verify hereditary succession—while giving weight to administrative authority is the root of internal governance. There are also four measures by which we plan for them: the first is to enforce demotion and reduction of territory; the second is to expose offenses and faults; the third is to isolate their factions and partisans; and the fourth is to prohibit instigators—while showing consideration for native conditions is the essential point of reigning them in. What is meant by making rewards and punishments trustworthy? The requisitioning and deployment of native chieftains depends entirely on the prestige of the state, and the enforcement of prestigious commands relies entirely on rewards and punishments. Recently, when levying troops to defend against bandits…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
甘言誘之罷役論功靦然食約以故兵出
如借師行如寇若奉驕子置不敢問賞旣
不信罰安從施哉宜申舊章明賞格獲級
者立驗轅門頒金紀籍擾民者按治戲下
請劒行誅夫啖之以財貨則羣然樂趨督
之以威刑則凜然服役緩急有令彼亦無
所藉口以干後至者矣何謂慎名器故事
土人有功惟優賞賚邇因邊方財詘始議
官階彼本猴冠旣難俛伏更加虎翼益肆
===
憑陵曩時單騎入郭屏息階下今則輿皁
充擁比跡漢官簾近堂卑冠下履上此其
漸不可長也自今鵰勦常勞惟多金帛大
征殊績始議品銜庶等威辨而覬覦消名
分嚴而激勸著何謂定經界夷漢櫛比疆
域易淆川谷星羅畦畛無別力强則蠶食
無厭勢弱則蝟縮受侵宜先之文告各守
舊封繼之丈勘一清兼并分圖畫界勒石
垂盟其挾衆仇鄰爭疆啓釁者廉其屈直
punctuated: 甘言誘之，罷役論功，靦然食約。以故兵出如借，師行如寇，若奉驕子，置不敢問。賞旣不信，罰安從施哉？宜申舊章，明賞格：獲級者立驗轅門，頒金紀籍；擾民者按治戲下，請劒行誅。夫啖之以財貨，則羣然樂趨；督之以威刑，則凜然服役。緩急有令，彼亦無所藉口以干後至者矣。何謂慎名器？故事，土人有功，惟優賞賚。邇因邊方財詘，始議官階。彼本猴冠，旣難俛伏，更加虎翼，益肆憑陵。曩時單騎入郭，屏息階下；今則輿皁充擁，比跡漢官。簾近堂卑，冠下履上，此其漸不可長也。自今鵰勦常勞，惟多金帛；大征殊績，始議品銜。庶等威辨而覬覦消，名分嚴而激勸著。何謂定經界？夷漢櫛比，疆域易淆；川谷星羅，畦畛無別。力强則蠶食無厭，勢弱則蝟縮受侵。宜先之文告，各守舊封；繼之丈勘，一清兼并。分圖畫界，勒石垂盟。其挾衆仇鄰、爭疆啓釁者，廉其屈直，
translation_en:
…enticing them with sweet words; yet when the campaign ends and merits are assessed, we brazenly break our promises. Consequently, when their troops are mobilized it is as if we are begging for a loan, and when their armies march they act like bandits; we coddle them like spoiled children, setting aside their offenses and not daring to question them. When rewards are already untrustworthy, how can punishments be enforced? We should reiterate the old statutes and clarify the scale of rewards: for those who take enemy heads, verify them immediately at the camp gate, distribute gold, and record their names in the registers; for those who harass the people, investigate and punish them right beneath the commander's banner, requesting the imperial sword to carry out executions. If we entice them with wealth and goods, they will flock to serve gladly; if we supervise them with awe-inspiring punishments, they will submit to service in fear and trembling. When orders are met in emergencies, they too will have no excuse to incur the penalty for arriving late.

What is meant by being circumspect with titles and insignia? According to precedent, when native chieftains achieved merit, they were only given generous material rewards. Recently, because finances on the frontier have been exhausted, we began conferring official ranks upon them. They are by nature like monkeys in caps, already hard to make bow in submission; adding wings to a tiger only makes them more unrestrained in their arrogance and encroachment. In the past, they entered the city walls as lone riders and held their breath at the foot of the steps; nowadays, they are surrounded by throngs of carriage attendants and runners, putting themselves on a par with Chinese officials. When the screen is close, the hall becomes low; when the cap is below, the shoes are above—this is a tendency that must not be allowed to grow. From now on, for routine service in swift raids, only give them abundant gold and silk; only for extraordinary achievements in grand campaigns should we deliberate on granting official rank and title. Thus, hierarchical prestige will be distinguished and presumptuous ambitions dispelled; status obligations will be strict and incentives made manifest.

What is meant by fixing boundaries? Native tribes and Chinese subjects live side by side like the teeth of a comb, so their territories are easily confused; rivers and valleys are scattered like stars, with no clear divisions between fields. The strong蠶-like nibble away at others' land without satiation, while the weak curl up like hedgehogs and suffer encroachment. We should first issue proclamations ordering each to keep to their old fiefs, and follow up with land surveys and inspections to completely clear up annexations, dividing the maps, drawing boundaries, and carving stones to hand down covenants. As for those who rely on their numbers to feud with neighbors and start hostilities over territory, we should investigate who is in the wrong and who is in the right, …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
移兵向之庶強梗絶廣地之謀柔懦獲保
境之便何謂嚴勘襲土人狤悍甘臣妾我
者以結勘之權在我也在考定譜牒則世
系可求預陳嫡孽則宗庶不紊先以合族
之議上之郡郡上之司司請之督撫類報
之部一如武職從事舊者未老不得謝事
繼者未勘不得署官則予奪在我釁孽不
萌何謂申降削土酋據地連城生殺予奪
惟其所使苟任其胷臆漸至恣睢為虺弗
===
摧為蛇奈何自今觖法觸憲愆期抗令者
一不悛白之督府革其章服再不悛請之
天朝削其世官或郡降為州州降為邑邑降為
巡司擇族之賢者易而立之夫奪彼與此
則為惡者懼以大更小則體勢自卑孰敢
有越厥志而自失操柄者何謂暴罪過諸
酋聲勢相軋誇詐自雄即罹譴呵削秩褫
裳而僻處一隅楊楊猶昔也自今有麗法
者按其罪狀暴之隣境曰某地某負慝作
punctuated:
移兵向之。庶強梗絶廣地之謀，柔懦獲保境之便。

何謂嚴勘襲？土人狤悍，甘臣妾我者，以結勘之權在我也。在考定譜牒，則世系可求；預陳嫡孽，則宗庶不紊。先以合族之議上之郡，郡上之司，司請之督撫，類報之部，一如武職從事。舊者未老不得謝事，繼者未勘不得署官，則予奪在我，釁孽不萌。

何謂申降削？土酋據地連城，生殺予奪，惟其所使。苟任其胷臆，漸至恣睢，為虺弗摧，為蛇奈何？自今觖法觸憲、愆期抗令者，一不悛，白之督府，革其章服；再不悛，請之天朝，削其世官。或郡降為州，州降為邑，邑降為巡司，擇族之賢者易而立之。夫奪彼與此，則為惡者懼；以大更小，則體勢自卑。孰敢有越厥志，而自失操柄者？

何謂暴罪過？諸酋聲勢相軋，誇詐自雄，即罹譴呵，削秩褫裳，而僻處一隅，楊楊猶昔也。自今有麗法者，按其罪狀，暴之隣境，曰：「某地某，負慝作
translation_en:
…and move troops against the culprit. In this way, the strong and obstinate will abandon their schemes to expand their territory, and the weak and timid will gain the advantage of preserving their borders.

What is meant by strictly verifying hereditary succession? The reason native peoples, fierce and unruly as they are, willingly submit to us as subjects and servants is that the authority to verify and guarantee their succession rests with us. This consists in examining and fixing their genealogical registers so that their lineages can be traced, and requiring prior declaration of legitimate and concubine-born sons so that the main and collateral lines are not confused. First, the consensus of the entire clan should be submitted to the prefecture; the prefecture submits it to the Provincial Administration Commission; the Commission requests approval from the Supreme Commander and Grand Coordinator, who then compile and report such cases to the Ministry, handling them in complete accordance with the procedures for military officers. If the incumbent is not yet old, he may not retire from his duties; if the successor has not yet been verified, he may not serve as acting official. Thus the power to grant and to deprive remains with us, and succession disputes will not sprout.

What is meant by enforcing demotion and deprivation of rank? Native chieftains occupy territories spanning連城相连的 walled towns, exercising the power of life and death, of giving and taking away, entirely at their own whim. If we indulge their willful desires, they will gradually become unbridled and overbearing: if a viper is not crushed when small, what can be done when it becomes a great serpent? Henceforth, for those who flout the law, violate regulations, miss deadlines, or defy orders: if they do not repent the first time, report them to the Supreme Commander's office and strip them of their official insignia and robes; if they fail to repent a second time, petition the Imperial Court to strip them of their hereditary offices. Alternatively, demote a prefecture to a subprefecture, a subprefecture to a district, or a district to a Police Office, and select a worthy member of their clan to replace them and be installed. Indeed, taking from one and giving to another makes evildoers afraid; replacing a larger jurisdiction with a smaller one naturally lowers their status and power. Who then would dare overstep his bounds and thereby lose his own grip on authority?

What is meant by publicizing offenses and transgressions? The various chieftains vie with one another in reputation and influence, boasting and using deceit to aggrandize themselves. Even when they incur reprimands and punishment, having their ranks reduced and their official robes stripped away, they live in isolated corners and remain just as arrogant and self-satisfied as before. Henceforth, whenever anyone runs afoul of the law, we should examine the particulars of his crime and publicize them throughout the neighboring jurisdictions, declaring: "So-and-so of such-and-such a place harbored evil and committed…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
奸戒諭不省今已裂裳罷秩正我典刑覆
轍不遠尔毋效尤彼酋聞之有不消阻閉
藏瞿然改行以冀復舊物者乎何謂禁撥
置土人椎魯戇于理道不敢吾抗者有文
法以牽制之也邇來無良亡命竄名其間
外煽內訌因緣為奸利宜詞其舞文用事
者治之五方流徙投夷有禁土目占恡法
與同科則奸宄不容徑竇自塞何謂孤黨
與力小則易使以義國小則無邪心今土
===
酋大者提封千里擁衆數萬鴟張鷙擊莫
敢誰何顧其御下少恩骨肉最忌一觸法
網人懷異圖俟其難作吾從中劈畫之或
裂地授官或分兵自部一寸之土一旅之
衆我無所利焉凡以定制耳夫勢分難合
息朋奸掉臂之謀地小易制絶恃强跋扈
之患孰肯發首難而貽利他人者由前四
事是我之所自治者也而重事權為急蓋
百粤夷獠帖然聽令者惟督撫耳自襄毅
punctuated: 奸，戒諭不省，今已裂裳罷秩，正我典刑。覆轍不遠，尔毋效尤。」彼酋聞之，有不消阻閉藏、瞿然改行，以冀復舊物者乎？何謂禁撥置？土人椎魯，戇于理道，不敢吾抗者，有文法以牽制之也。邇來無良亡命，竄名其間，外煽內訌，因緣為奸利。宜詞其舞文用事者治之；五方流徙投夷有禁，土目占恡法與同科，則奸宄不容，徑竇自塞。何謂孤黨與？力小則易使以義，國小則無邪心。今土酋大者，提封千里，擁衆數萬，鴟張鷙擊，莫敢誰何。顧其御下少恩，骨肉最忌，一觸法網，人懷異圖。俟其難作，吾從中劈畫之，或裂地授官，或分兵自部，一寸之土、一旅之衆，我無所利焉，凡以定制耳。夫勢分難合，息朋奸掉臂之謀；地小易制，絶恃强跋扈之患。孰肯發首難而貽利他人者？由前四事，是我之所自治者也，而重事權為急。蓋百粤夷獠，帖然聽令者，惟督撫耳。自襄毅…
translation_en:
… treachery; having been admonished without repenting, his robes have now been torn away and his rank dismissed to uphold our statutory punishments. The overturned cart is not far ahead; do not follow his bad example." When those chieftains hear this, will they not be cowed into withdrawing and hiding, startled into reforming their conduct in hopes of recovering their former possessions?

What is meant by prohibiting instigation? The native peoples are simple and uncouth, ignorant of moral principles; the reason they dare not defy us is that there are legal statutes to restrain them. Recently, unscrupulous fugitives have slipped their names in among them, stirring up trouble outside and sowing dissension within, taking advantage of opportunities for illicit profit. We ought to spy out [?] those who manipulate the written law and wield influence, and punish them. There should be prohibitions against vagrants from all regions fleeing to join the non-Chinese tribes, and native headmen who harbor and refuse to hand them over should be punished with the same penalty under the law. Thus villains and traitors will not be tolerated, and the crooked paths and loopholes will naturally be blocked up.

What is meant by isolating their partisans? When their strength is small, they are easy to employ through righteousness; when their territory is small, they harbor no wicked intentions. Nowadays, the greatest of the native chieftains control territories of a thousand li and command multitudes of tens of thousands, puffing themselves up like owls and striking like birds of prey, so that no one dares challenge them. Yet they treat their subordinates with little grace, and their own flesh and blood are most jealous of one another; once they run afoul of the net of the law, everyone harbors ulterior designs. Waiting until internal strife breaks out among them, we can divide and plan from the midst of it—either splitting up their land to confer offices, or dividing their troops into separate commands. From a single inch of land or a single brigade of troops, we seek no profit for ourselves; all is done simply to establish firm control. When their power is divided, it is hard to reunite, putting an end to plots of colluding in villainy and swaggering in defiance; when their territories are small, they are easy to control, cutting off the menace of relying on strength to act as overbearing despots. Who then would be willing to initiate rebellion only to bequeath the benefits to others?

Following the preceding four measures is how we govern ourselves, and among them, giving weight to administrative authority is the most urgent. For among the non-Chinese tribes of the Hundred Yue, the only ones they docilely obey are the Supreme Commander and the Grand Coordinator. Ever since Xiangyi…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
韓雍討平之後而所竄餘孽弘示包荒自
文成王守仁經略之餘而至今遺言尚謂
姑息故曩時赴調恐後今則催督或煩曩
時報兵必實今則名數多冒襲替廢置
朝廷雖假閫外之權而伸縮弛張臣子尚牽
域外之議自今震疊之威必行于土官土
官之命盡制于幕府一切便宜不從中制
則賞罰可信名器可慎經界可定勘襲可
嚴而中國威令常伸如震霆矣由後四事
===
===
是我之所爲彼謀也而體夷情爲急今夫
父兄之于子弟苟役使煩勞且不能無厭
況夷獷之性歲歲調發奔走道途不得顧
其室家治其田里其能無倦且怨乎及事
平則功歸于上而彼一無所與僨帥墨吏
又往往視爲奇貨其能無怒且慢乎既倦
且怨又慢且怒始而徵調違期既而空文
逃罪上嫉下憤月積日深當事者不惟開
誠之圖而直恃籠絡之術以故諭之益梗
punctuated: 韓雍討平之後，而所竄餘孽弘示包荒；自文成王守仁經略之餘，而至今遺言尚謂姑息。故曩時赴調恐後，今則催督或煩；曩時報兵必實，今則名數多冒。襲替廢置，朝廷雖假閫外之權，而伸縮弛張，臣子尚牽域外之議。自今震疊之威，必行于土官，土官之命，盡制于幕府，一切便宜，不從中制，則賞罰可信、名器可慎、經界可定、勘襲可嚴，而中國威令常伸如震霆矣。由後四事，是我之所爲彼謀也，而體夷情爲急。今夫父兄之于子弟，苟役使煩勞，且不能無厭；況夷獷之性，歲歲調發，奔走道途，不得顧其室家、治其田里，其能無倦且怨乎？及事平，則功歸于上，而彼一無所與，僨帥墨吏又往往視爲奇貨，其能無怒且慢乎？既倦且怨，又慢且怒，始而徵調違期，既而空文逃罪。上嫉下憤，月積日深，當事者不惟開誠之圖，而直恃籠絡之術，以故諭之益梗、
translation_en:
… Han Yong (韓雍) suppressed them, magnanimous forbearance was widely shown to the remaining rebels who had fled into hiding; and after the pacification campaigns of Wencheng, Wang Shouren (王守仁), persisting discussion to this day still calls his approach overly indulgent. Thus, whereas in the past they answered troop requisitions fearing to be last, now urging and pressing them has become troublesome; whereas in the past their reported troop numbers were always accurate, now the rosters and counts are full of fraud. Regarding hereditary succession and deposition, although the Court grants autonomous authority beyond the threshold to field commanders, in advancing or retreating and tightening or relaxing control, officials are still constrained by outside criticism. From now on, if awe-inspiring authority is strictly enforced upon the native officials, if the fate of the native officials is entirely controlled by the Supreme Commander's headquarters, and if all discretionary measures are free from remote interference from the capital, then rewards and punishments will be trustworthy, titles and ranks will be prudently guarded, boundaries will be settled, and the verification of succession will be strict, so that the prestige and commands of the Central State will always prevail like a thunderclap.

Following from the latter four points, these are the measures by which we plan on their behalf, and among them, sympathizing with the conditions of the native tribes is the most urgent. Now then, even in the relationship of fathers and elder brothers toward sons and younger brothers, if they are subjected to burdensome and exhausting labor, they cannot help but grow weary of it. How much more so with the fierce nature of the tribespeople, when they are requisitioned and mobilized year after year, rushing along the roads, unable to care for their families or cultivate their fields and villages—how could they not feel both exhausted and resentful? And when the campaign is pacified, the credit goes to their superiors while they have no share in it at all, and disgraced commanders and corrupt officials furthermore often treat them as rare merchandise to exploit—how could they not become both angry and defiant? Being already exhausted and resentful, and moreover defiant and angry, at first they miss the deadlines for troop requisitions, and subsequently they use empty paperwork to evade punishment. Resentment above and indignation below accumulate month by month and deepen day by day. Those in charge do not contemplate plans of sincere openness, but merely rely on tactics of manipulation; for this reason, the more one instructs them, the more obstinate they become, …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
撫之益疑卒至禍亂相尋而不解也故平
居無事則布信懷恩有事出征則宣威仗
義芻糗必豐毋使客兵一而當土兵五可
也功級必賞毋以冒死所得而攘之將校
可也廉晙刻之吏平爭鬭之端則降削可
申罪過可暴黨與可孤廢置可禁而土夷
中心誠服若腐鼠矣雖然愚生猶有說焉
漢得一谷永守鬱林而烏滸內屬唐得一
李靖撫嶺南而遠夷安堵我
===
明沐英守雲南而滇酋効順黃福治安南而交
人寢謀是故先王慎擇邊吏重于內地講
求曠度略于曲防寧使化理稍塞倔强一
隅毋俾輿圖廣收貽憂萬姓惟夫吏好蓄
積政多解弛或遠嫌自潔或求勝喜功則
遐陬日以多故耳故遠方之官非有爲不
足以戢亂非有守不足以服人非久事任
無以諳土俗非重權力無以專責成誠得
其人而任之寬其約束優以寵榮即滿考
punctuated: 撫之益疑，卒至禍亂相尋而不解也。故平居無事，則布信懷恩；有事出征，則宣威仗義。芻糗必豐，毋使客兵一而當土兵五，可也；功級必賞，毋以冒死所得而攘之將校，可也。廉晙刻之吏，平爭鬭之端，則降削可申、罪過可暴、黨與可孤、廢置可禁，而土夷中心誠服，若腐鼠矣。雖然，愚生猶有說焉。漢得一谷永守鬱林，而烏滸內屬；唐得一李靖撫嶺南，而遠夷安堵；我明沐英守雲南，而滇酋効順；黃福治安南，而交人寢謀。是故先王慎擇邊吏，重于內地；講求曠度，略于曲防。寧使化理稍塞、倔强一隅，毋俾輿圖廣收、貽憂萬姓。惟夫吏好蓄積、政多解弛，或遠嫌自潔，或求勝喜功，則遐陬日以多故耳。故遠方之官，非有爲不足以戢亂，非有守不足以服人，非久事任無以諳土俗，非重權力無以專責成。誠得其人而任之，寬其約束，優以寵榮，即滿考
translation_en: …and the more one attempts to pacify them, the more suspicious they grow, until finally disasters and rebellions follow one after another without resolution. Therefore, in peaceful times when there are no incidents, one should spread trust and make them cherish imperial grace; when troubles arise and expeditions are launched, one should manifest awe-inspiring authority and uphold righteousness. Forage and provisions must be abundant—do not let the allowance for one non-native soldier equal that of five native soldiers; that will suffice. Meritorious heads taken in battle must be rewarded—do not allow what the native troops have won by braving death to be seized from them by commanders and officers; that will suffice. Investigate harsh and rapacious officials and settle the causes of disputes and feuds; then demotions and reductions of territory can be enforced, offenses can be exposed, factions and confederates can be isolated, and arbitrary depositions and installations can be prohibited—whereupon the native tribesmen will sincerely submit in their hearts and become as harmless as a rotten rat. Even so, this foolish student still has more to say. When the Han dynasty obtained a single Gu Yong 谷永 as Grand Administrator of Yulin, the Wuhu tribes submitted; when the Tang obtained a single Li Jing 李靖 to pacify Lingnan, the distant barbarians lived in peace; under our Ming, when Mu Ying 沐英 guarded Yunnan, the chieftains of Dian rendered obedience, and when Huang Fu 黃福 governed Annan, the people of Jiaozhi abandoned their plots. For this reason, the former kings chose frontier officials with even greater care than those for the interior, and cultivated broad-minded magnanimity while paying less heed to petty precautions. They would rather allow civilizing governance to be slightly obstructed by stubborn defiance in one corner than to gather vast territories into the map at the cost of bequeathing anxiety to the myriad people. It is only when officials are fond of hoarding wealth and governance becomes largely lax—or when some hold aloof from suspicion merely to keep themselves pure, while others seek victory and delight in military exploits—that the distant marches become daily more troubled. Thus, for officials in distant regions, without administrative capability they cannot quell disorder; without personal integrity they cannot win people's allegiance; without long tenure in office they have no way to understand local customs; and without weighty authority they have no way to bear concentrated responsibility for results. If we truly find the right men and entrust them with office, relax the restrictions upon them, treat them generously with favor and honor, and even when their terms of evaluation are completed…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
不伐豈惟兩江土酋可繫頸而制命將百
粤夷獠亦伏喙而寒心矣復
祖宗之憲章而正夷夏之大分壯
國家之神氣而垂嶺海之久安要不出此語
曰明王有道守在四夷内治之謂也又曰
閫外之事一以付之任人之謂也敢以復
于執事
punctuated: 不伐，豈惟兩江土酋可繫頸而制命，將百粤夷獠亦伏喙而寒心矣。復祖宗之憲章，而正夷夏之大分；壯國家之神氣，而垂嶺海之久安，要不出此。語曰：「明王有道，守在四夷。」内治之謂也。又曰：「閫外之事，一以付之。」任人之謂也。敢以復于執事。
translation_en: … is not replaced, then not only could the native chieftains of the Two Rivers be bound by the neck and have their fates controlled, but the tribal peoples of the Hundred Yue would also hold their tongues in submission and tremble at heart. To restore the statutory institutions of our Imperial Ancestors and rectify the great demarcation between non-Chinese and Chinese; to strengthen the vital spirit of the Dynastic State and bequeath lasting peace to the mountain ranges and southern seas—in essence, nothing goes beyond this. As the saying goes: "When an enlightened king possesses the Way, his defense lies among the Four Barbarians." This refers to internal governance. And as another saying goes: "Affairs beyond the threshold are wholly entrusted to him." This refers to employing the right men. I venture to present this in reply to Your Excellency.

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
主上楙峻德章洪業深惟太平之
原右文賓賢以風寓內寓內
士無問遐逖靡不刮劘灑濯
軌策前塗以待登選是歲丙
子秋廣西鄉試事竣旣已得
士之雋者而籍
===
奏之矣故事信亮宜有言綴末
簡竊惟勳華之世道化郅隆
七旬格苗兩階舞干文德敷
於遐阻聲敎訖于要荒萬邦
黎獻共惟帝臣而徯帝舉抑
何盛也迺其知而舉之也則
敷納以言焉爾稽九德稽載
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序

主上楙峻德，章洪業，深惟太平之原，右文賓賢，以風寓內。寓內士無問遐逖，靡不刮劘灑濯，軌策前塗，以待登選。是歲丙子秋，廣西鄉試事竣，旣已得士之雋者而籍奏之矣。故事，信亮宜有言綴末簡。竊惟勳華之世，道化郅隆，七旬格苗，兩階舞干，文德敷於遐阻，聲敎訖于要荒，萬邦黎獻，共惟帝臣，而徯帝舉，抑何盛也！迺其知而舉之也，則敷納以言焉爾，稽九德、稽載…
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

His Majesty cultivates lofty virtue and manifests his great enterprise. Deeply reflecting upon the foundations of great peace, he esteems civil culture and treats the worthy as guests in order to inspire the realm. Throughout the realm, scholars, regardless of how distant or remote they may be, without exception polish and cleanse themselves, driving themselves onward along the path ahead as they await selection and advancement. In the autumn of this bingzi year [1576], the affairs of the Guangxi Provincial Examination were brought to completion, and the most outstanding scholars have already been selected, registered, and presented in a memorial to the throne. By precedent, I, Xinliang, ought to compose some words to append to the end of the volume.

I humbly reflect that in the ages of Yao [Fangxun 放勳] and Shun [Chonghua 重華], moral transformation reached the utmost flourishing. In seventy days the Miao were won over as the shield-dance was performed between the two staircases; civil virtue was spread to distant and rugged lands, and prestigious instruction reached the outer domains of the wilds. The eminent elders of the myriad states all served together as servants of the Emperor and awaited the Emperor's elevation—how magnificent indeed! Yet as for how they were recognized and elevated, they simply presented and were received by means of their words, and were examined according to the Nine Virtues and examined according to their conduct of affairs…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
采焉爾而科條簡闊不少概
見亡其所用者不必所養乎
比攷命官之詞勞來匡直輔
翼以振新其德者如此其備
故當其時士皆有常言罔攸
伏而孔子獨稱唐虞爲盛際
有繇也廣西距
===
京圻萬里古百粤地我
明統一區宇
文命誕敷武功丕振士之涵濡
衣被既久屬者醜類蕩夷四
郊新去湯火圭蓽奧渫之儒
摶心揖志益以脩其故業而
鄙閑疏邈未皇暇庠序之事
punctuated: 采焉爾，而科條簡闊，不少概見，亡其所用者不必所養乎？比攷命官之詞，勞來匡直輔翼，以振新其德者，如此其備。故當其時，士皆有常，言罔攸伏，而孔子獨稱唐虞爲盛際，有繇也。廣西距京圻萬里，古百粤地。我明統一區宇，文命誕敷，武功丕振，士之涵濡衣被既久。屬者醜類蕩夷，四郊新去湯火，圭蓽奧渫之儒，摶心揖志，益以脩其故業；而鄙閑疏邈、未皇暇庠序之事
translation_en:
… and examining their actual deeds, nothing more; whereas formal regulations and detailed statutes are scarcely to be seen at all. Could it really be that those whom they employed were not necessarily those whom they had nurtured? Yet when one examines the words spoken in commissioning officials—encouraging their coming, straightening the crooked, and assisting and supporting them so as to rouse and renew their virtue—their provision for this was so thorough. Therefore, in that era, scholars all had constancy, no worthy words lay hidden, and there was good reason why Confucius singled out the age of Tang and Yu as the apex of flourishing governance.

Guangxi lies ten thousand li from the capital domain, in the ancient land of the Hundred Yue. Since our Ming unified the realm, civil teachings have been broadly spread and martial achievements grandly displayed, so that scholars have long been steeped in and clothed by this transforming influence. Recently, the vile rebels have been swept away and pacified, and the four outskirts have newly escaped from boiling water and fire. Scholars from humble cottages and obscure backgrounds now concentrate their minds and compose their wills to cultivate their former studies all the more; and even those in remote, rustic borderlands who previously had no leisure for the affairs of schools…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者今皆為置學官弟子獲燿
闇習于光明必韜釰而聲文
闡視敷文舞干之世詎非越
千載而再覿哉
皇上天縱聖神雅嚮儒術頃慮士
習漸窳特
俞輔臣之請取儒林要束而更飭
===
之俾視學者奉以靡軼眞堯
舜振德
盛心也諸士躬際
昌期祗服
睿訓其所感奮踔厲者豈不烝烝
然景附響應愈益思乘時自
効哉乃今擷所為文觀之言
punctuated: 者，今皆為置學官，弟子獲燿闇習于光明，必韜釰而聲文闡。視敷文舞干之世，詎非越千載而再覿哉！皇上天縱聖神，雅嚮儒術。頃慮士習漸窳，特俞輔臣之請，取儒林要束而更飭之，俾視學者奉以靡軼，眞堯、舜振德盛心也。諸士躬際昌期，祗服睿訓，其所感奮踔厲者，豈不烝烝然景附響應，愈益思乘時自効哉！乃今擷所為文觀之，言
translation_en:
… those who previously had no leisure for matters of local schooling now all have Confucian school officials established for them. The students have been able to illuminate their benighted habits with the light of learning, and they will surely sheathe their swords and make their renown in the literary arena. Compared to the era when cultural virtue was spread and shields were brandished in ritual dance, is this not witnessing it once again across the span of a thousand years?

His Majesty the Emperor, endowed by Heaven with sagehood and divinity, has long inclined toward Confucian learning. Recently, concerned that the habits of scholars were gradually deteriorating, he specially approved the request of the Grand Secretaries, taking the essential regulations for the Confucian scholarly community and renewing their enforcement, so that Education Intendants would uphold them without deviation. This is truly the grand mind of Yao and Shun in rousing virtue!

The scholars, personally encountering this prosperous age and reverently submitting to the imperial instructions, are moved to rouse themselves and strive with vigor; how could they not advance in great numbers, following like shadows and echoing like sound, ever more eager to seize the moment and prove their worth? Now, when I gather the essays they have composed and examine them, their words …

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
卽人人殊大都根極理道揚
扢今往刋華芟秕闡發本實
彬彬乎質而文也夐逸疇曩
方寓內士且凌駕之作而嘆
曰斯非
主上德化所暨及者耶是可以言
揚矣雖然虞廷之知人匪獨
===
言焉爾已行有九德於是乎
徵故三六具而浚亮茂也今
諸士言之洵有文矣第令指
九者之德而數之而不能盡
讎其文空言之謂何古之君
子身所實有則言以宣之言
所自許則信以成之是以衷
punctuated: 卽人人殊，大都根極理道，揚扢今往，刋華芟秕，闡發本實，彬彬乎質而文也。夐逸疇曩，方寓內士且凌駕之。作而嘆曰：斯非主上德化所暨及者耶？是可以言揚矣。雖然，虞廷之知人，匪獨言焉爾已，行有九德，於是乎徵，故三六具而浚亮茂也。今諸士言之洵有文矣，第令指九者之德而數之，而不能盡讎其文，空言之謂何？古之君子，身所實有，則言以宣之；言所自許，則信以成之。是以衷
translation_en: …even if they differ from person to person, for the most part they are deeply rooted in principle and the Way, critically appraising the present and the past, pruning away showiness and weeding out chaff, and elucidating what is fundamental and substantive—how harmoniously balanced in substance and refinement! Far surpassing those of former times, they are even on the verge of outstripping the scholars within the heartland of the realm. I rose and sighed, saying: "Is this not the reach of our Sovereign's moral transformation? By this, they are worthy of being recommended for their words!" Even so, in knowing men at the court of Yu [Shun], it was not by words alone; their conduct possessed the Nine Virtues, and by these they were verified, so that when the three and the six virtues were present in them, earnestness and trustworthiness flourished in governance. Now, the words of you scholars are truly refined; yet if one were to point to the Nine Virtues and reckon them, and your conduct could not fully match your literary compositions, what would be the use of empty words? As for the gentlemen of antiquity, what they genuinely possessed in their persons, they expressed through their words; what they committed themselves to in their words, they brought to completion through trustworthiness. Therefore, within…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
外篤懿文行光融爲世誦美
信亮方執此以鏡考諸士而
諸士亦曷以成其信乎夫呑
舟之鱗不游淵垂天之翼不
控榆枋其志遠也辟閭巨闕
不以割驊騮騄駬不以捕鼠
其用巨也故尚友匹休所以
===
明志植德砥行所以利用諸
士誠能羽括鏃礪遠而志巨
而用無論以九見卽有二三
于玆亦足爲彦士使攝尺寸
之柄亢聲騰茂允無負
堯舜之世矣不者靜言庸違
帝世將棄之且以不適訛主司亦
punctuated: 外篤懿，文行光融，爲世誦美。信亮方執此以鏡考諸士，而諸士亦曷以成其信乎？夫呑舟之鱗不游淵，垂天之翼不控榆枋，其志遠也；辟閭、巨闕不以割，驊騮、騄駬不以捕鼠，其用巨也。故尚友匹休，所以明志；植德砥行，所以利用。諸士誠能羽括鏃礪，遠而志，巨而用，無論以九見，卽有二三于玆，亦足爲彦士。使攝尺寸之柄，亢聲騰茂，允無負堯舜之世矣！不者，靜言庸違，帝世將棄之，且以不適訛主司，亦
translation_en: … both inner and outer were sincerely virtuous, and their literary brilliance and conduct shone together, so that they were praised and admired by the world. I, Xinliang, am right now holding to this standard as a mirror to examine all you scholars—how then will you scholars fulfill your trustworthiness? Now, a fish large enough to swallow a boat does not swim in a mere pool, and wings that hang like clouds across the sky do not alight upon elms and sapanwood trees, because their ambitions are far-reaching; the treasured swords Pilü and Juque are not used for mere carving, and the fine steeds Hualiu and Lu'er are not used to catch mice, because their utility is great. Therefore, befriending the ancients and matching their excellence is the means to clarify one's ambition; establishing virtue and honing one's conduct is the means to make advantageous one's utility. If you scholars can trulyfeather your shafts and sharpen your arrowheads, making far-reaching your ambitions and great your utility, then regardless of whether you manifest all nine virtues, even if you possess two or three of them here, it will suffice to make you accomplished gentlemen. Should you be given even an inch or a foot of authority, you will raise your reputation and send forth flourishing merit, truly not failing an age of Yao and Shun! Otherwise, if you speak smoothly when quiet but act perversely when employed, this imperial age will cast you aside; moreover, by being unfit for service you will bring blame upon the examiners, who will also…

title: 萬曆四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
安所傅其咎也昔齊宣好竽
而南郭處士廩食者數百人
迨一一聽之有抱竽而走耳
諸士拔自倫比褒然續食縣

諭朱信亮謹序
punctuated:
安所傅其咎也？昔齊宣好竽，而南郭處士廩食者數百人；迨一一聽之，有抱竽而走耳。諸士拔自倫比，褒然續食縣次，信亮私幸其無濫吹也。繼自今上春官，將有一一而聽者在焉，其尚和其聲以善鳴也哉！
浙江紹興府上虞縣儒學教諭朱信亮謹序。
translation_en:
…how could the examiners escape blame for it? In antiquity, King Xuan of Qi 齊宣 loved the yu mouth organ, and the recluse Master Nanguo 南郭處士 was among several hundred who drew stipends to play it; yet when the succeeding king insisted on hearing them one by one, he could only clutch his instrument and flee. You scholars have now been selected from among your peers and stand preeminent, receiving ongoing provisions at the county staging posts as you travel; I, Xinliang 信亮, privately rejoice in the hope that none among you is merely pretending to play in the ensemble. Hereafter, when you go up to the Ministry of Rites for the Metropolitan Examination, there will be those who listen to you one by one—may you harmonize your notes and sound forth with true excellence!
Respectfully written as an afterword by Zhu Xinliang 朱信亮, Instructor in the Confucian School of Shangyu County 上虞縣, Shaoxing Prefecture 紹興府, Zhejiang 浙江.
